While i was paying I saw this pretty damn good looking sandwich and wished I knew that the option that was the Train Wreck po'boy existed before I made that decision. 

The gumbo was pretty good, I thought it was a little on the milder side but still pretty tasty and it wasn't just a big bowl of rice and just a little bit of of gumbo. Not bad!

Such an amazingly fulfilling meal. I ordered the 1/4 white meat chicken combo with  cilantro rice and black beans and this meal was worth way more than the $7.95 I paid! And the green sauce is delectable. All the servers are sweethearts and eager to assist. Food comes out near immediately after you order. Can't wait to bring my family here.

Damn guys,  don't know what happened since the last time but the food was terrible.   The calamari was very greasy and the fish had no taste at all.   The fries and cole slaw was the only thing of taste.  We had to keep asking other waitresses to get our waitress because she kept walking by our table so fast we couldn't catch her.

This was my first time at Reading Terminal and I am so glad I picked Beck's. I've never had gumbo or jambalaya before, and both blew my socks off. Admittedly, I was feeling overwhelmed by all the possible lunch choices, but the staff at Beck's stopped me with samples. Who can resist? I am so glad they did.

I may not have past experiences to compare, but the chicken and andouille gumbo was bold, hearty, full of meat, and had a nice kick to it. It is the perfect comfort food for a cold rainy day.

I asked for a sample of the gator gumbo, and it tasted just like the chicken gumbo, except that gator meat has an interesting taste. It's definitely tender, and it doesn't taste like something you haven't eaten before. The texture reminded me of the chicken, but not as stringy (not saying that the chicken was dry, but you know how chicken shreds).

Lastly, you must get the corn bread. It was moist and delicious; big contender for the best corn bread I've had. It's not as grainy as most, and almost has the texture of pound cake, but not as dense.

I wish I had more room in my stomach to try the po'boys and other things they serve, but I needed to try out the other food places in the market. This gives me another reason to return to Philly.

Place was clean but room was so hot you cannot control heat. We stayed 2 nights. Left in the morning at 8:00am came back at 6:00 and room wasn't serviced. They didn't seem to care. Probably won't stay again.

The crepes here are the best!!! The service however sucks!! I live down the block from the cafe and order here quite often. 4 out of 5 times the lady who answers the phone always picks up and hangs up on you. Once I didn't have a menu so asked what the bacon crepes were and she hung up on me mid order.
A friend wanted to build her own crepe with "Nutella and bacon" and the lady at the counter looked at her like she had 2 heads.

Quick efficient service, also very friendly. The pastries are a bit on the pricey side for the size of the pastries, but that's in my opinion. We got the tiramisu and the Sfogliatelle; tiramisu was a bit too sweet for a tiramisu (again in my opinion - I have tried a multitude of tiramisus before and this isn't my favorite) and the Sfoliatelle was great for my taste. 

Overall it's a nice small "bakery" in the Reading Terminal Market. And I would find myself coming back for other sweets.

I am a sucker for deep booths and snappy service, and Trident has both. I have to admit, though, that the head-banging music on a Sunday morning was a iittle much for our delicate sensibilities. The burgers here are pretty decent, although the Chesapeake is spiced up with an odd garlicky seasoning. Burgers are served with waffle fries which are just too vanilla for me (papas can be so creative) and are too big for the average girlie mouth. Yes, I used knife and fork here. Overall, Trident is pretty much a winner.

Unexpected delight! My husband and I stopped mainly because of Yelp reviews...outside wasn't that promising. Very charming inside, nicely mixed crowd ...ages and styles. Loved the New England clam chowder and I've sampled many! Good choices for tap beer. I want to come back and try Irish egg rolls and the crab cakes. Bar server Melissa was friendly, helpful and patient
The crepes are amazing! Very fluffy and flavorful. They have really great iced coffee as well.

This was a terrible experience. First off, be aware that you will not be allowed to sit at their counter unless you sit down first and order from the counter. If you have ordered your food from the line, you can't sit down to eat. Even if you have a small child with you, who you also bought an order for. This is not made clear beforehand in any way - they just shoo you if you sit down. So we had the fried Mac and cheese and the crawfish etoufee. The Mac and cheese is doughy, greasy and bland. My 7 year old is a huge Mac and cheese (and fried foods) fan. He tasted it, made a face and just picked at it. I didn't like it either. The crawfish etoufee was lukewarm and tasteless. There was very little crawfish in it - it was almost completely just rice plus a bland, gummy gravy. I didn't finish my meal either. It is lucky that we were able to go to Bassett's for double scoops of ice cream after, or we would have gone hungry. It is tragic that they call themselves Cajun/Creole food, as anyone from New Orleans would not agree. And their rude service does not enliven the meal. Don't waste your time or money - skip this one.

Great spot! Staying across the street and walked over for lunch around 1 on a Monday and surprised how full it was. Sat at the bar and got immediate service. The staff is friendly and check in regularly. I got the Buffalo chicken sandwich and it is huge I could only eat half. The prices are great. Definitely would  recommend stopping by if in the area.

One of my go-to joints @ Reading Terminal and with good reason. The food is good, the people are really nice and for the love of god try a piece of the grilled corn bread. That buttery crust is probably the photo next to the definition of "culinary perfection".  

Now, to catch one of their beigenet days when they aren't sold out....

Chef Joe is a Chinese firecracker with a big sense of humor and an even bigger heart!  I have eaten at his place twice and look forward to my next experience.  My daughter and I walked in very late one evening for a a post theater "snack".  She is vegetarian and we asked the waiter for a suggestion.  He went to the kitchen and almost immediately, Chef Joe arrived at our table and said he would take care of us.  He created a delicious vegetable dish, especially for us, even though it was nearly closing time.  Then he sent out a complimentary dessert - fresh watermelon, strawberries, pineapple, and his famous shortbread cookies. He had decorated each plate uniquely with drawings of animals done in chocolate.  We were delighted with this special and generous treatment!

On another occasion, I went with a friend for his specialty - Peking duck.  It was succulent and savory - absolutely delicious. 

I have heard from friends that his Chinatown Wok and Walk tours are a blast.

Everything I have had at this place has been well made and tasted great. Service is attentive and solid, and they operate well in the fast paced environment of the terminal market. 

Especially enjoy their breakfast options and the chicken po boy and fries. My wife has had the gator on a stick and snapper soup from here and enjoyed both so they do it all well. Great place!

The sushi taste fresh and it's reasonably priced. Two drawbacks are you can't add anything to your rolls and you can't sit at the bar and eat! Bar seating is only for the $35chef's tasting menu? Smh ‍ Hey, you're on a college campus. Either way, I'll back for the sushi!

We had a Friday night reservation, we had indicated it was an Anniversary celebration.  Arrived a half hour early, table was ready...strewn with rose petals!  Service was attentive, food was divine, everything was prompt, prepared as requested, wonderful!  The manager came by twice to check on us.  After dinner someone came to offer a photo memento, which we were delighted to accept!  All together, a wonderful meal, incredible experience, great anniversary celebration!  Lamb chops were delectable, petite filet perfectly done.  Sautéed spinach and mashed potatoes were terrific. We will return!

Woo wee!  The zippy andouille in Beck's gumbo made my mouth sing!  Each bite had a perfect combination of spice and heat, zesty enough to make this pepper lover happy without overwhelming the more timid palate of my dining partner.

The staff offered tastes of many of their dishes, but enticing as they looked, we couldn't eat another bite.

Eating at the counter was fun.  We even snagged a couple of seats at the counter during the lunch rush on Veteran's day.  So, don't let the crowds scare you away.

If I lived in Philly, I'm sure I'd stop by Beck's once a week.

I usually visit the Reading Terminal Market when I am in Philly and sometimes pick up cannoli at Termini Brothers.  On this last visit (first in 2 years), I opted for a chocolate eclair.  Big mistake!  It was a shocking $5 and would have been "meh" at half the price.  It was a really big disappointment in both flavor and texture.  Better chocolate eclairs can be found at just about any supermarket's bakery.  Maybe the lesson is to order only items that Termini is known for. . .and that definitely does NOT include eclairs.

This place loses 2 stars from me. an hour for delivery when I live right around the corner?..i ordered spaghetti and meatballs...wet thin noodle with terrible watery red sauce and the meat were clearly bought from the frozen food section at save a lot. It had ZERO taste and I had to throw it out. Step up the quality of your food.
Came for the gator gumbo with jambalaya rice and bread pudding, left without words to describe how good it was.

My low rating stems not from the quality of the cannoli but from the level of greed I experienced at the Philly Flower Show. I'll gladly pay $5 for cannoli because they're delicious and worth the price but I take issue with the price gouging for an iced tea. On what planet is an iced tea worth $6/bottle? I should have returned it for a refund and gone to the water fountain. Shame on you for your greed!
Charming bright place, wonderful & attentive staff, & fabulous crepes & eggs. Great espresso drinks too! Excellent breakfast choice. So happy!

An Uber driver told us to stop at Termini Bros and he was right.  The canoli was great, pignoli cookies were yummy and the macaroons were good.  My only complaint was that althought the almond horn tasted good, it was a little bit on the hard side.

We go all the time for the sushi which is very good.  The grill is a great show and is cool.  Our nieces like birthdays there and our out of town friends are wowed.  Service is usually quite good.  Fun place with a nice wine list.

MAC AND CHEESE BALLZZZZZZ!!! SOOO GOOOOD. I honestly don't even like mac and cheese but it was delish! I originally passed Beck's to try their gumbo. I ended up getting a sample of it and didn't really like it much. I think the mac and cheese balls are somewhat overpriced because you get 2 for about $5 and you definitely want more after eating the first two. AND the sauce that come with it goes so well with it. I thought they were going to serve me what they had on display but they actually fried them again once it was ordered which made it crispy and hot. I will be back to get me some more mac and cheese balls for sure! :)

If you're looking for a place to grab a pint and a burger while watching a game, you're looking at one of the best in Tucson.  Their beer selection is great, they generally have a few different IPAs on tap, and something to meet just about anyone's palate.  Their crabcake sandwich is worth a try as well.  Just make sure to get there early before a big game, it fills up quickly - if the parking lot is full it's a good indication that you won't be getting a seat any time soon.

Came here for lunch on a Friday and it wasn't very busy.  I ordered a tortilla soup and it came  with avocado and sour cream. The bowl is a good size, if you aren't very hungry order a cup. It was delicious and savory I finished the last drop. If you check in on Yelp you get free dessert and I got cheesecake to go yum! Our waiter was very nice too.

Great Happy Hour! 
Good bar food and drinks, nice selection of draught beers. Great prices! The atmosphere is definitely casual.

I hadn't been to this Ruth's Chris in years & it was a far cry from what it once was. To set the tone, our table (for 6) was in such a tight spot, the waiters each bumped into my friend & me EVERY time they walked by. Eventually, one knocked my handbag clean onto the floor. Once a tray the waitress carried bumped in my head as she delivered food to the table next to me. 

It was restaurant week & for course one, 4 out of 6 of us ordered lobster bisque then 4 out of 6 of us returned it. It was horrible!! Not a hint of seafood flavor. The texture was that of over thickened gravy from a bad Chinese take out spot. I posted a video on Instagram & the reactions said it all. The taste was the reason we all returned it. It tasted of a toasted BITTER cheese & left an awful aftertaste. We ordered Caesar salads instead & they had watered down Caesar dressing & some wilted romaine. 

My main course was broiled salmon. It was not great, just ok. A tad overlooked...just a tad. My side was sautéed spinach & it was very bland but cooked well, not over done. 

Dessert was the best part for me - creme brûlée. This is the only dish I recommend from my meal. With gratuity included, we each paid $60 for our meal, which included 1 cocktail. It was SO not worth it. I could have made each dish better at home for a lot less $. The conversation with my friends was the highlight of dinner.

Visiting Philly from D.C and everytime i come to philly i have to eat at reading terminal market! Today i came by and ran into Beck's cajun. The girls working in the front our super friendly! My boyfriend and I got the gator gumbo with jambalaya and fried mac and cheese they are both so awesome. We love southern food but D.C is terrible so I am so happy we got our gumbo fix. They offer everything from gumbo to fried platters to po boys! If you ever visiting this place is a must!

Excellent chicken and Peruvian drinks!  You WILL NOT be dissappointed. And the fried plantains are to die for. Even after I had eaten my fill and ordered a meal to go for a friend,  I once again salivated when she cracked open her box. Heavenly!
Very good food, excellent service, comfortable atmosphere, very accommodating. Would come back!

The service here was friendly. I tried the soft shell crab poboy sandwich was really good. The waitress herself recommended it. The crab was lightly battered and crispy and the crab pieces were a good size for the sandwich.

The bread they use to make their Po boys is amazing! Food always comes out quick and hot. I especially like this place in the winter, the gator gumbo warms me up (make sure to get corn bread with it). Don't miss the soft shell crab Po boy when they have it as a special in the summer, it's the best I've found in the city.
What a secret gem! Go here if you love crepes! I ordered two of them and ate both without regret :)

Since visiting NOLA in 2007 (and eating my way through the city) I have been un-apologetically obsessed with the cuisine.  But because I started with the best, nothing has even come close to pleasing my palate in the way authentic New Orleans food did. 
Until I finally tried Beck's Cajun Cafe. Um, yum. Their shrimp po boy was spot on. Their jambalaya looks absolutely fantastic. They even serve beignets! Also, the portions are ridiculously huge, which means i got to enjoy my po boy twice. Win.
Another huge plus to this place is that they even have a counter for customers to sit at and enjoy their meal. In a location as crowded as Reading Terminal, this is a big deal!

I was taken here last night on a first date and I can not express how this place exceeded our expectations. The ambiance was so romantic, and the food was beyond ANAZING!!! The staff was so sweet and welcoming and the service was exceptional. A def must go if you like a good steak...TWO THUMBS UP!!!!

We were looking for a new place for happy hour and decided to check these guys out.  Had a great time and look forward to returning!

Sat at the bar and did appetizers .... all of which were excellent.  We had the fish tacos - which I can't rave about enough, followed by the grilled avocado.  And then another order of the fish tacos (because they were just that good!).

Service was great.  It was crowded (as any good place would be on a Friday night), but we never felt neglected.

Well, the best part of Joseph Poon is that he'll send you out on a trip around Philadelphia Chinatown, for the uninitiated. Of course, for $50, I'd show you around and cook for you, too.

He has some good stories of the area and local food stops, plus various tips on buying different kinds of Chinese groceries, and his food isn't bad, but it's certainly not a tour you need to take if you're a foodie looking to try new and wonderful dishes. Never tried the holiday tour they're referring to, though.

Always excellent service and excellent food at a very reasonable price. People are always friendly. Unless you are a Redskins fan, stay away during game days. Big Redskin establishment. Have taken many friends here and they have always enjoyed the experience

Enjoyed lunch here the other day. Got to love sitting right at the counter to be able to see all the action going on. 

I started with Mac and Cheese. It was deep fried in balls and not all that flavorful unfortunately. Also the waitress forget I ordered them so they came mid meal. 

The shrimp po boy though, oh boy. I don't know what authentic Louisiana cuisine tastes like but I don't care, this was delicious. Worth the $8 price tag. 

Also, I was given a free sample of bread pudding which finished off the meal nicely. Will be back to try some other menu items soon.
I needed a cake for my pop's birthday.  Ran down here and bought a yellow pound cake. He loved it. I didn't care for all the icing but it was tasty and I think it was cheesecake frosting.
Dang yo this place is Poppin they have delicious treats and slamming coffee, do yourself a favor and go here

I have been to all 3 of the Parilla Suiza restaurants in Tucson now.  I lived in Baja 8 years,  so I've eaten a lot of Mexican food!  I find these to be the very best I have tried in the area so far.  I love the green salsa and the fresh one. I love the enchiladas and the service is always excellent.
I'm a Big Fan for lunch & Pre-Game at UA.  The Green Chille Burger is one of my Fav's.  I go there often, so I've gotten to know the staff and they are really great in my opinion.

Great service and enough of a variety of beer on tap to satisfy most. Second time here and I love the place. Wish I lived closer.....

The habanero jerk wings will melt your face clean off of your skull. But they're sooooooo good. It's fine until you stop eating. Then the heat kicks the door down. Get an extra side of celery....trust me!

ODE TO THE "TRAIN WRECK PO BOY"

Oh, great mash up of bovine and swine
Tossed greasily on a crusty roll with more satisfaction than 1,000 feasts
But unbeknownst to the tongues of those Muslim, & Hindu, & Vegan, & Jew...

As your name may suggest, you are the very depiction of carnage (in the flesh)
Just as wearily eyes are incapable of looking away, so are the mouths of men of turning away
As they yearn hungrily for your sloppy, beefy, cheesy goodness

Your creamy mayonnaise runs deep, deep within your warm center of salami and fried onions
And it is an obtainable spoil for even Scrawny Arms Rob Lowe to enjoy with messy dignity
For it is not without great condiments that any man should be laid to rest

Deliciousness is often fleeting
But yours is not, and it sends quivers down the spines of all with hearty appetites
Be it Adam Richmond, or Kobayashi, or Scooby Doo

The best description of its flavor: DIVINE
The best description of your affliction: INTOXICATING
And alas, the best description of your status post sandwich: COMATOSE

P.S. The Gator Gumbo rocks as well.  It's a spicy, smoky bowl of reptilian joy.

Unfortunately I can't agree with the other reviews on the canoli, was it just a bad batch that I had? I went to Termini's since all the reviews said this is the place to get canolis...as I said I was disappointed. It wasn't nasty, just had a weird texture and was a bit too sweet for me. I bake at home so I am very critical of baked goods. If they are not freshly made, not made with fresh ingredients,  or too dry I will pick up on those facts.  I didn't finish half of my canoli and my bf took two bites out of his.
Chicken andouille gumbo for the hubby and I had the fried oyster's for the first time delicious as usual!! Never disappointing when we go!!

I can't believe I've passed by this place everyday for many years and I've never thought to stop in!  We finally went before catching a movie at the Loft, and my husband and I both fell in love with it!!  The music was great! A great mix of 60's, 70's, and country!  The place was packed, and we were told it would be about 15 minutes to be seated, but we were seated in 5 - it's nice when expectations are exceeded.  We had local beers, my husband had the voodoo burger with sausage on it, and loved it (he's a bit hard to please).  I had the chicken tenders and the macaroni and cheese - both excellent.  I thought it really nice that I asked for a dozen chicken tenders, and the waitress told how big it was and talked me into the half dozen - I still took food home, so I really appreciated that!  As busy as they were, our plates were immediately cleared, and food and drinks were brought promptly.  This will now be a regular stop for us!
Ummm...Yummm! The tomatillo salsa is frigging fantastic! The food is phenomenal! I think there were opiates in my taco, it was so delicious that I don't even remember eating it.

I was thinking for some southern food for dinner but i wanted sth light not crazy heavy platter which i had before n shared it with my friends and it was delicious. So this time i just ordered couple of fried oysters n side salad with creole mayo which is their special sauce. At first i was looking at that pasta salad, i had a second thought about whether or not it was a good idea to eat the salad then i had a flashback when coincidentally i just watched an episode of series which people got sick because they were served pasta salad that was apparently out for too long. But i was like whatever i just went for it anyway. Well guess what, i should've listened to my first instinct! I was sick all nite, n had the worst let me emphasize that, THE WORST food poisoning!!! Sleepless nite, went to the bathroom way more often that i'd like too, diarrhea, vomiting!!!! N about 2 months later i am still traumatized with ANY pasta salads that's served "supposedly" cold. So the question whether or not i ever go back and have food there, i'd say may be but probably not ordering for another pasta salad EVER AGAIN!!

Run away!  Actually the food looked beautiful on the plates, although it took forever to arrive.  Our waitress never smiled.  Left my sweater there and when I went back 20 minutes later it was gone - no one else was at our table, so I think I can add theft to the service, even tho it was my fault.  The carne asada burrito looked great, but it was only a flour tortilla filled (yes, very well filled) with carne asada meat.  That's it.  There was some lettuce & tomato (salad) on the side, but nothing else in the burrito.  Where's the guacamole, onion, etc?  Side of beans was watery and about 1/4 cup spread thin to look like more.  Others in our party had problems with their choices too, many the thin beans and too much cheese everywhere.

This place was the cutest find and the perfect way to start my day trip in Philly. The atmosphere is so cozy and inviting, and the staff was very friendly and helpful. Myself and one other person shared 2 crepes, an iced coffee, and a side of bacon, all DELICIOUS. We had the honeybee and the apricot comfiture. While I'm not a fan of cheese or eggs, the honeybee seemed to be such unique mix of tastes so we decided to try it, and I was pleasantly surprised. The apricot was also a delicious choice, and the mix of one savory and one sweet flavor were a nice blend. They also offer fruit infused water as a courtesy, which was a very sweet touch. Overall I was glad I found this gem, and I would certainly recommend it.
Been to better steak houses and better Ruths Chris, cracked water glass, slow service during restaurant week, even though we were not ordering off the restaurant week menu

Not worth the time, money, or effort. Definitely would not return. We went in to get a table on a saturday night but the wait for hibachi was over 30 min however there were tons of free tables/hibachi grills with no workers at them. We didn't stay that night and decided to return on monday night. Went on monday and there was another 30+ min wait for hibachi even though there was only 1 party of people eating hibachi.

We ate from their kitchen menu at a table in the back. The service wasn't bad, considering it seemed like they were understaffed. We ordered an appetizer then waited 5-10 min before ordering our main course. When our food came out, it came all at once despite the time difference in ordering. We got our salad, soups, appetizer, and main course all at the same time. The noodles were bland and just luke warm. The main courses were pretty good size but everything on the menu was waaaay overpriced.

Would not recommend. Stay away!

Skip the corn bread!!!!!!!!!!!!!! As a southern girl, I cannot believe they actually sell corn bread like this.  

Outside of the cornbread, I have only positive things to say about Beck's Cajun Cafe. The Etouffee is DELISH. Served with some rice, it totally hit the spot. We also tried the shrimp po boy which was pretty delicious as well. The po boy came with a nice spicy mayo type sauce that really pulled the entire po boy together. 

Definitely recommend folks to try this place, just skip the corn bread. Save your money and use it for some ice cream. :)

AVOID FOR ANY HAIR COLORING!!!!!!!! Absolutely botched my hair and bleached it with foils WHO DOES THAT ANYMORE. Honestly, spend some more money and get a better job it's clear here you get what you pay for....

Dank food and big portions. Solid beer selection. I'd give 5 stars but the service was pretty average, and it took well over 2 hours total to get out order, them bring food, and get the check. Overall good place to get drinks and awesome (better than University ave quality) bar food in Tucson.

Scored a few great seats at The bar to watch the Ravens/Broncos.  What a game!!!

Not a huge, but a very diverse beer selection. Unique. Had three varieties that were new to me. One was on cask. Excellent. 

Made quick friends with the gentlemen to our right. Excellent conversation, friendly-not douchey- (i enjoy bars to just relax/not necessarily be picked up :)  and we all had a fantastic time screaming at the game. 

Will absolutely be back.

The pastries we purchased were good, but the customer service is awful. Like other reviewers on here, our cashier made a big fuss about the plastic bags, despite us saying ahead of time we wanted our pastries packed separately as they'd be going to two separate places. Is a second plastic bag too much to ask for after a $15 purchase?

No ketchup needed!

Let me preface this review by saying that I absolutely love an amazing burger.  Many burger joints serve good burgers.  Trident serves a masterpiece in their Steakhouse Burger.  

A soft and grilled brioche bun starts off this burger journey as the base.  Although you could savor the taste of the grass fed beef all by itself, Trident Grill perfectly pairs grilled onions and mushrooms, blue cheese, horseradish, and an amazing balsamic sauce that awakens your taste buds around every turn.  On the cook, I asked for medium, and the patty came out pink in the middle and succulent throughout each bite.

Instead of fries, I opted for the Mac and Cheese.  This side did NOT disappoint!  The cheddar was toasted on top to create a brownish hue that you can almost taste just by looking at it.  Underneath the layer of baked on cheese...shell noodles in a light creamy cheddar cheese sauce.  Awesome.

My taste buds have been worked over today...I wish I had room for ice cream!
Fantastic local eats! Great for watching the Cats play and NFL. It's a seat yourself kinda place, so come early if you want to indulge in happy hour!  Fried Pickles are a must!
Excellent food, atmosphere, and service.  The omelette on a baguette was AMAZING
Very impressed by the food and service. Especially the plantains and rotisserie chicken.
My most recent visit had me trying the oyster Poboy. What a delicious delight! Nice friendly service too

I love this place. We get a whole chicken and three sides (cilantro rice, spicy beans, and plantains). The friend yuca is super good. The spicy yuca appetizer is amazing. The liquados are also very good. The service is always great. It's a family friendly restaurant. We get the food for carry out once a month.

I've been here a few times with friends, and we always have a great meal. They have a fantastic happy hour menu, and if you are hungry for fish and chips, that's the best time to get it. You can never go wrong by ordering those, but be warned, it's a huge basket so bring your appetite or bring a friend. I also like their fish tacos. Grilled or fried, the fish tacos are delicious. My friends all like the burgers at Trident as well. And nothing goes better with these bites than some beer. Plus, they have several screens around the bar, so you're sure to catch whichever game you're into, even if it's jewellery and  antique appraisal (which was on last time I went haha). Always a blast at Trident.

Moist and flavorful rotisserie chicken.  The cilantro rice was delicious.  The white rice is not really plain steamed rice, it has a flavor to it.  The 1/4 and 1/2 chicken comes with 1 green spicy sauce and 1 yellow sauce. You can order extra sauce for $0.50.  I expected service to be a bit faster considering the chicken was already cooked and only needs to be chopped- but it wasn't slower than usual restaurants. There was a good lunch time crowd, so best to arrive early especially if you are a big group.

Coffee and food were delicious. Pesto crepe and veg omelette were both awesome! A unique breakfast menu and a great little corner spot with friendly staff. Nicely decorated with indoor and outdoor seating. Walked a mile to get here after I saw the Yelp reviews- well worth it!

Definitely recommend. The service was friendly and the food was excellent. One standard to judge any Mexican restaurant is the salsa. It will not disappoint. They bring a selection of 3 and each one was great.
They ran out of Beignets!  The main thing we drove over 3 hours for- Their are lucky Jami liked the other stuff. So disappointed
A great neighborhood cafe! I especially love the outdoor seating so I can hangout with my dog.

Worst Ruth's Chris experience I've ever had.  Like other reviewers have noted, I've been to many Ruth's Chris, and this has to rank the lowest in terms of overall experience.

Despite having a reservation, I had to wait a solid 15 minutes to get my table.  Hostess, who could well have been a final round Jersey Shores reject, was less than hospitable and dismissive.  When finally seated, it was at a small cramped table in the middle of the front room, in uncomfortably close proximity to other tables.  Am I at a Denny's???  Most intimate, in a bad way, spacing I've ever experienced at a Ruth's Chris.

No rolls, until I asked 15 minutes after ordering.  Slow water refills.  Slow service in general.  Over-salted and tiny lobster bisque.  Ordered a medium rare ribeye and got a gray piece of meat.  Only positive, the waitress replaced it immediately with one that was properly cooked.

Ruth Chris is, in general, my favorite chain steakhouse.  Unfortunately, will have to find an alternative in Philly because this one sucks.

Best cafe just opened up in the area. Crepes are the best of the best,  they have water filled with strawberry with mints inside which makes it really tasty for this hot summer. Downstairs sitting for those that need wifi to do business. Orest the owner with the stuff behind the kitchen are very accommodating on how u want ur crepes and coffee done. Try it this place you will not be disappointing. Highly recommend it.

Definetely the worse Parrila in Tucson, in terms of service and appearance.  Food is pretty good, I'd give it four stars, but the tables are always sticky and there's like ten billion flies buzzing around to snatch themselves some salsa.  The parrilla on Ina and Speedway are better so check those out instead of this one.

Went here today for a quick lunch. Place is bright with nice woodwork, service was friendly. I felt I had to get a crepe and glad I did. I had the Honeybee and it was delicious! Light and fluffy and not too sweet. Also had a latte that was tasty and oversized which I like. I highly recommend this place and hope to se more places pop up in Francisville.

Great cafe in the growing Francisville neighborhood! Delicious food and coffees! The crepes are savory and sweet; in our two visits thus far, we have had the goat bacon, goat turkey, and strudel crepes. The honey ham sandwich and salad was a huge serving and leftovers  taken home for another meal.  The downstairs seating offers a comfortable, cozy environment. Staff are friendly. Glad to support a local, small business!

The food at Beck's is some of the best cajun food I've ever had. My favorite dish is the chicken & andouille gumbo. It is wholesome, spicy and delicious. The jambalaya is also excellent. The po-boys are good as well, but not as exceptional as the gumbo or jambalaya. They give out free samples and the service is usually quick. If you don't like spicy food, this is not the place for you. However, if you do, then definitely check it out.

My husband and I went for dinner tonight.  It has been many years since we've been... it's not our favorite Tucson Mexican restaurant, but we left full and quite happy.  There were a lot of large parties in the restaurant tonight - probably because we're so close to the holidays.  The salsa's came with a red, green, and a pico, which was nice.  I had the enchiladas con mole, and my husband had the taco salad.  The chicken was in nice big shredded pieces, and the taco salad was good, but not great - it was kind a salad with some shredded beef added to it.  The rice and beans were both delicious - the pinto were well flavored in a bowl full of juice.  Our iced teas and chips and salsas could have been refilled faster - I think this was due to the number of large parties.  I would go again, but definitely not as my first choice.

I'm a big fan of Ruth's Chris, but for some reason the food at this location just wasn't as good as some of the other locations I've been to.  I went there with a livingsocial certificate ($100 certificate for $50!), so I definitely feel like I got my money's worth, but it just felt like something was missing with the seasoning.  So I give this location 4 stars when I'd normally give Ruth's Chris 5 stars.  

My wife and I got Ribeye steaks and they were good.  Not as good as the Ruth's Chris in Indianapolis or Atlanta, but still pretty good.  I ordered mine medium rare and hers medium.  Both were cooked to the correct "doneness", but just seemed to lack the flavor I'm used to with Ruth's Chris.  On a scale of 1-10 I'd say they were 7s, which is still good, but I'm used to 9s with Ruth's Chris.  (10 is reserved for my backyard BBQ  :)

For sides we got scalloped potatoes, asparagus, and the baked tomato.  While the potatoes were excellent, the asparagus and tomato were very plain tasting.  IE, it's like they forgot to season them.  I've had both before at other locations and loved them, so I was very surprised.  

We got lobster bisque and Ahi tuna appetizers, and both of these were absolutely fantastic!  

The very polite manager made the rounds and asked us how the food was, but I didn't have the heart or time to talk about the sides.  

The staff was fantastic!  From the hostess to the waitress to the busboy, all were very attentive to our needs.  We never had to wait for drink refills, and the food came out in a timely manner.  Not too fast, not too slow, just right.

I have another livingsocial certificate to use and I'll definitely use it, but I hope they re-train the chefs on how to cook Ruth's Chris meals as well as other locations do.

All of you writing reviews should throw yourselves into a wood chipper if you don't give Trident 5 Stars. 

Before I offer up my love to the owner for providing Arizona with one of the only Redskins bars in the state, I must preach the gospel of the glorious Clam Chowder Bread Bowl. Being born and raised in AZ but having parents and family from New England, I know my way around a fresh, authentic, steaming hot bowl of chowda. Trident is unmatched; eating the chowder was an understatement, I borderline inhaled it. 

The icing on the cake; redskins bar. Enough said. Cowboys fan ARE NOT WELCOME. 

....damn it feels good saying that. 

HTTR!!!!

It really saddens me to write this review, but I must.  Let me start off by saying I've been a customer of this establishment for over a decade, starting in 2002.  Just out of college, I remember my first experiences at this restaurant were simply remarkable.  Paying for a $50 steak was heavy on the budget, but I felt it was well worth it, the steak came out sizzling, the sides were plentiful, the ambience was alluring.  I would try other steak restaurants such as Morton's, Capital Grille, Union Trust, they were all good steaks, but I always came back to Ruth's Chris because they always made their steak, in my opinion, JUST right.  

Each year my wife treats me for my birthday at a steak restaurant because I love a great steak dinner.  I rotate between Ruth's Chris and another steak restaurant of my choosing on off years.  This year my wife asks me where I would like to go for dinner, I don't want to leave anything to chance, so I tell her to make reservations to Ruth's Chris.  Sadly, this will probably be the last reservation I ever make to this restaurant.  I order a steak, medium rare, and I'm positive that it's overcooked.  They send out another one, and same story, overcooked.  I cut through the center, showed it to the guy next to me, we're in complete agreement that it's a medium well to well done steak.  I feel horrible, and feel like a complete dick about this.  The third steak is completely undercooked, rightfully so, so I just ask for the check cause i didn't want to deal with another interaction with the management.  They were gracious enough to not bill me, but I feel horrible.  I've NEVER sent food back before in my entire life, and I spent this evening doing it twice.  The service was impeccable, and the management went out of their way to cater to me and my wife.  But I think through the years, something is lacking with the restaurant.  Whether it's their attempt at growing their demographic/clientelle, who knows, but it has diminished the quality of service that has brought me back all these years.  I honestly don't feel the same aura, that I once felt at this establishment.  

I guess I'll just have to find another favorite steak restaurant.  Thank you for the decade of great steaks, I wish it could have lasted.

The best canoli in town. Prepared like home and displayed perfectly, empty shell first and then fresh ricotta filling at the moment of consumption. Real delight to see how they respect the traditional recipe. Folks are in their 90's and still got it!
When we go to Reading Terminal we have to get some cannoli's from Termini.  They are always amazing.

Forget about getting a boring, plain old Philly Cheesesteak, you need to try Beck's Train Wreak -- a deliciously spicy mix of andouille sausage, steak, salami, cheese, and onions all served on French bread. The Train Wreak is a fantastic alternative to the classic cheesesteak for Philadelphians who are looking to spice it up (literally and metaphorically). 

The jambalaya is also tasty. If you wish to take it up another notch, add gumbo with it, particularly the alligator gumbo. The spectacular mixture of jambalaya and gumbo is absolutely delightful!

One food downside though: The Fried Mac n' Cheese Balls are not as appetizing as one would expect. They are rather bland in flavor. You can skip out on ordering these.

Amazing food... The Gator gumbo was delicious!! It was creamy and had a spicy kick to it. The batter on the fried shrimp was probably one of the best I have ever had and the cornbread was so soft and buttery.

Came in the middle of day for lunch with a friend. Couldn't drink because I had class in an hour. Will have to save the cocktails for another time. Their floor-to-ceiling shelf of liquor selections, however, is incredibly impressive. Bartender was friendly and very efficient.

[ food ]
I ordered:
 
-the duck fat fries, which came with the most amazing cheddar sauce
-crawfish hush puppies - perfect amount of jalapeno
-pickled cauliflower, which came with four slices of olive-oiled toasted bread, fresh ricotta, and a lovely olive tapenade

My non-vegetarian friend also got a burger, which she summarily dubbed "the best burger I have ever had". I'm guessing it must have been pretty good.

[ vibe ]
Classy-industrial-orange-fluorescent-tubes-neon-metal. Very cool. Literally floor to ceiling wall of liquor bottles with cool and esoteric names that you've probably never heard of before. Bartender throws stuff around like a BAMF. Great time.

[ conclusion ]
Great food and what I imagine to be great, strong drinks. A good mid-day stop, and probably even better at night. Definitely a gem.

I was craving a little bit of home so I decided to give Beck's another try. My first experience when I first moved here (over two years ago) wasn't memorable, so I figured...it must not have been bad? 

This was desperation speaking.

I walked into Reading knowing I would get the jambalaya. However, I saw the gator gumbo and the color and texture intrigued me. So I asked for a sample. The gumbo was bland and I wouldn't be surprised if it didn't have any gator and they just added it into the name as a selling point. I'm used to a thicker roux and darker color. I feel like that's where the flavor comes in.

Anyway, I ordered my "bowl" of jambalaya with a side of corn bread. They pour this tomato sauce over it? Even before then, the jambalaya looked stained with red from tomato paste. I just Wiki'ed "jambalaya" and apparently it is common to have tomato in your jambalaya, but the further south you go in Louisiana (central and south LA) the more uncommon it is to have tomatoes. So, tomato in my jambalaya is a no-no.

The corn bread was nice and sweet. However, this is more of a northern recipe, it was soft and baked like an individual cupcake, but in the shape of a loaf. I'm used to the crumbly texture and less sweet, baked in a cast iron pan and cut into squares.

All in all, I guess this is all about preference. If you want an authentic Creole meal, this is not the place to go. If you want to pretend, that works too.

The beignets were made fresh, but the powder sugar was old and gross. It's all clumped up hard sugar. The beignets was tiny & small for $5!  Not impressed at all! It's just tasteless dough fried up. The other food smells great. Hopefully when I go & try their jambalaya, I'll be impressed. The staff who took my order was friendly, however the cashier who rung me up wasn't so friendly. I thanked her as she gave me back my change, and I gave tips into the tip jar. No you're welcome. I thanked her a second time as she handed me my order, again RUDE with no manners to say you're welcome & have a nice day.

This place is AWESOME!  Pioneers in a developing neighborhood, I first went there to check it out and help support a new neighborhood business.  To my surprise, they are serving La Colombe coffee and are making Crapes and Bagel Sandwiches!  All the food I have tried has been great and the owners live in the neighborhood and really care about their customers.  I usually get a Crape on the weekend, when I have time to enjoy their downstairs dining area.  During the week I usually grab a Cappuccino and their "Philly" on a bagel.  I am there a few times a week.

This is our bi-weekly pub trivia spot on Wednesday night. The food is solid throughout the whole menu and better than what you perceive to be typical bar fare, for sure. It's as though they actually tried from the very beginning instead of just purchasing a deep fryer and hoping for the best. 

Now will somebody on the management end PLEASE tell the one blonde server to stop sticking her credit card book down the back of her yoga pants and waltzing around the establishment? It's gross and kind of offensive honestly, and I've heard tables next to us say something to the effect of "GASP!" on more than one occasion. This is just nasty, guys, regardless of how cute she is! The rest of the civilized world usually encourages aprons for servers, for crying out loud!

This has been my favorite spot to visit while I was in Reading Terminal Market. I had to order the gator gumbo each time I was there. I remembered it used to be more spicy with a darker color before. However, it still tasted great especially with the gator sausages inside. I also liked their gator sausages, which was tender, juicy and crispy outside. My husband preferred to have it inside the gumbo though.

I had the fried shrimp po boy and cajun fries. It's served on a baguette with lettuce, pickles, tomatoes and creole mayo(which I suggest you ask for extra on the side if your a mayo type of person). The shrimp were about medium size, crisp and seasoned just perfect. I believe it was anywhere from 9-12 inches long. The canjun fries weren't too spiced. They were topped with jalapeño slices. No complaints with the taste of the food. There were a lot of other dishes that I would've love to try but my stomach wouldn't have been able to handle all of that.
The total cost of my food was about $20. That's kind of pricey for a quick lunch. Also since it's located in Reading Terminal Market, you have to look around for a seat.

First, after reading many of the reviews, it seems really necessary to point out that the complaint that the refried beans are watery or soupy is wrong. The charro beans are soupy, that's how they are made. If you special order refried beans instead of charro beans, they will come on a plate and will be creamy just as they should be. 

As far as the food it's average and has really fallen far from 20 years ago. In it's day La Parilla was higher end and definitely a different menu from the normal Sonoran. The original owners must have retired or died, and the kids took over.

Trident is one of those places where it's impossible to have a good time. The staff is friendly, the drinks are flowing, and it has an all around good atmosphere. 

We had a larger group tonight that continued to grow, but the staff was very helpful and accommodating, allowing us to add extra tables and chairs so everybody could sit. Our server was knowledgeable about the beers on tap and answered all of our questions. She was one of those servers who never wrote a thing down but remembered everything. She didn't have a problem with our large group doing separate checks and was great with closing people out at different times. 

I wish the bathrooms were in a better location. Being across from the soda station and near the back makes it a little busy of an area to get to. The bathrooms could use a little updating and some TLC. 

Also, the kitchen seemed to take an exceptionally long time for what is simple bar food. I'm not sure if they were short staffed today, but they could use some extra help. On a positive note, the habanero sauce served with the chicken strips is amazing!

I was leery of trying Beck's as a native New Orleanian.  However, I just miss the city and wanted a bit of creole cuisine.  Beck's has a pretty good offering of New Orleans/Louisiana options.  The po-boys are loaded down, though the bread is wrong (sorry, hoagie rolls are too tough for a po-boy).  They offered Zapps and king cake, which made me homesick.  The Cajun fries are so-so.  
So far, this is the most authentic New Orleans experience in the greater Philly area.

I found this place through Yelp and came for a quick lunch with a coworker.  We were seated promptly and the service was great throughout our meal.  Both my coworker and I ordered the 1/4 pollo.  It comes with two side dishes.  The portion size was extremely generous, especially for lunch time.  I was able to finish the chicken, which was seasoned deliciously, but couldn't finish both the sides.  I was also pleased to see they had a selection of Latin drinks such as Inca cola and cremas. I will definitely return but probably for dinner.

Walked by Beck's today And was given a sample of their gumbo (it's awesome that they give samples out) and I was in awe of the deliciousness and flavor! I purchased the gumbo with a side of jambalaya. Both were delicious! They were flavorful and spicy! I can't believe that I've never tried this place before! I can't wait to go back!
The entrees are generally good here, although the blackened salmon is often dry. The cornbread side is sweet (extremely sugary) not savory.

I have visited multiple times and on multiple occasions. The food is good, but the service is becoming increasingly worse. The owner is very cheap and overly concerned with being charged a visa fee for each transaction. There is a minimum amount of $7 for credit card purchases, and they do not allow large parties to split checks. (Even when the amount is over $7)

A pretty great cafe in the Francisville area.  Upon arrival I was a little bit wary because it looked pretty tiny with only one table and some high top seating. I was pleasantly surprised to find out there's a floor downstairs with some extra tables and even couches! The aesthetic does what it can to be hip/trendy. It is also very clean and bright which I love. 

Vineyards seems to be known for their crepes, but I didn't get to try one during my first trip here. I got a hot latte. It was $6!!! That is v expensive for a cup of coffee and if I'm being honest it was not that good. That got me a bit turned off. My friend got a mocha chino which was just as expensive and a chocolate chip cookie.

I don't wanna hate on a local small business, so even though I do think that this place is overpriced, I'm gonna back it.  I'll definitely be back to give a crepe a try and recommend it if you need a cup of coffee or a place to get some work done.

The Trident Grill is just ok. It's a bar, serving plain food -- fresh, but mediocre. It was close to our hotel and in 107 degree heat, it was way too hot to walk around looking for another restaurant.  The nautical/military decor seemed out of place.  The service left a lot to be desired.

Beck's is one of only a few Cajun/Creole eateries in the city, and one of the ONLY places I would eat at again @ RTM. Big portions, bold flavors and friendly service keeps this place crowded, but I think its worth the wait. 

To start, cozy up to the counter and ask for a sample. You cant go wrong with their jambalaya or gator gumbo - both are dense and flavorful with the right amount of kick. Still hungry? Try a classic po'boy or one of their platters. I've had the fried catfish, and even though Im not a fan of cornmeal for coating, that fish is on point. Speaking of corn - the grilled cornbread is fantastic, and accompanies most platters. I also observed some ridiculous muffaletas flying out of the kitchen, and though I detest lunch meat, I approved of their generous size and apparent authenticity. 

On the flip side, I found the cajun meatloaf to be underwhelming, although it would probably be better if there were more BBQ onions on mine. My most recent side of cajun fries (not actually fries) were nothing more then very large potato wedges, a few of which I thought were not quite cooked through all the way. Relatively minor infractions in my book, just balanced feedback as my employer calls it. 

Dont forget to save room for Beck's decadent bread pudding. Even if you dont have room for a cup at the moment, ask for a sample. The endorfins your taste buds will send to your brain will force reserve capacity in your stomach to open within seconds.

It was late, just finished a business meeting and we were looking for some place for dinner. 
It was about 45 minutes to closing, and when we walked in, it was like the gave us that look of "oh no, we were going to close soon" but, now we have to work! 

Needless to say the service was terrible, I don't even remember the food. 

Too bad, customer/guest service is the most important component in any successful business. 
There was enough room in the parking lot for two limousines to get in and out of though ; )

One of my favorite lunch spots in Philly at the good old Reading Terminal Market! I always go for the Alligator sausage Po Boy! Animal lovers can now hate me and perspective women can be grossed out but this Po Boy is off the wall good! I never had the other selection of fine looking and smelling food but if it's anything like this sandwich it's gonna taste good!

RUDE AND INATTENTIVE.

I went there for the first time and ordered a Jambalaya platter, which was supposed to come with cornbread.

The cashier handed me the food and started spacing out. I don't think she even realized that I had not paid for the food yet. I offered to pay for the food. While she was ringing me up, I noticed that my dish was missing its cornbread.

I filled out my credit card receipt and heard the cashier complaining to the manager that I didn't tip her. Why the hell would I tip her?

1. She didn't cook the food.
2. She didn't prepare my plate, which wasn't even done correctly.
3. She had to be told to ring me up.
4. 80% of customers DO NOT TIP for carryout.

Does she complain within earshot of 80% of the customers?

If the owner/manager is reading this, I would recommend you retrain/fire your cashier. She's the young African American with the silver-colored jewelry. You are located in a food market where your customers are surrounded by affordable and tasty alternatives.

Cannolis!!!! They have become my new obsession, seriously. 

I tried the anise biscotti (per Brian S.'s review :) and it was good! Tasted a tad too licoricey for my liking, but I was impressed by the texture and crumb that the actual biscotti had to it. Typically biscotti is either too rock hard or too, too stale tasting, but their biscotti was wonderfully executed.

More importantly though, the cannoli I got from here was to die for.

When I first walked up to Termini Bros in the Market, I was freaking out because I didn't see any cannoli in the display cases. Then I realized, duh, they can't be sitting out all day and getting soggy - they're always stuffed to order! Yay! Sure enough, I asked the lady behind the counter and she came back with that beautifully ricotta-stuffed shell :)

When I dug into the masterpiece shortly thereafter, I could not stop eating it. I had mentally prepared myself for this internal conflict that I knew I would face at first bite...and I had planned on stopping there with just a taste...but, I soon realized the impossibility of that intention. It was just too delicious :)
Vineyards is AMAZING! Would highly recommend eating here. The food is amazing and the service is great!
This is my go-to spot for coffee. Great staff, great atmosphere, delicious coffee and AWESOME food. What are you waiting for? Get here!

Totally garden variety cheap Mexican food that isn't even all that cheap. They were out of club soda, no biggie. Sprite was flat though. Anyway, the food: had the three enchiladas which I think was #36 if I recall. The red and green chili sauce they put on is really watered down and way to tangy/sweet - it's weird. The chicken and beef was totally dry. I ate about half.  Way too much cheese. The refried beans were completely diluted and almost soupy. Not appetizing! I don't understand people who say how amazing this place is. They are welcome to think that but I will never come here again.

Quick service with great food. Its a small place but the turn around is great. It's a place you go eat and leave. Prefect for lunch time. I will be back for sure. So inexpensive as well. I think three of us was a bill of $20. Can't beat it. Great job.

Great coffee, and best crêpes in town!!!
Beautiful interior, and owners and staffs are friendly.
You have to visit at least once, c'est magnifique!!!

Got the gumbo and it was good tasted like a regular gumbo but the portion was very disappointing for the price. I have been to other places they hooked it up but this one left me hungry and looking for somewhere else to eat.

Also, the person serving was very rude for whatever reason and even rolled their eyes at me.

One of my favorite neighborhood bar/restaurants. Great ambience, great crowd, great food (especially brunch, though a little pricey, but worth it considering the Bloody Mary bar!), and great beer/liquor selection.

REALLY wanted to love their crepes - but alas, it does not compare to other crepe places I've frequented. The little cafe is situated in a weird (but up and coming) neighborhood - super close to my boyfriend's house. I was so excited to try!

Their sandwiches are good. Their crepes (we ordered take-out) got soggy after the 4 minute walk home! It seems like they make their crepes a little watered down, so I noticed a lot of air bubbles when taking a bite of the crepe. It wasn't anything special and the ingredients were a little lacking. 

Their drinks menu could be a little more creative, but for a small place like this, I think it's pretty good. I enjoy their iced lattes and their quiet and quaint little study area.

They have not lost their touch. I was invited to Cuenelli's on Friday by the owner after running into her at the grocery store for a complimentary dinner for my food blog. I wasn't disappointed. I started with the Papa a la Huancaina ($5.99). Normally I skip appetizers at restaurants and dive right into my meal, but this appetizer is hard to resist. The eggs and potatoes go well with the spicy yellow sauce. Normally my friend and I destroy it while we wait for dinner (which normally comes pretty quick at this restaurant).

The tough decision one always makes at Cuenelli's is: chicken or steak? Both are excellent and have their own, unique taste. My friend and I, being the smart two university students we are decided to order both and then mix and match. The chicken sandwich ($6.99) being well worth the cost. If Cuenelli's sandwiches were available to me -  I would certainly want one every week because they are just that good. I searched the streets of Seoul looking for some decent Peruvian food for four months without anything hinting to some of the great Spanish cuisine we have here in Florida.

The Bistec a lo Pobre ($11.99) was a delicious treat as well. The over-easy egg yolk went excellent with the rice, beans, and plantains. Cuenelli's homemade french fries are always a great hit to have on the side. 

The last entree we had was the Peruvian ceviche which was both spicy and tangy. It hit the right palate and was enjoyable. Packed in my favorite vegetable: onions. The pumpkin and corn on the side was a nice addition and it was my first time trying this dish. I consider ceviche to be more of an appetizer than an entree, but this portion was certainly an entree size.

Overall, great food is still to be had at Cuenelli's. If you haven't tried this Peruvian restaurant, you owe it to yourself to take some time and drive down Hillsborough for some delicious Peruvian cuisine.

If you like rotisserie chicken, GO HERE! Seriously, don't bother with the supermarket variety or any of the few chains in Tampa. Cuenelli's is simple, quick, inexpensive, and absolutely delicious. I ordered a half chicken, spicy beans, and cilantro rice since all the other yelpers raved about it. It's more than enough food for 2 people and about $10.  This is now going to be my favorite take-out spot during work hours.

The lunch specials are great. Good food, good portion size and good price.  Our waiter Ishamel was wonderful. So friendly, funny, engaging but also not intrusive. I enjoyed a 2 hour lunch and he was there when I needed him but also let me and my guest just relax and enjoy the afternoon. I live in Phoenix but it was worth the trip.

I had the Ruben sandwich. Kinda bland. The toast needed to be brushed with butter, better thousand island dressing and sauerkraut added to the sandwich. The next day (only because a client wanted to meet there) I had a cheeseburger. It was supposed to be medium but it was raw in the middle. The waitress disappeared so I could not tell her until she brought my check. Note to waitress...when a customer only eats half of the food ask if it was good!

It's not the customers job to track the waitress down if the food was not acceptable. He/She should be checking every 15 mins. This is a hang-out for ex-military which is the only positive note.

Food comes out quick and hot.  Service is also really good good too.  I was in town on business and came here with my coworkers twice!  Everything from the chips and salsa to my carne asada enchiladas was on point!  They handled our group of eight with excellent execution and delight.  Would definitely come back when I'm in town!

Excellent shrimp with old bay, great fish and chips, also once a year in August they get crab shipped in from Maryland Excellent.  You have to prepay for the crab in August.The reason is it is the owners birthday.

They have great bartenders and food there. I go there all the time.  It does get packed so get there early.

Celeste makes great drinks and always has food recommendations that make my mouth water. ....yummy.

My coworkers and I had a three hour team building event hosted by Chef Poon. Everyone had a wonderful time and we would like to do it again next year! Once we arrived, we received some background on Chef Poon's childhood as well as education. Then the fun started! 

We were split up in groups of four where we made dim sum. Chef Poon instructed us on how to make six different wontons and dumplings with all sorts of fillings! We then went out on a walking tour of Chinatown where we stopped at an underground Chinese grocery store where we receieved samples of different candies and then at the Fortune Cookie factory we each received a large bag of freshly baked fortune cookies. 

Once we arrived back to Chef Poon's we sat down and ate everything that we made, plus a large bowl of soup and additional dim sum made by Chef Poon. Everything was wonderful and tasted great! There was so much food that he gave us take out containers to take the rest of the food home with us. He is sensitive to food allergies and dietary restrictions, including gluten-free diets. 

Chef Poon has tons of energy and he made the whole afternoon very fun! 

I 100% recommend Chef Poon, I would ignore the bad yelp reviews which are extremely out dated!

trident is my default bar b/c it's 3 blocks from my place.  i like the food, which is slightly more varied and a bit better than your standard bar fare.  they have a pretty decent selection of beers on tap.  the waitress and bartenders are pretty competent and friendly, and the karaoke friday nights is always a good time.  it's a pretty big greek spot, but i don't have a problem with that.  it's pretty much good vibes whenever i go.  there's kind of a weird military/uber-patriotic thing going on, but it doesn't detract from the experience.  overall, a god place.  better than dirtbags, in my opinion.
Had shrimp tacos today which was awesome and Ashleigh served me which was even more awesome!!!

This is the only review less than four starts I have written about.  Unfortunately, this place has gone a little downhill from when I used to go.  We had been to the one on Speedway lately, which as far as I know, it still great, but we moved closer to the one on Oracle, and went.  Growing up, my family alternated between the two, and it was awesome!  We went a couple of weeks ago, and it just wasn't what it used to be.

We both got the platter with the corizo and the beef and the cheese in the bell pepper, which used to be just incredible, but when we went last, it was just not good.  The chorizo and beef were both low quality, gristly and chewy, and the margaritas were very, very sweet.  It didn't seem busy enough for us not to have our waters filled, or to have to attempt to flag down other people, without prevail.  

I am really sorry to have to write this review, because I loved this place growing up.  I will have to stick to driving out to the Speedway location from on.

I love Cuenelli's.  On every trip to Tampa, I stop at Cuenelli's either when I land or when I leave.  Very convenient to the airport and parking is always easy!

Chicken is super juicy.  I really like the yucca, cilantro rice and sauces, but the Ceviche is yummy and super healthy!! 
Lots of good choices and I will be back in Florida next week - can't wait to eat there!

This is some good food. I had the blackened chicken with the cajun fries (these aren't french fries but are potato wedges that are not fried- which is a plus). The corn bread is some of the best I have had. My husband liked his jumbalaya and he tried the gator gumbo which he also liked. The king cake is great if they have it. Go there!!! On top of this you couldn't ask for nicer people or better service. We can't wait to go back.

My husband and I went to Trident on Sunday to watch the Patriots Broncos game.  The place isn't too big and was pretty crowded, but we managed to find a few spots by the bar.  Trident is owned by a Navy veteran.  The entire place is covered in military memorabilia.  It's really neat.  I wished it wasn't so crowded so I could really scope the place out.  The atmosphere was great.  Both the staff and the patrons were friendly.  Our bartender, Sarah, was attentive, down to earth, and funny.  Trident has about 12 beers on tap, as well as wine and liquor.  They have a full menu with appetizers, salads, and sandwiches.  I hear the fish n' chips is awesome.  My husband and I went in between lunch and dinner, so we ordered the fried pickle spears for a snack.  Hands down the best fried pickles I have ever had.  The pickle to breading ratio was perfect.  I definitely recommend going to Trident if you're looking for a unique - and friendly! - bar.

Delicious Cajun food! Since it was my first time trying out this cuisine, I was taken aback with its splendid concoction of flavours. I recommend the Jambalaya bowl with Cajun seasoning and the Creole Chicken Corn Chowder. Helpful staff, he even allowed us a sampling before we decided on our final order. Total value for money and definitely worth it.

Ah Beck's. This was the first place I ever ate at Reading Terminal and I keep coming back. This is comfort food, pure and simple. I love the fried mac and cheese, the gumbo, the blackened catfish, and most of all: the po boys. Crusty french bread, creole mayo, and delicious fried goodness inside. Most times I eat here, I default to the Train Wreck - which is basically a cheesesteak with andouille sausage and bacon. It is one of the best cheesesteaks in town. Top this off with some tasty root beer, and I'm a happy customer.

I have to say, there are few places where I am happy to have eaten so much that I have to take a nap afterwards. The food was fantastic, and so were the margaritas. The wait staff was attentive and pleasant. Recommended.

Trident has undoubtedly the best bar/pub food in Tucson. I have been coming here since 2010 and enjoy the camaraderie between all of the regulars. I equate Trident to a classier, younger version of a VFW or American Legion Post (minus the nasty, murky cigarette stench and with way better food). I know at any given point throughout the day, I can come and shoot the breeze with someone I know, watch a variety of sporting events, and drink from a solid beer selection, while enjoying some good grub.

Sundays are one of my favorite times to go. It's all day happy hour on Sundays, which means discounted draft beer and select appetizers. The fried pickles are scrumptious, as well as the Redskins. You really cannot go wrong with fried potato skins coated in cheese and bacon. I am also a big fan of their burgers and they even have a pretty decent rack of ribs (show me a bar anywhere near the UA campus that can compete with that). Maybe I am a bit partial being a Vet myself, but I find that I eat/drink here more often than anywhere else in the Campus/Downtown area.
Get a cannoli! It was a little crunchier than I had expected but still delicious.

Trident is one of my favorite bars in Tucson. It is always busy but never overpacked, the atmosphere is perfect. The bartenders are among the best in town and you will surely have a great time here. The food is also very good, they have so many different options on the regular and happy hour menu and I have never been disappointed. Happy Hour is 4-7PM, $3 drafts!
Excellent service and great food.  The seafood is excellent. I would totally recommend the Williams center restaurant.

Let's start by saying I normally love Ruth's Chris.  I've used to live in Baltimore and must have gone to that one more than 20 times.  We moved to Philly last year and my wife decided to surprise me for my birthday and take me there.  

Unfortunately, they sat us right near the bathroom on what must be the smallest table in the house.  We tried to get over it and enjoy our meal.  Unfortunately, our waiter must have been lonely b/c I can't remember having a server ask me so many things.  What are you celebrating?  There are NFL players in the restaurant, are you fans?  Oh, you're new to the city... where are you from, what brings you here?  

I think that it must have been a left-over pricing deal from Restaurant week, b/c they were doing a fixed price deal..  appetizer, entree and dessert for set price.  So, it was a better deal than normal pricing.  But for some reason the menu in Philly is more limited than the one in Baltimore, so my favorite appetizer and side dish aren't even available at this location.  The last hitch was the desserts..  It was supposed to be some sort of mousse with fresh berries on top.  My wife's allergic to berries so we tell our new friend the waiter.  When they come out, neither have berries. I would have like the berries on mine.  Haha.

I come here a lot, but it isn't usually for the food.  It is for a good peach colada and queso fundido.

It is one of the better Mexican restaurants in town, in my humble opinion, but it isn't the best and by no means close to the worst.  

My favorite thing on the menu are the green enchiladas either cheese or shredded beef.  The fixings are nothing special, but the green sauce is awesome, sometimes spicy, but never sweet.  I also enjoy the alambre tacos, a mix of bacon, beef or chicken, with peppers and onions.  The chilaquiles are ok, the sauce is sometimes sweet rather than savory, which is not how I enjoy my chilaqules.  

The sopa de tortilla is great, just a simple broth, tortilla strips and queso oaxaca.  It's great for gloomy days and when you are craving soup.  The chips and salsa are great and plentiful.  

It's a reliable place for consistantly average mexican food.

Had a hankering for Cajun and work took me close to the Market so I made a special stop to pick up lunch for the gang back in the office.

Very disappointed in everything - the food AND the portion sizes. 

First of all, they STIFFED me in charging for jambalaya and not including it in my bags. 

The gumbo was weak. Where's the dark roux for legit gumbo? I'm a NOLA regular and the gumbos there are dark in color and much more favorable. 

The red beans and rice were different than traditional red beans and rice I get on bourbon street. It was okay but not what I expected.

The fried Mac and cheese was two tiny balls of Mac. Spicy but not a hit with the person who ordered it. 

The corn chowder was better than the gumbo. 

The portion sizes are ridiculously small for the price. 

If you want legit delicious Cajun food served in generous portions head to Cajun Kate's at the Booths Corner market. It's as close to NOLA food without the plane trip. AND the portions are excellent

Ate here twice on our visit to Philly. The jambalaya and gumbo are wonderful- nice spice and great flavor. Reading Terminal can be pretty busy, but if there is room at their counter, take a seat and enjoy. You can bring over a beer or drink from the bar too.

Twelve of us decided to try this place after my granddaughter's graduation.  It was late, like a half hour before closing time, so I was kind of afraid we wouldn't be welcomed.  Happy to say I was wrong.  Our server, Cynthia, was incredible!  She took the time to answer everybody's questions, and told us about all of their specials that were not on the menu. 
When the food arrived, she served it perfectly without ever asking who had what. Impressive for that type of restaurant.  The food itself varied, some of it was excellent while other dishes looked just average.  Fresh chips, great salsa, both red and green were served.  We were happy.

So let me start off by saying that I used to work at RCSH back in the mid 90's. I thought the restaurant was good then, maybe not great. Not much steakhouse competition in Philadelphia back then so it didn't have anything to compare it's self to.  I left in 1997 and hadn't been back...until this past Saturday night with a friend who manages a high-end steahouse in the city (she needs to check-out the competition). WOW! I was completely blown away. BBQ shrimp, to die for! T-bone melted in our mouths! Sides and salads were great too. Dave is an excellent bartender, and the support staff made sure we had everything we needed before we needed them (silverware, share plates, etc) The restaurant its self has been updated including the removal of the banquets in the middle of the dining room, for that I give them a thumbs down...I always loved those tables. Keep up the good work RCSH, you'll always have a place in my heart and my stomach!

Wish I could give it more stars, pastries are great but service was very rude. The girl at the counter had a huge attitude problem- this was on a Tuesday evening right before close. Management should have a discussion with employees on common courtesy and customer service.

Besides Isgro Pastries, Termini is my next  go to spot for fresh filled cannoli. Growing up in Philly, Termini is one of my favorite Italian place for yummy delicious Italian cookies and cannolis. Despite being overrun by tourist on the weekend, Termini is still one of the best place in town for a cannoli and they filled them when you ordered.

This is in Port Richmond, NOT Kensington. Get it right.

Great place. Good people. Not too pricey. But it is not in Kensington.

Plus, the pizza there can be the best. It is thin crust and they do not overdo the cheese
like some tacky Fishtown and Port Richmond pizza places.

But it is NOT in Kensington!

This is the bomb!!!!
Becks is the best thing next to Cafe du Monde and more!
Sundays- The Beignets are outstanding, but arrive before 11am because they always sell out. 
The food is just as good, and better, as what you can get in Louisiana. 
We will always look forward to Becks while in Philly.

Came here for a quick lunch with a friend around 1 on a Saturday afternoon. There was limited seating (bar style), but we managed to find a couple of open spots. I got the daily special which was the blackened catfish wrap. The food was decent, and service was good. The pricing was on par with other lunch options.

Hmmm DELICIOUS! Decided on a whim to try La Parrilla Suiza on my way back from my Dr appointment and wow was I pleasantly surprised. I ordered a Shredded Beef Chimichanga and my bf ordered their Enchilada. My Chimichanga came SMOTHERED in thick layer of gooey Queso, so much cheesy goodness! The crust was super crunchy and the shredded beef inside was soft and flavorful, red sauce was a plus. My Chimichanga also came with rice and bean, the rice was standard, nothing out of the ordinary, but the bean though...Super Good!

My bf loved his Enchiladas as well. He is Mexican himself and he said these are just like the way his Grandma used to make them.

We went to the La Parrila Suiza at Oracle, the ambiance and decor was very nice there. Not sure about the other locations as we've drove by them before and they tend to look a little run down from the outside.

We paid about $30ish for the two of us, which is not bad for such deliciousness. Next time though, I'll be bringing a coupon, I got one from the mail the other day, if only I kept my coupons in the car I'd been able to use it this time! :P
Had a delicious cannoli and some Italian sesame seed cookies.  Just like my nonna's baked goods.

Probably the best crepes I've ever had! Both sweet and savory are amazing, I cannot wait to try all the others! The staff is super sweet and friendly, which makes this place that much better. Wonderful spot for a quick visit or for a couple of hours to work/study.

Anyone else remember the stellar episode of "Curb Your Enthusiasm" where Larry David and Jeff discover the greatest chicken ever in a place where they would never be found by friends and family?

Ok...probably just a few of you know what I'm talking about and why the episode was so good.

I thought about that episode as I made my way into this restaurant. While things didn't turn out as well for me as Larry David, the delicious chicken itself was worth the visit. (I enjoyed the yellow sauce more than the green sauce if you're keeping score.)

Honestly, I spent more money than I should have because I wanted plantains and yuca instead of the rice, fries or salad that comes with the usual combo meal. C'mon, I had to have plantains at a place like this.

Oh, and then I added a couple empanadas as well. Yes, I was hungry and had been curious about this place for months, so why not?

The food was fresh, prepared quickly and I truly enjoyed every bite of it.

Service was friendly, unfortunately just not quite as friendly as in the Curb Your Enthusiasm episode. (Yes, I highly recommend checking it out online.)
Worst cream puff and eclair ever.. dried and soggy puffs and the cream was just off. I havent opened the pig ear yet, hope this one is good

Absolute garbage..I order a bacon, egg, potato, and cheese burrito. The bacon was hard and tasted a couple days old, the potatoes were dry and chalky and the egg were ok and melted cheese, but for 6 dollars i would think you would put at least a little love into your food and make a customer want to come back.
