This is my favorite café to go to whenever I'm in town. It's the perfect spot to grab a coffee and do some work in their downstairs lounge area. They have plenty of outlets, free WiFi, and a comfortable atmosphere. Definitely, worth a trip for a quick lunch as well!

The USF Japanese Club planned a Sushi Social at Sushi Tsu and I was really impressed with how they catered to us as their customers. They went above and beyond, doing whatever they could do to make us feel comfortable, although it must have been challenging with such a big group in their restaurant. The food was good and everyone had a really great time there. You can read a more in-depth review with pictures in my Creative Loafing article at: http://blogs.creativeloafing.com/dailyloaf/2010/09/13/local-japanese-restaurant-sushi-tsu-goes-the-extra-mile-for-its-guests/

I had to try the number 1, 2 and 8 items that were rated as some of the best (pending on who's list).

Number 1... the train wreck... very tasty. An unconventional steak and cheese. It has sausage, salami, steak, onions and cheese. I think it's my new favorite steak and cheese.

Number 2... mac and cheese balls... very well done. Typically from other places they come dried out and barely and mac and cheese inside. Becks was cheese and gooey. Fantastic and fun item.

Number 8..my gator gumbo. It's tasty. No complaints. Their gumbo is thick and not watery which I love. I preferred the chicken and shrimp instead of gator.

Was in the area and wanted something yum for lunch that wasn't a chain or fast food and went to good ol' trusty yelp and found this little gem. I have never tried Peruvian before, so I thought yeah, why the hell not! It was pretty awesome. Very chill and inviting vibe. As everyone well tell you, the rotisserie chicken is where it's at - seasoned great, tender, fall off the bone, just what you'd want. I got the rice with cilantro and peas in it instead of the plain side of rice and was all the more merry for it. I also recommend you try the Yuca fries app, they come with this crazy cheese sauce that will knock your socks off. The bf was all fancy and got the tuna as his lunch - I won't go near raw fish, but by his standards I think it was pretty great as he finished his entire plate of it. The waitress mentioned they only make it as ordered so it might take an extra 15 minutes, but then you knew it was going to be good and fresh so we didn't mind the wait.

If you want to branch out from your every day hum drum lunch or dinner, I say you should definitely give Cuenelli's a shot!
Came in to watch the Warriors game and stayed for the food and drinks. Fun environment, attentive but not annoying, and full of sports fans. I love that they're repping DC sports in Tucson, AZ.

The Parrilla Suiza chicken salad and queso Suiza is bomb.  This is my 2nd time going in the last month or so. We used to go quite often and till the whole scandal with the owner taking pictures underneath women skirts...eek!

They have lunch specials during the week that begin at 11am until 1pm (I think).

A good choice for tasty, high quality Mexican food. Lunch specials are a great value. Two salsas and pico de Gallo with in-house chips are flavorful and not too spicy. The bean side dish is wonderful.

This place was surprisingly good.  It's a mishmash of Italian and French inspired sandwiches and crepes.  The crepes were great -- not too sweet, which seems to be a common pitfall of American made crepes.  

The pesto sandwich with mozzarella was good as well.

Am I happy I stopped here for lunch? No. Am I full? No. Am I itching to try more? No. For a quick, casual lunch, the price is not right and neither is the quality. I've heard about their $35 special, but for less, I can get all I can eat sushi at a place in the city, and the quality is more my style. The salmon was average and the wasabi didn't taste like anything. Laughed when I saw the size of my $6 roll. Shook my head, tried the warm fish and rice (I've read that is how it is supposed to be, but considering I've never had that except in a poke bowl, that wasn't great either). Miso soup was a little tangier than I've had so maybe homemade, but could easily just be the same soup at any Chinese restaurant for $1.50. Now I'm hungry and craving more substantial sushi. Best deal was the 50 cent side of avocado! But watch that sky rocket to $1.50 soon.

I had a working lunch (hence the device) and went with the Lomo Salgado, very heavy on the steak and sauce--a plus, but the fries were old. To drink I had juego de mango, I've had better, it was drinkable. Clean restrooms and nice atmosphere. I like the open kitchen, the rotisserie chicken smelled delicious! And service was exceptional. My only stain is the old fries.

I know Ruth's Chris is suppose to be THE steak house, but I still think the best steak I've ever had (and I've had Morton's, Capital Grille, Ruth's Chris, Miami's Forge and Smith & Wollensky) is at Barclay Prime. Don't hate the Death Starr 'cause he's beautiful.

Ruth's, however is better than Morton's I feel. Their location o Broad is great and service is welcoming. Sides are buttery and perfect, and the plates warm. Perfectly pink centers, but some cuts lack that melt-in-your-mouth medium-rare orgasm you meat-aholics may be looking for.

Trident has proved a reliable place to get a beer and some food. Their menu is pretty standard bar food, but what they do, they do well. Their fries, fried pickles, and Mac and cheese are seriously delicious. There are a few unexpected things on the menu, such as a long list of salads,  an awesome caprese, and a cheese board I'd like to try at some point. The staff is friendly and the service is consistently good. It's a great place to play some trivia, catch a game, or simply get a drink with friends.

Such good iced coffee. Tastes like hot coffee tastes but actually is iced coffee. Some iced coffees are more bitter or not enough bitter but this one is the nice amount of bitter. And good ice to coffee ratio. Love the Halloween decorations too. Lovely.

We came on a rainy morning not long after the cafe opened, and the cafe was understandably empty. Boyfriend and I grabbed the lone table upstairs. There were window bar seats though and a downstairs I didn't get a chance to check out. I ordered a caramel ricotta crepe and boyfriend got a smoked salmon avocado one. Service was super friendly and fast. My crepe came out larger than I'd anticipated, but I still managed to finish it; it was drizzled with diluted caramel syrup (so not overly sweet) and dusted with powdered sugar. I usually dislike smoked salmon and avocado, but I tried the Boyfriend's crepe, and I surprisingly really liked it. I liked it just as much as the crepe I ordered. This is a cafe I'd revisit if I were in the area again just to try their other creations.

Love Trident... in my neighborhood... great, great food for a pub (chicken sliders with H2 or Fish & Chips are my go to)  and the service is always very chipper and friendly. 

Seems that they are closing a little earlier during the week than I remember, 11?,  which is a little bit of a bummer but still love it!

During Easter week they make traditional Easter pies and Easter bread. The Easter cookie in the form of Easter basket has interesting flavor of mixed sweet and salty. It's okay.

The square cheesecake is delicious. Pineapple or cherry. It's not too heavy.
The food is delicious and for a very affordable price. The people are really nice and the place itself is very clean and well decorated. Had the eggs on bacon and the Nutella + strawberries crepes.

The good:  Room concept is great. Large sectional, half wall, then two beds. 

The rest:  room 505.  Filthy, filthy carpet in room. Asked for more coffee to be brought up, twice. Never came. Heavy storm, window and the area ceiling spewed water into the room onto the ac unit. Nice. Mildew in shower, the bath floor, and ceiling. The safe is placed directly under the pipes of the bar sink.  Doesn't seem like a great placement... Doors are Loud and Slam. A lot. 

The breakfast was doable. The wheat based breakfast sandwiches were legit and they had a healthy option, which is appreciated. Fresh fruit, great coffee, and cottage cheese. Didn't look at much else, as it was the standard carb/sugar bombs like donuts, muffins, frosted flakes, white breads and bagels.  

The lobby area is nice and comfy to sit a while. Bar area for a quick drink is nice. Staff is nice. Computer and printer to do boarding passes was great. 

Summary:  hotel concept is great. However, the room was filthy. I would not walk in bare feet here.  Ever. And if you need something, don't count on it coming...not even a follow up call to say they can't/won't bring up the coffee pods I asked twice for...
Went there for lunch with my son and his girlfriend. The food was good, however, the Cashier was extremely rude.
If there was an option of no star thats what this place would get, the new management is horrible, as well as the food and service. DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME

Prepare yourself for flavors you're either very familiar with, or not familiar at all. 

Beck's offers delicious Po Boys, anything from chicken, steak, and seafood, to GATOR! And they are all uniquely delicious in their own way. But I'm only going to write about the ones I've tried.

(+)The GOODS:

Their spread. It's almost on every Po Boy, and if it isn't, ASK FOR IT!!!! DO NOT MISS OUT!!

Fried Mac n Cheese Balls are unlike anything I've had before. It's simple, it's tasteful, and most importantly, it's FRIED MAC N CHEESE!!

The Fried Shrimp Po Boy is SO good. The shrimp is super fresh (Gotta love reading Terminal Market), and each bite bursts in your mouth with so much flavor. I also got to add fried oysters to mine, and as heavenly as it was I wish I got the two separate sandwiches.

The Train Wreck is MIGHTY delicious. Who would've thought Salami and Andouille added to steak would add SUCH a kick!!! It's cheesy, it's meaty, and it's messy!!! Just writing about it is making me drool...

(-) The BAD:

The Gator Po Boy could have been more exciting. I love their Gator Gumbo, which is insanely delicious, so I automatically assumed the Po Boy is going to be off the hook. But I have two problems with it:

1. Too many green peppers.
2. And too much spicy mustard. (I was expecting their delicious spread to begin with, so I was already a bit disappointed to see mustard in there.)

These two problems just took away the flavor I was looking for; GATOR!
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I'm going to give Beck's Cajun Cafe 4 Stars because their staff has always been SUPER nice, and somewhat entertaining with their shenanigans. And you can see everything if you sit there; from the first step of the food being prep'd, to cooking and serving of it.

I ordered the cat fish platter, which was satisfying. Cooked properly and seasoned right I was very happy. My girlfriend ordered the blackened chicken pasta which was good. She sprinkled extra Cajun seasoning on it which made taste even better.
Fried mac n cheese bites are a great snack to munch on as you peruse around Reading Terminal Market!

Simply delicious! Had a CAJUN twist to the Philly cheesesteak. 5 hours later and I can still smell it on my fingers. I just close my eyes and savor the taste. I may not want to wash it off! Will definitely come back!!

I used this laundromat for the first time today. I had hesitated coming here due to the negative reviews it has received. We have camped at Catalina State Park at least 4 weeks every year for the past 5 years, and there really aren't any laundry facilities nearby. I'm so glad I finally decided to try Catalina Laundry. 

I arrived at 8 am and the place was empty, sparkling clean, and all the machines were in working order. I will definitely make this my place to go in the future. Washes are $2 and the dryer is .25 for 6 minutes.

O...M...G. Why is this not in my area... the food was AMAZING! It was just the right amount that nothing went to waste or I felt hungry afterwards.  The chicken and sausage gumbo and the blackened chicken alfredo...made me wanna hug everyone next to me and the ladies that served the dishes...

So we went back to Trident this past Sunday afternoon and had a completely different experience than the first time.  We had gone over a year ago and pretty much been completely ignored by the waitresses even though it was not very busy.  

This time, the place was full, being Sunday and packed with football watchers, but the wait staff was quite attentive and the food was delicious (A couple different burgers and a really good salad).

Much much better the second time around.
Had the pecan bar.  Was so very good. Tasty and not too sweet.   Was just perfect and and great with a cup of coffee. Great place to stop

Trident is great. We've been coming here once a week for a few months now for Geeks Who Drink on Wednesdays. The servers have been consistently awesome every week! I totally agree that they have the best fish and chips in Tucson, but to mention the other food. It's nice that it is not all greasy bar food offerings- their salads are yummy too!

Nice atmosphere, we sat for 20 minutes before our Waiter took our order and 45 minutes to get our food. Chips and salsa were good! Prices are high in comparison to other favorites! Chicken chimichanga was good size, chicken over boiled no flavor, you get tiny portion of rice and beans which were ok. Service was poor waiter was not attentive. I have been to this location before where service was better and food tasty! My experience with this establishment is that each visit is inconsistent as far as food flavor? This visit was not pleasing.

First off the totones are sooo good. Crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside. Love them.

Had the tilapia salad which was "OK". It would be excellent if the fish was seasoned before it was fried. It kinda taste too "fresh"for lack of a better word. Tastes like the tank where it came from. Other than that the greens were fresh and crispy

Great food and a nice spot to get a quick bite. I really wanted to give 5 stars, but their counter help was a bit clueless/aloof. Also, counter wasn't really wiped down. 

If definitely come here again.

The shrimp and chicken gumbo here was just delicious !! The service was fast and friendly and it was worth every penny. 

I make it a point to stop by here when I am in reading terminal. You won't be disappointed.

Hands down the worst Peruvian food we've ever had. The ceviche took 30 min, was warm and the fish tasted bad, but they still made us pay for it. The chicken looked and tasted like fried pigeon. The Lomos Saltado was the only decent plate we tried, but even then the meat was over cooked. I wish I had my $40 back, hoping the bad fish doesn't give us food poisoning.

Ordered the blackened chicken alfredo for lunch. It's alright I guess, but there's basically no chicken in this. It's just cajun-spiced penne alfredo. When I did find the only two pieces of chicken in the bowl, they were tough, dry, and not the slightest bit spicy. It was such bad "blackened chicken" that I actually lowered my review from three stars to two.

Been dying to try and finally made it today! Amazing!! Crepes were perfect the sweat and the meaty ones! Goat turkey on the baguette was also amazing.. ice lattes on point! After 3 years I finally found my neighborhood spot 6 stars

We visited Termini Bros as we toured Reading Market. The cannoli we ordered was very good. The pig ear pastry was bland, dry and hard to chew. A lot of other baked goods to choose from at Termini Bros. We would order the cannoli again but not the pig ear pastry.

A bit of a tourist trap.  Had a family dinner party and expected a really fantastic dinner.  The staff was just ok - would have expected much better.  The steaks were very good but everything else was just okay for the high prices.  Will choose somewhere else next time.

I found this place to be pretty darn cool. This place bleeds american pride, honor and beer! Good selections!
We had the chicken skewers. Juicy! Loved em! 
Only stayed for a bit but I give 5 stars for the beers, skewers, and ambiance.
I'll be back....

Hands-down, the best cupcakes I have ever had... in my entire life!  Both the chocolate and vanilla are equally amazing, and they have extra icing in the middle.  No trendy flavors, just the classic kind of cupcakes you had when you were a kid.

I'm only giving 4 stars instead of 5 because The canolis and rum cake (I forget the correct name) were good, but nothing I would run back for.

Let me first say that I am writing this review having only experienced Trident's happy hour. I have not been here for lunch or dinner, which, if I were to guess are probably both great.. I loooove their happy hour, because it's extremely cheap and gives me the pub food fix I need. My personal favorites are the fried pickles and potatoes skins. They're happy hour atmosphere is a perfect place to meet with a friend after work (or, in my case, school) and catch up. They have comfy booths, and large tables for bigger parties. Their service is always timely and their servers have been pleasant. If you're looking for a happy hour with a great beer selection, pub food, and low prices, stop by Trident.

This is my first time here. I recently got a Groupon for it and couldn't decide a better day to try their food on a nice chilly day.

When I first got there I sampled a few of their gumbos. They were good. 

So my girlfriend and I ended up getting the 
1. Andouille Sausage Po Boy
2. Shrimp Salad Po Boy (I think these usually aren't offered) 
3. Cajun Fries w/ Jalepenos and fried onions
4. Abita Root Beer (Striaght outta Abita Springs, Louisiana)

Everything was good! But I gotta say, I'm definitely coming back for some more gumbo! Very satisfied with everything.

Firstly, it's located in Reading Terminal Market which is a destination unto itself. Wander around, look at all the offerings, and smell all the amazing smells that are coming from every stall. Secondly, Termini Brothers is iconic. This is on the culinary Philly bucket list. You must have the cannoli at least once. Third, the cannoli is good!! Shell is crispy without falling apart after one bite and the filling is creamy without being watery. Eat the cannoli. Just do it.

Meh...at best.  What we took home was a mere shell for which flavor could have been, but never was, applied.

The sushi was old, the edamame was tasteless. They forgot to include chopsticks in the stapled to go bag. The soy sauce was served in a perfectly inconvenient size, where the sushi roll is slightly larger than the soy sauce cup.

Not the worst sushi I have eaten, but close.

I picked up a tiramisu ($5) at Termini Bros inside Reading Terminal Market yesterday. 

It was not bad but definitely not the best either. I don't think it was made with ladyfingers for the cake base and real mascarpone cheese for the cream like how real, authentic home-made tiramisu tends to be made. Not much espresso taste either. 
 
I will try a cannoli next time.

I didn't go to the U of A, so naturally Trident hasn't always been on my radar, but my boyfriend urged us to come here to watch the game with some friends. I'm not sure if it's because I was starving after a major workout, but aside from our servers poor attitude, Trident was pretty much a home run or slam dunk, or what ever on this visit! 

Cold as* Barrio Blonde hit the spot right away. Next, fried pickles. WOW. Best I've ever had: Pickle spears in a crispy and light batter, not greasy with a side of ranch. That's a legit bar snack.

Sliders: Um....probably the next best bar snack ever. Medium rare thinly sliced filet with horseradish aioli on teeny tiny buns. So unexpected and super tasty. I'd for sure order this again.

Build Your Own Burger: I went with a medium cooked burger with cheddar cheese, sauteed mushrooms, lettuce, tomato and onion with a side of waffle fries. The burger was large and in charge and I ate it ALL BY MYSELF. I really can't complain. It was cooked to perfection and all the toppings were super fresh. 

The Trident experience has room for improvement in the service department. I know this is a sports bar in the middle of the University area, but a mix of students (graduate and undergrad), young professionals and old peeps alike frequent this place and we're all spending money here, so smile at the door and smile while you're at work :)

If you're planning on catching a game here, get there early! The line gets long quickly and it's no fun being ignored at the door.

I am a HUGE fan of Vineyards Cafe! The staff is all super friendly, and I am a big fan of how they do iced coffee (essentially a red eye, which is DELICIOUS!) And honestly, their pesto sandwich is one of my top favorite sandwiches. I love that they're right down the street from me, and I appreciate that they were able to open up again to do takeout service during the pandemic. Definitely check them out!!!

Wok N Walk
An enthusiastic  walking tour of Chinatown. Includes a Buddhist temple, Asian market, bakery, and fortune cookie factory. Joseph gives you samples and food at most stops, then returns and cooks you a  delicious 3 course dinner. He is generous with his time, his food and his knowledge and his philosophy of living. A one of a kind experience.

Wanted to step out of our comfort zone and try Nawlins cuisine. We ordered short rib po boy, vegetable po boy, Cajun fries and beignets. This being our first time purchasing lunch here proved to be enlightening, folk walking by can get samples of food served, and you can watch the two cooks prepare your food and smile while employees bump into each other. 

We both enjoyed our po boys, she had plenty of meat inside the baguette and I had a good amount of spinach and eggplant on mine. The fries were good, would've enjoyed more onions and jalapeños throughout. My only complaint was when ordering the beignets, it would've been nice to have been informed that one order could feed 2-3 people. My friend ordered 3 beignets, not knowing that was three separate orders of 6 beignets each. 

All in all, I cCan't wait to try another item soon.

[ sundays ]
The cutely named Sunday School menu is an amazing deal - choice wines and cheeses for about $7-9 each. If you're on a budget but still want to have a classy, cozy evening with a close friend or date without emptying your wallet, Sunday is the perfect night to come. 

[ getting a table ]
We have walked in on many nights without reservations and been seated quite promptly, though the place is always very close to being full. Surprising that this location isn't more popular, given that I can't make a single complaint about anything here.

[ food and drink ]
Normal-priced wines are $9 - $14 each, as are the tapas and cheese plates. I have never gotten anything here that wasn't precisely balanced in flavour or elegant in presentation. You can always count on Tria to get the food and drink on point.

They are also quite generous with bread refills - fresh bageutte pieces which pair well with all their cheeses.

[ ambience and service ]
Gorgeous modern décor, friendly and warm servers (with a beautiful and classy fashion sense). Real candles on the tables. Quiet without being still, and elegant music choices. Beautiful and relaxing without being stuffy or pretentious.

Menu descriptions are also beautiful, well-written, and great fun to read.

[ overall ]
The perfect place for a real conversation. Definitely a Philly gem and a Center City favourite!
Love this place. The green rice and the green sauce are great. Yuca a la huancaina has one of the best pepper/cheese sauces in a Peruvian place in Tampa. Their chicken is very tasty as well.

This is what you need to know about this place, especially the South Philly location - it is a staple of Philadelphia and the South Philly store is the first and most famous one.

As someone who comes from a traditional Italian family who additionally, originates in South Philly (after Italy), I can tell you that the goods they sell here are the most traditional and most high quality you can get in Philadelphia or the surrounding areas.
The cannoli are out of this world, as well as the traditional cookies such as the pinnoli cookies.

The place is always packed, but around the holidays, it's obscene.  Just make sure you get there at the crack of dawn on Christmas Eve morning or else you could be in line for hours (even though they are working really fast back there), that's how many people pour into Terminis around Christmas time!
Their sushi is just okay but stick to their fish over rice. The tuna over rice is absolutely amazing! Perfectly seasoned and all of the flavors compliment one another so well.

I saw that the Trident Grill was serving the Impossible Burger, and we were eager to to try it out. My wife is pescavegan, fish, but no meat or dairy. We tried the Vegan Patty melt. Unfortunately, we were disappointed. The burger was over-cooked, and the the bread was burned. I've read care needs to be taken in cooking the Impossible Burger so that it doesn't get over-done. This confirms it. 

On the other hand, the salmon was great as always, nice tasty crust and moist, but done on the inside. 

I'm giving it four stars based on all our other visits. It's usually a dependable late-night venue.
Stopped in as I was passing by around lunchtime, figured I would give it a try.  The pizza is great.  Fantastic food, very reasonable prices and friendly staff.  LOVE THAT PLACE !

I have been going to Sushi Tsu fairly regularly for a year now. The sushi is delicious, especially the Volcano roll. The sushi and hibachi chefs are all very talented. Prices are very reasonable, especially during lunch and the early bird times. I can't name any other places where you can get filet for such a low price. I would recommend Sushi Tsu to everyone!
Located in the Reading Market, the Termini Bros. Bakery is a visual delight showcasing scrumptious pastries of all kinds! The palmier cookies were the largest we've even seen!

Never had Peruvian food so I thought I would give it a try. Nothing fancy in the decor department but clean with a super friendly staff. I got the dark chicken special with spicy beans and cilantro rice. The rice was great and the beans had a nice spice. At 6.99 and came out in minutes a great lunch deal. The were taking the chickens right off if the rotisserie so super fresh. It comes with two sauces a green spicy salsa and a yellow that tasted like aioli. The chicken was seasoned nice juicy with a crispy skin. I would definitely do it again for a cheap fast lunch.

Great Experience & Incredibly Fresh! I'm sitting here right now eating The Blackened Catfish Platter with red beans and rice.... In the middle of the hustle and bustle of the Reading Terminal. I was engaged by friendly staff that made it super easy to order. I chose to "dine in" and I'm glad I did. The Catfish: "Wow!" The Fried Cornbread: "Oh. My. Goodness." I'm a huge Red Beans & Rice fan and I'd say it's pretty good here. I prefer the more "earthy" taste and it is lacking in that department. At this point, though, I'm splitting hairs... Great spot! DEFINITELY recommend.

It was my first time visiting this amazing vegan restaurant and the staff were amazing and nice. 
Visit this place when you go to Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.   
I ordered the Philadelphia cheesesteak of course, and my wife got the chicken, ranch wrap

Wow what a great dinner for a last minute decision....  The burger was perfectly cooked and came with the sweet potato fries which were served hot.  The friendly server offered to put the house sauce on the side when we could not decide on which one to try and it was delicious.  They had a very good IPA selection including Fresh Squeezed.  Perfect dinner!

I can honestly say that the food and service here is always exceptional! The food is so amazing!! Try the rotisserie chicken and the cilantro rice. You will not be disappointed!! The service is absolutely wonderful. The staff is very polite and accommodating. This is definitely one of my favorite places in Tampa.

Dear Management, 

Please clean your filthy restaurant, including the vaulted ceiling area that hasn't been cleaned since the place was built. Don't look up at the dust museum! lol.  The food here is always below average & served luke-warm.  Hispanic/Latino staff seems to be a bit unresponsive towards Caucasian customers, which is a joke since they don't even serve authentic Mexican Food.

As our first stop on the food tour of Reading Terminal Market, The Trainwreck ($9.95 Steak, Salami, Andouille Sausage, Cheese and Onions).  Dripping in steak juice, melted cheese, the blend of spicy sausage and salami are a great topping for this southern version of a cheese-steak.  

If it wasn't for my desire to eat 15 other things while in the market, I'd have had another Trainwreck!

I'm so sorry that I didn't try this place out sooner.  I lost two years of good chicken.

I love pollo a la brasa.  Having it in Pucallpa, Peru was one of the brightest spots during my Peruvian trip (and that includes visiting Machu Picchu). Living in Tampa, I figured I'd have to make it myself, but lacking a rotisserie left me with subpar attempts.  Thankfully, now I can go to Cuenelli's.

The chicken is moist and flavorful.  The aji sauce is addictive.  I really like the salad dressing on the salad, and the fries aren't bad, especially with a little aji and ketchup.

After reading the other reviews, I'm looking forward to returning and trying the steak with the egg dripping into the black beans and rice.  I just ate a few hours ago, and just thinking about bistek has my stomach growling.

Came back today to indulge in the lobster mac and cheese, as well as drinks (no class on Sundays!). Arrived around 6pm and we were seated immediately at one of the outdoor tables, on a nice and warm evening.

I ordered the Pimm's Cup, which was a fantastic, well-balanced, light drink with lemon, real ginger, and cucumber flavours. It was less of a punch to the head than a real whiskey while still being more legitimate than some fruity girly "drink" that is really just juice. A perfect accompaniment to the meal.

My friend ordered "Canucks in Tennessee", which I got a kick out of as a Canadian (eh?). Strong rye whiskey with a nice sweet note from maple syrup. Both drinks were very well-balanced.

The lobster mac and cheese was a lovely $18 indulgence, but not something I'd casually go for again due to calorie count and price. That said, absolutely worth trying at least once, since it was quite well made. A substantial amount of meat too, and unlike other reviewers, I don't think it was all rubbery claw meat.

[ conclusion ]
Still a bit pricey, but absolutely worth it. Drinks are on point and food is great. Lovely spot.

This place is a good place for what it is.  It is sports bar in a college town, across the street from the university.  The drinks are affordable, the food is good for the price you pay.  The staff can sometimes be a little preoccupied, but most of the staff say 70% is college students.  However, on the plus side, this place is owned and operated by a retired Navy SEAL.  It is actually similar to a bar in Coronado California.McP's Pub.  However, I believe Nelson spent more time in Dam Neck Virginia based on all the Redskins memrobilia.  All in all a good place to grab a beer, a burger/sandwich and watch a game.

They have really good food.  From the jambalaya to the Po Boys.  You really can't go wrong with their food.  If you like to know when you are eating good food, this is a great place for lunch.  The food is delicious and the spice is on point.  I think this is the closest to bayou food you will get in the Philadelphia area.  They even have gator, which is one of my favorite foods, so definitely worth checking out.

They're kind, hardworking people. The breakfast selection is large considering and the owner is so sweet. The coffee is very strong and you can tell it comes from a good source! An A+ place to grab a coffee, though, I wouldn't suggest eating in, its rather small.

Holy cannoli! These treats are absolutely amazing. I love cannoli and I was so excited to try these on my last trip to Reading Terminal Market. The cannoli were absolutely amazing and the perfect combination of sweet and crunchy. 

I feel like often times when I eat a connoli, the shell is soggy from the cream, but this is not the case here! The shell has a perfectly, fresh baked crisp and a beautiful cream filling on the inside. The cream is not too sweet and there are just enough chocolate chips, that you get the perfect amount in every bite.

Definitely coming here again to get more cannoli!

A taste of New Orleans in Philly. Their shrimp po-boy hit the spot- a standout was their Cajun mayo (like a remoulade). We also dig their Cajun fries... although be warned that it is more like breakfast potatoes. Sample some of their gumbos - they have little sample cups available!
Not the best pollo restaurant around bit decent. A bit overpriced and food is smoky. I guess you get what you pay for.

I just had their cannolis for the second time this past weekend and again was amazing as the first time I had it.  I recommend Termini's if you want a wonderful and authentic cannoli at the Reading Terminal Market.

This is a solid bar - great crowd here. The food is pretty good as far as bar food goes, too. I'd recommend this place for drinks with friends, a casual meal, catching up with loved ones... Of all the bars in Tucson (and there are A LOT), this is one of the best.

Beck's sits in the middle of the Reading Terminal Market and serves up tasty Cajun cuisine with a kick. You can try jambalaya, étouffée, gumbo, rice and beans, and other Cajun staples. The food is filling, and prices are fair. Stop by for a delicious meal, next time you're here at the market!

One of the hot spots in the Reading Terminal. My girlfriend and I ordered the Fried Oyster Platter and man was it delicious and filling Right off the bat I noticed how big each oyster was. The Oysters were beautifully fried  because it had the right amount of coding and wasn't so much that it covered up the deliciousness of Oyster itself. The platter came with Mini Cajun potato wedges and Corn Bread, which was a good addition on the side but the Cornbread was a bit on the dry side for me. 

One again, this is one of my favorite place to eat at the Reading Terminal. P.S. I did try their free sample of the seafood gumbo and man was it on the salty side! ANYWAYS, Fried Oyster Platter is a must!
I enjoy the portion sizes and the food in general. The place is very casual.  The rice was some of the best cilantro rice I've tasted.

Top notch. Great place. Awesome food. There is nothing like their pizza, strombolis, or their service, always smiling. 

Love this place, love the food, love the people. An absolute must!!

Tried the bread pudding and was very happy with it.. I lived in New Orleans for two years, so I have some previous bread pudding experience on my resume.. staff is very friendly and cool.. eager to try some of their other stuff.. Reading Terminal Market is a cool place to hang out in general, but I particularly liked the vibe at this place...

This is one of the few Cajun places in the Philly area that I recommend if you are feeling adventurous or having a Cajun craving.

I recommend trying the gator sausage (by itself versus Po Boy style) to get the full taste of it.  It comes with a hot dipping sauce which compliments it well.  The Train Wreck is a classic if you are looking to be filled - it's packed with various meats, cheeses, and a sauce that melts in your mouth.  I must say the sauce they add is strong and the sandwich itself may be heavy for one's liking, but otherwise good in my opinion!
Great little breakfast spot! It's super quick and the basement eating area is cute without looking like a basement at all.

If you entered the Reading Terminal Market from the 12th St. entrance, you will no doubt see this alluring dessert bakery if you go straight down the aisle. Don't doubt it: the stuff that you see on the shelf tastes good as it looks!

Sadly my family was leaving Philadelphia so we decided to drop by Reading Terminal for one last Philly snack. My sister who is a huge dessert fan could not keep her eyes off the huge, delicious-looking dessert selection Termini Bros displayed. It was her birthday soon so I decided to buy her a small cake but she wasn't able to make a choice.

What can I say? The paradox of choice can be quite paralyzing.

Fortunately, the nice cashier girl gave my sisters suggestions and she settled with the chocolate cake with a slice of banana on top. The size was around 3 inches in diameter and was $5. Even though I said I was buying it for my sister, I ended up eating half of it.

It was a truly decent chocolate cake with satisfying sweetness that does not overwhelm. Each eat was complemented with a light touch of banana taste. Although I am usually not banana about banana, I thought it adds a nice, new dimension.

Termini Bros Bakery was a dessert eye-candy that offers actual good taste behind good visual. Try out this solid dessert place if you are visiting the Reading Terminal Market.

I highly recommend ordering for pickup. 
Simple and tasteful. Great packaging as well. Location can be crowded during the lunch hour. Ask for extra dressing on salads.

Alligator on a  stick - a very tasty, spicy sausage with a nice spicy whole grain mustard on the side. This sausage is not pure alligator, which is too lean to make a good sausage, so I know there was some pork or something mixed in but it was good. 

Jambalaya rice - good, could have had more goodies mixed in with it though

Etoufee - not bad, but not enough shrimp and crawfish, mostly gravy, nice spice to it and loved the okra. 

Beignets - nothing special, sorry. 

Service was very friendly, prices were very high for the portion size though.

Was told to go here by a local co worker (i live in Phoenix). The wings were awesome, the cod fish tacos were amazing!! And the Mac and cheese side was so good! The burger was OK. It was the steakhouse burger. Overall a very cool place. As a veteran I appreciated all the military pictures on the wall! 
Excited to try something new next time!
Shrimp poboy and beignets were very good. Wife says if she had to choose between this and a Philly cheese steak she'd choose the poboy hands down.

Love this place! I live just right up the street on poplar. I come here at least 2-3 times a week for my morning coffee. Their customer service is great btw! I advise anyone who is in the area or even just visiting the city to take a visit. You won't be disappointed with their menu. Btw their lounge is a huge plus! Great place to study when trying to escape the noise of the city.

Its a little bit overpriced. The food was okay, it has taste but I wasnt jumping up and down. The lemonade is full of ice. Spent almost $15 just for lemonade and 1 entree. I probably will not try it again.

We were at the Reading Terminal and so happy to know there was a Termini Bros location here. I heard we needed to try a cannoli from Termini and now I know why. I don't even have the words to describe how good they were and I'm not even a big fan of cannolis. These were delicious. The filling was not to sweet yet rich and full of flavor. You will want more. My biggest mistake was ordering only and sharing it! Don't make the same mistake I made. Order a few because you're gonna want more! They cost about $4 for each cannoli. Not cheap

My husband and I went to Ruth's Chris Steak House for a restaurant week date night on Friday and had an excellent meal and experience.

We were lucky to snag a reservation but it was a little early at 6:00pm. We were seated promptly at a booth by the bar. We've eaten here before and were hoping to sit in the dining room. Luckily they were able to move us to another table not in the bar.

We started with a nice bottle of Sileni Gooseberry Sauvignon Blanc. I'd recommend it for any Sauv Blanc fan. For our appetizers, I went with the lobster bisque and my husband went with the salad. I know it's restaurant week but the portions were really tiny. My little soup cup only had one medium piece of lobster in it. The bisque was tasty though. It was creamy just a slight bitterness. According to my husband, his salad was small and wasn't anything special.

But the appetizers weren't why we were there. We went for the steak! We both ordered the 8 ounce fillet which was cooked to medium rare perfection. The plate came out steaming and you could hear and see the sizzle. The outside of the steak was slightly thicker and had an extra seasoning from the inside. This was the quintessential, melt in your mouth type of meat. I had the creamed spinach as my side and thought the portion was pretty hearty. It was creamy and enjoyable. My husband went with the garlic mashed potatoes which were pretty tasty as well.

So the service was everything one would want from a steakhouse. Upon ordering, we were asked if we were celebrating anything special. In addition to date night, we were out for my husbands birthday. When it came time for dessert, his creme brulee came out with a candle. They didn't sing or anything cheesy. It was just a nice little acknowledgment. There was also a gentleman with a camera who took our picture and printed out a copy for us as a souvenir. The service was generally prompt, attentive and proper. 

The desserts were also on the smaller side but after a decent sized steak and side, that was fine by me. As mentioned, my husband went with the creme brulee. I had the chocolate mousse. It was rich with little pieces of chocolate crumbles accentuating the flavor.

The timing of our meal was another positive to note. Clearly they were pretty busy the night of our visit. We didn't feel rushed and were able to enjoy a dining experience. They easily could have just pushed us a long.

While Ruth's Chris won't be every day dinner trip for us, it's a great special occasion steak house.
Went at lunch time. Service OK. Food not that good.  Ordered beef tamal with enchilada suiza. Tamal was hard as a rock on the ends.  The enchilada sauce tasted like canned. Would not return.

I've been going to this chain (I use the term loosely since it has such negative connotations) for over a decade. Regardless of whether I'm having their ribeye in Chicago, NJ, or in Philly, it definitely hits the spot. 

Our waiter was Chris - a friendly gentleman who was opinionated enough about his recommendations. 

The GF and I started off with a raspberry lemon drop martini for her and a Bloody Mary for me (she originally asked for one of the cocktails with ginger ale in it, but Chris steered us away - we'll never know how bad it was ...). She enjoyed her lemon drop and my Bloody Mary had a nice kick - sans celery stick. 

For our apps, we had the caprese salad - with mozzarella supposedly procured daily from Italian Market. Tasted fresh and the accompanying balsamic dressing hit the spot with the fresh beefsteak tomatoes. We also had the BBQ shrimp (listed as being 'Voted Philly's Best') which were a bit different from what I expected. Rather than being BBQ, it was more of a tangy light cream sauce topped with snappy, yummy shrimp. Two butter baguette ends rounded out the dish. Quite nice - 5 shrimp ... $3 a piece essentially. The shrimp dish was OK, but not something I would necessarily order again. But we weren't here for the shrimp were we?

So onto the entrees ... can't go wrong with the Ribeye here. Medium for her ... medium-rare for me. Nicely marbled, juicy, perfect pink. 

Chris made the bernaise sauce for the night and brought us out bernaise and peppercorn for us to try (on the house). Now I'm not normally a sauce man with my steak, but these were very good! Bernaise had that lemony twang ... the peppercorn was more savory. In fact - I may have accidentally drizzled a few spoonfuls on top of the garlic mashed potatoes we ordered as a side. Delicious. 

Desert - we ended with the creme brulee - topped with ripe strawberries and blueberries. Very nice.

Service was very good. Water was replenished without having to ask for it. 

But at these prices - it's to be expected no? 

I know that the prices aren't listed on the website so here is what they were for the night (I figure this might help folks out some):

Ribeye - $41
Filet - $39
Garlic Mashed - $8.50
BBQ Shrimp - $15
Caprese Salad - $12
Creme Brulee - $7.50
Drinks - around $10-12 

These 4 stars are for consistency and an excellent steakhouse rib-eye. It's not on par with Peter Luger's but it can hold its own.

Friend and I came here during restaurant week because we heard it was good in other areas. The decor was a little old school was me, probably meant to attract people of the older age group. 

The food I had to say is a little bit too pricey for the quality.  I had the lobster bisque and it was really bitter. I don't really like to waste food, but I couldn't stuff it down. My friend on the other hand got a salad, and that was actually quite tasty. 

Our entrees, which I got filet Mignon and the friend porkchops came extremely quickly- like it was rushed. The food was still sizzling on the plates when handed to us. The steak was actually pretty bland and closer to rare then medium rare. The pork chops were dry. The best thing I probably had was the creme brulee. It was rich and tasty. 

Maybe the food wasn't all that great because of the hectic restaurant week, but if you want to grab a bite before heading to the kimmel center. Look elsewhere.

Family place with taste

We drove up from St. Pete just to give Peruvian food a try. I'm glad we did. The fish was wonderful, the steak was good as well as the chicken! We samples a variety of items, shared, savored and snuck bites and we all agreed it was a very nice meal. I want to sample more and see what else the Peruvian palate has to offer. So far, so good!
Best food truck in the city hands down.  Healthy and delicious

Caramel ricotta crepe was amazing and so was my mochaccino but the Norwegian crepe was sadly not for me at all. I normally love goat cheese but this crepe was totally overpowered by the goat cheese which was slathered on very thick. Also I just felt like the goat cheese, avocado, and salmon were all way too similar with slimy texture. I would not recommend that crepe but their other stuff looked and tasted good. I want to come back and try other things.
This place rocks. Delicious, fresh crawdads and catfish, jambalaya gumbos and ettouffee, po boys and creol breakfast. Alligator sausage, snapper soup and its all so fresh and yummy. Best lunch idea.

I'm late posting this Yelp review. I stayed for the weekend in Philly nearby this gem. Stopped in on a Sunday AM looking for a cup of good coffee and maybe just a quick bite. The menu is pretty varied (who knew there were so many choices for crepes?). I decided on the goat bacon and was not disappointed. 
There was a small wait, but the ingredients are fresh, and made as ordered. Grabbed a great cup of coffee, sat down for a bit and took in the sights. It is located in a neighborhood that is undergoing a resonance. 
The crepe was just scrumptious! Great way to start my day. 
Highly recommend.

This is a fun place to eat and watch a Wildcat game, though it does get very crowded, especially on game days. The food is typical bar grub, but done exceptionally well. Their burgers are big and juicy, their shrimp tacos are outstanding, and they have a huge number of brews. Try it, you'll like it.

The bread on the po' boys is back to the quality it used to be and Beck's Cajun has been back in my regular lunch rotation for a while now. I used to do pick-up all the time but now I plop my behind on a stool and eat there most of the time. The staff is always so friendly that it makes the experience of eating those delicious po' boys that much better! The fried shrimp is my usual go to, but I've had the trainwreck and that is amazing as well. They may not be 100% New Orleans authentic po' boys, but it's still the best version I've found in Philly.

Seven years ago, I was fortunate enough to have a chance to spend a couple of weeks in South Louisiana visiting my signifiant other's grandparents; who lived in New Iberia.  This town is barely mile from Avery Island, which is where Tabasco is made and is surrounded by swampland.  It's as authentic Cajun as you can get! 

Accents may be impossible to understand sometimes, but you don't need words to have their food speak to you.  Gumbo, jambalaya, blackened chicken, you name it.  I had it all right from kitchen tables in the homes and local businesses in those small towns right outside of New Orleans.

After coming back to Pennsylvania, I found myself craving these foods constantly.  Pretty much any "Cajun Restaurant" I'd found was always a disappointment.  I was able to re-create some of the dishes after spending some time learning to cook.  

When I moved to Philly, one of my first stops was through Reading Terminal Market.  I'd even made a stop to the spices shop to grab some cayenne pepper and noticed a sign for Beck's Cajun Cafe!  My expectations were low, as they've had to be after years of disappointment with so called "Cajun food".  

Much to my surprise, as soon as I got close I could tell right away I'd found something special.  Since then, I've pretty much become a Beck's evangelist.  The Gator Gumbo is thick and spiced, the blackened chicken is cooked to perfection with just the right amount of spices for that perfect cajun flavor.

I can definitively say that Beck's is the closest to authentic home-made country Cajun food I've found since leaving South Louisiana.  The staff is always super friendly and always takes my special requests with a smile.  

If you love Cajun food, this place is a must.  If you've never had Cajun food, it's still a must.  Bring your appetite and don't be afraid to try the gator, you'll thank me later!
They Forgot my chicken on my chicken Cesar salad that i picked up  but still charged me for the chicken but still pizza is dank

It's a must stop anytime in Reading Terminal Market for a quick snack, if not for a large order.  Let me just preface this review that I've only come here for their cannoli's. 

Their cannoli's are sick.  The ricotta cheese with chocolate chip reigns king here as the go to order, though I'm a personal fan of the vanilla flavor.  The custard to carb combination is just one of a kind and has a great mix of texture against the cannoli shell.  The chocolate cannoli's come in at a not so distant third to the other flavors.

A bit pricey for each, but worth the coin for a quick snack or dozen.

There aren't a lot of destination dining spots in Francisville...yet, but Vineyards is certainly an exception.  The owners took a bit of a gamble by opening this fantastic european style corner cafe at 16th and Ogden amidst a ton of residential development.  After watching the place fill up to the brim today, I think they made a smart move by fulfilling a need here in the Francisville community.  

The space is bright, clean and feels comfortable with all the reclaimed wood.  The upstairs doesn't have much space, but surprisingly, there's a cozy garden level seating area below.  The menu consists of savory and sweet crepes, sandwiches, salads and a few omelets.  The drink menu is diverse, and while we don't drink coffee, everyone else seemed to be enjoying it.  

We loved the ham, gouda and walnut with maple syrup crepe.  (It was a little bit better than the crepes we had in Paris.)  The Norwegian crepe was loaded with goat cheese, smoked salmon and avocado, and the ricotta/caramel variety had just the right amount of sweetness.  

We'll be back for sure and we wish them the best of luck as a cornerstone eatery in the neighborhood.  As the density continues to fill in, I'm certain they will be in good company.

I got food poisoning after eating here on the evening of Thursday February 2nd. I had the quarter dark chicken and spicy beans and salad. 3 hours later I became violently ill. I believe there could be a sanitation problem as I was very sick. Stay away.
Absolutely the best crepes I have ever tasted. This place is a must go when you visit Philly. Btw, the crepes are HUGE. They also have delicious coffee and tea options. Highly recommend

Ordered the steak medallions and asparagus. Ordered the steak cooked medium and was cooked perfectly and was seasoned well too. Asparagus was grilled and seasoning was great. Also came with some fried potatoes that were crunchy and delicious. Ordered and ate at the bar. The bartender was really "smart".  My Buffalo Trace was poured just right too.  Will definitely come back next time I'm in town.

No stars... I ordered 2 carne asada tortas and ground beef super nachos....the lady kept saying i wanted a ground beef burrito3x....gave her the benefit of the doubt since the speaker is shifty.... Went to the window and asked to repeat the order.... She said um i think its was 2 tortas and a burrito right?...corrected her paid and took off..... Got home to find a slab of burnt meat on my tortas and my wifes nachos had burnt meat and more sour than usual sour cream.... I called and asked who i was speaking with and the girl said why do u need to know ...i explained i have a right to know the name of my server and asked for a manager which she rudely declined and hung up

The food here is okay. It didnt have much flavor, relying on cheeses instead of spices for taste. It is inexpensive and plentiful though. The service was great and I like the ambience. Nice you can get a drink from the bar and relax.

The Train Wreck. My night at Reading Terminal was a train wreck including the parking vending machine not giving me my change. The sandwich was bursting with flavor. I would call it an 'Adouille Sausage' sandwich with a bunch of stuff including cheesesteak meat. Apparently Adouille Sausage is greasy because a lot of greasy ended up in the bottom of my basket. The good news is the French baguette was amazing and held up very well while being attacked by grease. Aside from the grease, the sandwich was very flavorful, we enjoyed it while drinking a beer from Molly Malloy's, famous 4th street cookie company had cookies for $1 and on the way home Carole and I stopped at the Navy Yard to walk around so overall it was a good night.

For all of the talk about traditional Philly cheese steaks, this was the best sandwich with steak and cheese that I had in Philadelphia. Overflowing with meat, perfectly melted and gooey cheese and a warm soft roll that held it all together, none of the ingredients overwhelmed each other. Each bite had the robust flavor from the sausage, the hints of saltiness from the salami and the meatiness of the steak.

I would normally doc a point from their "cajun fries" as they're definitely not fries, more of a cajun hash. Not bad but not what I was expecting or hoping for in that moment, but the sandwich was just too good not to.
The space looks small but downstairs says otherwise! Got some crepes to start off my morning.
Delicious! Highly recommend the chicken and shrimp gumbo! Friendly staff. And don't forget a sweet tea!

This place is amazing. We order take out for lunch a lot and every time it is great. I love the salad and the dipping sauces for the chicken are probably the main reason I like it so much. I really prefer the yellow over the green but they are both good. Only thing is if you try to ask for two yellows instead of a green, you still get a yellow and a green sauce anyway. It's ok though since they are both good. I pretty much get the chicken, salad and fries every time but I'm planning on trying everything!

Stopped in for lunch. Prices are good. I order 1/4 chicken with rice and spicy beans. I thought it was ok nothing special. The two sauces that come with it I didn't care for. The creamy sauce taste like a spiced up salad dressing. Glad I tried it out but wouldn't go again.
Good bar food with good beer selection. My favorites are their wings and fried pickles. Also has some seafood options at fair prices.

Working in striking distance to Termini Brothers Bakery is dangerous- both to my wallet and my waistline.

I have suddenly realized at about 4pm on a Friday that I offered to bring dessert to dinner and Termini Brothers has immediately been my go to. The cheesecakes, Tiramisu, and Chocolate Cakes are all to die for.

However, my most recent experience with them has made them stand out even more- about a week before my wedding I realized I never ordered a groom's cake for the rehearsal dinner- it was on my to do list, but things like weddings have a way of sneaking up on you.

I ran down there and talked to an employee and they had me covered. For about $100- I got a red velvet cake with Phillies decorations on it which was supposed to serve 35-50 people. 

All the guests at the rehearsal dinner were raving about the cake - the amazing cream cheese frosting, how delicious the red velvet cake part was and how well they decorated it. In fact, I ended up eating it the next morning while getting ready- and it was STILL amazing. 

Definitely can't go wrong here!

I really enjoyed my Sunday brunch at Vineyards cafe. A friend and I met for coffee and crepes and I really enjoyed myself. I ordered the "American" crepe and added spinach, and a hot latte. Our food and coffees were ready within minutes, and everything was very tasty. The seating inside is a bit limited, but there were tables outside. I also really liked the complimentary water with lemon and lime slices - very refreshing. I will definitely return!

New location on Ina Rd. is excellent, just as good as Speedway.
Great Reuben, and fish and chips
All I have to say about this place: A 16 dollar pitcher. Enough said. I will never go here again. Too Greek for me, too!
Great place to watch NFL with a DC-area crowd in Southern AZ.
Amazing breakfast!! Crepes are great!!!  Coffee is tasty!!! The atmosphere is beautiful!!!

Since coming to this restaurant I have been back at least four times now. I have ordered their special which includes rice and beans with the beautiful fried egg on top. The steak is extemely well flavored and their green sauce is addictive. 
I have nothing but great things to say about their server Valerie as she is so pleasant and has treated me and my people really good. 
I can tell there is a lot of passion behind their good and business so I will drive out of my way to come eat. I wasn't sure when I sat down the first time but I'm so glad I did. 
Don't forget an espresso and a tres leches before you leave!
Yummy food and cool service. This place is located in the market place if downtown Philadelphia on Market place. There is too much to choose from but Becks Cajun Cafe gets my vote

What a great choice we made for breakfast. Kimber was so helpful and fun and had great recommendations.  The brioche pecan praline French toast that comes with a side of Cajun potatoes and choice of meat would have been enough for two! But we also ordered the Bourbon Street breakfast which is yummy red beans and rice with an egg on it with grilled corn bread--OMG.  So good. We felt like we made the best choice in Reading Market.

Tucked away in Reading Terminal Market - this place is a gem. I was skeptical at first, mainly because we are so far removed from Louisiana. If you want just a taste of the goods, you can walk by their booth and they will usually let you have a sample of their Gator Gumbo. We got their Fried Mac and Cheese Topped with Gator Gumbo. The Fried Mac and Cheese was perfectly fried and came in the shape of two fried balls, and cracking open the hushpuppy crust makes for a pretty Instagram worthy site. They also didn't skimp on the amount of meat that was topped over it. It was very flavorable, but I wished they had poured over more. It's a delicious dish, albeit a little on the smaller side.

I was going to give this a 5, because the food is THAT good - but I decided to give it a 4, because it takes a LONG time to get your meal. We did go during the lunch hour, but I felt that it should come out faster especially when you are trying to move people out. The last point is their container. The dish comes out in a little paper tray, which might not be the best form of delivery because it's hard to mop up the gumbo.

It's a solid contender in this foodie-paradise of Reading Terminal Market.

While we were walking around the touristed-out Reading Terminal Market, my wife needed to boost her blood sugar level.  We were standing in front of this Termini operation, so she asked the counter clerk for a biscotti and bottle of water.   The woman acted like we were idiots, rude-splaining that since biscotti is sold by the pound, there's no way she could sell just one.  So much for brotherly love, eh?

Amazing food! We had clams as an appetizer & both the fish and the shrimp tacos. All were very good, we would definitely order them all again. The salsa was incredible. I would've given 5 stars, but the service was VERY slow. It was worth it, but I would probably pick someplace else if I was fairly hungry.

I wonder how long that display muffuletta's been sitting there under that glass case? It still looks pristine and like it was made that same morning of the day I look at it. Maybe it IS made freshly every morning for display. Ah, the wonders of Reading Terminal Market.

Anyway, that glorious muffuletta was the one thing I wanted from Beck's... although the rest of the menu looks good, too, it'll have to wait until another RTM adventure. It was the first muffuletta I'd ever had, and it did not disappoint. OK, I had to smash it down a little to get it to fit inside my mouth... but for all that filling, it sure was worth it. Though the sandwich was packed with like three different types of cured meat, that salty, savory olive salad is what really shined for me, especially against the sharp provolone. And the soft, slightly crispy roll that it's served on... I just wanted to roll myself up in it and take a nap. Next time, I'll have to try some of their gator dishes.

When we get to Philly we always try to stop in. Hands down the best cannolis and coconut macaroons around. If you park at the garage across the street, they will validate parking if you spend more than 10 dollars which brings it down to 5 dollars if you are there less than an hour.

Wow!!!! Best Cannoli's ever. Attended a Subaru celebration event after Reading Terminal closed for the day. I had to finish my evening with a cannoli. Wow!!! What can I say but amazing!!! Perfect crunch and the filling was incredible. Cannot wait to have these again!! Service was the best!!!
Soooo yummy! I got the paleo bowl and now I crave it all the time! Service was good can't complain . Love the patio allows dogs
Terrible service. I walked in to pick up my order 15 minutes AFTER it was supposed to be ready and they were just putting my pizza in the oven as I walked in.
My new favourite spot to grab something delicious and have a drink! Great atmosphere and did I mention it was delicious!
The quality of the bread here has gone downhill since I wrote my original review. Plus, I have actually been to New Orleans now, and the po boy is not an authentic 5 star New Orleans po boy.

Food pretty solid. Got the fried catfish po boy and was very satisfied. Sandwich could've been a bit more spicy but good nonetheless! Portion size is very large. Would say some menu items seem pricey, but would go back to try the jambalaya
Great for solo dining! They have a dine in counter around the corner. Came here twice while visiting Philadelphia cause the food was that good. Waitstaff was helpful and the food was delicious.

I just got back from Lima, Peru on Thursday and lo and behold a friend of mine mentioned that there was a peruvian style restaurant in the Riverview/ Brandon area and that he had eaten there the night before so immediately I asked him if they had Lomo Saltado, he said he didnt know but the people there were very nice and that if they didnt have it they could probably fix it, so guess were I immediately headed, yes.... Cuenelli's. 
  I walked in and was greeted by a lady who took away from her phone conversation to say Hello and Welcome, as I looked over the menu I was delighted to see that they did in fact have Lomo Saltado but to be sure i asked the lady what she recommened and she said the Chicken was Outstanding! so I asked her if the Lomo was good and she kinda looked surprised that this big country gringo was asking about the Lomo.. hahaha, she said they did it very good there and she assured it would be delicious. SOLD! I waited about 5 mins all the while taking in the permeating scents from the grill and getting more and more anxious by the minute, Please lord let this be a good dish! 
 The lady brings it out and it looks and smells FANTASTIC, steaming, hot  and loaded with spices, (by the way for the YELPers like me who didnt know what Lomo Saltado was until last week it is a mix of Sirloin steak, Onions, Culantro, Spices, over white rice and french fries). I took my first bite and joy came over my body, I have found Great peruvian food within a short drive from the house. EXCELLENT!
  I eat every little morsel of the food that was on my plate including the little dish of AJI a mayo based sauce with really delicious flavors. The lady asked me how it was and I told her Outstanding, I continued to talk to her and the cook whom came out from the kitchen about Lima and my visit and the delicious food. I ended with telling them that I would be back very soon and that I would tell all my friends about the great food at there restaurant, well Yelpers here it is Please do your self a favor and go eat at this little taste of peruvian heaven!!

Tried the sushi rice bowl, which seemed a little more worth it than getting a tiny roll. The food was extremely fast, as it's a rainy day and less people were out and about eating lunch. The soy sauce mixture they give you to put on top was pretty good too.

Holy yum - stopped in on our way into town based on my uncle's recommendation. We just ordered apps: crab cakes, coconut curry mussels, crab stuffed mushrooms, bacon wrapped scallops and fried pickles. Each one was awesome and our server was super attentive. Everyone at table was happy. Definitely recommend.

We are South Americans and we are always looking for good Latin  food! 
This place is awesome!  We tried the bistec a lo pobre and Lomo Saltado.  The portions are decent size so make sure you come hungry. 
The only thing I wish they had in their menu is Chaufa.
Oh and they have Romeo Santos playing non stop (I don't mind )

After a recommendation from one of my Yelp friends I decided to give this place a try, for those of you who do not know the area it's right next to the Green Iguana.  This place makes some of the best chicken I have ever had.  The meat is tender and juicy while the outside is done with a crispy and well seasoned skin.

The fries and perfect as well and their seasoning on the fries are perfect and compliment the chicken nicely, also when you get a chicken meal if you get fries as a side they also throw in a small salad which is perfectly dressed (the onion in the salad is thinly sliced so the onion does not overpower when you eat).  I did also try their black beans which are little bland, but still does not detract me from going there again to try other items on the menu.

Also I would be wrong if I did not mention the service, the service is top notch, ultra-courteous, and attentive to your needs.  There is no reason with food and service like this for this place not to succeed.  If you do not at least try this place out then you are truly missing something good.

Excellent chicken, taste was fantastic with the meat falling off the bone. They know how to cook here. Pollo Tropical look out!
The cilantro rice was also tasty and plentiful.
The two sauces the green and yellow were flavorful and not spicy.  The salad with the house dressing was a perfect compliment. Lunch was as 11.00, well worth it.
This place is really chill. I have gone there a few times and liked how calm it was. I don't like it when places are loud or crowded but this place is a great in between. It's popular but not crowded

If you are a guy with a big and/or tall frame, this Casual Male is an excellent choice for casual, business or dress clothing. The store is very well kept, the selection includes everything from shoes to hats and everything between, and is easy to find whatever  is needed. Prices are right on target (especially with their specials, sales and 'frequent user club' offers), and the service is perfect: cheerful, helpful and no pressure. (Andrew is very helpful!)

Service - Outstanding. 
Food - Excellent flavor.

The hotel we stayed at did not serve fresh food. Thankfully, Trident was super accommodating and fixed up a couple pieces of salmon cooked to perfection. Delicious!

The main reason to eat at this restaurant would be if your sole requirement for a meal involves it being smothered with cheese. Otherwise, this town offers much tastier Mexican food, in much more pleasant environments.

I've now eaten at all 3 locations, most recently at this one, and found the experience pretty much the same. My husband loves the appetizer that comprises a dish of melted cheese, and, in my experience, this is the best thing on the menu. It's hot and flavorful and perfect in a tortilla or a chip, maybe with some salsa on top. Unless you're a fan of rubbery canned mushrooms, you might want to get plain cheese. 

Otherwise, most of the food is just cheesy and greasy without much to recommend it. The beans are completely without flavor and there's no a la carte menu. I wanted an enchilada, which came with a tamal. The enchilada was OK but nothing very exciting, just another pile of melted cheese. The tamal was almost as dry as eating a straight-up pile of corn meal, and the filling inside was about as thick as a piece of dental floss. Although the rice is molded into various shapes, presentation doesn't go much further. Your plate features something covered in cheese, a cylinder of rice, and a salad of lettuce and tomatoes, which looks all right but does not taste fresh.

When I asked my husband how his steak was, he said, "Covered in cheese." (He said this happily.)

This location is really run-down looking. The plates and bowls are new and modern looking, but the rest of the restaurant could use a facelift. The booth in which we were seated was patched with red duct tape and the stone wall was covered with crayon. The bathrooms were wrecked.

Found this place hidden behind the Circle K not too long ago.  Very happy I did.  I like this place because it is well hidden and hard to see so it's not very crowded when I go in to get some great food.  I usually get some breakfast burritos or a chimmy.  Everything has been real good.  The usual server is very friendly and I get my order right in a few minutes.  The salsa bar is satisfactory and my drink is plenty big.  It's fine with me if no one thinks they want to go here and eat - means I never have to wait and there's always an empty table.  Besides they seem to have a steady drive through business.  Keep up the good work!

Ordering takeout was a MISTAKE!  Portions were way off to what they usually serve when dining in.  It was like, "WHERE'S THE BEEF?!?"  The frustrating part is the fact they continue to jack up prices to compensate for the lack of business they are desperately needing to these days!  I speak as a person that used to give them from the 1st started eating at their restaurant, back in 92!

Seriously doubt I'll be back!
This was the BEST Mexican restaurant I've ever been to! My 82 year old mother-in-law said it was the best enchilada she'd ever had, and she's lived in the Southwest most of her life.

I love this place, the blackened chicken with the Cajun potato fries are the best. I only wish I had more time here to try some of the other stuff they have. Everything looks great. 
They have a small sit down area and the order to go area. Lots of people to help you and they are all very nice! It's one of my favorite places in this location known as the Reading Terminal as you have many things to choose from. I'm coming back!
Thanks for making good stuff to eat

Rib eye with  mashed potatoes and asparagus tips in hallindase sauce. The memory of a great meal stays with you long after the table's been cleared. Which is why they use only the freshest and finest ingredients, like USDA Prime steaks, fresh-squeezed juices and locally sourced produce.

Only the very best will do:
The people you want to attract to your next development - upscale, tasteful and loyal - all know what to expect from the Ruth's Chris Steak House experience. They look for there inviting atmosphere, award-winning wine list, USDA Prime steaks, homemade dishes and quality ingredients.

Quality ingredients, attention to detail and that special sizzle - it's what There passionate about.

If you are on the north side of TPA  (Tampa Airport) this place is definitely worth checking out 

Their chicken is excellent,  crisp and well seasoned skin, and the meat is still moist and flavorful.

Green sauce adds to the flavor of the chicken,  it's not there to mask a bland piece of meat. 

If this is a way they do it in Peru,  think I'd like to visit.

Service here is horrible. Placed an order, waited 15 minutes only to discover cashier didn't write up my ticket. When I questioned this she rudely treated me like I was wrong. Finally one of the line cooks asked me what was going on and he saw she didn't write up an order slip. He took over and apologized. That cashier has ruined a perfectly good establishment for me.

Ahoy Shipmates! This was our first visit to The Trident Grill. My wife had the Steakhouse Burger, my son had the Grilled Cheese, and I had the Mushroom Swiss Burger. OMG! Those were some of the best burgers ever! Great job Shipmate! Ask for your Veteran discount!

Being a cheese lover, nothing beats LaParilla Suiza and their queso with chorizo. Tacos are excellent, along with the bisteak and the charro beans. I love the traditional decor and the friendly service. Fried ice cream, great margaritas, never had a bad meal.
Who doesn't toast the bread on a club sandwich? How am I suppose to eat this? I waited an hour and a half for this and I live two blocks away.
I was surprised to see that they served a Paleo Bowl here! It was huge and delicious!  Would definitely come back if I am ever in Tucson again

This is one of my top restaurants to visit whenever I'm in Tucson. They never disappoint. The attention to customers is always above and beyond and the food is always overly satisfying. The menu is pretty extensive which I love. I've ordered different dishes on each visit and have always left satisfied to the core by each. This time around, I ordered the carne asada steak and enchilada plate (No. 45). The carne asada was a more-than-decent size for me and found it to be super flavorful, tender, and perfectly cooked. The enchiladas are good here, but I have to mention,  it's different from what I'm used to. Their red sauce has more of a tomato taste to it rather than the taste of spices and dried chilis which is fine with me. Just mentioning in case that may be a deal breaker for you. My BF ordered the mole enchilada dish which he orders on every visit. And, of course, he loved it. Thank you.

On a journey to find some great Philly gifts to take to friends who were kindly allowing me to stay at their house for 10 days during my vacation, I ventured out to...where else but Reading Terminal Market?! 

Prior to entering, I was really unsure what to buy. Now...I pride myself on being a pretty good gift-giver, and so I didn't want to disappoint. I had landed on food. But now my dilemma was..."Well...what foods?!" And being inside Reading Terminal Market without a plan was not one of my better and smarter moves. I did a round and landed on La Colombe coffee and some sweet treats from Philly brands. I stopped by Termini Bros Bakery who had a large La Colombe sign. I hadn't realized at the time that I was actually at Termini Bros and just bought the coffee. Had I realized it, I would have easily just bought some treats there. Oh well. 

The employee who helped me was very kind and even suggested other locations for some of the other La Colombe blends (they only carried Corsica). I let her know that while I prefer a different blend, it wasn't a big deal because it was a gift. The fact that she was willing to help me find the product that I really preferred says a lot. AND it was CHEAPER than where I get my coffee in my neighborhood! 

Anyways, I love Reading Terminal Market and I really appreciated the kindness of Termini Bros. I will absolutely go back! Love it!

I was in town for Family Weekend at U of A, the manager/owner was super cool for reserving me a table for a large party. They don't normally take reservations. A little customer service goes a long way. 
Make sure you try the Tucson Blonde, it's really good.
retired Navy SEAL Miller's bar is the best bar in town. Feels like a big family in there. Great food and East Coast vibe. Best place to watch Skins games!

I went here twice because it was that good!

I had the shrimp & crawfish étouffée, jambalaya, fried oysters, fried catfish, and Cajun fries.

They were all good but I would say that the catfish and étouffée was super tasty!

I recommend coming here and I'd love to come back again.

One of my favorite places to eat.
Some how the food is cooked slightly better here then Ruth's Chris else where.
But the service is not as great, still very good just not over the top like at King of Prussia.
Shrimp cocktail with remoulade sauce is an absolute must every time.
Besides that everything else is on point too.
Parking is hard but it is CC Philly what do u expect?
Just pay a couple bucks extra and valet.

This place is one of the few in the city that specializes in cuisine from NOLA. The employees are eager, armed, and ready for passerbys, who can potentially turn into customers with their samples. The Train Wreck po boy is their interpretation of a cheesesteak and it is seriously mouthwatering artery clogger on a french baguette. So much meat and cheese and onions! It's truly a stomach stuffer. It's also hands down the best thing I've tried there. The other po boys I've tried with the exception of a shrimp salad po boy, which they had as a limited time special, were just OK. I wasn't really wowed. I wish the pickles were a little thicker and just a tad more lettuce and tomato. The creole mayo may be the star of the sandwich, adding a much needed kick. 

The gator gumbo is alright, but can be a forgettable dish. I think it's because it's served on the milder side and needs some more oomph. The mac and cheese balls are a great idea, but I found the inside a bit on the dry side and the outside quite crunchy. The little sauce that comes with it is good and the best way to eat it is to drizzle it on the ball and not dip it, due to the tiny container size.

The beignets are great! It's a shame that they're served only on Wednesdays and Sundays. Can be a bit messy to eat, but that's half of the fun. The bread pudding to me lacks consistency.
