I always order it to go and I feel like sometimes the pieces I'm receiving are either pretty big or pretty small in comparison from a previous order. Great flavor, though. Because of that, I've been kind of turned off from ordering it altogether. I still think overall it's a good lunch option.
Stopped in for a bite to eat and watch the second half of the UofA basketball game last night. Buffalo Chicken Sliders were awesome. Beer was ice cold. Service was great. What more do you need?

I wish I can give this place 0/5 stars!

I went here tonight for a pharm dinner with my co-workers and we were in for a "treat"

The decor was like the dirty living room of a frat house.  The appetizers were ALL deep fried chinese-american foods (egg roll, crab rangoon, etc).  

The service by Joseph Poon himself was deplorable.  We have a large group of ~20 people, some of which are vegetarian and some of which eat seafood only but no beef/chicken.  When he found out we didn't give him advance notice of the number of people with vegetarian/seafood only diets, he literally had an panic attack in front of our party of 20 physicians and pharmaceutical reps.  He started yelling at our vegetarian colleagues and lectured us about how "if this was morimoto, you guys would be kicked out".  Those are his words VERBATIM!

This guys needs some serious Haldol and Ativan STAT!

When the non-vegetarian dishes came out, he again proceeded to ridicule our vegetarian friends by saying "finally we have some NORMAL people".  

The food was not traditional chinese at all, but Americanized just like the chinese takeout food you can get from any neighborhood restaurant.  

His waiters and waitresses were very nice and tried to apologize for their boss, but Mr Poon has some seriously ego issues (he has his picture put on the back of every seat in the "restaurant).  His histrionic temper is uncalled for.  

I would not recommend anyone to goto this so called restaurant.  He may be able to get away with it because the chef only caters to private events, but if he had a mainstream restaurant, the public will know the nasty temperament of this guy.


We were astonished that this guy could be literally yelling at the top of his lungs in order to criticize our vegetarian friends in front of the ~20 person group.

Do yourself a favor and goto one of the many other fine establishes in Chinatown, run away from this self-proclaimed "chef best in the world"

This small, unassuming booth in the RTM is a culinary godsend. You laugh now, but once you try their fried mac-and-cheese balls, you'll be a convert too.

I don't want to say too much and spoil this otherworldly experience, but in a summary: I can't vouch for the other food because I didn't have any, but the mac-and-cheese balls are glorious. Service is very, very friendly. The atmosphere is homey. You'll come in a skeptic, and come out a believer. 

Have a wonderful day.

nice enough spot. great to have a korean spa in these parts. men's area is small, so be advised when the cruisey types are around to keep watch. 
also, know that the food services are down on Tuesdays. I've been told from friends in the area that their food is great, but I unfortunately did not get to try it.

I love this place!  Kinda off the beaten path on the eastern end of rapidly gentrifying Francisville, it is a beautiful space with the best crepes in town, period.  The Norwegian is my fave - goat cheese, lox, avocado, in perfectly done buckwheat crele. And La Colombe coffee.

Beck's Cajun Cafe has become my favorite spot in all of Reading Terminal. I've grown to like Beck's even more than DiNic's famous roast pork sandwich. Don't get me wrong DiNic's is still on my favorite list, just Beck's has been my top goto spot whenever I'm in Philly.

The gator gumbo in my opinion is always a must. Don't think too much about the gator. It's more like a pork sausage if anything since it does contain pork. But the gumbo itself is savory and full of robust flavors mixed with plain rice or jambalaya, it's a delicious combination.

I ordered just a gator sausage on a stick. It seemed pretty good because my dad hogged it! Guy didn't even share one piece. He kept dunking the sausage into their mustard and finished it within seconds so it must be good.

The train wreck po'boy was a first for me. Prior to this visit, we've only come to Beck's for their gator gumbo and fried Mac and cheese. I wanted something different this time so I gave the po'boy a shot and it did not disappoint. The hoagie for one was probably a better hoagie than most sandwiches spots I've been to in Philly. The taste and juiciness of the meat and ingredients inside was like an explosive orgasm in your mouth. It's not a sandwich that you need to rush and eat before it gets cold. Take your time with this one because it likes it slow. Comparing this sandwich to DiNic's, you have to rush to eat the roast pork sandwich at DiNic's because that sandwich taste like crap when it gets cold and dried up.

Verdict - It's probably no secret to folks who goto Reading Terminal regularly. Beck's has to be one of the best spots to eat in this place. The Cajun flavors here are just spot on and reminds you of New Orleans. Whether you been there or not, this is a taste of New Orleans and a must try for those who like like Cajun spices.
I really like Trident. I just stopped in a few years ago for a beer and it slowly became my favorite happy hour spot. Great burgers and beer. Good people.

Dined here late on 04/06/18.

My boyfriend and I walked in at 9pm on a Friday night, shocked to find the place empty for it being right next to a college campus. We were promptly seated and greeted by a server. 

I had a mango margarita to drink which was absolutely amazing and I strongly recommend everyone try! It was by far my favorite drink in Tucson! We ordered the crab stuffed mushrooms and bacon wrapped scallops. Both were good but they came out with our meal. My boyfriend did not specify that we wanted them as appetizers so I don't blame the server but I wish she would have clarified.

For entrees I had the salmon, which was delicious and a decent portion for the price. My boyfriend had the paleo bowl which he also enjoyed.

The ambiance was nice and the service was decent. All around 4 stars, and I would visit again. Bars aren't really my scene but this bar definitely had a more upscale food selection than most!

I used to LOVE coming here and even introduced co worker when I lived, worked and went to HCC. I even got close to the owners daughter(such an amazing person to!) My daughters loved coming here. I lived now in Brandon and the last three times I have come the services has went down. The quality and quantity has reduced from when I used to order here as well. The fact that I spent nearly sixty dollars of food and my seven year old was thirsty and was going to buy three cans of soda to say, that I had to spend seven dollars on top of what I had was insane. The owner really said they have to follow policy which is seven dollars is a joke considering they did a separate charge of 5.99 with taxes of .51 cents which totaled 6.50. Hmmm yes, YOU follow policy,NOT!!!! I have seen been coming here since it opened and for my the fact that they DO NOT appreciate their customers. It's sad because it's ALL ABOUT MONEY.

Customer service was horrible. My order was incorrect and their worker cursed at me and tried to convince me that the order was correct. I specifically ordered no cheese on my order and it was loaded with cheese. My coworker is highly allergic to cheese. After cursing at me when I called she told me she would never correct our order again. Never will order here again!

We finally went to Trident Grill IV ... My husband and I are Newport News / Hampton Va natives and to say we miss "our" Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Ocean seafood prepared the southeast way is an understatement! 

Typical sports bar atmosphere - multiple large screen TV's lots of people talking .... BUT the food as promised was not your typical sports bar fare. 

We ate light so we could try a variety of choices. We had seafood of course and gumbo. Everything was excellent. Scallops are one of my husband's favorite dishes. He savored each bite. They were perfectly prepared as were my Shrimp.... 

We will definitely become regulars and are anxious to return and eat our way through the menu. 

My ASU alumni (Old Pueblo Chapter) recently had game day at Trident IV and I regret not attending  It's not easy being a SunDevil in Wildcat Country

Let's start off by saying I am a die hard Redskins fan!  So some of you Giants, Cowboys, and Eagles fans might feel intimidated....but that makes sense!  Watching the games here is fun no matter what team you like.  But to hear the "Hail to the Redskins" playing after ever score just makes it a lot better!  The people that come to Trident are pretty nice cool people that love football.  The waitresses and bartenders are also really nice and always on top of getting you food and drinks quickly.
I am not used to going to bar at 10AM to watch football since most games start at 1PM on the East Coast.  But Trident has a nice breakfast till 11AM and then the normal bar/lunch menu.  The food was really good, and they are huge portions!  We had a half order of nachos and I needed a half of that order!
They have a raffle at half time where they give out Redskins gear which was a lot of fun.  Everyone gets one free ticket and you can buy more.  I got a nice Koozie!  So now I have a permanent Sunday spot.  A little bit of DC in AZ!

The best cannoli I've ever had was on a vacation in Greece. Crispy and crunchy outer shell, creamy fresh filling with just the right amount of sweetness. The cannoli here stirs my memory and let's me relive the joy of biting into deliciousness. Definitely worth a try.

Super friendly staff & great pastries. I bought a chocolate chip ricotta filled cannoli & a bag of freshly ground coffee. They gave me a sample of the coffee with a biscotti to try. The coffee had no sugar or milk & it was still delicious. I would highly recommend visiting if you are ever in Philly!
Had the taco plate with salmon, cod and pork. Great food and excellent service. Highly recommend and will be coming back! Our server Kellynn was very attentive and mode the experience enjoyable.

I've been to Beck's several times and every one was a good experience. The staff is super friendly and they offer samples before you order! The gumbos are really savory and have a good consistency. The friend Mac & cheese wasn't the flavor I was expecting but they were still pretty tasty. Overall, the food and service was up to par, but also keep in mind it's not the south. With this restaurant being in the middle of Reading Terminal, it is very easy to miss. Additionally, there is very limited seating so go at an unpopular time if you want to sit!
Very chill place. Love the chicken tenders, buffalo chicken sandwich, skewers and hummus plate to begin with. Lots of tvs for sports games, great crowds and servers. Nice spot to hang out

Read on Yelp about these amazing crepes, and they did not disappoint!  We sampled the Pesto and many savory ones including Strudel and Nutella.  All were made fresh to order and were fantastic.  Service was super friendly and quick. Seating is on short supply so we took them to go. We'll be back again and will try more flavors.

I've always had solid Peruvian food here. Lomo saltado is on point. Rotisserie chicken has always been flavorful and juicy. There are better Peruvian places around town but I've never had a bad experience at Cuenelli's.

We really like good ceviche and other Peruvian dishes, but skipped the ceviche here because not available in appetizer size and made with tilapia.....just not willing to have another dose of that ubiquitious farm critter.  Opted for the family dinner, featuring a complete roasted/grilled chicken plus 3 sides and sauces.  Their chicken rivals Colombia Pequena and Antoquena.   Salad came with a fine cilantro-flavored house dressing that hit the spot...and we do not like heavy cilantro. Maduros were good and spicy pinto beans very nicely seasoned.  Was able to get a bottle of chicha, unusual to find purple corn drink......sweet and vaguely fruity.    No beer or wine, which is a pity with this kind of food.
As others noted, the dining room has a fast-food feel and table-service service was fast for us on a slow Friday night.   Value was excellent and next time I will try the sampler platter.

i haven't been to the main termini bakery- only the one in reading terminal market. i've gotta say, they were a lifesaver the first time i went, and I came all the way back a few months later just for a cannoli. 

i was in the area for a conference at the convention center and it was the few days before a friend's baby shower. among other things, i was in charge of the cake. luckily, the staff at termini accommodated my last-minute order and whipped up a beautiful and super delicious cake with less than 24-hr notice. the cake was perfectly moist, with a great cake-to-filling ratio. the buttercream wasn't overly sweet. it really was perfect. the decorations were adorable, and the price was very reasonable.

and the cannoli. as if it's not in a ton of the other reviews: the cannoli is amazingggg. the filling is the perfect creamy, ricotta-y, not grainy, not too sweet, not too thick kind, which is hard to find. the ratio of chocolate chips is just right. skip the powdered sugar. even the cannoli shell, which i usually don't eat, is a great texture and crumbles just right with every bite- i ate the whole thing. no, i don't regret it (i'll just have to remember that at the gym later)... yes, i came all the way back to philly for one (just one, i promise. the rest were for my uh, family. yeah.)

one thing, though, on the cannolis: there's no way one cannoli should cost $4. just sayin.

Trainwreck! My wife and I decided to to have a nice lunch for Easter. We had a coupon for this place, so decided to give it a try. The only thing that went right was we got our beers fairly quick. We asked for another minute or two to look at the menu. The waiter disappeared for about 10 -15 minutes. The manager actually brought over the chips and salsa in the mean time. Once we did get to order, it took about another 30 minutes or so to get the food. I ordered fish tacos, and my wife ordered some sort of pork loin dish. Both dishes were missing key ingredients,(sauces, sides). When I pointed it out to the waiter, he tried to BS me that is what the menu states how it is prepared. My wife went and got a menu just so we could confirm. My fish tacos were bland, but my wife's dish was horrible. It basically was a tortilla folded over a dry pork pattie with cheese on top. The fact that both dishes were missing sauces, and sides to cover it up made it even worse. My wife called the manager over, and we expressed our dissatisfaction with the whole experience. He apologized several times, and took the remaining food away. The waiter then brought the tab, and they still charged us for the food anyway! The only relief was that we had a coupon, but they were not aware of that until the end. That still would not be an excuse for the terrible food, and service we got. We will never set foot in that place again!
Peruvian food at its finest, this place takes me back to Machu Picchu Peru. Order the cilantro rice and black beans.
This bar never gets old.  The food is great as usually and my server, Baliz, was awesome!

Our go-to Peruvian polla a la brasa. It took us some time before finding this place and the food and laid back atmosphere keeps us coming back. Good but my bar is set high from our favorite DC haunt that had smoke billowing out of the brasa always in full tilt pumping out hot, juicy pollo. 

What we like. Well the family enjoys the chicken dinner with lots of sides. The fries are good especially with the yellow sauce. The fried yuca is always a favorite. A bowl of black beans. Cilantro rice can be awesome but tonight was ok (not that hot and a bit dry). Chicken is good but sometimes the white meat gets dry. And they seem to be getting smaller. So this starts my few pet peeves...pollo a la brasa to me is hot and juicy chicken. And the for the sauces...charging 50 cents each is steep. I'd rather it be included in the price. 

Sorry but we haven't tried the other dishes but the bistec with egg sounds good. 

Service is attentive and always pleasant. We usually get the churros. Good but not knock your socks off. 

In summary, it is always a good meal despite the little things.

I have mixed feelings about this place. From its menu they have the potential to be great, but they seem to lose in the category of service in the Dine-in aspect. 

I was recommended to come here for their "Knockout Sauce" which you can get on an order of wings. 

It took no time to be seated. The tables came prepped with menus and the server acknowledged us immediately. About 10 minutes passed and the server continued to acknowledge we were there but didn't come over to at least get a drink order while she tended to other customers. There was a larger party of Philadelphia's finest (Police) but that's still no excuse, every customer is just as important. As the time passed I was trying to figure out if the dinning room was as cold as it seemed or if I was just that frozen from being outside. The feeling of bitter cold wasn't just in my mind, the dinning room truly had a feeling of frozenness. Not sure if they knew about the heating problem or not and I didn't bring it up either, which would have given clarity to the situation. At this point, service was my main concern. 

Once she gave them their bill she finally came over to take our drink order. We noticed the last party ordered soup, but when we read the menu to look for a list of soups, there was no indication of its existence. Also while looking for "Knockout Sauce", it wasn't listed either. She came back with our drinks and asked if we were ready to order and I asked my questions regarding soup, the sauce for the wings....etc. The server had to go ask someone if the "Knockout Sauce" was a thing. She returned and told us it was on the new menu which is why she didn't have a clue about it. 

Where do my issues lie? The sampler platter I ordered came with marinara sauce(as indicated on the menu) yet when it arrived it came with no dipping sauces; The wings came out with no blue cheese dipping sauces either; The soup was lukewarm but great flavor; The entire dining room was as cold as the exterior; There were two menus and we were never given the updated one, and why in the world did it take 20 minutes to order drinks let alone food when the dinning room wasn't busy? 

My biggest issue was the bill. The prices listed on the menu didn't reflect that of the check. We were charged a dollar more for wings, fifty cents more for the sampler platter and the soup was more than she verbally informed us it would be. Why wouldn't they update the dining room menus and expect customers to pay a different price than reflected? That pisses me off. By the way, the server told me we were her last table as she was sweeping underneath and around us. 

The saving grace in this all were the wings. The sauces had great flavor and the size of the wings were perfect. An order of 10 Wings is satisfactory for one person, but 20 would be too much. They have tons of meat on them. Oh and they were the hottest (temperature related) thing that hit the table. 

So in order for this business to receive more satisfactory reviews from myself and possibly other clients, THEY NEED TO UPDATE THEIR MENUS or charge customers according to the menu they originally gave out. If the dish comes with other items listed then again, they should honor what is on the menu. I'm not sure if the server wasn't familiar with the new menu or if the ball was just dropped in general but it's ethically incorrect to inform customers of one thing and then turn around to do another.

I see a lot of mixed reviews here, but I just had a great meal here this week.  It wasn't our first choice but it had an open table reservation available.  I had never been there and was looking to try it.  It was late so we skipped appetizers and got filet mignon, creamed spinach (yum!) and shoestring fries.  I love how the steak comes out sizzling.  That was why I really want to try Ruth's Chris and I wasn't disappointed.  You have to get the spinach.  Service was excellent also.

Great food, very well-made drinks.  I wish I had gotten the name of the girl behind the bar...long, dark hair....super great bartender!  Friendly, personable, and attentive. So many bartenders will walk right past you four or five times and never even look at you or check your drink level...not this girl.  Always checkin' on her customers but still keeping busy pumping out drinks.  She's a real pro!  Great place!!

We had so much fun today! We went with several families with little ones from 15 months to 2 years went for the afternoon and had a blast. The playground was crowded with kids (many different ages) so we had to stay close to our daughter as she ran around but in general it went really well. The beers were tasty and we liked the food a lot. The pizza, soft pretzel and wings were great. We'll be back! Love what you did with the space!

Good place for a beer or inexpensive lunch or maybe a wildcat game. It's bar food. Cool that is a Navy and SEAL themed and your supporting a vet. If your looking for a bar is a good option. 

Burgers used to be awesome but then they were hit and miss so I have since given up on them. I don't like wasting my cheat meals. So I usually get the chicken skewers app as a meal for my healthy choice. 

I do feel the food has been inconsistent, seems like product gets changed a lot like different buns, fries. But the service is always good, great servers. One of the bartenders used to pour a great guiness.

If you want to try the best rotisserie chicken in Tampa, this is the place to go. The sauces that come with the fries are amazing. The green one, the salsa huacatay is incredibly good if you are into mildly spicy sauces. If you don't like spicy food, then you will enjoy the yellow one. The green rice is a great side, and a must have if you are ordering the chicken. The other Peruvian plates range between "ok" and "good". The chicken is the star.
In Philly for conference and hotel is right across The reading Market. Tried this little spot 2 times now and it packs a punch! will definitely come back over and over again!

Yes!! So good! Cuenellis is near my work and it's such a great place to get lunch. I always get their 1/4 chicken with two sides. They have other items on the menu but not a whole lot. I wouldn't come here if I was craving a Peruvian food because of that- but if you're looking for rotisserie chicken this is IT. Service can be really hit or miss depending how busy they get. During a rush you may wait a while to flag down a server.

La Parilla Suiza specializes in Mexico City cuisine (read: cheeeeeeeeeeeeeese). It used to have the greatest happy hour ever: half-price appetizers and buy one, get one free margaritas.

With the expiration of that deal, it has become just another restaurant. Following my dad's tried & true method of evaluating Mexican restaurants, I will comment on the following, in descending order of importance: margaritas, chips & salsa, and food. 

1. The margaritas are good and will succeed in getting you soused; you can order them by the pitcher to insure this. Unfortunately, though, they are relatively costly.
2. The chips & salsa are some of the best in the area, but I am somewhat biased because I am a sucker for the 3-sauce presentation: a green chile sauce, a guac-y dip, and some spicy, fresh pico de gallo. Oh, pico, you slay me. 
3. The food is decent, but nothing is particularly outstanding except the broiled-cheese appetizer, oh sweet clogging arteries. It is definitely NOT worth the cost: it is simply a violation of the natural order of things for two people to spend nearly $40 for Mexican in Tucson. 

The food and atmosphere are better at this branch than at the other Tucson locations. Really I would only deem this 2.5 stars, though.
Love happy hour at Trident. Great service. Our favorite is the chicken skewers with peanut sauce!

Love this place since I used to go to their Lenola, NJ location as a kid growing up.  The idea is that you buy a raw pizza from them, bring it home, and bake it in your own oven.

The pizzas are always made of the freshest ingredients and they really have everything--gluten-free, white, or whole wheat crusts and a great assortment of the freshest ingredients.  Plus you can add your own little flourishes as you see fit.  Like scrambled eggs and ketchup on your pizza?  No problem, and no strange glances!  Buy one of theirs and add your own toppings.  Like to add your own blend of spices?  Easy to do at home.  The pies always come out great and much less greasy than you get from an overworked restaurant pizza oven.  And unlike delivery, you always know that you'll get teh pizza hot from the oven.

We also love their other bake-at-home specialties like Stromboli and cookies!

We  were at Reading Terminal Market when we chanced upon Termini Bros Bakery.  We bought a pound of Anise Biscotti and Cherry Walnut Biscottis to bring home to enjoy.

We enjoyed the Biscottis 4 days later.  The Anise Biscottis were excellent with my morning coffee.  Strong Anise aroma.

The Cherry Walnut Biscottis were sweet with the Walnuts playing second fiddle.

Both were perfect with the BJs drip Coffee  I prepare at home.

Service at the Reading Terminal Market was fast, friendly and efficient.

This is a really nice place for sushi and poke bowls. It's inside Franklin's Table (food court), which is quite new and modern. The staff are quite friendly and helpful, and you don't have to wait too long for the food. However, the main downside of this place is definitely the price of their sushi, which is comparatively quite expensive. However, their ingredients seem fresh, and the flavors are really nice.

Walking into Reading Terminal Market, it can be very overwhelming to decide what you want to eat. After doing some laps this place caught my eye! The menu looked super appetizing and had some awesome choices. I was a little sad because I wanted to order one of the breakfast options but they stop serving breakfast at 11. Definitely would come earlier to try those though. I was looking at the Trainwreck and it won me over when the girl behind the counter had told me that it won awards for the last 2 years in a row. Our food came out really quick and was steaming hot. The sandwich was SO good. The meat was perfectly chopped and the sauce that was on it made my mouth water. 10/10 would order again. My sister ordered the turkey po' boy and it seemed a little plain tasting. The staff all seemed really nice here and the girl who helped us was so sweet and talkative. Stop by this place to satisfy your Cajun cravings!

Natural juices are horrible that I can't give any respect. 
The food and the service it's amazing. The service is what's really awesome here. The food ain't bad for the price. Would go back.

We have recently added this place to our rotation of places to eat.  The kitchen is open until midnight, and since my husband works until late and we live close by, this is a good place for us. 

The first time we went, we got the scallop appetizer, and we both thought that it was very overpriced.  They were tiny scallops, and the blue cheese on them was crazy overwhelming.  We were both of the opinion that maybe we just didn't understand what kind of place it was and tried to get too fancy with it.

The feel of the place is great!  It feels like one of the bars we would go to on the East coast.  Very nautical, but not in a cheesy way.  They got the vibe down really well!

The next time, I had the T-Town burger with a boca patty, and hubs got the Voodoo burger.  Both were really yummy!  My burger had avocado and this tasty spicy sauce.  I was a fan!  It's actually become my go-to order here (all three times that I've been there).

The service has a big range.  It can go from really great to really rude.  We were in this most recent time and when we sat down, our server made a big show about looking at her watch before offering us menus, nevermind that we were there an hour and a half before the kitchen closed.  She only gave us one menu and wasn't shy about her disdain at having another table.  Other times, though, our servers were fun and helpful and nice and made us feel really welcomed.

I'm perfectly willing to say that I have given it three stars because nothing I have had is really exceptional, and that perhaps I need to branch out more to to find what is spectacular about this place.  I'm very willing to rewrite this review when I find something amazing here.  As for now, it's A-OK, and a good place to grab a late night bite and a beer (which is really well priced).

Trident shows the UFC fights and all the UofA games and doesn't charge a cover! !!!!!! It's liked I died sms went to competition heaven!!! The service and food also is excellent!  It's Gonna be a crazy night! !!!

Thought about coming here everytime I passes by the joint and finally decided to give it a try. I ordered the Muffalata and the Cajun French Fries to go. The host/cashier was helpful. She suggested to only get the 1/4 of the Muffalata which was a great decision after seeing the size of it. Service was fast and while walking home the wafting smell of the Cajun spiced fries got my mouth watering. Got home and unwrapped my grub. The Muffalata was nothing to rave about. It did taste ok but more like a extremely large olive loaf sandwhich and the fries... Not really fries at all. They were quartered red skinned potatoes deep fried and topped with some fried peppers, onions and a single slice of jalepano. My belly was left full but oh so disappointed. I should have gotten one of the Po-Boys or the Gumbo. Maybe next time.

HOW did I ever miss THIS place??? Superbowl today! Many screens, fantastic HEALTHY-ish food, great service, great atmosphere, clean, friendly, relaxing & alot of fun. HIGHLY RECOMMEND. Will be going back for sure!!!

Terrific cajun food. I had the jambalaya and it was finger licking good. They give you the devils dust, which is their spice mix that can be sprinkled on your food and this was DA Bomb. 

Wife had the shrimp poboy and it was yummy. I took the muffuletta to go and for $5.75, the muffuletta is so huge that you can have it for 2 medium meals.

Ohh and they have the best cajun fries ever ......

Coffee is delicious! I ordered a pesto sandwich and it was very tasty, actually delicious. Bread was fresh and the other ingredients very good as well. They have a very cozy sitting area underground and very relaxing ambience. Place is very clean. And the girls are lovely. I am so glad I found it!

Really tasty Cajun food.

Had the chicken and shrimp gumbo over jambalaya, which was delicious!  The gumbo base had great flavor, the kind that comes only from making it with care from a good recipe.  It was packed with lots of chicken, shrimp and andouille sausage, and was the perfect portion size - filling and satisfying without making you grossly overfull (so you'll still have room for that donut at Beiler's afterward).  

Protip:  you can order the rice-based jamabalaya on its own, with no gumbo on top, but that looked like it might be a little dry.  Getting it topped off with the delicious, soupy gumbo was definitely the way to go, and worth the few extra dollars.  

If you're here off-peak or just get lucky, they do have seating at the counter.  

As an aside: why is Cajun food so rare outside of Louisiana?  It's a popular cuisine, and yet most cities seem to have hundreds of Chinese / Italian / Mexican restaurants for every Cajun place.  Even sushi is more common.  Someone needs to remedy this, and pronto . . .

We came here for my moms birthday party of 7. 
The service was kind of slow in my opinion and it wasn't even that busy, a lot of the staff appeared to be jist standing around cracking jokes. The food came out fairly quick after our order was finally taken..
The food itself was great, if you don't like cheese then don't go here. They love their cheese here! Every thing has a ton of cheese on it. I personally love me some cheese so I liked this place haha. 
Still not normal mexican food I'm used to but it will do.
The food is too grease and oily! Also the service was not very good! The waitress didn't alow me to sit on the counter to eat my food! Very disappointing!

I have traveled past Trident Grill many times, and finally visited when some friends suggested we go there. The inside interior was not as I expected but was really cool! The food was good and the service was friendly. There were TV's throughout the establishment and it was kind of loud. Sometimes it was hard to hear what my friends were saying across the table. 

You can tell Trident Grill is a happening spot and that there are many regulars that go there.

Unfortunately this was the worst meal I have had in a long time. I ordered shrimp enchiladas. It was clear that the enchiladas simply contained overboiled shrimp with the same pico de Gallo mix they had served us as an appetizer. Only the tomatoes in the shrimp pico tasted the way tomatoes taste when they have been diced and then left to sit out for hours or a day. The sauce was flavorless. I ate a little and couldn't finish it, took a to-go box to be polite (should have said something but was with a group). The smell of the enchilada on the table as we waited for our bill made me nauseous. AND to top it all off, the server took 30 minutes (!!) between the time we asked for the check and finally got to sign a credit card slip. La Parilla used to be the place to go for Mexico City style food in town, but unfortunately not anymore.

Amazing place!!! Cozy atmosphere!!!
Such a friendly stuff!!! Sooo delicious food and COFFEE
Pretty good New Orleans food in the Reading Terminal Market

This is inside the market so it is verrrryy busy and the market overall is chaotic. I bought the train wreck and Cajun fries. The train wreck is a combination of a cheesesteak, sausage, peppers, and cheese. It was really yummy and savory. I could only eat half. I would share it next time. The Cajun fries weren't that great. They didn't have much flavor and they could have been crispier.  The price wasn't bad at all. It took about 10 minutes for them to cook it. After I ate it, I felt heavy and immediately wanted a nap. It was worth it
Best rotisserie chicken ever!  Great service and excellent food.  I especially enjoyed the sauce options which they make from scratch.

Usually good idea to make a reservation. Also, bring a light sweater....the a/c works overtime!
Sushi Tsu has been my all time FAVE restaurant in New Tampa, but my last trip there...???? What happened?? They really dropped the ball!! My daughters dinner was missing half the food that came with it and we had to wait for them to cook it.. Service was a dodgy as  well.  Certainly not the standard we've come to expect there.I'd like to chalk this experience up to them just having an off day. Hopefully things will be as good as they've always been in the past when we return again.

Not good place to eat New Orleans food. Ordered the fried oyster po boy. For $13.49 for four oysters is horrible it was more lettuce and bread than oysters. Sad experience I will never go back to. To the owner I paid with a card very poor quality of food.
The go to place for cannoli. The fact that they fill them fresh makes a huge difference & the quality is unbeatable. I now live in NC and wish they would open a location in the south!

Wow so so so yummy. Def an expensive lunch will go for a casual din instead next time but honestly so worth the money. Wow I am so impressed by how yummy that was and I feel extremely full afterwards!!!

A bit out of my usual lunch price range, but I shared this delicious sushi sampler with a friend and everything was delicious. Great option for sushi west of the schuylkill - of which there are sadly not many! Double knot is one of my absolute favorites in Philly so it's nice to have access to their food without the challenge of finding a table at DK...
Favorite Place for Peruvian Chicken. The sauces and the salad keep me coming back.  Love the green sauce on everything.  Never have a bad experience here.

I'm really glad I found this place!!! The place is awesome! I enjoy everything about this place! I will definitely be back!! Its just a regular Wendy's. No frills. No extras. Been here for years. Not bad.

This is the second Ruth's Chris that i have visited, the other being in San Diego. This experience was FAR different. My experience in California was AMAZING, hands down the best steak i had ever eaten. My experience in Philadelphia was the complete opposite. I felt like i was being served a cheap steak burnt to a crisp by some amateur chef. I did not perceive the value of my experience given how expensive it costs to eat at the Philadelphia location. I will never go back here again.

OK jambalaya, with chicken, andouille and shrimp.  A couple more pieces of shrimp and andouille would have been appreciated, too much damn rice.  Anyhow, you can also order po` boys, gumbo, mac n` cheese and some other items here, where the focus is on "cajun style" grub.  If you are hungry and don`t eat this stuff too often, give it a shot.  But, nothing to make a special trip for.

This coffee shop makes me so happy to have moved to the neighborhood. The staff are always very friendly, the crepes are out of this world (salmon, goat cheese, and avocado), and coffee is always tasty. The atmosphere is warm and welcoming. The perfect spot for lunch or a coffee date.

Obviously liquor is watered down!
 First drink was shot of whiskey. It was so weak.....it was a straight shot but clearly diluted!! A friend at table had a mixed drink and it too was weak beyond belief. I told the waitress that these were obviously watered down. She told me she watched the bar make them and I informed her that the bottles are probably watered down.  Not wanting to pay for watered down liquor I ordered a diet coke....I am not posting for dilute alcohol. My diet Coke arrives.....it is not diet Coke!  It is diet RC.  You might be thinking "no big deal" but diet RC uses sucralose as its sweetener which makes me ill.  The waitress should have told me they were serving RC products when I asked for a diet Coke. 
The food is at best a C-, it is hard to screw up nachos.
If you want diluted liquor, sucralose, and food that is less than memorable, this is your place. 
Oh one more thing, I don't think they have a back entrance or a loading area as they were hauling tables and chairs through the bar area out front to someones truck.  yeah that was irritating.
Got the Train wreck po boy. Simply Outstanding!  Very flavorful. Would definitely come back every time I'm in philly.  Just a fabulous sandwich place

Best grilled salmon and crab cakes.  Who knew??? In Tucson??  Excellent seafood!!! Stop by, open late and great beer selection. Even Kilkenny on draft. I'm impressed.  The clam chowder was amazing, too.  I will definitely stop to eat here every time when I am back in Tucson.

I've eaten at this specific location at least four times and have never been disappointed. Steaks have always been spot on, and the sides are always plentiful and delicious. Service has always been impeccable and the check comes in lower then Morton's for the same quality steaks.

I never would have thought of having gator gumbo, but it's delicious.  They let you sample their pre-prepared hot foods too, which ends up confusing me even more because I end up wanting everything.  The staff are so nice and helpful.  I love trying new things, and they are more than happy to let you have a small sample!

Delicious food! Went here with my mom to grab lunch and the food was excellent. The highlight actually was the hush puppies, which featured shrimp, jalapenos and corn. They were so addictive. 

I also enjoyed their blackened chicken Alfredo, although it didn't come out piping hot (I believe they serve it pre-cooked from a pan, but at least it came out in a timely manner). It was was warm enough to still be good.

The beignets were OK, nothing remarkable. My mom commented that they did not compare to those she had in New Orleans, as they were not as 'light'. I'm not surprised by that, so that wasn't a big deal to me. I do wish the dough was a bit sweeter, but there was plenty of powdered sugar to give it some balance.

We sat down at their counter space where were were served. The waitress was great. A bit odd that they don't offer glasses of water there, but they do have bottled water if you want to pay for it.

Look forward to visiting again and trying some of their other options!

Giddyup! Everything here looked amazing but the gals said they were famous for their cannoli, so I thought I'd give it a shot. I asked for one of those but was hoping it might have some chocolate or something on it, which it didn't, but I was not disappointed. It was pretty freaking amazing though and I'd definitely go back!

This is a non-review. I was interested to try many items on the menu here, and arrived around 715. They were busy, but not full. I waited about 15 minutes as my server passed by me several times, but never stopped to take my order. I decided it was not worth waiting any longer.  I could not have made it more obvious that I was ready to order.

OK, so I found this place on yelp and boy am I glad I tried it out!  Yummmmmyyyy!  I got my food to go and they were quick and efficient.  The service was great!  Very friendly and on point with the recommendations.  The chicken was seasoned well and very tender and not dry.  The cilantro rice was mild and the spicy beans had just enough kick and good flavor.  The two sauces--yellow and green--were both awesome compliments to my food.  The yellow sauce is my fave and I felt like I could just drink it!  I also got an order of plantains and let me tell you that they were well worth it.

I encourage anyone to go and try it out.  The only reason for four stars versus five is that I wanted an empanada after I ordered and couldn't pay by card because of the price (you have to charge a minimum of $8 to use your card and that was frustrating), so I didn't get one.  However, I will be back!

If flying from PHL to BOS, JetBlue is your best choice, especially over AA.
JetBlue's  staff is friendly,  smile, makes eye contact, helps customers with disabilities and their planes are much more comfortable- more padding, seats seem wider and the aisles definitely wider. Also each seat has its own entertainment screen and even better snacks.
I only wish JetBlue flew to more cities in the Northeast.

Wow! Beck's has one of the best gumbos I have ever had! Seriously, who knew that this small counter service spot in Philadelphia would be better then some of the places I've eaten at in New Orleans?!?!?! 

Over the summer we had a quick weekend trip to Philly. In my planning I found Reading Terminal Market and planned on having lunch there. We're from New England so we are used to food halls like Quincy Market in Boston, well Reading Terminal is like Quincy Market on steroids! There are a lot of options, but I had read about the Trainwreck sandwich at Beck's so we knew we wanted to stop by there. We walked by when we were checking all the different stands out and a girl behind the counter offered us a sample of the gumbo, the sealed the deal, we knew we were  going to eat something here. Well after walking around we decided all we wanted was cajun food so back to Beck's we went. Luckily there were 2 stools open and the waitress behind the counter welcomed us very enthusiastically.

We decided to split a Trainwreck, I got the chicken & andouille gumbo, and my husband got the gator gumbo. We were blown away by everything! First I appreciate them having a non-seafood option for gumbo. I don't like seafood so often I have to skip the gumbo at most cajun places. The gumbo was so rich and flavorful and had a little heat to it. My husband was over the moon with his gator gumbo, I tried a bite and it was good. We had to force ourselves to put the gumbos aside so we could tackle the sandwich. The trainwreck is such an interesting take on the classic cheesesteak sandwich. It also was delicious and big, good thing we chose to split it. The serving sizes here are pretty large, we ended up having to pack up our leftover gumbos to take home. They were still just as delicious re-heated!

I wish Philly wasn't a 6 hour drive away, because I might make the trip just for more of Beck's gumbo!

This Termini Bros Bakery shop in the Reading Terminal Market has all sorts of baked goods to delight your senses. Choose from cookies, pastries, cakes, pies, and more. However, their most notable item is their cannoli, so this is what I tried. I wouldn't quite rank it up there with cannoli from Boston (or actual Italy, I'd imagine). But it was creamy and indulgent, and it certainly hit the spot. So if you have a sweet treat craving, count on Termini Bros to satisfy.

We love it here. Quite simply the best Rotisserie chicken in Tampa hands down! The cilantro rice and spicy beans make for an exceptionally fantastic complement to the chicken. My only criticism is that you guys dont have a location closer to Ybor
Best rotisserie chicken in town. Nice sides: Cilantro rice, French fries... The chicken sandwich is really good too. Love the home made "ají" (hot sauce).

This was a nice surprise. I decided to try some place different. And boy am I happy I did! I ordered a couple things to try, like their chicken, bacon and ranch fries are awesome. It contains so much grilled chicken and crispy bacon. These fries are awesome with the added ranch. I also tried their veal parm hoagie. The roll was nice and fresh. And the veal was great. I did also taste a steak sandwich, which was very good. I would definitely recommend this place to friends and associates!

Second time here and the food was great. Good spot for a cozy lunch for two or a family dinner. The chicken with white rice, black beans and plantain is my favorite.. the chicken topped with the yellow sauce is recommended. The staff makes the visit more enjoyable.

I can only review the train wreck sandwich but it was mouth watering delicious!  Like the best cheese steak sandwich you ever had and throw in some sausage and salami. The bread, meat, and cheese were prefect, definitely one of the best sandwiches I have ever had!

Located in Reading Terminal Station, busy hustle and bustle all around you -- I have never felt so comfortable and more relaxed sitting at the diner style bar with so many people around.  The mac'n'cheese balls with bacon, with their own Arnold Palmer mix, and the fresh smells of delicious cajun food... no better place to sit down, eat, relax, and enjoy life for a little while.

The fried mac and cheese was great in theory and pretty decent in execution, but for some reason I detected an odd sour flavor in mine. I hope this was because they use sour cream or some sourish kind of cheese, and not because the milk they used had gone bad. 

The muffuletta was okay, but nowhere near the same ballpark as the ones I had in New Orleans. Maybe the Trainwreck should have been the way to go.

A solid Double Knot satellite location inside of Franklin's Table food hall on Penn's campus.

The menu is pretty varied, with rolls, sushi, sashimi, rice bowls, and combination boxes. 

I ordered a Yellowtail Scallion Roll and Salmon Avocado Roll, plus the pickled cucumber salad. Everything was fresh and tasted great. I especially loved the pickled cucumber salad. 

Service was super friendly and easy going. On my next visit I want to try one of the rice bowls, or combination boxes (which from the looks of it is A LOT of food - but you get a good sample of the menu.)
Hooray!  Read in this morning's newspaper that Trident Grill is coming to Northwest Tucson this summer!!  Can't wait!!

Fried mac & cheese balls... YES PLEASE. These were divine- very cheesy, crunchy outside, and made fresh. Delish. The cornbread was also really good. I'll be back when I'm back in the Reading Terminal Market!
I had the shrimp and crawfish etoufee with jambalaya rice. It was creamy and delicious. The service was quick and efficient even when Reading Terminal was crowded. The meal was filling and worth it!

The best broccoli rabe and provolone sausage around! This Italian Market butcher shop is "old school", and definitely worth the stop for their homemade sausage. The rib eye steaks and bacon are very good as well.  Honorable mention to the Sicilian Wine sausage.

When for lunch and again, enjoyed the food very much.  This place is always packed!  Service is good and large portions!  Too bad prices have had to increase so much due to increases in minimum wage and cost of goods (it's happening all around). Very happy to see that you guys can keep it going and even expand to additional locations!  Thank you for honoring the armed services and thank you for your service!  Keep up the great work!
The bakery is awesome. There are so many choices. The staffs are friendly. The price is fair.

Great food. The waitress is on top of it.   Drinks are fair.  Beer is the best thing to order for me.   Food is great.    Awesome environment military friendly which is awesome as always.   Thanks for the good time.

Most unprofessional service I have ever received.. Not exaggerating. The employee who "assisted" me was named April. First, she charged me extra for an optional warranty on the frames I purchased without even asking if I wanted it. Next, she tried to sell me the display frames thinking I wouldn't notice. They were clearly not in "new" condition. After I noticed this, I asked for a new frame. She told me they did not have any in stock, but she could order a new pair to the store and have them overnighted to my address by Friday. It was a Tuesday. It has now been over 2 weeks since I made this purchase and I still have not received my glasses. This store clearly only encourages sales volume and disregards customer service/loyalty. Also, their 50% off lenses deal is still a rip-off. My lenses were still over $200. I guess that makes them a little less of a rip-off than $400+. When you add in the not-so-optional warranty you are looking at a ridiculous upcharge. If you are planning on saving money this is not the place for you. If you don't mind spending a little extra, don't spend it here. Go to a non-chain institution that actually employs professionals. Also, if you want decent customer service and dislike uncomfortable sales pressure, steer clear.

The location is isolated but well worth the hunt to find it. The staff is was very helpful. They explained the menu very well. Service was very quick. We had a large party and everyone was served at the same time. Serving size are more than ample to share or have a second meal. The roasted chicken is specialty and packed full of flavor.

I've eaten here twice, and you can recreate the experience as follows:

Buy a nice stick of butter. Heat butter in saucepan. Put butter on gristle steak. Lick off butter. Get wife to say something snide to you. Burn a $100 bill.

The food here is not steak augmented by butter.  It's steak-flavored butter.

Ruth's Chris symbolizes everything I can't stand about Philly: Devastatingly unhealthy, delicious food, paired with terrible service.  Ruth's has an air of faux-classe; its steaks are slathered in butter rather than being of high quality, its walls are dirty, the light is way too low and the room is freezing cold.  All the little touches that you would expect from good managers are out the window.

What's worse is, as one reviewer mentioned, the place is still run by snobs.  If you are under 30 and you come here, the whore-dressing receptionist will ask you, "Are you here for a special occasion?" As if you couldn't afford to otherwise.

My recommendation is to answer, "Yes, we are here for *Insert Holiday Occurring at Opposite Time of Year*".

We were at the terminal and ordered three sandwiches from three places. I tried to "check in" to all three and yelp told me to slow down lmao!!! Hells no!! Muffuletta, delicious, great bread consistency, nice spice to the olive. A quarter is really quite enough to share. Mmmmm
One of the best and biggest Reuben sandwiches in town.  Cole slaw is great too.  I'm coming back!
Great menu, decent prices, lots of TV's, and veteran owned!  What more could you ask for!
The trainwreck po boy is insane. They amount of flavor was incredible, the sausage and the steak with the sauce worked so well. Bread stood up to all the stuff well!
Their cannolis are delicious! They have plenty of pastries and cakes to choose from. Excellent service as well!

This place is awesome with an inviting neighborhood hood bar feel. The servers are friendly and the beer selection is awesome. The wings are big, juicy and the flavors are great. My favorite is the steak and spinich salad. The steak is well seasoned and it is combined with roasted potatoes, boiled eggs and blue cheese make it a salAd that you will come back for! I promise you

Im glad I found this place because there is a lack of good coffee in the area and this place is good.

I like the room downstairs because it's comfortable and a good layout.  They play chill music.

Good Place.
This place was great! I would give 4.5 if I could because it took a while to get our food even when it wasn't very busy, but other than that food, service, and atmosphere were great!

Bread pudding w/ caramelized raisins, pears w/ a whiskey sauce. This is one of the best bread pudding's I've had. The whiskey sauce gives the bread just a bit more sweetness and the moistness of the bread pudding was scrumptous.

This is the first time I every had bread pudding with pears.

I've been getting my locs done by Trina B at Bella Locs since 2017 and let me tell you , she is THE BEST. I get so many compliments on my hair every where I go. She takes her time, doesn't rush through, and has excellent customer service. Every question you could ever have about her signature locs are on her website and Instagram but she still takes the time to make videos, tutorials, and go live to connect with her clients. The hair itself is easy to manage, not heavy at all and can be styled any way you wish. You also will be given an option to choose from several different colors which I thought was great. She also uses her own product when styling her clients' hair and I personally love it. It smells great and works wonders because my hair has grown so much!! If I could give Bella Locs a 10, I would!!

This has become our favorite bar for just about everything.  Lately to watch football but even before then for food (wings, burgers!), beers and just hang out.  We were in to watch the Eagles v Redskins game and we had a great time - even though Eagles lost.  Although we were VERY outnumbered we never felt intimidated or bullied and I think everyone had a good time jeering each other.  To top it off again service was just above and beyond, we never waited for a beer even though the place was packed and the girls were BUSY.  This is a great local bar!

We normally stop at the creperie in Reading Terminal for breakfast... but I'm pretty over that place, so I circled until I found another "breakfast" sign and a short line. Grabbed a quick breakfast -- fried egg, cheese and andouille po boy and bread pudding. The po boy got better with every bite!  As a bread pudding fanatic, I can honestly say this was heads and shoulders the best I've ever had-- they use french bread and top it with a warm, sweet, and buttery whiskey sauce. Nom nom...  

This is definitely my new favorite place to eat in the Market, and I've seriously been considering the 2-hour drive back to Philly just to load up on the Cajun deliciousness. It would be well worth the trip.

Went to Reading Terminal for lunch and found this gem of a place in the middle of the market.  They serve an assortment of cajun food, po boys, jambalaya, and an assortment of fried seafoods.  I decided to order a fried shrimp platter for about $12 that came with red beans and rice and a piece of their cornbread.  The lunch rush was moderately busy for a weekday but the meal did not dissapoint.  Looking forward to visiting again.

Truly the best coffee shop in Francisville. So happy they are able to be open during COVID through the mini window. My go to here is iced chi & their Maple Ham crepe  (best crepe EVER). I come here for a morning work drink or after a long night where I KNOW I need my crepe. Staff is so friendly, highly recommend if you are in the area!

A food informer of mine told me that Philly Dawgz had a Chicago style Hot Dog complete with the neon green relish. Well I had to see this for myself, so broke camp and slid on down to the Temple University area. 
I walked into the spot around 6 pm and there was only 1 customer there, and I noticed the walls were plastered with posters of Hot Dogs, Polish sausage and other foods. 
I went to the counter and ordered a Chicago Dog with all the trimmings. I asked the owner, a delightful guy named Stan, if he had the neon green relish and he replied "yes, I'm the only one in Philly that has it and I use the poppy seeded hot dog bun and Vienna Beef hot dogs and sausages. The Dog came and it was just like the ones I had in Chicago, piled high with the relish, tomato, onion, mustard, peppers and a kosher pickle spear. Talk about your daily servings of veggies! And most of all it was delicious! 
But the star of the show wasn't the hot dog, it was the owner Stan. He migrated here from India over 30 years ago and he was penniless so he lived in Atlantic City. Under the Boardwalk. For 2 years. His belongings in a shopping cart. He finally got a job at a hotel and worked his way to Philly, working at all the major hotels here before opening his own restaurant. 
Since it wasn't busy, he sat down with me and talked about improving his business and I gave him the same advice I give people from other countries selling food here. I ask them to sell a version of your product prepare in the style of your homeland, for instance I suggested that he serve a hot dog in Indian bread with a Masala sauce and I swear I saw A light bulb over his head! 
I don't know if it's just me, but It pains me to see all the Dominicans, Koreans etc selling Cheese steaks and Hoagies. I hope Stan makes it there and his spot is between my house and Center City and it will be like dropping in on a old friend.

Excellent food and service...I like burgers well done...I have ordered several times and always get it as ordered...my friend had salmon tacos today and said they were great...she is picky, so I take her comment as a high recommendation

Went to Sushi Tsu last night, sushi was good, not great, wait staff friendly and responsive.  The problem is I had two Sushi Tsu gift cards that they would not honor since they were issued by previous management.  These cards were won as silent auction from cancer fundraiser.  The manager would not talk to us and left the waitress to deliver the bad news even after we asked for more information and to speak with the manager.  The only thing they said was that the cards were old and they could not verify they had not been used before.  I'm disappointed they did not offer any other ways to accommodate us, not even a discount.  Needless to say we will not return to Sushi Tsu since there are much better sushi restaurants that care about their customers.

I rarely visit Reading Terminal these days, but had to stop in today because I was in the area and I had a sweet tooth. Where else can I get a great Cannoli this side of South street? Termini Bros was just the answer. I got a cannoli, tiramisu, and chocolate cake. The desserts are pretty, let's start there. The cakes are moist, light, and no one flavor is overpowering. Let's not forget the cannoli, I went with the chocolate since I'm a chocoholic and what a treat.

Outstanding experience and customer service!  So I've got to drop a 5 star review for Casual Male in Citrus Park.  

I walked into the store needing a suit in less than a week for a trip to the state capitol with co-workers.  Thomas and Pattie were awesome!  Let me start from the beginning....   

Initially, I went to Men's Wearhouse for a suit.  I figured they would have a good selection for a person my size (6'2"/250 lbs- right on the border of Big and Tall), and to fit what I needed in a suit.  After getting measured up - and looking at the few suits on hand that would fit me (poor selection for a 48 long) - I was told the best price they could do was was around $750.  I was also told it would take two weeks to tailor the suit, one week if they put a rush on it.  I told the salesman that was too much money for me to spend, nor did I have the time to wait for it, and they recommended checking out Casual Male as a fallback, but assured me they would have even less of a selection. 


I walked in and described what I needed to Thomas, he measured me up and had me try on a couple of suits.  Rather than the 48 long that MW recommended, Thomas fit me in a 46 long - which wound up being a better fit due to the lack of bowing in the lapel when it laid over my chest.  Unfortunately, they did not have a suit in stock that I needed, but Thomas was able to get a suit overnighted to me (free of charge!) from their manufacturer. He also recommended a tailor to me who was able to make my alterations the same day I received the suit. 

When I was checking out, I was added to their rewards list, and one of the perks is a discount in your birthday month.  Pattie included the birthday discount for me because it happened to be my birthday month. 

I was able to walk out of Casual Male with a brand new Jean-Paul Germain suit, a new dress shirt, a new pair of socks and a new tie for less than $450.  I received a suit that had a better fit, was prepared quicker, and looks fantastic for half the cost of Men's Warehouse.  I don't wear a lot of suits or dress clothing, but if I ever need some again I will start my search at Casual Male, and I will definitely be back to see Thomas and Pattie!

This is the first new place I've been to in a while!  Keto doesn't really allow me to try so many things :/

Went here for a going-away party for one of the guys in our lab.  The atmosphere was fun and it was fairly packed.  It wasn't really a major sports night, so the TV was filled with random snippets of golf and Nascar.  I built my own (bunless) burger with bacon and avocado.  It was actually fairly good, tasty and they gave me waaaay more avocado than any other place!!  I was also pleasantly surprised by the variety of foods (the redskins looked delicious and I was a bit sad I couldn't eat any and they have seafood!) and drinks (another place with pear cider!) they have.

Service was meh.  It was fairly busy, but I never once had my water refilled, and the waitress was definitely forgetful about a lot of things..

I am just leaving from my dinner. This review is solely based on the service. The worst service I have ever received. First of all, our waitress, Celia, did not greet us in a kind way at all. I thought maybe that would change. My husband and friends ordered micheladas and they did not like that they had sou sauce added so they kindly asked for a new mix but she only brought two back. My husband stated he wanted a new mix as well and she seriously said "ugh!" And made a body gesture as if he asked for the impossible to be done. Our appetizer and main dishes both took forever to come out. The plates were not even hot and food was cold. Better off going to the location on Speedway.

This time I had the rice and beans, as opposed to a double order of beans. 

The cilantro rice is great. The black beans delicious. The chicken yummy. 

Can't wait to return. 

PS the service is great

This review is only for the ricotta + chocolate chip cannoli:

It is wonderful. Fantastic! One of the best cannolis I've ever had, if not the best. It has the perfect amount of sweetness and a beautiful light consistency, complimented by the chocolate chips. The shell is even good too. 

Must try!

I went last night 1-14-2021 for some drinks.

Nice place to relax after work; great customer service;

Employees very nice and friendly and professional.

Drinks were Fantastic!

We are going back next week for Dinner.

5-Star's All-The-Way:

People are very friendly and the restaurant is very clean.  My daughter loved the garlic bread. The calzones are Texas size as well as the meatball sandwiches. We were in the Richmond area for 5 days and ate here three times
Great lunch!!!! Love this place! Awesome service and the train wreck is the best, hopefully all these spices put me into labor!

In the short time since I wrote my previous review, I have run into three new waitresses that are EXCELLENT.  To me this is huge & gets the place closer to 4.5 stars.  Unfortunately there are still some mediocre ones plus that damned juke box, so 5 stars seems unobtanium at this point.

Great first experience  !!! Being a local and stationed in San Diego where bars are very different and not alike. this one has that feel to it and not because it's  by the university but as soon as you walk in you see the seats and bar area. They offered beer that I had only seen in  Cali and other parts of the world! If you never had a Kilkenny definitely one of my fav beers and in that environment made me feel like a young sailor coming back and enjoying time on land.

added 2 stars. even though the place is packed and sometimes it is hard to get in, the food quality has gone way up! The service is fun, the people diverse, the waitress Sky is amazing, remembers my drink everytime. this is THE place

Visited the terminal Market and was sampling all the good Eats! We stopped fiirst at Becks Canjun Cafe it was delightful. The gumbo was awesome the service was great. I even bought the devil's dust. Definitely recommend if you love cajun.

Any time I am in Philly, I know I have to bring home food lol Not that I don't cook at home, but you know 
I ordered Jambalaya, Fried Oysters platter, Cajun fries  and Fried Mac and cheese  balls. Everything was great per usual. The only thing that irked my nerve was...one female (I am not shouting her out because maybe it was an off day for her) she had just come to work (03/06/2021 around 1 something in the afternoon) and she... DID. NOT. PUT. HER. HAIR. BACK 
It was hanging over the food, and I just hoped and prayed she washed it earlier or something at least  Something to soothe my urge to tell her something. She handed me my food and I was like "Gurl... you don't even know" Still coming back, but I will speak up next time,
Would go here all the time if I lived in Philly. Fresh and delicious flavors! I had the goat cheese, ham and fig sandwich and it was delicious!

This is very very good steak.  The prices are steep and I don't care for the way the sides are ordered but for good steak you just have to put up with it.  I've been to the Philly location along with the Annapolis, MD and Atlantic city location.  I have always had a top notch steak.
Must stop destination in the reading terminal!! Po Boy sandwich, fried Mac n cheese, Cajun fries, shrimp and crawfish salad all my favorites! Margaret at the counter was great!

Really surprised by the negative early reviews of this spot. The sushi rice is the signature delicious rice from Double Knot in Center City that sets it apart from all other sushi places in Philly. Everything is packaged beautifully, & the sauces on the side are delicious. I've literally had lunch here 3 days in a row since realizing they were open. I highly recommend the "Over Rice" bowls. The tuna over rice is basically the tuna tartare from Double Knot & a great amount of food for $9 & the sauce it comes with is stellar. Compare the prices to the other mediocre sushi places in UCity (Ochatto does a 2 sushi roll lunch special for $10, Pod is WAY overpriced because it's a Starr restaurant, Hai Street sushi burritos are $10+) & you'll see you're really only paying $1/$2 more for food that is better quality. Or, split a chef box with someone & you're golden. There are only a couple places in Philly that really do sushi right & this is now one of them.

I can not say enough about the Norwegian and Honey Bee crepes. The only thing better would be the cappuccino, easily one of the best I've ever enjoyed. 

The staff is very friendly and though they said our food would take 15 to 20 minutes it seemed closer to 5. 

Definitely on the short list for a return!

Who'd a thunk it, in Reading Terminal Market and the last place I'd expect to find Cajun food, let alone good Cajun food.  But the eternal lesson of NOLA is that a place doesn't have to look fancy or be in the right place to have great food.  Beck's has some of the best jambalaya I've had and it is my favorite Cajun dish and go-to during my time in NOLA.  Full of flavor with just the right bite.  Laissez les Bon temps roulez, y'all.  Keep it up.

Such a cute little neighborhood cafe, I met with clients here and their basement space is perfect for a meeting or just a quiet breakfast/lunch. It makes you feel you are in your own leaving room.

Tea and coffee are very good and their crepes are delicious, although I am giving 4 stars because I ordered a Nutella crepe but it was not fully Nutella, it was more of a mix between Nutella and chocolate syrup, I was expecting pure Nutella filling (as the name says) and not a mix of chocolates so that was a bit disappointing.

Best yellow tail sashimi in town!  We ordered red and green angel rolls and a few others all were incredible.  Sushi chef is Japanese and the owner, you get the authentic sushi here!  A true hidden gem in Tampa!  Must try!
Been hittin' this joint since the mid 90's. My favorite spot for my favorite food-Cajun! Always bring home dishes. Awesome gumbo, crawfish etouffee and alligator sausage plus many more
Always a solid experience. Good food and a really fun environment. I have enjoyed everything from the appetizers to the main courses.

During this pandemic I have become quite fond of TikTok sooooo while walking through Reading Terminal with my girlfriend we literally had a Tik Tok moment when I stopped at Beck's Cajun Cafe. 
Me: looking at the alligator gumbo
My girlfriend : girl don't do it. It's just not worth it . Don't do it girl
Me: I'm not going to do it girl , I was just thinking about it, I'm not going to do it. 
Store Employee: Hi , May I help you 
Me: I would like an order of the gator gumbo over white rice ... then looking at my girlfriend and saying I DID IT 

... and it was delicious

This little hidden cafe has AMAZING bagels. I think it's French owned. Their bagels are soft and tasty! They're pretty affordable too! I am putting them on my list of favorite cafe/coffee shops in Philly.

We went here for lunch on a week day because I had never experienced Peruvian style food. I was told the main reason you go here is for the Peruvian style rotisserie chicken.

We went around 11 and there was hardly anyone in the restaurant. We got sat down almost immediately and ordered very shortly after that. Everyone got some variation of the rotisserie chicken. I got a Quarter with the Cilantro rice and fries. The chicken comes with two sauces and both are very flavorful and tasty. The meat fell off the bone and was super juicy. I literally hate Cilantro and loved the rice. It did not taste like cilantro at all. I recommend giving the rice a try even if you think cilantro tastes like soap.

The inside is between a fast food restaurant and sit down restaurant. It is a very casual vibe and you can see from looking around that it is quick service and somewhere you would go for a "quicker" meal. 

I definitely have this place on my list to go back to.

Wow I never knew crepes could taste sooo good! LOVE this place! new favorite!! The strawberry au sucre was absolutely on point. It melted in my mouth lol. Their savory crepes taste amazing and are quite filling as well.

I order from here twice a week and the past month the delivery driver has been forgetting our main platters, or mixing orders.. Takes away from whole take out experience. Each time i have to wait another half an hour for food that should have been delivered in the 1st place. Service and or delivery  is getting sloppy

The husbeast is going to Washington, to make a presentation. He has to look nice! Since he's a large man, buying clothing can be a challenge. It used to be that Men's sizes were easy, now they're leaning towards some vanity sizing as well.  

We were able to find the pants and vest, 2 shirts and 2 ties he needed for a 2 night stay in the DC area, and yes, it wasn't cheap. For some reason clothing manufacturers believe that larger clothing needs to be higher priced. It really doesn't. Especially Tees and polos. There isn't that much more fabric. 

The store was clean and well maintained, save for the bathroom which had a lack of a working towel dispenser or toilet paper holder, both were just rolls set on top of things. Stay classy Tampa. 

The store is necessary. Yes, They carry Big and Tall sizes, Emphasize on the TALL. They seem to have a LOT in that category.

We went to Vineyards Cafe for breakfast after reading about how delicious their crepes are. The inside is pretty small, but has a very warm and inviting atmosphere.  There's also more room downstairs but we never got a chance to check it out. Both servers were very friendly. This place really does feel like your neighborhood cafe, just like their sign says!

I ordered the Norwegian crepe. These were really packed with salmon and avocado.  I never had this combination of foodstuffs together before, but it somehow works. Even my girlfriend who admittedly doesn't like goat cheese or avocados commented on how much she liked the dish. 

I was also able to try a bite or two of her caramel ricotta crepe. Also very delicious and not too sweet. Would be interested in coming back here to try more of their crepes and some of their coffee.

I came for the cannolis. My Bostonian coworker came with me and also got one. It was hard for him, but he admitted that this cannoli was better than the ones from Boston. If that's not the best review for a cannoli ever, then I'm not sure what is.

Philly's best gator spot hands down. My gator po boy and baguette brought me back to NOLA. 

Don't forget to check in on Yelp for 5% off.

They have breakfast options, but breakfast stops at 11am, which is unfortunate.

Becks is popular and the food is made to order so expect a wait. It's worth it though.

DO NOT HEM your pants here.  I went into this place because the had a giant banner outside advertising that they hem pants.  I took in my pants from a suit I just bought and they told him that for an extra $3 they can hem in one day.  I said not problem and paid.  To my amazement, when I picked up my pants the next day, you can see ever stitch on the outside.  I have never ever seen anyone so poorly hem dress pants.  

I asked the lady there how can this be acceptable, please take all your stitching out and I want a refund.  She said no problem and then proceeded to tell me that her hem machine is more than 40 years old lol.  I told her, why in the world would you advertise pants hemming when you have a machine that can potentially ruin clothes.

I am not sure what anyone elses experience is here, but I am certain that I will not be back.

The sign on the door says, "Tell us your mood, and we'll make the food." That's a tall order. But it delivers!

A friend and I stopped into Mood Cafe one Saturday morning, not having any idea what it was, but with grumbling bellies and having seen a woman sitting in the window eating something very colorful. Mood's menu isn't extensive, (lassi, chaat, dahl, and desserts from the Indian subcontinent), but there are lots of varieties of each item, and the food's flavor is EXPLOSIVE! 

The owner immediately walked us through the menu and made some suggestions based on the kinds of flavors we said we liked. He then customized two chaat dishes and two lassis for us. Fresh mango, spicy peanuts, sweet cranberries, radish, chickpeas, yogurt, mint, chutneys, and a rich samosa were in my chaat. My friend got the chicken version, which was like my vegetarian dish, but with juicy chunks of tandoori chicken. 

While we were waiting for our order, two other folks came in--one who ordered a mint/honey lassi. The owner said, "Wait a minute. I have to go get some mint." He walked out the store, went to a small garden on the sidewalk, cut some fresh mint leaves, and returned to make her lassi. Amazingly fresh!
 
While we were only visiting Philly for the weekend and won't be able to return with any frequency, I HIGHLY encourage any locals to visit this gem!

Ok, I've tried this place three times now, so I'm ready to call it. It's another Latin spot that specializes in rotisserie chicken that I feel would be at home on the Colombian Corridor, Armenia. My favorite is the cilantro rice with the chicken. The service is friendly even if they insist on speaking Spanish to everyone. Watching your sodium? You'll probably wanna skip this then. It seems that a lot of the flavor is derived from seasonings unlike the Colombian folks who rely on cooking style a bit more. It's flavorful, juicy, and addictive. The dipping sauces add punch, as if it needs it! There's ample seating, and clean restrooms, so bring a crowd if you wanna. All this salt is perfectly washed down with one of he many soda offerings. mmm..

So glad I finally tried this place out because it's GREAT!!! The woman who took my order, Kim, was super sweet and welcoming. 

I ordered the shrimp and crawfish etouffee with Cajun rice and it was very tasty! Has a lot of flavor and a bit of heat to it! She recommended ordering the corn bread to crumble into it and I'm glad she did! 


Can't wait to come back and try some more of their dishes!
Delicious crepes! Highly recommend the Philly--salmon cooked perfectly. Make sure you check out the super cozy downstairs seating area. Great place to work/study/have a meeting.

Awesome food. Great bar tenders.  You can't go wrong.  Make sure you check out the pictures on the wall.  This place, owner, has history of serving our country with the Navy Seals, hence the name Trident.  You owe it to our country to stop in and have one.

I went to Termini Bros because they are one of the "tried and true" bakeries I've come to depend on. My daughter and I went to the original location on 8th street only to find it closed although online it stated it was open. I purchases a birthday cake and two small tirmisus...all of which were stale and gross. I dont mean one day old either. The tiramisu tasted at least a week old. Even the coffee bean on top was stale. Never the hell again. The only  saving grace was the cannolis which were fresh and delicious. If you go, get the cannoli!!
Leave the gun, take the cannoli...

La Parrilla Suiza was my favorite local restaurant in the past. Sad that it has gone downhill. We had a friend visiting from out of town and brought her here for Cinco de Mayo.
