The most mediocre bagel I've had in quite some time. Very dry and small amount of cream cheese. The coffee is much better. Overall, an average of experience.

Sign clearly states OPEN.
Yet staff says they are closed.
Lost sales & confusion, not sound business practice or customer service
Awesome place! Got the iced coffee mocha and a slice of peanut butter chocolate cake! Really good stuff :). Will definitely be back!

Came here to see Moonlight last week.  It's a small, charming theater.  A little busted up, some of the seats seemed to be on their way to being broken, leaning quite a bit in one direction or another.  However, this place focuses on independent films that you can't find anywhere else.  This was the only place in 50 miles that was showing Moonlight.  The Ritz East gets an extra star or two just for that.

Tickets are still a bit more than I think movies should cost.  Snacks are still ridiculously priced.  But neither of these budgetary concerns are any different than any other theater.  Staff was pleasant, even if a lot of them seemed to be a little clueless about what was going on around them.

I really wanted to like this place.  It is a Vegetarian/Vegan place, but also has other options for people that wanted fish (Pescatarians). 

My friend and I met there yesterday (1-3-11) for lunch and the staff was just not friendly.  They honestly where annoyed when  you asked questions, felt I needed to apologize since I just moved here from Illinois. 
Examples of how they were rude: 
 I ordered the Veggie sandwich and the cashier asked me if I wanted cheese, I said yes the cheese that comes on the sandwich, the menu states it comes with swiss.  She got rude and told me that there is four cheeses to choose from.  

Chips come with sandwiches and you have a choice of four different kinds.  My friend asked how the sweet onion bag tasted and wanted to know if they were good and the cashier goes I don't know what they taste like, probably oniony (I guess that is a word, lol)

There menu looks great, but I probably won't be back because I enjoy optimistic people over pessimistic people.

I decided to try the cafe out on a whim... was looking for a place to grab coffee after 9pm. Very good choice. I got the peanut butter mocha which was perfect, not too sweet like I was expecting it to be... I also caved and got a slice of pumpkin pie to satisfy my sweet tooth... man such a perfect combo. I highly recommend this place for a great late night dessert... they had a huge selection of unique desserts displayed.

All three of the Ritz's are awesome. I love this one especially because of the old school brick street and its choice Olde City location. 

The Ritzes are the only place to see great indie films in the city. My only qualm is that there isn't one around Market East. That would be a great way to kill some time there.

My favorite place to watch movies in philly. Situated in old city, the theater has an old fashioned feel to it with with an old school popcorn machine, etc. the chairs are so comfy and when you go with a friend or significant other it feels like you're really out on a date night. If you can go here for a movie I recommend it above anywhere else in philly. It makes me want to go out to the theater for my movies rather than wait for them to be available online :).

I had high hopes for this place, but unless all you want is coffee, it's far less than epic. They advertise desserts and much more, but nothing they serve is that special. Service was slow. Dog hair was all over the seating. Dirty old silverware was unappealing and led me to use their flimsy pastic which does not hold up to the ice cream. It tasted blah like some generic grocery store brand. In all it was a dirty, hippy dippy, unkept,  place with very misleading advertising. The owner needs to seriously look at some cleanup, replacement of utensils, and step up the food and service to even come close to matching how it's advertised, and look at things from a customer's point of view. I was embarrassed to have suggested Epic Cafe to my group. It's was a sad and disappointing experience. I'll never go again.

Epic, I want to wrap you in a napkin and put you in my pocket and take you to all the cities I visit where I can't find a decent coffee shop- you're that yummy. 

They have an extensive menu of coffee beverages, and even more options when you take a look at their syrups and customize a bevie of your own. I'm not a coffee connoisseur, but I gotta say they have one mean bean. I'm also always amazed at the variety of pastries that they offer. Muffins to scones and everything in between, you're sure to find something to please your carb tooth.

Today I had a muffin, which for a morning eat was a little out of the ordinary for me. It was super enjoyable though. Cherry, vanilla, a dash of sweetness...it muffin topped any muffin I've ever had.  

On a few occasions the internet has been down, and that's been a little annoying, but they are always super quick to fix it once they know and it's totally not a regular occurrence. I've heard people gripe that Epic is a little crunchy, it's a little granola, and yeah there's an interesting crowd, but that's the cool thing about a coffee shop that bookends a pretty transient main drag in Tucson. It's a great place to catch up with a friend, pound on the laptop keys or hang back and people watch. Crunchy or smooth the place is Epic.

As far as bánh mì in Philly goes, this is as good as it gets!  While I have had better in other states, you would be hard-pressed to find better in the greater Philadelphia area.  I especially love that the roll itself isn't the crusty kind that falls apart & leaves a mess everywhere (like they use at Ba Le & several other places).  The street parking is sometimes a problem, but if you can deal with the occasional looping around the block to find a parking spot, then definitely go here for some tasty, authentic bánh mì!
Their current hours of operations are Tuesday - Sunday, 7:30 AM - 5:00 PM (closed Mondays).

Very casual place along a very walkable street. They have a few vegan options, and a few more veganizable options, including a soup, veggie sandwich and some pastries. Sandwich was ordinary but tasty enough, and the soup was well done. Some botching of our orders, but they were friendly enough. Wouldn't overly recommend the place, but it's a nice casual place in a great neighbourhood.

How does one rate the quality of a movie theater? The length of ticket lines, politeness of staff, stickiness of the floors & seats? Price of candy & popcorn perhaps? I'm going to say the fact that the ticket itself was 10$ which is pretty much the cheapest one can see a movie anywhere, the fact that I saw a student discount on the ticket window (after I ordered my ticket online) would lead me to think that I could have gotten it cheaper, and the fact that the movie seats were enough stadium styled that nobody of the average range of heights would have disturbed my view, would all lead me to decide on 4 stars. I have been in theaters where the sounds is as if they had Bang & Olufson speakers and I made no such realization here. This place is certainly a great venue to see a movie, especially if you're into some of the lesser known/successful movies that come out of those festivals, you can find them here.

The Ritz East provides a solid venue to watch an independent film in the city, but it is actually my least favorite of the three Ritz locations.

I end up here when a movie that I want to see is not playing anywhere else, and I certainly can't complain about the diversity and quality of films that play here.  Most recently I caught the Woody Allen flick, Blue Jasmine, but that is about as mainstream as the selections get.  The usual offerings lean to the independent, artsy, foreign variety, and the clientele is always there to enjoy the movies.

The stars are lost for overall venue quality.  Even though this Ritz is ostensibly in "nicest" location nestled in the same chichi Society Hill enclave as Zahav and Positano Coast, it has an overall run-down feel.  The lobby and concession stand are tiny.  A line forms out the door to buy tickets.  The restrooms have a weird porta-potty trailer vibe to them, though they are usually kept clean.  The theaters themselves also leave a bit to be desired with squeaky seats and stuffy ventilation.  The screens and acoustics are in good condition though, so they seem to have paid attention to what counts most.

Bottom line: if you want to see something that's playing here you will likely enjoy the movie.  However, it is not worth a special visit for the "experience".

Hidden away behind a cement "park" and a noodle shop, this is like the Ritz they don't want you to know about. With just two screens, there's usually only one bigger/newer indie film playing, and it is never, ever crowded. The theaters are larger (with stadium seating) and maybe a little younger than those at the Ritz 5. Other than that, this Ritz shares the same well-chosen film selection, friendly employees, tasty snack bar and considerate audiences that make us love all the Ritzes.
Thank you for hosting our big party of 20. We had a wonderful time and the food was great!!

Super friendly staff. Very laid back and willing to cut you a break say if you are trying to use a debit card for a refill and don't meet the minimum. Moderately fast WiFi depending on the time of day and the amount of people. Good location and chill atmosphere. Very family friendly.

This was my first ever visit to Epic (what took me so long?) and I was looking for a comfy place to read, relax, and just generally hang out for an hour or so before I had to go to work.  Epic delivered what I needed.  There was a comfortable, if somewhat worn, couch, a stack of Tucson Weeklies, and I really enjoyed my iced peanut butter mocha.  Be warned that this drink is not for everyone.  I understand that some may be put off by the idea of espresso and peanut butter, but I found it delightful.

I'll visit Epic again another day and try their food.  The desserts in the case looked great.
Great lil coffeehouse and sandwich spot.  Reasonable, friendly.  Really enjoyed the lemonade.

I read in one of the previous reviews that Epic Cafe has a chill atmosphere. That's true, but in my two experiences there, the only chill comes from the staff working behind the counter. 

Neither time that I visited Epic was I greeted warmly and in fact, it seemed that I was an inconvenience to them. 

Epic tries to be a Coffee House that is welcome and inviting but comes up short. Most tables are small with only enough room for two and even then, we were so close to the next table it was hard to carry on a conversation without hearing every bit of the conversation of our next door neighbors. 

The tea was not so good...but that was probably my fault. I usually like something more along the lines of Earl Grey but I wanted to try something new so I went for the Raspberry Hibiscus or something like that. It was awful but perhaps it just wasn't my "cup of tea" 

The peach cobbler was bland and still cold, even after they warmed it up from the refrigerated display case. 

How Tucson Weekly readers came about naming this place the Best Café Hangout is beyond me. With a name like Epic, I expected something better than mediocrity.

It IS the best banh mi in the city! Not a fancy place. They don't have BBQ pork or anything like that. Only the basics: cold cut ham, cured pork, combo, chicken. But their ingredients are top notch. You can actually taste the pate and  mayonnaise spread but they don't overwhelm the meat. The bread is toasted just right - some places over toast them and they're like rocks when you take your first bite. The price is $4.50  & $5.00 now. Banh mi everywhere used to be $3.50-$3.75 but they got popular these past couple of years so hence the price increase, everywhere. Still cheaper and healthier compared to a lot of sandwich options out there. You won't be disappointed with this place. Just know that it's nothing fancy and is authentic Vietnamese so don't expect to be treated like you're in a Stephen Starr restaurant.
Unless you're a hipster plugged into a laptop, I wouldn't bother. Coffee was not bad. Bread pudding was incredibly dry and somewhat bland. As my friend said, an "Epic(ally dull)" experience.

It's kind of sad; I wanted to like Epic a lot more than I actually did.  The place was highly recommended by a friend who gave me a list of great places to try in Tucson.  I love little coffee shop/cafe places, so I was particularly excited to try this one.

The place is nice enough and the staff all pleasant.  But the food and the coffee were just not up to snuff.  My chicken salad sandwich was dry and served on a yet dryer roll.  I briefly suspected I might be eating an old sponge, but the sesame seeds on top suggested that was slightly less likely.  And later when I stopped back for a cup of coffee, it honestly tasted burnt.  Sure, it's a fun looking place but I don't generally go to coffee shops for the view.  Based on the generally glowing reviews, I'd give it another try when I'm in the area, but I can't say my hopes are notable elevated.

Ahh so long I've wanted to talk about the irony of this place. The truth is, I could give it more stars, but the areas that it is lacking in needs such improvement that I want these two stars to stand out. In fact, it's such a great offense, I should only give them one star.

The truth is, this is probably the best cafe in Tucson to hang out at. It is large with high ceilings and comfortable seating - something that is for some reason lacking in most cafes. The music is generally good and ranges all styles. It has a nice corner location with windows in the front. All in all the ambience is comfortable and you don't ever feel rushed to leave.

It's too bad this place is a cafe, though. Their coffee is abysmal. Maybe at some point in the past they received complaints from people who don't really like coffee, that their coffee is too strong. It tastes like hot water. This is true of their medium and dark roast. They have no business making such weak coffee. Their espresso is a little bit better; in the past it had an amazing earthiness to it, almost like Turkish coffee. Today they still serve an espresso that qualifies to be called such, but I expect better. Anyways, with a decent automatic espresso machine it really isn't that hard to succeed in this area.

Now the cafe as a bakery: you walk in and you cannot help but see the beautifully tall cakes at the front. They look so good. Yes, they do look good. And that's about it. They're expensive and taste like something a child put together. This is harsh, but they just have don't have the mature richness that someone over the age of fifteen would appreciate. The exception would be anything made with just chocolate, since chocolate is so amazing how can you screw it up? Yet a memory keeps trying to insist that the chocolate cake was maybe a bit dry... too bad I am not willing to risk the six dollars a piece to verify this.

The rest of their food is pretty much hippie/vegan/celiac fare. Honestly, I hate this crap. I understand that they probably get a lot of customers who prefer this, but it's crap. Have I tried it? No, not theirs specifically. I'm just complaining that they make so much of it. The savory food always looks old, yet somehow inviting. Weird.

Then there's the bathroom. Wtf. This place has some audacity making customers use that nasty key to get in there. Knowing that many people neglect to wash their hands, how does one go about staying hygenic? That is, when you can wash your hands here. For some reason, there is an automatic paper towel dispenser, but usually they have nothing but diluted dishwashing soap in an old plastic water bottle or no soap at all. They must know how crazy this is.

All in all, this place is just outright confusing. I've debated buying my own goodies and coffee from somewhere else, then coming here to buy maybe... something that I can give to my dog later on, and just relaxing on a comfortable old couch. Yes, that's what this place is good for.

Still serving drinks in styrofoam cups. I'LL PAY AN EXTRA .50 CENTS FOR THE UPGRADE. At least give us the option. I like this place too much to give up on it. My review goes up two stars as soon as the switch goes down.

Great foreign film selection and good deals.

I'm disappointed to say that it doesn't get 5 full stars. Why? 

Because some racist old white lady douchebag turned around and mean mugged me twice in disgust as soon as I sat down (oh I guess I dont belong at this place, huh? Eff you) and shifted in her seat. As soon as I started to eat popcorn - not in a loud and obnoxious way but whatever, you eat it...it's the movies - and she started to get up because I was ruining her experience, so I got up instead with a "don't bother" attitude and moved up a good 5 rows. Nice. 

All I wanted to do was relax and watch a movie and this old-school nerd had to get all "woe is me suburbia" about it.

I had the good fortune of ordering Sahara 2 weeks. Long story short, I called the number, they answered, and although they weren't opening until the following day, they let me order. The food was exceptional- and let me say that I frequent Tiffin, Ekta, and Saffron and Sahara has them beat!

It sounds like the owners' business model recognizes the Tiffin/Ekta price point and they plan to undercut them in price and surpass them in quality. I had a straightforward order of Chicken Tikka Masala, Onion Naan, and a Mango Lassi. The Chicken was extremely tender and the sauce was robust and hearty, the Naan was stuffed with a generous amount of fresh onion, and the lassi was standard lassi fare (I've never had a bad one anywhere.)

Anyway, I'm looking forward to exploring other selections on the menu and due to the aforementioned price point, I can actually afford to! I have no affiliation with the restaurant, I just had a surprisingly exceptional experience and encourage you to check it out.

Somehow I always get myself lost trying to find the Ritz East vs the Ritz, but I always leave pleased. This is where I come a) to see movies that don't make it to the large, mega theaters and b) to see grown up flicks that don't involve texting teenagers or whining toddlers in the audience. I recommend purchasing tickets in advance as a number of shows I have seen here have sold out rather quickly. The tickets for both the 8p and 10p shows of Black Swan on a Saturday night were gone within minutes which resulted in many boyfriends receiving rather pouty faces from their significant others! The prices are reasonable and relatively comparable to the rest of the city/suburbs. I always skip the snacks in favor of visiting a favorite, local restaurant instead. They do have better fare than your average theater, though. Who doesn't love Pocky!? While it probably sucks to get caught in this predicament, it is kind of nice that they prohibit folks from entering the theater 15 minutes after the main event has begun. There is nothing worse than being stepped upon after you've gotten all settled and into the rhythm of the story. The seats are large and I'm always comfortable even when the place is packed. The best part is that you're probably not likely to find yourself in danger of being shot while any of the Ritz theaters. I wish I could say the same for the Riverview or Bridge cinemas!

POSITIVES:
+ coffee was delicious
+ so was the strawberry italian iced tea

NEGATIVES:
-I feel like this place is a haphazard mess of decor, almost dirty.  You can totally do funky without feeling old and run-down, Epic does not understand that.

In my opinion this is the best place to get you Banh mi fix in Philly. Ba Le and cafe nhu quynh can't compare to the deliciousness found here. My go to is the Banh mi dat biet. If I'm feeling hangry I would get the flan too.

We're just in town for the week and I was craving vegan sweet treats and tea, so after reading the reviews here we decided to try it. It's a cool place (there was a group of three guys sitting outside just playing guitars for fun) and they did have several vegan cookies, etc. the girl behind the counter was friendly and helpful and she even gave me some day old vegan scones for free! Definitely a good experience

This is the banh mi I grew up eating for the past 10 years.
They also have a daily special which is buy 10, get 1 free.
Everything about the banh mi here is just so perfect, from the bread to the pate.

NOTE: They are closed on Mondays.

Good coffee, Ridiculous scones, muffins, and morning goodies that put the local bakery to shame.  Recently had a blueberry maple bacon scone, and it was GOOD!  comfortable seating inside or out, and lots of it (inside)!  Great atmosphere, great service!  My new favorite coffee place!  Did I mention locally owned!

I almost always get their Hibiscus tea when i go here and it is always perfectly tasty. The atmosphere here is really  laid back and the cooling system here is one of the best i've been to during the summer months. The staff are colorful and generally amiable and the desserts always look amazing :)

If your looking for real smoked wings and amazing pulled chicken DONT come here! I ordered smoked wings and they looked fried; I asked the server of these are "smoked" and she said yes and walked away.  I tried one and was certain it was fried, I asked the server if they were fried she said "we smoke the wings, let them sit to room temperature and when they're ordered we flash fry them for a min" that's pathetic to say the least! I also ordered a pulled chicken salad, it took more than 30 min to come out, the wait wasn't the bad part, the fact that the chicken was ice cold was the part that pissed me off.  I asked our charming server, why is the chicken cold? She said, it because "we grill it, then pull it, then chill it in the fridge".   

Bottom line is the name is quite misleading, chicken tastes left over and they just best it up for you.  They have ribs, burgers, steaks and pasta here too: you can try it, I'm gonna pass. 

For BBQ in this area I recommend Jazzy's and Alex's BBQ.

I'm an Epic regular.  It's still got the vibe of pre-revitalization 4th Ave/downtown- a little bit grimy, lotsa locals, and mediocre coffee.  

The breakfast burrito is amazing, and I also love that they have different muffins and scones every day.  Always tasty.  :)

It's a decent place to hang out and work, lots of space.  The wi-fi is kind of sketchy, but it usually works alright. 

I do wish they would clean the furniture though.  Seriously, some of the couches look pretty nasty.

The staff are mostly pretty nice. Once in awhile you'll get somebody who doesn't seem to know what's going on, but the folks who are usually there are cool.

At the Epic Cafe, if you order a cortado you'll get a latté, and if you order a macchiato you'll get an extra-dry cappuccino. My brother likes the decor though.

Added a star to my previous review because my gripes were mitigated by their cheap, quality cold brew. The kindness of employees is hit or miss.

This is a great place to see an independent film.  I like all of the Ritz theaters.  I can always count on them to have that kind of obscure film, I've been wanting to see.  Also, it's a little cheaper than the AMCs of the world.  There's occasionally a small sound or picture glitch, but they rectify things pretty quickly.  The seats are comfortable, and the popcorn is fresher than the big theaters.  There are good deals for matinees and students, and the staff is very friendly.

Epic Cafe is nice. It's pleasant. It's A-OK, but it's not epic. We do come here every time we're in Tucson because of its convenience and decent prices. Nothing about their selections screams AWESOME, but after some wild Tucson nights, you are in no position to be picky. 

I usually get the veggie sandwich ($8) sans the sprouts. My friends like their morning egg and bacon sandwich. Their breakfast burrito was just all right. And one really cool (and almost epic) option? Pancakes (or was it a waffle?) with a scoop of ice cream.  

I feel like this place could be substantially better if they sourced their bread from a local bakery, rather than a grocery store (at least that's how it tastes).

Sahara is great. The delivery is prompt and the food is great! 
A Friday night dinner for 2 was full of spice and flavor, and even enough for lunch on Saturday!

Not having a menu, only a recommendation... the staff was able to help me get exactly what I wanted. 

In case you don't have a menu ... http://www.saharaindiancuisine.com/

I love that from my little perch in Kenzo I have the choice of 3 different Indian restaurants. All with their merits, but I"ll have to give it to Sahara! Nicely done.

I walk here all the time from campus and I enjoy this cafe! The sweets are amazing and so are the quiches! I had a the turkey bacon avocado sandwich this week and it was really good! I recommend coming here! Not that bad prices but I wish they had pretty outdoor seating. I gave this cafe 3 stars because every time I come here it seems they always forget about my food or it takes a long time. -___-

Pretty good coffee and the ultimate 4th Ave stop. Lots of different food and drink items. Almost always comfortably crowded and a good atmosphere in which to study and people watch. It's a really eclectic clientele. Yes, hispter-ish, but it's much deeper than that.  

I prefer the coffee at Caffe Luce, but it's much easier to get (free) parking near Epic and I find it a more comfortable atmosphere in which to study.

Great place! I love the vegetarian soup options, only 2, but that's good enough for me. there are plenty of vegetable toppings to have and more as add-ons if you would like. It's a nice seating area, quick service. There are waits at times, but the usual times that you would expect (ie.. Friday and Saturday nights).

I definitely recommend this place if you're looking for a vegetarian broth soups. I also definitely recommend this place if you're looking for good soups.

The good:
Free wi-fi, good coffee and tea, yummy desserts and baked goods, good soup, knowledgeable staff, many vegetarian and vegan options, dog-friendly outside seating.

The bad:
Creepy-ass bathroom, too-loud music, awful open-mic night, no parking.

I think the only part of Epic I missed out on was breakfast, but I have no doubts that it is good.  The sandwich was good, but the chickpea salad was fantastic.  The coffee kept me coming back, and the desserts were tasty enough I am not sure I believe that they were vegan.  

Epic reminds me of some of my favorite coffee shops, but definitely has a personality of it's own.

These guys just rock...  went there two nights in a row. The second night the owner remembered who I was the first night and gave us preferential treatment because we were a repeated customer.

He made sure our pizza orders were handled promptly and delivers to our table by himself with a note to enjoy the food.

The food itself was just incredible. I travel to NYC a lot and they have nothing on Due Amici!!!
Very clean and well managed. Two screens with each seating about 250 viewers. Reasonable admissions prices and quality snack bar.

DO NOT GET YOUR WEDDING SERVICE FROM THIS PLACE.  High rating for this place was written by the owners! Annie which is the owner will made everything sound so good and promises to do everything we asked but nothing was what she said. She did a horrible job. She left before she finished the job on the wedding day. We signed a contract and everything that was listed was supposed to be included in our package but nothing was doing correctly or not do at all. Then she had the nerves to tell us that she did her job and it was beautiful in her eyes. Our guest thought we had kids decorating our wedding not a professional.  The reception table was just covered with an old dirty white table cloth with nothing but she promised to have decorations on it but nothing was there. The stage was suppose to have colored curtains but we got dirty white half ripped sheer drapes. We paid her 3k for dirty white chair coverings, table cloth and backdrop. She left before the job was done leaving my family to pick up what she didn't finish like putting ribbons on the chairs. Worst service ever!!!!

My group came here for a study date. Ordered the peanutbutter mocha (I Felt a little let down at first sip. Couldn't taste a hint of peanutbutter.) Their desserts are awesome though and they have a great variety of food for a coffee house. The guy behind the counter could have used some help because the night-time rush kinda swamped him working alone. Decent place, with a nice atmosphere and music. Maybe I need to try another coffee drink next time.

Ah, Epic.  Epic in its fixture status:  in many ways, there's no value in reviewing Epic, because people come here for all kinds of reasons not tied into quality and from which they can never be dissuaded.

Having been a cyclical fixture here, myself, I have an ambivalent relationship with Epic.  The vibe has deteriorated since the HA took over fully.  The music routinely sucks and is completely wrong for a cafe.  The treats are often good, except the scones and muffins, which rely too heavily on sugar and not enough on fat.  

What has been sad recently are the changes in staff.  Epic used to be admirable for a long run staff in a notoriously high turnover industry.  Recently, they purged a great many and instead hired newbies - presumably, to save money.  Except that it missed the point:  cafes are inherently cults of personality.  You change the barista, you change the cult.  Sometimes, that's good.  Sometimes, that's bad.  Right now, they have a bunch of people who are new and irritating, highly untrained, unprofessional and who think playing rap is the right vibe.  Sigh.  

The coffee is on the lower end of the yum spectrum in town, unless you're getting sugar in a glass with one of the blended drinks.  Not as "street friendly" as Shot in the Dark or whatever the hell we call it these days, many will nevertheless encounter more homeless people on the couch next to you than is pleasant.

Plus, kids come here and treat it like their living room, putting their bare, stinky feet all over all the furniture like that's appropriate.  I'd hate to bring a black light in here for the upholstery surfaces.

Nevertheless, I still spend time here.  6am-12am makes it sometimes the only game in town for a certain set of needs.

I used to love the casual atmosphere here but things have changed. The second to the last time I was in here, the barista kept me waiting while she and the customer ahead of me (who'd already ordered and paid) caught up on life. The very last time I was in here, a different barista kept me waiting while she talked to her friend about how much they both enjoyed Jameson's whiskey. I get it; you're hip and cool but you're still a business. Act like one. Thankfully, Fourth Ave. has a ton of good options for coffee.

Places like Epic are the reason I love Tucson. I've been to Epic several times. Relaxed atmosphere. Friendly staff. Plenty of vegan options. And get this - they don't charge extra for non-dairy milk in your latte! Yay Epic! :)

I love love love love love love love this place.

I am here practically every night when I come to Tucson. The crowd is just weird enough, the decor is nice, the seating is adequate (without being too plentiful) and comfortable, drinks and food are great, and most importantly, the free wireless Internet access is FAST. I don't know how they do it, but it's seriously just like being on my home network. Since I don't have Internet access at my Tucson house, that's really huge to me. (That's right, I'm sitting in Epic right now.) I'm tempted to watch NHL games on my computer here, but that would just seem mean.

Food: The pasta is fantastic and not too expensive--I just paid somewhere around $3.30 for a bowl that was good enough to satisfy the munchies. The cookies are too hard to be worth the cost; I've had fresher cookies at 7-Eleven back home in SD for less. The sandwiches, however, are fantastic.

Drinks: The coffee is pretty damn good, and as a former barista I have high standards. It's not necessarily the best in the world--back home, Influx in Golden Hill comes to mind as being higher in quality--but I am sipping on an herbal Arnold Palmer that's actually delicious, which I would have never expected. Seriously, Arnold Palmer with herbal tea? And it tastes *good*? Who the hell would have thought?

Location: Right on 4th Ave & University Blvd, so you can park on the curb on University for free, walk in, and unwind before walking down to the busier part of 4th Ave to get your drink on. I dig being able to hop from one 4th Ave drinking spot to another without worrying about driving or parking. Out-of-towners beware, though: make sure you watch out for the City of Tucson Parking Permit Required signs, because Fourth Ave is crawling with Old Pueblo's porcine citizens.

To wrap this thing up, I heartily recommend that everyone staying in or passing through Tucson give Epic a try.

Epic Café is way overrated.

The "atmosphere" is hateful, not cool at all. Most of the customers are like zombies, at least when they're not acting elitist. That goes for the staff too, I suppose. The coffee isn't great, but the desserts are tasty.

Honestly, don't bother with the place. If you're not already a regular, you'll just get glares and be treated like shit.

Want a family doctor that you have to wait three hours to see even when you have an appointment? How about a rude front desk staff that carries on their own conversations or fights with each other when they have a waiting room full of patients? Or a doctor that thinks everyone is there for narcotics so they can become three toothed addicts? Then this is definitely the place for you!

Ok, so now that I got that out of my system... There are two doctors and a physician's assistant there. You really do wait hours to see any of them, and there is little to no communication between any of them or their front desk staff. Dr. Oxenberg spent five minutes with my mom when I brought her for follow up from a stroke, during which he had his head down fumbling through her chart the entire time, and then asked why she was a month late having her mammogram. Well, sir, she was busy recovering FROM A STROKE. After numerous bad experiences there, that was the last straw. Also, the doctors quite often fail to close the door when they go in with a patient, so that's a huge confidentiality issue. We've changed primary care physicians, and now that we have a legitimate doctor, I can see so much more clearly how dysfunctional that place actually is.

Decent burger with great bun

In the airport due to travel for leisure - hadn't had a burger in awhile and was thinking I could sacrifice my calorie count for a little beef. Burger 21 did not disappoint on the burger. Juicy burger with melty American on a Hawaiian thick bun with let & tom. Once I was in it, I didn't notice that I hadn't added condiments -  the flavoring was just right.  Got regular fries with it that were not the greatest until you like them done and crunchy. Solving it just changing the oil, changing the temp or pulling the out earlier. 

Free refills on fountain drink which my companion didn't take advantage of but glad it was offered. 

Note: This is in Terminal/Airside C (not in other location in Airside A).

Bottom line, I wish I could give this place more than 2 stars because I love supporting local business. Unfortunately, (without even prefacing with my experience I had here today) when compared with other coffee shops in the area, it's subpar. 

They're under new ownership, and some of the aesthetics of the place have been improved, but the ambiance is still low energy, chairs are rickety, and the air conditioning struggles in this humid summer heat. 

My experience here today wasn't the best, though the barista/chef was friendly. I ordered (and paid for) a turkey breakfast burrito as well as a refill on my lemonade. I waited for an hour before I inquired about my food and the employee told me unfortunately there was miss communication and they'd forgotten my order. She was very apologetic and asked if there was anything I wanted as I had to leave that moment. She also wrote down my name so if I come in again I can get the burrito I paid for. 

Like I said, it pains me because this is my neighborhood, but it would be simply a lie if I gave any more than 2 stars to Epic Cafe as it stands at the moment.

This is located in the Strawberry Square Shopping center with Save-a Lot, KFC and all that.

Their prices are really reasonable, and they deliver for $2.00 delivery charge. I think it's a great choice for breakfast and lunch (they close after lunch hours). 

I've gotten their crab cake breakfast platter, pancakes, Special Cheeseburger, and their breakfast burritos so far. Special cheeseburger was really good (not a frozen patty and you could taste it). 

Breakfast sandwiches (meat egg and cheese) go for 3.25+ tax  and my breakfast burrito was 4.27 including tax.

I wouldn't say this is somewhere you go out of your way for. But if you're in the neighborhood, work around here -- great for breakfast or lunch!

Quality 'indie'-ish showings, convenient parking/validation, nice theater set up, comfy seats, and free advanced screenings. What more could you want in an intimate movie theater choice? 

I'm still trying to decide which Ritz I love the most. And it very well may be this one.

First, I love the concept of the Ritz Theaters and I recommend all 3 of them.

Second, SPOILER ALERT: this theater will most likely not be showing the big-budget action adventure you've been wanting to see...that is by design, and I am OK with it.  However, that indie comedy that caught your eye a few weeks ago or the one that your girlfriend wants to see, will probably be here.

I have had the privilege of seeing Moonrise Kingdom, Argo, Perks of Being a Wallflower, and others here.  Both theaters are large, the seats are very comfortable, and there is plenty of space.  The staff is always friendly and accommodating.  I usually don't get concessions at movies, but I believe your expectations will be met.

They have a deal on Wednesdays: all showings are $6.50.  That is an insane bargain for a large city and I would like to take advantage of it more in 2013!  Even their regular admission prices of $9 or $9.50 aren't unreasonable.  

I would absolutely recommend this theater over the AMC's and UA's of the world: not only because they are classy and well-appointed, but because they show off-beat, non-mainstream movies that we should all take some time to enjoy.
This is my favorite movie theatre. I love to come and watch new indie films. Such a treat

A decent Vietnamese restaurant that is a welcome find in this neighborhood where diversity is somewhat lacking.

It was close to my client's office and street parking was available a block away. Inside it's clean and up-to-date and the menu was easy to browse. Their spicy basket was neatly organized and ready for action.

I ordered Pho Tai Nam (beef briskets and round) large and it came in a large bowl filled with a generous quantity of meat and noodles. 

Noodle wasn't visible because they were all on the bottom, so I had to untangle 'em a bit. This is normal in most Pho joints. 
The meat, while generous in portion also showed signs of pre-made preparation. Few thin slaps were stuck together in the bottom of the bowl, and some chunks were unusually thick. Had a good taste, but it could've been more uniformly sliced and prepared after-order. 

I would give 2 stars except the service was pretty commendable - cashier lady came to me with a spare napkin when she realized that I was using one as an apron to prevent my work shirt from the noodle splatters. Food also came out quickly and I was in-and-out within 15 minutes, no joke. 

While not the best it can be, this is a great place to get a quick Pho in this neighborhood.

Epic Cafe is the kind of cafe that I will ride through the monsoon season to get to, only to find as I sit outside and have a cigarette, soaked, getting offered a light, that the rain stops and I never manage to dry.

I don't know about the food, I have the occasional sandwich and it's delicious, the pastries all look good but I've only had one or two and that was enough to keep me on those alone most times I stop by; the coffee is good as my girlfriend tells me, but I wouldn't know, as I tend to order Chai, which always feels a little watered down and with enough ice to warrant them to put up a sign pointing out that there will be ice in your drink.

The atmosphere is what I come for, the people that tend to be strange or worthwhile, the conversations between strangers. I guess it's nice inside, there's music and the atmosphere is bright and full of life, occasionally if the outside smoking seats are taken I'll plot down and write some on a couch or window seat.

But, outside, in the not-properly covered smoking seats, as the sun beats down on metal tables bolted to the ground (surely I deserve these problems as I am a smoker, no?), listening to people talk about how snowbirds can't drive through rain while someone beats the shit out of someone else for trying to steal their bike in broad daylight, I take a drag from my cigarette and move my chess pieces in awkward angles in a game that has become ridiculous with the hippie sitting by who wanted to play in exchange for teaching me to roll cigarettes "the right way."

Well. Whatever, I enjoy the place, but perhaps I'm one of these hipsters everyone talks about. College students (close to the University), old frugal men (on 4th), everyone stops in and spends a bit. I've always enjoyed doing homework here but get distracted by the atmosphere. Plus they sell a decent selection of American Spirits for far too much.

Love this place, The chicken tikka masala is excellent! Sahara is becoming a bit of an addiction for me, I get their delivery 2-3 times a week. Its cheaper than the competition and they deliver usually within 30 minutes or so.

Tried Tiffin the other day after some recommendations, and I was not impressed at all, considering its reputation. It took over 90 minutes to deliver and the food is way too Americanized... I felt like I was eating spicy italian food. Never again. Eat at Sahara for the authentic, delicious food and prompt, courteous service.

They are absolutely rude here!
The guy at the counter immediately dropped F bombs when a friend went into the store with a mini bike and the counter guy greeted with "get the fu-k out of my  store!!" His aggression with us was totally unnecessary, we even had a group of 8!  He continued with following us out of the store as If looking for a fight.   He also tried to sic hells angels on us, mentioning how "he doesn't call the cops, just Hells Angels". Haha this was the most outrageous experience. The only thing epic about this cafe was how overwhelmingly bad their service is. 
Don't go to this place! It really needs to be shutdown.

This is a nice, clean, small, art house theater. Only four stars because I can't help but compare it to my beloved E Street Cinema in DC. While both are Landmark theaters, E Street serves booze and has much higher-end snacks (wasabi peas, Tim Tams, etc.) than does Ritz East. I understand why they can't serve alcohol here, due to the cracked out alcohol laws in this city, but I was disappointed that they don't have fancy snacks, as I thought that was the norm at Landmark Theaters. They do, however, have a leg up on E Street because they actually have stadium seating! That is a huge plus for me. 

Word to the wise, though - wait to visit Ritz East until something other than Tree of Life is playing. I want my $10 back. Seriously, if you told Tina Fey and Steve Carell to make an independent film as a joke, this is what they would make. I've ever seen a "film" so far up it's own ass.
Would have loved to try this place while in Tucson. Yelp said open til 8:30, arrived at 6:50 to find them closed.

My 10th time getting pick up from here and my husbands , probably like 15th time. I absolutely love the French toast and the turkey sausage patties. My husband and I aren't too fond of the eggs or the grits though. They're unseasoned. The customer service over the phone is great but not so good when you go in to sit down and eat. Our first time going to eat in we sat at a table for 10 minutes without anyone acknowledging us. We had to go up to the counter to find out there aren't any servers. Overall we give them a 3 star rating.

Tucked away off of 2nd street, this theatre does offer the biggest theatre space of all of the Ritz theatres, so you have the best chance of seeing a movie here without having to worry if it is sold out. One small bonus about the concessions--if you buy a large drink and popcorn, you can get free refills if you need it. Then again, if you are consuming more than a full large drink and popcorn, your stomach won't be feeling so hot by the end of the movie.

Quiet environment, okay desserts, great coffee, sometimes a slow environment (mostly because the customers there are so high or "alt" that they have to examine every detail before ordering [i.e. what the cups are made of, what kind of trash bags they use, how often they compost]).

I've been to Ritz Five and this theater. I think I sort of love this one a bit more for no real reason, other than the fact that I took myself on a date here to see Black Swan and had a fabulous time by myself. 

I like that the theatre is tucked back off the street and the little restaurants near it, that I didn't know existed. I thought it would make for a perfect afternoon to walk around olde city, pop in for a movie, sit by the theatre and have some noodles and head home.

I really love the Ritz theatre and that Landmark keeps putting out more indie-styled films at their theaters.

Just experienced my first film at this theater, Moonrise Kingdom. The theater is immaculately clean. It's much larger inside than I ever imagined and very comfortable atmosphere and temperature. I went to a matinee and paid 13.00 for two tickets. I am looking forward to my next visit very soon!!!!
Nice selection of artsy films and great during the festival time but otherwise, this place doesn't have the character of the Ritz Five. It is newer though and more convenient to access.

I was blown away by this tiny little joint in Terminal C at the Tampa Airport.  My expectations were very low, but I needed food and I was intrigued by a tot-based breakfast bowl.  I ordered the bowl on it's own (you have the option to make it a combo, but I opted for Starbucks which is like 10 feet away), and it was $8.02 with tax.  Money well spent!  My order was ready in two or so minutes, and it was fresh and hot.  The tots were crispy, but still moist and flavorful inside.  There was  good amount of ale sauce and green onions on top which boosted the flavor profile, and to my surprise...plenty of scrambled egg.  The bacon was a little blah...I think it was just slightly overdone and maybe cut too small, but overall the taste and presentation were awesome!  Especially considering this is just a little joint in the airport.  I will definitely stop here again for a burger while waiting on my next flight in Tampa.

Not the best meal I have ever had. The food was rather unremarkable. The service is not the best. And the inside of the restaurant is kind of depressing. 
I have eaten here two or three times, but would not recommend to others to try. If you are looking for Mexican in the neighborhood, hit up the Cantina.

I'm staying 5 minutes away at the Hilton and wanted to see Jojo Rabbit so I walked over there. It's a cute, small theater. Prices for tickets are very reasonable. It's a no thrills theater inside which I don't mind. Went on a Thursday night for a 6pm show and it was empty. Maybe 8 people including myself. Would return if im back in town.

HORRIBLE customer service. There is NO reason why I should be greeted with a frown and attitude when you are taking MY money. I won't be back. Food was good, but your front of house is less than desirable.
Best chicken Banh Mi in Bella Vista. You can always catch a soccer match. Champions League is always on.  The coffee is good, hot or cold.

The coffee was terrible but the food was okay.  The best part of about the place was the atmosphere...a relaxed atmosphere for sitting and reading or working on the laptop.  (I only went there once during a stay in Tucson so I'm not sure if I just happened to get an unusually badly made espresso, but I don't think I'd try the coffee again.)
They make the best fried chicken sandwiches here! Super tasty, tender, juicy and thick! Full of flavor and not MSG like CFA's. I always make it a point to grab one before or after a flight.

Love the South Philly Tap Room! It's a real chill atmosphere and the food is great. They have awesome beer on tap as well. Servers and bartenders do a nice job.
I recommend the wild boar tacos and the mac and cheese. They have some really good specials as well. 
They own the coffee shop up the block, Ultimo, which is a great place for coffee and sandwiches.

Boo to this overpriced burger join. Too bad you're forced to eat at one of these high priced low flavor, cold, soggy sweet potato fries. 4.20$ for 12 oz Bud Lite domestic beer. So sad that an airport like Tampa does not offer a finer dining experience for burgers with some affordability for travelers. Won't eat here again. Chicken sucked.

Asked for no lettuce or tomato on my burger (was supposed to come with avocados and several other toppings). My burger came completely plain, which I only realized when I started eating on the flight. Fries were cold. Waste of money.

I just saw Black Swan at this theater.  I really enjoyed my experience.

The layout of the theater is really well done and they have extremely comfortable seats.  We sat against the back wall, dead center under the projector and the seats were great.  I remember commenting on how even the back seats had full travel on their swing.  That's a goo design detail.

It was a touch warm but that might have been because of all the people in there.  Normally theaters are freezing so this was a nice detail.  It was 6 dollar Wednesday and let's face it, seeing a movie for 6 bucks in philly is pretty sweet.

I'll be back here.  I'm a fan.

I've bee here several times and have always had a great experience. 

This morning my wife and I took our dog on a walk along fourth ave and decided to grab breakfast here. 

We like this place a lot because they allow dogs inside! We have a small dog so we thought it wouldn't be obnoxious for us to bring the dog in. 

The servers/order takers are always nice with good attitudes. Always. Maybe it's because the place is just a fun place to work. 

Their food always looks good. But today I ordered hot food. A breakfast burrito with ham. My wife got one too. The burritos are so big! Think Chipotle size. 

I really liked mine and my wife liked hers. 

I ordered a regular coffee and my wife got an almond milk latte. We got them in "for here" cups. I should have asked for to-go cups. 

The food came out relatively quickly. It was hot, fresh and yummy. 

The place also got pretty busy. I like the atmosphere inside, the workers and their dog-friendly policy. 

I'll totally come back!

Oh my yes. It's been far, far too long since that "knowing" experience, the dawn of realization that this, this right here, is a five star Yelp review.

Everything was flawless. The coffee was most excellent. There is a discourse on the wall equating coffee with God. (I'd argue that the former is far more valuable -- but anyway...) 

I learned more here per unit time than I did in college. Finally I can open a bottle with a lighter, and know that there is a shrimp that can see many times more colors than us. I hated school, but this place made me wish for one insane second that I was a grad student again.

The whole experience was so sublime that I nearly forgot that the "ding-ding everything bagel!" was meant for me. It too was delicious.

I travel frequently and have stopped by here a few times. It has been renovated in the last year. I absolutely LOVE their condiment section. I know that seems an odd thing to love, but you should check it out! They do not just have ketchup and mustard. Little cups and lids are also provided so you can easily take them along with you. I have gotten the blue cheese bacon sliders with regular or sweet potato fries. It is a winner in my book! The staff has been friendly and courteous as well. You will find this location to the left of security all the way down on your left. If you get to Starbucks, turn around as it's right across from it. :-)

Such a nostalgic and unchanged early 2000s vibe here at the Ritz East. We came here to watch "The Farewell" -- which I highly recommend -- but for the movie theatre itself I also highly recommend. While the seats are visibly old, the feeling of watching a movie that is played at select theatres in Old City is timeless. I'm excited to come back and visit the related Ritz theatres nearby!
Best banh mi in Philly. This place is closed every Monday. Other than that very nice staff and very good Vietnamese hoagies.

Grad student heaven.  You'll often see people here grading, reading, writing...and painting, hosting drum circles, planning protests, or hanging out with their kids.  Epic really attracts a range of Tucson locals, from homeless folks on 4th to local artists and students.  It's got a great Tucson vibe.

The director of my grad program says that the key to success in grad school is a German concept that loosely translates as "butt-power"--the ability to sit on your butt and get the work done.  This is much easier at Epic, because they have couches and booths, and not just hard wooden chairs like many coffee shops.  The cushions are a little thin, but you can still get a few hours in before your butt starts getting sore and your "butt-power" wanes.  Plus they don't mind if you stay awhile.

Plenty of outlets and free wifi.

The desserts are pricey, but really good and homemade.  My favorite is the banana cream pie.  They give you a fifth of the pie...HUGE. For breakfast, I also love the breakfast couscous.  It's great hot with hot soy milk.

Pretentious ambiance: 

Pretentious ambiance which hosts crowded, annoying hipsters, crowded around old tables, drinking bad coffee and stale food. Works the first time, gets tiring after many visits.  I esp hate the choice of music, some metal crap instead of classical ambiance & the graffiti type colors all over the place reminds me of puke.  Rude employees nearly tossed a cup of coffee on me last time.  Wow, wish I could be as hip as them.

If you use  the rubber chicken that is the bathroom key be sure to wear rubber gloves, as it's been soaked in the toilet/sink and has enough germs to kill a monkey.

I wouldn't eat here often as the kitchen probably looks as bad as the pisser & the employees are about as hygenic as a sewer fly.

TO Epic Cafe:  Turn down the music at night, some people want to read or relax, not listen to rap metal at loud levels.
Amazing burger and the workers where awesome great service. Pice is good for an airport restaurant. Lots of food.

It was cool here, I like the neighborhood and I like that it was part of the Philadelphia Film Festival. 
I saw this movie called Baghead. I loved it. 

Anyway, I liked this place, i like the crowd, i had fun. 

I enjoy independent films and theaters that play them.

Quiet, great study space, large. Decent sized tables with lots of seats, outlets, and WiFi.

Coffee and food are fine but nothing amazing. Vibe is clean and gallery-like with lots of natural lighting.

Overall, a study/reading staple and a nice escape in the city from campus.

[ as a study space ]
Might actually not be the best place to come have a conversation because people are working quietly and would be disturbed by chatter. You could probably get away with a conversation by the window bar, but anything other than quiet whispers would be disruptive at the rooms inside.

Outlets are plentiful. That said, the WiFi is actually quite slow and spotty, probably due to all the people using it. Probably best to bring work that isn't heavily reliant on the internet, although it's certainly workable.

[ décor ]
Big wood tables, comfy chairs with elastic band backs. Definitely an art gallery vibe, with concrete floors, spot lighting, and small framed pieces on the wall, though I didn't find the art itself to be too compelling.

Middle room has dimmer spot lighting, while the room in the back has large windows with lots of sunlight.

[ food and drink ]
Iced latte: according to my friend, terrible

$5 shake: banana, rice milk, and chocolate. Good, but I'm not sure it's worth $5.
 
Coffee: solid. Came in a chipped cup though, almost cut myself

Iced green tea: well done

Also a decent selection of bagels, oatmeal, sandwiches etc. If you come too late in the day though, they will run out of fresh stuff.

[ overall ]
Satisfactory on all fronts, but not blown away. Added to my list of staples.

Quiet lil coffee shop on 4th that is great to get some work done or meet a friend for a cup of coffee. The coffee was tasty and lots of other drinks/snacks/pastries to choose from. The ambiance of Epic is kind of like a living room and quite cozy. Parking (as w/a lot of spots on 4th) can be tricky, but otherwise is a great coffee shop in town!
Best place for banh mi in philly love the dac biet and the chicken is awesome as well!!
Flavor was excellent but the tostadas where very soggy. I suggest putting the beans on the side rather than letting the water from the bean soak everything.

Walking to this restaurant was a little suspect at first... not going to lie, my friend and I were discussing the possibility of us being robbed if we came here after dark. During the day it still is a little shady, but the food and experience are worth it. As soon as we walked in we were taken to a table immediately. greeted with water and menus before we could even pull out our chairs to sit. The restaurant definitely does not reflect the neighborhood its in, with a clean area, tables, and a bound book for the menu my friend and I were shocked. 

I ordered the small ($7.50) Pho Ga and ($4) fried chicken wings that came out relatively quickly. Just like most Pho places the small bowl is more than enough, a huge bowl that could feed someone at least twice. The broth had a light flavor and you can definitely taste the star anise and clove slow-cooked, so you know they know what they're doing. It was refreshing and what was needed on a chilly Sunday morning. They provided plenty of noodles, but i did feel the chicken was a little bland. Using some hoison sauce, sriracha (I like it HOT) and the toppings that come with it (jalapenos, bean sprouts, lime, basil leaves) balanced everything out. The fried chicken wings- to my surprise were really good!! They were the perfect amount of crispiness and were hot and fresh when served. It was lightly seasoned and the chicken was extremely juicy and tender. I expected 5-6 wings with a price so low, but I got 10 wings! definitely bang for your buck! eating those two had me so stuffed, and I definitely would come back here when I want some warm comfort food. four stars bc the pho needed some help but everything else was great! I can't wait to try other things on their menu.

Pros:
-------

Solid, good-value choice for breakfast. Omelettes and scrambled eggs are hearty and substantial, and very reasonably priced ($5 - $7 for 3 eggs, depending on what you order). I sometimes don't finish and have enough for a lunch or second breakfast the next day. Comes with 2 slices of toast, fruit or home fries, and ample condiments (butter, jam, ketchup etc).

French toast is pretty good too, if you're feeling indulgent - comes with ample butter, syrup, and real whipped cream.

**Excellent business judgment calls:
This morning the fruit we got with our eggs wasn't fresh (watermelon was clearly rubbery etc) - we talked to the server and he immediately gave us a fresh fruit salad free of charge and apologized. +brownie points for good customer service!

Cons:
--------

Have never gotten anything else because I don't like falafel and I'm vegetarian. Wait times can be kind of long during busy hours. Coffee here's not very good.

Overall: best value for brunch on campus!

Excellent find!  These guys have been around for two years but new management six months ago.  Personally, I'm a huge fan of fresh fish and seafood.  I ordered there grouper salad and calamari and it was great!  They cook directly in front of you and you can see and taste all the fresh and local ingredients.  I will definitely be back more often!

In order of Ritz Philadelphia theater complexes preferences, they are ordered as such:

Ritz Five
Ritz East
Ritz at the Bourse

I base this list entirely on screen and theater size, because the service and all that jazz across all three theaters is pretty much the same (Landmark Theaters, of course).  Through many a film festival and because I go to these theaters more than I do mainstream movie theaters ( um.  because let's just say, you're never going to find a kid high on sugar running up and down the aisles, or a dude interjecting his commentary on the goings-on on the screen, nor will you find a roaming band of teenagers synchronizing their Iphones and text messaging throughout a film), I've had many an experience at all these theaters, in all the screens.  There's always ample, clean seating, solid sound and image.  The only complaint I would have across the board, is that the bathrooms need to be bigger and have more stalls (especially for the ladies' - why haven't businesses/theaters/concert venues discovered this by now?)

This theater is part of the parking garage that I typically use in case I'm in a rush and running late - you can get discounted parking at both here and Ritz Five (ask at concessions or at the box office) - although they've raised the prices and you have to now fork over $8.  In any event, there's never a wait, - and big plus - less crowds than the other two Ritzes, because 1) the whole place is bigger and  2) there are only two screens.  While Screen 2 is bigger, and has more seating - some seats are missing the actual cushioned set, and the actual screen is not comparatively sized to the size of the huge theater, so you don't get as much of a visceral movie experience here.  The first screen is better sized, but the seating is more crammed and nearly too close to the screen.  All in all, for a still true movie experience, avoid your big box movie theaters, seek refuge in all that is Ritz.

[ summary ]
One of the best places for brunch that is within walking distance of Penn campus. Best items are challah french toast and the eggs benedict florentine. Minus one star for the trouble of getting a table, long wait times, lacklustre coffee, and sometimes running out of ingredients. But worth it, and definitely a must-try for Philly brunch.

[ getting a table ]
** PROTIP - install the NoWait app to put yourself in line without having to call the hostess, and for a live-updated wait time. When you try to get in line over the phone, they have to listen to you say your phone number over alot of background noise - if they get your number wrong and you don't get the text when your table is ready you are SOL. Don't make my rookie mistake!

It's pretty much impossible to just walk in and grab a seat on popular brunch mornings (weekends from 10 to 2pm). Most people opt to call about 45 minutes ahead of time to put their name on the list (don't say "I'd like to make a reservation" - they don't do "reservations") and check with the hostess when you arrive. Make sure you get a confirmation text on your phone. Otherwise you'll never get a table. 

That said, they are pretty timely with their estimates. Explore the rest of the house if you have nothing to do - lots of beautiful rooms and couches to lounge around in, and pool tables on the second floor!

[ food ]
I am pescetarian so I have never tried any of the meats, but my personal go-to is the challah french toast with fruit and the eggs benedict florentine for savoury mornings.

The vegan brunch is decidedly meh. Omelettes are fine but nothing special. Portion sizes are nice and big - you will certainly have leftovers and/or be food coma'd out.

They ran out of lox once when we arrived at 1:30pm :(

Coffee tastes a little weak but you do get free refills.

[ service ]
Friendly and casual vibe. Waiters are usually students so it's entirely possible that a friend will be bussing your table. No complaints here.

[ decor ]
Cute and homely - like someone's living room, but with alot more tables and bustle. The window and balcony seats are lovely, if you can get one.

[ conclusion ]
Grab someone you like, install NoWait, and give it a go on a lazy Sunday morning! Follow up with optional food coma nap. :)

3.5-stars

Anyway, I ordered an iced earl grey tea. It was rather strong but rather good. They blend their other teas and have assorted baked goods.

 I really liked the vibe of this place. It reminded me of Berkeley.

The Ritz East was the ONLY theater in the city that was playing "Bully," and since I had wanted to see the movie ever since before it was released, I saw it as a great opportunity to do that and to check out a theater I had never been to before.  The ticket price was unbeatable--$6.50 for a matinee?? Sign me up!  They also offer student discounts with a valid ID.   The staff was very friendly, and while I didn't buy any concessions, I headed right into the theater, where I was one of only a few people seeing the movie, where old, nostalgic photographs of Philadelphia were displayed before the previews came on.  Very conveniently located to a number of great restaurants and bars in Old City, as well as to Penn's Landing.  Will definitely come back and see another movie provided it's not playing at one of the larger theaters!
Anytime you are in the mood for an independent film, this is a good place to go.

Delicious!!! The Tex-Mex burger was so good. Probably one of the best burgers I ever had.  The sweet potato fries were very good too. A lot of good for your money. Wish they had one of these back home!

Great little coffee shop! The iced coffee is a little weak but I tried the latte here and it was great! I've also tried and highly recommend the everything bagel with cream cheese and the pumpkin loaf warmed. Such a perfect place for studying and getting work done!

Went last night with a few friends to see La La Land. Theater was clean, service was friendly, parking was easy. However, the best part of any movie going experience is the snacking. Before we headed to the theater we debated, "Do we get one large popcorn to split or 3 smalls for ourselves?" "Do we get Gummy Bears or Sour Patch kids?' "Do we drink Cokes or Root Beers?" we headed to the concession stand excited to make our purchases. To our horror we saw a worker rip open a bag of pre-made popcorn and dump it in the popcorn machine! Sad and confused, my friend looked at me and whispered, "well that's depressing". We still bought the large and ate it, but it was cold and left such a hole in my movie going experience. 

Will we be back? Probably. Will we consider smuggling in our own popcorn in our pockets?Probably not (completely impractical). Will we call ahead and see if they have fresh popcorn awaiting our arrival? 100%.
Small local cafe that sells the best vietnamese hoagies.  Natives' favorites for hoagies

I've been ordering from here quite a bit via Postmates. Noddy Toddy is really good. Had the breakfast burrito usually. Today I decided to get an avocado toast on an everything bagel and a muffin. Now I hadn't written a review before because, though everything was good, I didn't feel it was review worthy. Today was different. Surprisingly, it was the muffin that did it. On Postmates they don't give you the option to choose what flavor, but you can choose if you want it vegan or not. CHOOSE VEGAN. They are amazing and I honestly regret getting just one. I'll definitely have to come in store and try out their other flavors but I'm savoring the blueberry one that was sent and getting slightly sad that I just have less than half left as I'm writing this review. EPIC WORK!!!! (Pun intended)
Very good service and excellent tea and lattes. A charming place to get a beverage or snack.

Solid and consistent food. Good flavors, fresh ingredients, and great service. As long as they keep offering fast, quality, delicious food, I'll keep showing up and happily giving them my money. Great work to the Pho Don Team!

It surprised me to learn that the chef is vegan.  This is terrific news for me since I have dietary restrictions and cannot eat anything dairy.  Lindsey our server was wonderful.  She made sure that my food arrived without any dairy.  Usually, I feel that Mexican food is a bit easier for me because it's easy to leave it out - no sour cream on the side or cheese on top,...  This was a fun restaurant and I felt completely comfortable that I was in good hands.  I also felt like I had a fair bit of selection to pick from.  I agree with the other reviewers that it's well done Mexican food.  This restaurant has great atmosphere, terrific service and quality food.  What more can you ask for.  Oh, by the way, I only gave it 4 stars because I ordered a pumpkin margarita and it was only O.K.

I do not profess any expertise in Chinese food, other than knowing what I like and what I don't like.  But based upon the food, service and authenticity, in my view Shang Hai 1 is first rate.  Like many Chinese restaurants the menu is overflowing with choices.  Our party had General Tso's Chicken, a couple of varied chicken dishes, and an eggplant dish.  Everyone in our party of four agreed, that the food was quite good.  Only our son was able to finish his whole meal.  Main courses are accompanied by a bowl of rice.  Place settings include nicely lacquered chopsticks--not the throw away wood ones.  Service was first rate.  Our water glasses and tea cups were never empty.

Two things stood out for me as a visitor.  First, the majority of customers were Chinese or Chinese Americans.  Second, the menu is in Chinese completely, along with English translations.

Putting together an authentic Chinese restaurant, where many local Chinese folks go, the use of the Chinese language, which says even more about having Chinese guests, and first rate service, makes this a first rate place in the eyes of my family and me.  We all happily recommend Shang Hai 1.

It's a bit of time warp here today, but in a very good way. "Stairway to Heaven," "Suite for Judy Blue Eyes," are on the soundtrack to my cold brew coffee and toasted bagel. I watch the streetcar round the corner and admire the way the plant grows in the window. Nice and relaxed. Just exactly what I needed before I hop on that streetcar and continue my Tucson trek.

What a wonderful coffee shop! It has a funky vibe with lots of interesting decorations and such on the walls. Very delicious coffee and pastries as well.... Last time I got a latte (which I enjoyed because it was strong enough without having to add extra shots) and took home a slice of banana creme pie... It held up very well and tasted amazing (especially now in the summer!!). 

The cafe has a variety of other food options, as well as plenty of seating options and free wifi. Great place to do work alone or to enjoy a cup of coffee with friends. I love this place!

Small theater but huge for the budget.  The student discount is fantastic.  The seats are comfortable and there's not much of a crowd most time so you can have your pick.  The place is clean, a big plus.  Not to mention that the type of films showed here you can't find anywhere else in the city.  In conclusion, I love this place.
Amazing service - stayed open late to serve us. Peanut butter mocha cake was AMAZING. coffee was excellent!
I love this place !!! They have awesome pastries and the best coconut tea. The atmosphere is cool too. The employees have always been nice as well.

This place is absolutely amazing. I work at Temple Hospital and love walking over for dinner. They are so nice and the service is top notch. Prices are very manageable and the food is absolutely delicious. Also love the mango smoothies.

What a wonderful movie theater in the heart of Philadelphia. With the expectation of going to a indie movie theater, I did not expect much, but WOW this place exceeds all expectations. The theater is a lot bigger than I expected, the seats are very comfortable and recline back and to top it all off, it is some of the best popcorn I have ever had at a movie theater. My girlfriend needed a Band-Aid after the walk there due to a blister and the staff was quick to help us and in a very friendly manner. Did I mention it was some of the best popcorn I have ever had. I will definitely be back. My only suggestion is that we struggled to find the main entrance as first time visitors and could have benefited from some more signage.
They have the best soft chocolate chip cookies. I used to regularly go down from the Foothills to grab one.

I have be coming here to this small family owned Vietnamese hoagie shop for over 25yrs. Even when I live out of state, I make it point to buy a week supply. Of course they sell other Vietnamese food item, and prices have change over the years, but I will always come back for the Vietnamese Hoagies!

Awful service and room temperature food. I ordered my food and waited about 30 minutes for counter service food. Several of us were waiting for 25-30 minutes. Our orders were not being called and any sort of order and they seemed to forget about some orders and made them only when a customer followed up.

I ordered the Shroom Burger with fries, a soda, and the cheese and ale sauce. 

I asked for more napkins once I finally received my order and she said "no I already put napkins in the bag." There were 5 napkins but I wanted and ended up needing more napkins. 

The fries were cold shoestring fries. The cheese and ale sauce was a cheese sauce filled with green onions and undercooked bacon. The burger was messy and room temperature at best. 

Awful and slow service and room temperature food. Not happy with my meal, the staff, or service.
i like this spot great produce for salsa and for carne cook outs and always very nice customer service. thanks

Awful place, still never want to come back. Horrible service from the get go. They need to hire friendlier staff, esp if the person who runs the cafe is a total jerk. Sadly b/c they're on forth they're bound to get lots of business and continue staying open. Anyone working in a cafe that threatens you with a bike gang is only asking for trouble. I'm above all that, but what goes around comes around.

Had a marvelous dinner at this VERY BYOB-friendly restaurant, where we brought bottles of Hakkaisan Junmai Ginjo Sake, 2011 Le Cailleret Puligny-Montrachet "La Pousse d'Or," and an amazing 1989 Château Lynch Bages (Pauillac) Red Bordeaux (arguably the best vintage of Lynch Bages ever).  We had a wonderful combination of food, which the kitchen chose for us, and they were sensitive to both allergies and aversions - the first time we've been asked the more applicable/logical "aversion" question.  I'm not allergic to chilies, I just don't like them.  What did we eat?

Rhode Island Razor Clam, Trout Roe, Cucumber,  Frozen Buttermilk:  80/100 - tasty, nice cucumber taste, the coldness of the buttermilk component added real interest!

Cured Foie Gras, Kohlrabi, Black Walnut:  95/100, lets a person know COLD foie gras can be delicious, too!  Nice textures, foie gras was very creamy and delicious, and a GENEROUS portion was served.

Wild Burgundy Snails, Shiitake, Spring Onion, Potato:  100/100 - kudos!  Everything about this dish was a delight for the palate, and the foam was such a rich and delicious treat, light, but also rich and creamy.

Maryland Crab, Sea Urchin Custard, Day Lily, Truffle Broth: 90/100, really enjoyed the black garlic croutons, crunchy, crispy, tasty, a real treat!

Halibut Cheek - sorry, the full written description isn't on our text copy - 90/100 - nice crispy crust and properly cooked, a bit sweet, (delightfully so) and still moist.

Lamb Neck, Patience Dock, Stinging Nettle, Wood Ear Mushroom: 100/100 - and we had it paired with A5 Miyazaki beef.  We loved both equally, and that's a real compliment to what the kitchen did with the lamb!  (and another 100/100 for the Miyazaki beef!)

Vanilla-Fromage Blanc Panna Cotta, Delaware Strawberries, Basil - 70/100 - tasted good, but nothing amazing or inspiring.  Paired with a 2007 Selbach-Oster Riesling from the Mosel, in Germany.

Alpha Tolman cheese, Almond Crumble, Huckleberry: 90/100 - nice accompaniment for the 10-year-old Cossart Gordan Bual Madeira, a firm Appenzeller-styled 8-11 month old cows-milk cheese with a washed natural rind made by Jasper Hill Farm in Vermont.  The cheese was so notable I'm including a link to a pdf from the maker's website, if yelp! allows me to:
http://www.jasperhillfarm.com/s/Alpha-Tolman.pdf

The service was impeccable.  They took very good care to keep our glasses supplied with appropriate amounts of the different wines we enjoyed, poured us the types of water we wanted, and were very attentive without being intrusive.  We could have enjoyed things better without the couple drinking Coca-Cola next to us, but you can't take points off for something like that.  We'd also like to note that nobody introduced herself or himself to us, the meal was all about us, and not about the staff, and while we quite liked everyone working there who waited on us, it was great not to have the added element of introductions that other restaurants have done, and which sometimes gets the dining experience to be a bit too much about the server.  One particular Chicago restaurant comes to mind, see my other reviews, I'm sure you can pick it out.

So, all-in-all, we are pleased to say we'd score this fine restaurant a favorable 91.5/100.  If you're lucky enough to get a reservation, be prepared to be wowed!

Great casual atmosphere. Indoor and outdoor bar area. All the food/specials are always very good. Slightly more expensive that comparable local places but it's worth it. Large selection of beer/alcohol, great outdoor area, when the weather is nice.
Definitely some awesome Indian. Slightly to a lot cheaper than Tiffin and Ekta and just as, if not better.

I just wanted to get to my hotel and not have to order food, so I swung by this place on my way to baggage claim. I ordered the current special, the Bayou Burger, a sausage burger with slaw, spicy aioli, and blackened shrimp. It was amazing! Delicious! Messy, but absolutely wonderful. To be honest, I'll probably grab another when I fly out next week. Best food I've ever had in an airport.
In a neighborhood with cookie cutter halal carts and shitty cheesesteak spots I'm honored to have such an amazing spot to grab lunch at. Hands down best restaurant in the neighborhood!
