So I guess, while I'm at it, I will praise their Toddy. Thank you Epic for making damn good Toddy. I hope the construction finishes soon so all the great business on 4th can get their feet back on the ground.

Wich city has the most Mexicans? Give up? food city! This spot has tecate on sale like its going out of style. If you dont like it eat shit and die! This the spot word to your mom who cares bout the long lines and no speak English.
Literally my favorite spot for Pho I always get the steak flank pho and grilled pork vermicelli. The pho has such depth of flavor and the grilled pork is cooked to perfection so delish!

After reading the reviews I decided to make an appointment for my dog Bean that had an eye issue. All the reviews are spot on as Dr. Callahan was so caring and spent the time to figure out the issue. I have been to many vets over the years and finally found the vet to go forward with. Bean's eye is almost completely cleared up in just one day from the medication she gave. Thank you Dr. Callahan and Laurie!

Great food, but the service is terrible. Starting off with the hostesses. Been there a few times now and they never say hello or smile. And the last time we were there our 2 year old daughter had a long hair in the middle of her ice cream which we we told our waitress about, not a  big deal but the least she could have done was apologize. Didn't receive an apology or have it taken off our bill.

We had a birthday party at Wild Katz. Everyone has the best time. Parents were excited that kids were safe and entertained. The staff were courteous and were watching to make sure kids followed the rules. only once did one of the staff members get carried away scolding a kid. Our host was amazing. He quickly helped us set everything up and was extremely kind about letting us know how much time the kids had left. I highly recommend this place. Everything was clean and perfect!

I was really turned off by the aggressive pricing policies of this place. Be ready to be treated like garbage. First, you have to wear grip socks. That is understandable. But they are forcing you to buy their grip socks and can't use grippies you have from other places like Defy. If that is not enough, if you are a parent just watching your kids, you still have to buy a pair of their socks for yourself. That is a the definition of a ripoff. 

If that is not enough, you have to pay for a tiny locker (in defy, big lockers are free). The master locker key is held at the drink kiosk which is usually very busy, so you have to wait in line every time you need something from your locker. 

The insults do not stop here. You have to check out on your way out so they can cut your wristband, to ensure you don't pass it to someone else. Talk about customer care. 

Otherwise, place is ok. They clean very often. The airguns were all broken.

I shouldn't be too critical since they were the only
Place open at the airport at 5a so that's nice. 

The food tasty and pretty well priced for an airport eatery and the lady taking my order was nice. 

But that's why my good review has to stop unfortunately. 

Portions on the small side, and food wait times LONNNNNG. 
I ordered just before their "rush" that occurred and ordered a single burrito.  The kitchen clearly put a priority on sandwhich orders which were FLYING out of the window and burritos were at a stand still. 

13 orders after me went out before I got my burrito.  It was worth the wait, although on the smaller side and prob would have tasted better if the experience matched 

The expeditor never made a mention of the slow wait time, or apologize for the delay she just kept walking by like it was expected. 

Pretty disappointing overall. 

But hey at least I got to eat at 5a I guess.

Horrible service was supposed to move into a unit September 5th went to pick up the keys was told  the unit had been  cleaned but the unit smelled like mold was offered another unit same issue we were given 24 hours to decide if we would be taking the unit multiple tenants at Cheri court have said they have had the same issues I am currently complaining about.. we decide to clean the filthy apartment aNd see if maybe that was the issue when I spoke to the lady the following morning mind you she showed up late September 5th with her baby to give me the Keys she was rude condescending and basically said I should've waited for maintenance to come on the 6th and clean the apartment I explained to her we didn't have the luxury of a leisure move so we tried to make the best and clean the apartment instead of taking the mold infested one she had ready for me i asked if the unit we were taking would be painted or fixed she acted like she was doing me a favor by getting this apartment ready they would not be painting the walls and since I already cleaned there was no need for her maintenance to do it but they would still be taking the full deposit and not crediting my account anything ..... DO NOT RENT FROM RENTAL SOLUTIONS ESPECIALLY PROPERTIES AROUND CHERI COURT NEW PORT RICHEY AREA especially if you have children

After driving around,  I was seeking a local down to earth coffee stop. And I am so glad I found this spot. Coffee was great. Banana bread, corn green chili quiche, bagels and more! A MUST try is the Prickly pear lemonade....so refreshing. Plenty of tables to sit, cute coffee/tea cup decor and just overall good vibes. Give them a try when you're in the area.

Driving out of the city I was lucky to find a parking spot near the cafe. Parking is impossible in South Philly on the weekends. The store owner was very friendly. No menu posted it I knew what I wanted. I ordered the ham and pork roll. 30 secs later my sandwich was ready. after 30 min commute to the grocery store -20 min in the grocery store and then home. Bahn Mi was still fresh and bread crusty on the outside.veggies were fresh with cilantro,cucumbers, and radish pickles, little Mayo. Couple of slices of jalapeño. Delicious- so far the best in Philly! 4 stars as I would like a bit more meat slices as the ends did not have meat in the bite. Def going back.

Dr. Callahan and Lauri are amazing. I have moved to Phoenix and drive all the way to Tucson just to go to Mission Pet.  Dr. Callahan! will never suggest a service that is not needed and is always very caring and to the point on everything she does. I have had to have 2 dogs put down and the staff at Mission Pet made this horrible necessity comfortable  due to their experience and empathy. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!

Food is absolutely delicious and the customer service over the phone is excellent.. I ordered the shrimp pho and asked for it to be spicy.. job well done.. the flavor of the broth is amazing. Very good value of food.. my new favorite Vietnamese place to eat.

I had low expectations going into this lunch. Most of my meals at TPA Airside C have been mediocre at best and some have been downright bad. This place was a bit of a surprise. I was real hungry so I ordered the black and blue burger well done. Since no one else was waiting for food, it arrived quickly after only five minutes. I opened the box and saw a very nice looking burger. The bun was medium brown and was not squished flat like so many. Part of the meat with lettuce, bacon, and sauce was showing. It looked appetizing. 

The flavor was good and they cooked it well done like I requested. I thought the cost was reasonable for the airport at a bit under $10. I don't eat many burgers but I will keep this place in mind for future trips. On a side note, there are a lot of new restaurants, so someone must have gotten the word that the food in this terminal was not good.

Ordered delivery from here tonight while staying with my son at Shriner's Hospital.  The Shrimp Pho (tail-on but deveined) and Bubble Tea were exactly what I was craving!  Perfectly packaged for takeout with separate containers for broth (a full quart) plus Thai basil, lime, sprouts & chiles in a baggie.  Everything was fresh and the pho had good flavor & plenty of spice.  I'll be ordering again!

With movies getting to be 2+ hours, I need a chair that's comfortable. By the end of the movie yesterday, my back and butt were aching. 

Other than the chairs, I had a pleasant experience here. There is a parking garage that you can pay for if you decide to drive to this theater. The theater itself is pretty small - I'm not sure how many theaters but I think less than 5. Concessions were good and reasonable priced for a movie theater!


Because of the chair experience, I don't think I will be returning.

We love locally owned, family run businesses. Mission Pet Clinic is one of these. Dr. Callahan's is a no-nonsense, straight shooter, yet extremely caring. When we brought our very sick cat in to see her, despite the fact that we are just staying in Tucson for the winter, she went above and beyond to thoroughly examine him and explore all possible treatments - giving us the pros and cons of each. Ultimately, he did survive, much to everyone's amazement. We don't feel that he would have made it without Dr. Callahan's expertise and care.  Thank you!!

Stopped here to grab a quick snack before we got on our flight at 6am. Syreeta was awesome! So friendly got my food super quick because it was just the tater tots. Asked if I needed ketchup or salt. I know that's their job but this early it can be hard to remember and be kind! So thank you Syreeta!

Dr. Callahan is one of the most compassionate healthcare providers I have ever met. She has the scientific knowledge and the intuition of a true healer. I wish more people doctors had her gifts. 
She has been my vet for my three cats. She and Lori are a wonderful team. Dr. Callahan has seen me walk through the loss of my beloved cat Cleo, a year later my husband and 6 months later his cat. She is very understanding about my concern and worries about my Patty Cat.
I went there with a friend and the staff was nice, the coffee was good, and the environment was great. I'd go again for sure!

Epic was once the reigning queen of coffee houses in Tucson. Constant construction on 4th Avenue and a host of competitors caused it to fall off that perch and to go through a number of owners over the last several years.
I needed a place that opened at 6 a.m. and they did.
The new owners are pleasent, friendly and enterprising. The muffins are fresh and so are the quiches the coffee is excellent and the service is friendly and prompt. And now they'll make omelets in the morning if you ask them. If you haven't tried Epic for a few years, go back and give them another try I think it'll be worth your while.

BEST BANH MI IN THE MOTHEREFFIN WORLD! I am an avid banh mi eater and this is *the* place. Ba Le is good too, but they overprice and their meat is a bit too fatty for my taste. I am telling you this Banh Mi cafe will not disappoint. 11/10

I am really careful when I rate a place and I must say that perhaps the owners of the Epic Don't really care about these reviews because they feel they have enough transient business to support them on 4th. 

I visited The Epic for the first time last night ans as I was approaching the front door I noticed this large paper take to the door and it was address to the citizens and the students of Tucson. It read " During the impending construction we will suffer greatly financially and asked that we remember them in this time of trouble. 

I went through the front door and went to the register and ordered my coffee to go. I was not very observant when I was handed a cup that was made out of STYRAFOM. I was beside myself, then I looked up and noticed that their place was packed with this stuff. 

Styrafom is really bad stuff. Bad for the body, bad for the environment BAD BAD BAD. ECO PRODUCTS IN BOULDER COLORADO have cups that are made out of corn and potato........................ 

The Coffee? I don't know because I threw it away once I left the store.

Epic is a nice little hipsterish cafe with a mellow atmosphere. Indoor and outdoor seating. Delicious home baked meals and desserts; big mugs for coffee of all kinds and very reasonable prices (why go to Starbucks, when you go support local AND get quality cold and hot beverages.. Okay, there's no drive-through, but still..)

Epic is wonderful to hang out and read or talk or do art. It's friendly, and can be quite busy! Excellent chilling place.

I've had many friends tell me about this small banh mi spot and recommended I try their famous chicken banh mi. The chicken was not what I expected, it was shredded. I don't really like my meats shredded because they tend to be soggy but OMG It wasn't soggy nor dry... it was perfect... It had all the normal banh mi toppings but my favorite has got to be the scallion oil! Who would've thought something so small can be so big. Anyways, I'll def be back for their banh Mi but ask for extra scallion oil this time, I just love it. 

I took off one star because their banh mi thit nuoi was too dry, don't skimp on the pate and butter

Very small operation but excellent pet care.  Our schnauzer got bit while on a RV trip and the staff and vet got us right in and took excellent care of her and helped us carry on with our trip without hassles.  Very reasonably priced too.
First timer i tried several of the different sandwiches the chicken was my favorite it was a small cafe but the customer service prices and vibe was amazing !!

Wonderful Doctor- Dr. Callahan-
She is very patient, knowledgeable, and kind.
If you need a GOOD Veterinarian- She your best bet. 
It's clear this is not just a career to her, she truly loves animals.

Very kind people, not about the money yet quality service. They care about your animal and not "how we can rip you off" like other vets. My dog was put down here and they comforted me throughout and worked things out. Brought my cat in and didn't even charge me for checkup because I adopted! I would recommend everyone to support this clinic! They also do grooming!!! Long story short, they're great people with great service!

This place is like a hidden gem! I've ordered a bunch of different things there (club sandwiches, salad, breakfast sandwiches, coffee, wraps) and everything I've ever ordered has been delicious! The prices are really cheap and the staff/service is so friendly. It's also a nice place to sit down if you have time and they play good music.

This place is an awesome time for kids. My sons had a great time. The staff was fun and friendly, they also continuously sanitized the building and systematically shut down certain play zones for cleaning periodically. We had a blast and will deff be going back soon.
Hands down the best Banh Mi in Philadelphia. Their special Banh Mi & the chicken Banh Mai are must try. It's a take out kinda place so don't expect many seatings here.

I love this place! It's my go to for a bahn mi and coffee but today I walk in and the lady doesn't have a mask on and is coughinggg. As another man there doesn't have one on either. When she sees me come in she puts it on and I was uncomfortable and then I hear more people in the back coughing. I just said to hold off on the food and left. Really disappointed because she didn't even wash her hands and was attempted to making a sandwich. I'm concerned. I love this place a lot but won't be back for a while. I want to let people know.

First time here and my nephew loved it!! They have rock climbing, trampolines, ball pits, and a huge jungle gym. You have to sign a waiver online and it's like 12$ for 1hr of play time, or you could pay more for a longer period of time. They even have areas where you can hold a bday parties. They do require masks, but I noticed several adults not wearing theirs. I know it's hard for the staff to follow these people around and enforce it. They did mention it several times over they loud speaker. They also have a little food area, where you can charge your phone order snacks and drinks. Overall it was a good experience. We will def be back

This has been my go-to spot for over 10 years now. Hands down the best and most authentic banh mi in South Philly! I love that they open early @ 8 am (closed on Mondays) so I can get it for breakfast for me and the fam. I always call in my order for 5 or 6 regular banh mi and my kids are picky and doesn't want veggies in theirs so I ask for it on the side as well as no jalapeño peppers in mine. 

They will customize it however you want and they make it super quick too. Their Vietnamese iced coffee is also really good (and strong!). The owners are very nice, they truly make some delicious banh mi here, the baguette is toasted perfectly, crusty on the outside, soft on the inside and the meats & veggies are always fresh along with their housemade mayo and pate. I love it!

The very best in the Tucson area. I recently moved an hour away but I still drive back to Mission. They have taken care of my pets from simple care like shots to the loss of a pet to recent cancer surgery for my dog. No sales push here. No fancy waiting room. They work their butts off every day. I'm retired and they gave me an affordable price for my dogs cancer surgery. The fancy vets were way out of reach.
Croissants definitely not fresh.  Maybe day old and hard.  Won't be back.  Grocery store quality at best.  Coffee was good.

After skimming the stellar reviews for this place, I wanted to try their food, and I was craving a banh mi, so I ordered a shrimp banh mi and shrimp summer rolls. I'm not exaggerating when I tell you this was the worst banh mi I've ever had. Like, it was a complete horror show.

First off, I was disgusted to find that, upon taking the first bite, the shrimps still had their shells and tails on. Yuck. The bread was soft and laden with mayonnaise and soy sauce, along with copious amounts of black pepper. The soy sauce was a huge problem and reduced the roll to a soggy mess. There were way too many pickled vegetables on there, too, which added even more wetness and overpowering flavor. I don't know how, but everything that could be wrong with this sandwich, was. Nothing was right about it.

This order came to me from UberEats, but let's be clear: all of the issues described were the establishment's fault. Naturally, UE refused my refund, despite the photographic evidence and strong case made for terrible food unfit for consumption. They "shared my concerns with the business," but that accomplished jack shit, as Pho Don never attempted to contact me to rectify the situation.

I will say that the shrimp summer rolls were fresh, tasty, and overall excellent, hence the upgrade from one star to two.

I'd be back to try some pho, albeit reluctantly, but I'm putting a personal ban on their banh mis for the rest of my natural life.

Amazing indoor playground for kids. We frequent "tot time" for kids 5 & under (M- Sat from 9-10a). The place is always clean and the staff is friendly and actually keeps an out for potentially dangerous situations (little ones climbing up the slides etc). They also have a snack bar with coffee & every soda flavor you could want. This is exactly what Tucson needed!
Such a fun little place to bring the kids! This place is different from other jump places because it is smaller/easier to keep the kids safe from getting hurt from other kids and such!

It is a fun spot for kids and good prices! It seems clean, but no real COVID protocol. You just have to wear masks if you are not inside a play place. No cap on guest limit. Unfortunately it's a place for kids that seems to be run by kids. Lots of rude staff, not wearing shoes in the kitchen as well as deciding to stop serving pizza at 3pm when they are still open for hours because they feel like it... the front on weekends for checking in is unorganized and they don't let people know right when they walk in if they have never been they need to ALL fill out a waiver. Also the exit.... yikes. Be careful because there is no staff watching the exit to check who is taking your kids out or locks on the swinging doors if your kid runs that way out of site, it's an easy escape.

Stopped in on the way home because I needed a handheld snack and the reviews looked promising. The place is small and charming - a few seats but you can tell most people order their food to go. I got the chicken banh mi and have to say I was pleasantly surprised at how tasty it was. Nice, crusty bread and the jalapeno and cilantro were fresh and light. 

For less than $6, I'll definitely be back to try all of the sandwiches on the menu. Also need to get my Vietnamese Iced Coffee fix.

Mushy shrimps the consistency of mashed potatoes were in my pho.
I told  the people about the shrimps thar worked there, they said they were probably over cooked. That is all!! They offered nothing no apology nothing!! I had to throw all of them away. Really disappointed this spot is in the hood I guess they think they can give you any type of service.

Wow! This place is a must check out for those needing to find entertainment for kids! My three and seven year old had a blast here! The playgrounds were huge! They have areas specifically for toddlers, smaller kids, etc. they also have a trampoline area, and a climbing area! (30 lb minimum for climbing.) There is a reasonably priced snack bar, although it's a little understaffed, the poor kid was running back and forth and oh so sweet to everyone! We really appreciated his service! You will need to purchase their socks!

My second favorite Ritz theater. while it doesn't have the abundance of movies and theaters that the other 3 offer, it does have the biggest theaters. It also has a nice sized enclave outside that can be relaxing to sit in for the Old City area that it's in. And it has a great Japanese noodle house that is worth checking out if you have time to kill before a movie.
Ritz East is also the Ritz Theater that gets the bulk of the Film Fest movies, due to it's size. And when it does it generally has the high profile movies that have a director or someone that was in it introducing it.

Decent enough for airport food.   They have keto options, double burger on a salad.  Wasn't bad, guess you have to ask for cheese on the burger.  Service was slow, but friendly.  The girl out front can only go as fast as the cook.

Got an order here through UberEats and was disappointed. The shrimp summer roll only had noodles, rice and shrimp. Other places usually add bean sprouts or other things to give it more substance. The deluxe pho was very fatty with a thick layer of oil on the top. There were 4 pieces of meat, a slice of meatball and the hugest chunk of tendon. There was also a small hair intertwined in the tendon. The broth was salty too. It would be better if they didn't combine the hoisin and sriracha in the same sauce container. I was also surprised to see the meat cooked in the same container as the broth. I thought the beef would be raw and separated.
One of the best banh mi places in philly!!!! Located near south street, banh mi is super authentic!! $4.00 for a regular one. LOVE IT!

Cafe Cuong's Chicken Banh Mi is one of my favorite Banh Mis ever. The bread is fresh and just the right amount of chewy, the proportions of the ingredients are just right, they're made fresh, and I love the long skewers of cucumber giving them a satisfying crunch and cooling counter balance to the jalapeños. 

I enjoy it most with one of their iced coffees, while sitting on a bench at Palumbo park or Cianfrani park talking with a loved one.

Stopped on a layover at Tampa airport on a busy and crowded Saturday afternoon. The line to order  was over 8 people deep but moved at a good pace. We were hungry but didn't want to get too stuffed so my husband and I decided to split the Cheesy Slider meal combo which came with 3 sliders, fries and a drink. 

The cashier who took my order was friendly. The wait for our order took over 10 minutes before our # was called. I saw it on the order prep area bagged and heard the employees state a few times that she needed an order of fries. 

Despite our sliders being ready for a while sitting on the counter, they were still very hot and tasty. After waiting so long for our food I thought surely it would be a disappointment but I was mistaken. 

The sliders were so flavorful! They are made with Hawaiian bread rolls and the mini burgers had such wonder fresh off the grill flavor. They were cooked just right. Not too dry and not too under cooked. 

We will certainly try Burger 21 again and recommend you stop by if you are ever on a layover at Tampa Airport!

The one star is for the performers who deserve something.  But the service beyond sucks!  We paid $100 just for the table and not only did service not exist, but it was rude when we tried to get it.  The server didn't check on us for 45 min, when they finally did we ordered food and 45 min later we still didn't have it.  Finally an hour later we chased down our server and asked for the check minus the food we never got and they brought the check with the food still on there  As we're closing our tab they brought out our food IN A TO-GO BOX!  We told them we don't want it anymore, they told us too bad they're charging us for it!

Can I leave this place zero star. The staff was so rude and unprofessional. I and my daughter come here by recommendations from my friends. I don't know where to start and sign up or anything, I asked the staff and she was unhelpful, she talked something about us to another staff. So freaking rude. I will tell all my friends about this . Definitely won't be back.

Cash only. Strong Vietnamese coffee, amazing banh Mi. 

This is a spot that I've selfishly refrained from giving a review on Yelp because I don't want people to find out. That's how amazing their foods (and drinks) are. 

Being a northerner Vietnamese, it's very rare for me to find a spot in Philly that make it like how it authentically taste where I grew up in Vietnam. 

This hole in the wall place has very limited menu and pushes out the most amazing banh mi and Vietnamese iced coffee. Honestly you can point with your eyes closed and wouldn't be disappointed with what that left you, but if I have to pick favorites, they would be the special cold cut and the shredded chicken. They put so much love in their selection of ingredients, everything tasted fresh. The chicken is lean yet moist, the cold cut is stuffed with meat slices. 

If I have a choice, I'd buy banh mi from Cafe Cuong over Ba Le any day no questions asked, but being an only husband and wife team, their opening hours are limited. So sometimes I have to settled for Ba Le.

For airport food, this was pretty good. There aren't many options in this area of the airport and I did see at least two other places that also served burgers, but they weren't rated as highly as this one nor did they have a long line of people waiting. 

I got the bacon cheeseburger meal with fries and the only issue I have is I wish they would have put more of their sauce on the burger. This place is like the best of Five Guys and Shake Shack basically and for about the same price you get a bigger burger and they have waaaaayyyy more options.

I hate to be negative because this food is amazing but the worker putting the orders together was working like a turtle. If you have a good hour before your flight than I suggest coming to this place. The worker putting the orders together looked tired miserable and could care less about the orders. Also she worked very slow.

Funny that Food City is owned by Bashas and AJs. Because Food City seems to be the low end ghetto grocery store, but with prices so ridiculously high it's not funny. Shopping here is a sad thing because of that. People come in here expecting and needing low priced groceries but of a higher quality than a dollar store, and yet they get slapped with high costs. Food City is crummy everywhere, dirty floors, nasty stocking, questionable looking meats and veggies. Everything is suspect at Food City. I feel it is a safety issue going there too from the look of the place and the people. It's better to just go to another regular grocery store and pay the same price or less because Food City is just trashy.

When I hear free skating and $4 rentals, all I know is that I'm down. I have my own skates so I brought those and had a pretty good time. You know what you're paying (or not) for - it's a public area with lots of kids ranging from 5 to 16. The speakers don't have great music and there's screaming from said kids but honestly, I had an awesome time. The people working there are nice, their rental skates are kept pretty well, and the guys around the rink will make sure you're alright if you fall. 

Don't expect it to be the most beautiful rink you've seen or nicest ice you've skated on. It's a decent surface until about 1.5 hours in, free if you have skates, and nice if you just wanna skate in south Philly. If I was a kid growing up, I'd come here all the time. To be honest, I've skated at Bryant Park in NYC before (free too, but $20 for rentals and $10 for a lock to use their lockers) and there's less people here and I probably had just as much fun.
A must try.. always friendly... good always delicious.. and the quantity is very good for the price.. yummy

I've been here a few times now and I'll start off by saying it's pretty good food but the cafe is kind of disgusting. Also each time I've been there they've messed up my order, once an item was missing completely on a take out order and another time there was no avocado in my TBA. They fix it but it's just a bit annoying. Today I went and the bathroom was horrid. Super dirty, the toilet was clogged and smelled so bad. The tables weren't wiped down and had crumbs from previous guests. It sucks that they don't take care of the restaurant because the food is delicious. Everything seems somewhat fresh. The chips has a sell by date that passed but they still tasted fresh. I've only had an americano, I haven't tried many coffee drinks but I see why students like to sit in there on their laptops. Lots of choices for drinks and pastry type things.  Honestly idk with this place. It's like 50/50 for me. My bf and I got a sandwich and a drink (lemonade) and it was almost $30, to me it's a tad over priced but since it's on 4th ave I see why it's like that.

I am a loyal customer to food city and shop there all the time but this is the last time I'm visiting this location. The customer service was beyond terrible. The cashier by the name of Nayeli was very rude to my friend. She gave her a lot of attitude for asking a simple question and then was refusing to sell her alcohol with a vertical ID when the law in AZ is that you can sell alcohol up to 30 days after their 21st birthday, then the ID has to be horizontal. As we proceeded to tell her that it was her 21st birthday she goes "happy birthday i guess". Excuse me? I was in absolute disbelief. I can not believe how they can allow someone so disrespectful and rude to work for them.

The epic cafe is great, the baristas are amazing at what they do and give great customer service! Oh and the pastries are fantasic, I really enjoyed the epic cafe while I was visiting in Tucson! I wish I was closer :)

Went to pho Don for lunch during a weekday. Initial impressions were excellent- the space was clean, well lit, and was obvious the owners put a lot of pride into the restaurant.  The menu covers the standard Vietnamese food with pho, bun, and bahn mi. We went with the bbq pork bun and banh mi. Service was super quick, but you could tell everything was fresh. Both of the dishes were amazing- you could really taste the individual components and fee the crunch of the veggies. We also used the condiments- all of them were clearly new bc the peppers and the sriacha sauce were super hot. In my mind that is a clear sign the owners know their stuff. Highly recommended- I only wish grub hub would deliver their food further south!

I've been going here for years and glad to see they're still open during the pandemic. A lot of my favorite places growing up have closed. 

I really like this place because of their pate and ratio of bread, veges and meat. One of the underrated places that I don't see many people outside of town really talk about. But one of the best banh mi's in the area for sure. Wished they expanded and found a place with better parking, because parking in this area can be rough.

We stumbled upon Pho Don and we're really happy to come across it! We ordered the chicken pho and the grilled pork with vermicelli (bun) to go. Both were fantastic with generous portions for the price. The vermicelli really hit the spot and the broth in the pho is really tasty.

We had wanted to return to Caffé Lucé  (CL) for lattes before we headed out of Tuscon.  However, CL wasn't going to open for another hour when we stopped by, so we found Epic Cafe while we were looking for something else open.  The lattes were served promptly and were almost as good as we'd had the morning before at CL, and they were noticeably less expensive.  We also had a berry scone that was light, flakey, and full of juicy berries.

This was a fun spot for the kids. I thought it was very reasonably priced. The receptionist was friendly and the place was sooo clean, which is a nice change from many kid play spots we've been too. You do have to buy thier socks but you can bring them for the next play. No outside drinks except the refill thermals. But it's clean. Fun and enough to have the kids start their free play which is at 10 a.m most days. Love it here!

Very impressed.  This place is hands down the cleanest child play place I have been to.  The staff was very sweet and had tons of patience with all the kids.  They keep a good eye on them.  One little guy climbed on the outside of the slide and the staff ran over and was able to help him down before the parent made it over.  Someone on here mentioned them cutting off the wrist bands which they clearly do because they check you out with the amount of kids you have.  They are color coded so they know what time you arrived and paid for.  So not sure why that was even something they mentioned. There are tons of cubbies for shoes and the party areas are really cute and set apart.  They have lockers I didn't use one but there are enough for sure.  Kids ate hotdogs and the staff at the food section was really nice.  Absolutely would be back and the price was fair for the time, experience and cleanliness of this place.

Stopped in for brunch around 1230 on a weekday, and it was busy but not crowded. Positive experience from top to bottom- polite staff, timely service and food, excellent tasting meal and coffee. We ordered the scramble with home fries and the sausage gravy cornbread waffle, and thoroughly enjoyed both. Would recommend, will return.

My wife and I drove through Tucson on a road trip and this place was a pleasant surprise, crust is delicious, ingredients are fresh and you rarely find pizzas this good around... make sure you try it out!

This was bar #2 for me during my Erin Express and it was not bad at all!!! There was a DJ who played pretty good music and although the place was crowded it wasn't horrible. I definitely want to go back when it's not as crowded and filled with drunk people (especially drunk college students who say racist, unpleasant words) which made my mood sour, but nothing against the bar itself!!!

I just came here this morning for my mini poodle's rabies vaccine. I told the receptionist at the first desk what I was here for and then was taken to the back to have what I thought was the vaccine... Nope, they preformed an annual exam WITHOUT MY PERMISSION(not due for one yet) and gave her a distemperment vaccine WITHOUT MY PERMISSION and then the doctor had the nerve to talk to me in a condescending fashion, pushing me to get my 3 year old mini poodle neutered... Charged me 90 dollars when I was only supposed to be spending $25. I like 2 blocks away and will NEVER be back.

Not the biggest fan. It's in between two universities- UPenn and Drexel so it's more focused towards college kids than families. I've seen them deny entrance to students who are over 21. So we end up going to Blarneys around the corner. Sometimes they charge a cover which is ridiculous because it's not a club, it's a dive bar. 
Sometimes there's dancing. Or people attempting to play drinking games. There's a zillion TVs blasting. Or they'll try to fit some live entertainment in the corner. It's just not big enough to host students. And the bathrooms are gross. 
I came here once to celebrate my friends 21st. They didn't even care. No happy birthdays or free drinks or maybe a shirt. We went around the corner to another bar and they gave her a free mug. 
I came here another time to celebrate Erin Express- these jerks raised the prices instead of giving out deals. We left to go to Wahoos. 
I've come here on several occasions to give them more chances but I've never been happy. We always leave to go somewhere else. There's better bars in university city if you're looking for a good time

Went here for lunch a few days ago. Memories of my grandmother taking me here as a youngin' to feed ducks came flooding back... and immediately halted as I was chased into the restaurant by an aggressive goose. D:

Great setting and nice building tucked down next to the Wissahickon creek. For the historically inclined they've got an album with lots of information/pictures about the inn. 

The food was pretty good, I had the meatloaf with mashed potatoes and green beans. Reasonable serving, not huge. Came with a little cup of fresh fruit! Also had a bite of the grilled cheese, made with brie, gruyere, bacon and tomato. Good as well, and probably made with at least one stick of butter. 

Prices were reasonable with the most expensive entree being $12 or $13. You could easily pay twice as much to eat somewhere half as nice. 

Definitely a place to take the parents, people visiting from out of town, etc.

In early Oct. 2013 on a lovely fall night my husband and myself decided to try the
Inn for dinner.  Everyone agrees that it is a lovely place to dine.  The scenery and the
peacefulness is totally relaxing.  We have had lunch here many times and always
enjoyed it very much.  We did not enjoy dinner at all.  High priced, bad presentation
and the food was not very good.  We will never have dinner here again but as I said
IT IS A GREAT PLACE FOR LUNCH AND THE MENU IS MUCH BETTER AT LUNCH TIME.  Also, I want to mention that we only eat here in nice weather because we like to have lunch on the porch.

Reserved a table for 8 for my son's small wedding reception (the bride and groom exchanged vows outside the Inn which was fabulous). As others have said, food was terrific but servers were not at all friendly, seemed depressed! Nevertheless, we had a great time.

Definitely a hipster coffee joint, but casual, friendly, clean, and very comfortable.  Fantastic coffee selection, and expertly made pour-overs, French presses, and siphon style.  Also, SUPERB eats. Have only had breakfast so far, but food is exceptionally fresh and delicious with a wide variety.  I especially recommend the Brioche French toast with berries pressed in a waffle iron.
Cute little spot right on Forbidden Drive, yummy food and great atmosphere.  Really feels like you've transported back in time.

This store is the WORST in customer service I have ever seen. 
They are totally full of themselves and treat you really badly, though they are happy to take your money.
I was ready to spend more than $100 for my project and I needed a demo of a stitch - just one stitch -  and the salesgirl would not give me the assistance without me buying a lesson. There were no other customers in the store but she said she was too busy to help me without the lesson. 
So I agreed to buy the lesson and then she said I had to arrange it in advance even tho no one was there. Since I had left work early to do this (she told me on Saturday when she would not help me that I had to come on a weekday) it was a severe blow that she would not help. 
I have tried to buy materials in this store on three separate days and never succeeded as they would not help me. 
What a shame -such TERRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE!! They showed no regard for the effort someone makes to get to the store in town, park the car, and get there during work hours - and then not help me. Who do they think they are - You cannot treat customers like that and think they will not mind.
THIS IS A TERRIBLE TERRIBLE STORE AND YOU SHOULD NOT SHOP THERE.
GIVE YOUR BUSINESS TO ANOTHER SHOP THAT WANTS TO HELP YOU.

Incredibly rude and aloof staff.  Super slow, inadequate service, even if the place is dead.  Food is okay, but overpriced for the simplicity of the menu. Worst of all, the place has TERRIBLE FENG SHUI, which is hilarious since Chhaya means 'shelter, a place of shady tranquility.'  This particular 'haven' is a cramped, stuffy hellacious hole of a place with an inhospitable staff that makes crass remarks about customers, which is a huge turn off.  All that aside, the coffee is pretty good, but I would definitely go to-go.

We had a dilemma on a recent Saturday morning.  We had friends staying with us for a friend's wedding later that day.  We needed a fairly quick breakfast, but wanted something substantial (to make it through the day to cocktail hour) AND it had to be somewhere that was open prior to 1030 am.  Chhya fit the bill.

Unfortunately, we were one of three tables that were sat at the same time.  Because of this, our food took forever (especially since we were on a time crunch).  This is no fault of the cafe's... it was bad timing.  But I felt like I should note this in case you want to visit for a REALLY quick meal.

I ordered a dish that I had eaten here a while back-- an overeasy egg on toast covered with truffle oil dressed argula.  I could eat that meal every day!  Just to note- it isn't the largest dish, so I'd order a side of something else (I got potatoes, which were excellent).

Overall, Chhya is a really cute cafe that has good coffee and tasty food, AND it's in my neighborhood (always a plus).  I would recommend visiting with a party of four or less- this space is extremely small.

even when the place becomes a proper mob scene w/ the young'uns, the servers do their best to keep everyone happy and take care of the regulars. i am always treated well, which is why i've been coming round for 8+ years and continue to do so after having left the neighbourhood. good people = good bar. as important as the service, of course, is what they serve. the food's very good w/ some decent variety, there are always several interesting tap offerings among the more run-of-the-mill sorts and the take-away selection never disappoints. welcome to cavanaugh's! :)

Our favorite lunch place and we've been to pretty much every place of reputation in the city.  I almost hate to help spread the word, but it seems the secret is already out.

I'm not a coffee buff but the coffee I had was great and everyone seemed very happy with their offerings.

The food is fantastic and I have trouble choosing a single brunch option.  I highly recommend their waffle version of huevas rancheros - the corn based waffle is a great variation.  I can also recommend the crepes and pancakes.

Only word of warning is that the place is pretty small and so there is limited seating.  We try to go early (they get bonus points in my book for the early open).

13 years I have been going here for our wedding anniversary. !7 years we have been going as a couple. This year I walked away in tears in the parking lot. My Dinner, the pork chop dish was so over salted it was uneatable. It tasted like someone dumped a salt shaker, the cap fell off, and they brushed it off. We switched plates and he couldn't bear it either. We complained, and they brought back out the same dish. I think they rinsed it off with water and gave it back. Our meal was $73 for two. No drinks, no desert. Normally I wouldn't care because it was a special occasion, but when I walk out hungry, angry and in tears I can not forgive. We will NEVER be back!!!!

Alexa and I were so excited to try the beginner needlepoint class that we've had it on our calendars for over a month.  I am so glad we made it.  Headed to the beginner class yesterday with two friends and what a WONDERFUL experience it was.  The shop itself is so inviting and we were welcomed with coffee and a great selection of teas (not to mention adorable rittenhouse needlepoint glass mugs).  Stephen was so patient with our beginner group (we needed lots of assistance).  We're all going back next week for class 2 and cannot wait!

Worst place Togo for pizza in town wow! Went there with wife and kid to have fun but ended up having a horrible time. Half the games are broken or dated the employees using there phones while people waited in long long lines. One employee standing behind the kid prize counter was playing with a rubix cube wtf! Only one ticket counter machine worked making for a long wait there. Bathrooms filthy. Never again will we go back there!

Excellent time and meal. At outside on the porch with a great view of the creek. Had dinner this past Friday night.  We had the crab cake app, scallop entree, and Filet of Mig with a bottle of Malbec. I highly recommend this place. Great staff and awesome atmosphere.

L'endroit hipster idéal pour un brunch ou un petit dej' dans le south philly. C'est cosy, chaleureux et comme dans beaucoup de cafés, les serveurs sont aux petits soins, et de très bon conseil. Si vous hésitez face au menu, surtout demandez quelles sont leurs recommandations.

Voici les miennes :
- Yogourt parfait. Muesli maison, fruits, yaourt bio. à se damner.
- Mocha. délicieux
- Gaufres (toutes leurs variations sont top)
- Jus d'orange pressé. Rien à dire

Les portions sont assez conséquentes, veillez à ne pas trop vous lâcher sur la commande !

We stepped into this spot one Saturday afternoon for brunch.  It's small, informal and has great service with great food.  The food was so good that even the amount was generous, I couldn't stop at just having the French Toast Waffle, but instead added on a bacon, egg and cheese sandwich on multi-grain bread.  Of course, the now standard, La Columbe coffee was had on the side.  

The environment is relaxed, so it's a good place to head if you have a few hours and are out with friends who want to catch up.  I think we were there for two hours when we went - and they kept our coffees full and let us have a great time decompressing over good coffee and great food.

Highly recommended

Good food, good coffee.  I've had the huevos rancheros waffles - which are great - but the sausage gravy with cornbread waffle and "the kate" are where I think it's at.  May be a little pricey - but a damn tasty treat.

The corn waffles with sausage gravy are just delish. Lots of chunks of sausage in the gravy as there should be, so many places skimp on actual sausage in a sausage gravy. Add a perfectly sunny side egg to it and its a damn good breakfast/brunch/any time meal. For coffee I tried their indian decoction which seems to be a specific method of slow drip brewing finished with steamed milk. The end result was kind of like a really airy frothy latte that had just a touch of sweetness. The quality of the coffee and food was excellent and I will be back.

Very delicious and affordable white pizza, incredible cannoli, tiramisu, and baklava. The delivery driver had to wait like ten minutes before I opened my door but he was still very friendly, patient and kind about it. Very nice business, I also don't get why it only has two stars.

Worst possible delivery service ever. When I called to inquire as to why it was taking so long, I was given four different versions of what I'm sure was the truth. I told the person that this isn't really no way to treat somebody and that it is gone past the time I was promised. Very rude man told me he doesn't care if I ever order from them again. The food from there not too terrific to begin with to put up with this kind of abuse
Excellent service. Owner was very nice. Food was fresh. Similar to New York style pizza. The kitchen is impressively clean. Plus, Cold beer, you can't go wrong! Would definitely return.

Just got married at VG this past weekend, it was a amazing. The staff well exceeded our expectations, especially the wedding/events manager, Tegan. The surroundings are just perfect for any couple that enjoys the outdoors and an intimate setting in a fabulous historical landmark. The food was excellent and VG takes care of so much of the details -- getting all our decorations set-up, food, vendor suggestions. We are so pleased with how this special day turned out, thank you Tegan and the Valley Green staff!!

This park is like a mini get-away from city life. They have several options as far as trail systems for different activities. They have a long gravel road for easy bike riding/ running walking the dog and so on. They also have some pretty sick MTB trails that will test your skills and is a known hot spot for raiding in the city. You can get maps online for the MTB trail system. If you go to the opposite side of the creek there are really good hiking trails that are some what challenging at some points (rocky,steep). It's a really nice place just look out for no parking signs because PPA is always on the prowl on the weekends when it's hard to park.

A friend and I came here for dinner and a few beers. Located in the heart of the University City section of Philly, Cavanaugh's signature is their wings while offering a wide variety of draft and bottle beers along with a nice menu selection from wraps to wings.
We walked in to an empty bar but by the time we left, business had picked up. Multiple TV around the bar provide whatever sports are playing at the time. Our server (Alexis?) was pleasant, friendly and knew the menu well.
I had the Reuben on Rye with mixed veggies and a side of the wings. Our food came out in a reasonable time and was very good. The wings are nice-sized.
Other Info.: A clean restaurant/bar, easy to find and has 6-packs to go. The presence of security in the area gives you a safe feeling while walking around.

I went this past Sunday for Brunch. I had received a gift certificate for Christmas, and I have been anxiously waiting for the right time to use it. 

The location is amazing, we sat outside on the porch it was nice and serene. 

To start I got the soup of the day, scallop, fennel and potato. This was nothing more than a broth. No thickness from potato, No heartiness at all!  To the point my bf states maybe you misunderstood the waitress, and she said scallion instead of scallop. But after hearing 3 different waiters describe the same dish. I was in fact correct when I heard scallop, you just couldn't find or taste them in the soup. 

Next up I ordered I got filet benedict- medium well. What I received was a bloody, filet on one croissant and a grey over cooked filet on the other croissant! Maybe if you put them together, it made it medium well? I understand how a chef's idea of temperature could be different than the patron but this was ridiculous. Each filet was cooked completely different!!!

It was the worst food experience I have ever had!
Small portions huge prices. Plates are too small most of our food ended up on the table. Wrap that shit up b.

I usually don't give out 5 stars but the setting of this restaurant in the middle of a state forest on the edge of Philadelphia is unbeatable.  I was looking for a cool date activity so ended up taking my BF on a hike and then to an early dinner here.  The park itself is beautiful.  I have been several times but never to this restaurant, usually just to swim and hike, but from now on I will skip bringing my lunch/dinner and hit up this place (when I can afford it as it isn't the cheapest place in the world!)

We had an excellent table near the fire place and enjoyed the crackle of the wood against the soft classical music playing.  The crab cake sliders and short rib Mac and Cheese were very  tasty.  We were satiated already BUT we each got a pan roasted chicken with sweet potato puree that was excellent and so worth the stuffed feeling afterwards.  Obviously to full for desert we had to leave but we enjoyed everything along with the fine service.  We will be back.
good pancakes.  bacon side not worth it...2 rashers for $3. place still worth it tho.lots of good drinks
Food is good but overpriced. Coffee products are not good. When they make latte, milk is too hot and there is not creamy, silky foam.

I was in town for work and this place was just slid under my door at the hotel so it was easy. I ordered a veggie calzone with a side of blue cheese. It came covered with olives which I hate and we're not on the menu description. It was also giant and the white sauce was leaking all over the place with a soggy bottom. No side of blue cheese. The mozzarella sticks had a funny taste to them as well. Would not recommend this

Had lunch this afternoon and was amazed by the great food and unique setting.  This gem is tucked away from the city bustle and well worth the 20 minute trip from center city.  Without a doubt, Valley Green is a must-do experience.  A peaceful after-meal quiet walk is just outside the front porch.

I like Girard Vet a lot. They're practical and reasonably priced. I had previously brought my pets to the Penn Vet, where I was charged exorbitant prices for impractical remedies and poor advice. I bring my two dogs to Girard Vet, one rescue, one purebred. We've been through treatments for heart worm (the rescue) and ear infections (the purebred). Both recovered just fine.

The only cons are sometimes long waiting times (which I also experienced at Penn) and the size of the waiting room. It's challenging to keep a 100-pound young dog controlled in a tiny waiting room filled with other animals and people. :)

Note that the doctors have changed at Girard Vet in the last year. There had been a female doctor who was sometimes condescending and unfriendly. She is no longer with Girard Vet. Dr Wilkerson now runs the clinic. https://www.girardvetphila.com/staff

My husband and I had our wedding here and it was amazing. The price was right, the food was delicious, and all the decorations and tables looked wonderful. The weather that day was a little hot but other than that everything else was perfect. Besides having our wedding here, I have gone here as a child with my parents on their wedding anniversary and we always enjoyed it. I recommend this place to anyone that is going to be getting married.

I love the staff and the food. Actually I've been going here since they opened their first location. The coffee cups often leak and the owner can be standoffish and rude. A different vibe than what one would expect from a neighborhood hotspot. A morning stop for a bagel and a coffee takes 20 minutes. Next time I'll take my $20 elsewhere.

Great food, great service. One of my dining companions wanted her eggs cooked longer and not only was the request graciously received, the dish was comped. Fantastic coffee, waffles, eggs, and bagel sandwiches.

Nice staff, mediocre overpriced food. 

For starters, the staff is nice and the service was very good. The server was quite accommodating and helpful. 

The food on the other hand was nothing to write home about. We had the chicken and waffles and the huevos rancheros waffle. Both were bland. The honey gravy that came with the chicken and waffle was nothing special. The chicken was over breaded and the waffle tasted no different than something you would get from the frozen section in the grocery store. 

To make things worse, the food was quite overpriced compared to the good food you can get in the vicinity.
Cute and hip place but not much for the palette. The potatoes were really yummy but I was disappointed in the sandwiches.

In town for the night and ordered some delivery to the hotel. Food was delivered in less than 45 minutes. My wife had the stuffed shells which she said were very good. I had a Greek salad which was also very good but it had something in it that I couldn't figure out what it was. I told my wife it was almost like potato salad.   I finally had to look at the menu to find out what I was eating. I was right, it was potato salad. What a surprise. I have eaten a lot of Greek salads but have never had one with potato salad, however it was very good
We had a lovely lunch, with great service! It's SOOOO beautiful. The prices are great. It's inside the lovely park. I loved it.

I cannot say enough good things about my great experience with a luncheon at the Valley Green Inn.  The luncheon was held on short notice and despite just two days notice went off without any issues despite my miscalculation on start time (we ended up arriving 30 minutes before my estimated time) and my underestimating the number of attendees by about 25.  Maggie was great to work with, although I think I stressed her a little with the underestimate on attendees, sorry about that Maggie.  The setting was wonderful, room comfortably accommodated the nearly 90 people we had in attendance and everyone commented on how delicious the food was.

Thank you again Maggie for making the luncheon planning and execution the easiest thing I had to do that week!

I enjoyed brunch here while visiting home. It's a pretty small place (which I like) with friendly service and a pretty good ambiance. I had the french toast waffle with eggs and turkey sausage. Also tried the savory waffle with sausage gravy. Everything was A+. 

They also have great green tea
Great wings and late-night specials.  I only wish I was still a few years younger and could still enjoy the college girls...

The best Dominican restaurant I've been to in the Tampa area! The most authentic, the best tasting and where the people are the friendliest !! Everyone in our party absolutely loved it!!!! Will definitely come back!

Would not let us sit on the porch for drinks.
Had to have them in the dining room.
Reason given was that they would have to clean up the table after we left.
Does that mean they leave the table in the dining room dirty?
2 drinks = no mess.
Hostess was a frumpy young woman.
No pleasantness at all.
Another couple left w/o ordering because they were left waiting.
Manager needs to wake up.
Did get an excellent Margarita..
This was at 5 PM on Memorial day.

we were here for a wedding not too long ago. the setting is gorgeous, because it sits right along the wissahickon creek. the wedding was all outside under a lovely patio with stone floors and walls. the cocktail hour was throughout the place, but with cold appetizers and extra tables along the front porch. there were also the typical butlered hors d'oeurves like bacon-wrapped scallops. (i know they're frozen - they always are. but like everyone else, i can't get enough bacon-wrapped anything.) there were also stuffed marinated mushrooms, which were really tasty. the cold appetizers included cheeses, cold grilled veggies, hummus, etc. i had never seen hummus for a cocktail hour, but was pleasantly surprised. 

for dinner, my fiance had the filet, which was cooked very well and was very tender - much better than lots of other places that serve random pieces of cow, cut into filet-shaped pieces.  i had the duck. it was very well cooked. quite frankly i don't remember what it came with... because of the open bar. on that note, i will say that the bar is very small. other than that, the place is great for a small affair (less than 100 people). i would love to go back and have a real meal here.

Such a wonderful restaurant! We've had many dishes here - pancakes, waffles, omelettes, salads, soups and sandwiches. Everything is well-prepared and the staff is efficient and attentive. They have a serious coffee bar, which serves every style of coffee brewing imaginable, as well as a wide variety of teas.

Cute place, Nice concept, the oven is gas and seems to heat up the crust nicely, 700 degrees plus!

However not quite the same as the coal and wood ovens on flavor of the crust! 
This is why I didn't give them 5 stars, with that being said, the flavors of the ingredients, and concepts are great! 

Negative is the prices like NYC and LA! 
Not sure Tucson can handle the price point?

I will return when in the area, and refer, but not worth driving from the north side for me!

Good luck!

It's been nearly 2 years and I still giggle with excitement when we get to go to this place.  Since my last entry I've moved across the city, but I do try to still come here when I have time. Chhaya will always be the place I go when I'm craving excellent coffee (and some salivating bacon).

I took my rabbit for a spay at Girard Vet. It was the first time I took her to any vet so I was hesitant. Phone service was fantastic, they gave me lots of info.

On the date, the front desk seemed new, I waited over 15 mins for a drop off. However, They accepted the low cost spay/neuter program, which was fantastic. I just paid a copay for medications.

I never actually saw the doc. A nurse brought bunny out to me at pick up. She gave me pain meds and instructions on how to care for her and told me to call with any issues. It's been 2 days and she's back to herself.

I'm very pleased they took good care of her.

Long time patron, have had some great expreciences & until the past few months some not great ones until my wife and I finally said ok enough, so I will write a review in hopes the owner will see this.  I won't bother with all my past bad experiences but since most of the same issues happening yet again today it should all pretty much be covered:
PROS: 
Love the new place, it's so open an yet cozy at the same time, love sitting in any seat so for ambiance, big win.
CONS: 
- Specials listed - no specials today.
- Wait on weekends - very long and wait staff not very friendly, they kind of approach you like yes, I'm standing at your table so obviously I am here to take your order.
- was in a few weeks ago & ordered the baguette & cheese plate, sorry, we ran out of bread, this was my Mom's 1st experience here so we then just decided to have coffee & went to get lunch down the street.
- They open at 7am, no scones or muffins daily until at LEAST 8:30am, it's gotten to the point where I now call ahead to ask if they are out yet b/c even on some weekdays I have been there as late at 9:30am and still no muffins or scones so why waste time going out of my way on the way to work just to be disappointed.  Finally I asked the waitress today (who pointed out she wasn't a server after my portion of our meal came out 10 mins after my wife's did) and she said the kitchen help doesn't get in until 6:30am so yeah, it's not going to be ready at 7am when we open, I asked her if they were ready yet she said no, I asked if she knew when & her response (without asking the kitchen) was, a while.  So imagine my surprise when half way through my bagel a big plate of muffins & scones comes out of the kitchen. ugh  The time was approx 8:45am.
- our bagels had zero flavor and they should have had cream cheese, avocado, bacon & tomato, I attached pics of the lack of cream cheese and the tomatoes were inedible, seriously wonder how they were even ok putting them on my sandwich.  We would have mentioned this to our server had she come over at any point and asked how our meal was, she was chatting up the customers at the counter though, maybe sit there next time, unless she is also eating, which she was when I tried to get her attn for more cream cheese.
- no check was brought so we go up to the counter to pay, I see the scones & ask about the flavors, she explains, I order a honey almond, it's my fav and here it is lunch time, I walk to my office cafeteria get a nice cup of coffee and get back to my desk to setlle in and guess what, it's NOT honey almond, it's some cinnamon something with either walnuts or pecans, both of which I do not like so... scone, in the trash.  very frustrated.

Thank you Chhaya for another bad experience.  You have finally gone and lost 2 looong time neighborhood patrons due to your staff's lack of attn to detail and the fact that you don't have breakfast pasties available until most of the working world is already at work so any chance of grabbing one in the morning with you coffee is pretty slim.  Is it too much to ask to have friendly prompt service & get a dang pastry with your coffee in the mornings anymore, that's literally all I expect.

I walked from my hotel in over 100 degree heat to eat at Pizza Luna, and it was worth every miserable step.  I ordered the small Neopolitan meatball pizza.  It was far too much for one person, so I ended up taking more than half of it to go.  The tomatoes on the pie were so fresh and lent a nice kick of acidity.  The restaurant is very cute and quaint, so be prepared to be pretty close to the people sitting in the other tables.

I wasn't impressed by the iceberg lettuce, as another reviewer commented on as well. The food was barely warm upon delivery and very stale, as if it had been left out for hours. Very odd. I'm giving one extra star for the delivery service but will not eat here again.

Probably the best place to get Chinese in this area. The price to quality ratio is great. They give a nice amount too, and treat you nicely. I've never had bad service from them, and I order from the quite often. A must try if you live nearby!

I would give this place 5 stars if the hostess want funny about the wait. The place is small and cute. They have a coffee bar the seats about 4 people, which is where we sat. Food was delicious and coffee was very good. When we first asked for a table she said there was a wait of about 15 min although there were tables open, I asked if we could be seated there and she said no because the kitchen would be very backed up with a full house of customers. I thought that was the point of being in business?? Anyways we walked next door to a gift shop, Occasionette, that was super cute and then she said we could be seated at the coffee bar. Food came out quick and hot. Overall I would definitely come back!

Where do I begin ? I been in Tampa Wesley Chapel for 1 1/2 years after living in nyc for 32 years the home to Dominicans. In ny you find a Dominican restaurant in almost every corner. So here in Tampa unless I cook the meals at home I don't find a spot where I live in Wesley Chapel 
And being 4 months prego I had to get my good share of mangu with moris sonando wow I was impressed.
The staff super friendly and very attentive they make you feel super welcomed and confortable will go back to try their other hot meals! 

Must go to spot !!

We ordered 3 dishes- a fish with tostones (fried green plantain) , the grill beef with white rice and a tripe soup. Tripe soup was very testy with good amount of tender tripe and pork feet in there .  The fish and beef were just OK for me. The interior was clean and the service was friendly. The pricing was average.

Have been here for a few Mother's Day brunches which were average.  But had not been here for dinner in many years. Decided to give it a try. Don't do it!!  I had the scallops which are normally one of my favorite foods.  These tasted like scallops in salt water.  Perhaps they are soaked in a salt preservative and the chef forgot to rinse them off.  I could not eat them. They were laying on a soggy risotto that absorbed all the salt water as well.  I actually had to get up twice during the night to drink water!  My husband had crab cakes that did not taste anything like crab. The most peculiar taste that I could not identify. Waitress asked how our food was because she could see that we did not eat it. We did not make a big fuss- just told her the truth.  They only charged us for one entree which was decent.  Seems that it may be ok for brunch and for al fresco dining but would def not suggest dinner. So tired of paying so much for dinner and everything just seems so mediocre!

Tried Chhaya this past Saturday for brunch.  As described by their blackboard "Chhaya" means "shadow" in Sanskrit, "life" in Hebrew and "teahouse" in Japanese.  (How this is three languages I am not certain.)  A small space, it felt cozy but also a bit cramped with closely spaced tables.  There was some pleasant pseudo-electronica playing in the background (I asked the waiter.  Zola Jesus anyone?)

On the blackboard there were lots of options for coffee and how you want it brewed.  Also some tea options and I ended up getting a pretty delicious chai latte ($3).  The brunch menu is pretty excellent.  They have options for quick meals (like yogurt, bagel, etc.) as well as sandwiches and their various waffle options as described by other Yelpers here.

We opted to try the waffles and both went with a special huevos rancheros waffle.  The waffle initially looked small and came on a plate that barely fit the waffle.  It was a tasty cornmeal waffle (fabulous idea) and included black beans, chorizo, hollandaise, avocado with a fried egg on top.  Admittedly it was pretty delicious and more filling than I originally thought it would be.

Did it taste good and was the meal well prepared?  Yes.  But, unfortunately, as far as my normal brunch parameters are concerned, I just don't think it was enough food to be worth the cost of $12.  After a night of even minimal drinking I would have liked a few side dishes for $12.  Also, the 2 servers were busting their humps, but were a bit "inefficient" as my ex-server girlfriend would put it.  Some elements of the meal including the check took awhile.  We weren't in a rush, but considering we were an arms length from the counter you'd think we might have gotten the check a little sooner.

Overall, a good experience, just a tad pricey in my eyes for me to give it a raving review.

I loved this place! Came out for a walk with my boyfriend and grabbed a light dinner. It was a beautiful misty late afternoon and we sat out on the porch and had a fantastic waitress who reminded us very much of a pleasant and slightly whimsical family member. She made us feel as though we were over her house for supper and she answered all of our questions about the menu with enthusiasm. I ended up getting the appetizer she suggested and I absolutely LOVED it. The baked Brie with fruit is to die for. Everything about this place is fantastic. I highly recommend :)

Although, I haven't been here in a while, I've been coming here for years! I had my favorite suicide hot wings. If you enjoy heat, these will definitely do the trick. I also had the Cajun flavored mussels for the first time and I'm so glad I did. I love mussels and they didn't disappoint. Can you say flavor! To help wash it all down, I had the Monday special peach margarita. The flavor was delicious, but it had no kick at all. I'm not s drinker and I felt absolutely nothing. It was more like a peach juice. Nonetheless, it was still delicious and I'll continue to return like I have been for years. Now especially if I'm in the mood for some good mussels in addition to their fantastic hot wings. Might I add, it was late afternoon, we sat in the bar area and the service was great!

My husband and I ate there last week.  AMAZING food!  Everything was super fresh and tasty.  We both had breakfast sandwiches on a delicious whole grain bread and shared a waffle that was just perfect.  Coffee was just how we like it and service was great.  We would totally eat there again.

We are done with Girard Vet Clinic. 

Around the time my dog turned 4 years old, I decided that I wanted to take her to a full-service vet for a complete check-up after mainly doing vet care at clinics in her younger years. When I searched for reasonably-priced veterinarians in my area, GVC kept coming up as the number one result on both Google and Yelp. However, after two years with GVC, my advice to anyone reading this because they need affordable vet care is to look elsewhere. 

My dog has chronic ear infections and has been seen at GVC for ear issues a number of times since I first took her there in late 2014. A couple weeks ago, she developed a fresh infection and I realized that we were about to run out of her prescribed medication so I called GVC for a refill. I was informed that because she "hadn't been seen recently" they would not re-prescribe the medication and that she would need to come in for an appointment and they wanted to see if she would be a candidate for a new treatment that their new vet recommends. I expressed that it would be about 10 days before I would be able to get her in for an appointment and I was concerned about what I would do to keep her comfortable in the meantime. GVC was not moved. I probably should've told them to forget it and called PAWS Wellness Clinic right then but I did not and, for some stupid reason, still did not even when I checked my records and realized that it had actually only been 10 months since she'd last been seen. I am a human and my doctor will re-prescribe ingestible schedule II medications to me as long as I've been seen within a year - yet a vet won't re-prescribe a topical antibiotic to a dog that was seen 10 months ago? How humane.

When GVC called the day before the appointment to confirm, I inquired about the cost of the appointment itself and the new treatment they were recommending, which is called BNT, *and was quoted $20*. I was clear when asking about the cost that I needed to know in order to determine if I could afford it. Flash forward to the next day: I take the morning off to take my dog to GVC. The experience is stressful and hectic as usual due to their tiny waiting room and complete inability to adequately accommodate dogs who are nervous or aggressive around other animals. We are eventually seen by the new vet who tests her ears for bacteria and yeast, applies the BNT, and prescribes an antibiotic and prednisone as well. By the time we checked out, I knew the visit was probably going to cost me more than $100 but was reluctantly okay with it since the infection had gotten so bad in the 10 days since GVC refused to refill the previous prescription that, at that point, I was pretty much willing to do whatever it took to get my dog some relief. 

I go to check out. My total bill is $202. The BNT? $80. I won't walk through my entire exchange with the receptionist/tech who checked me out but suffice it to say she was entirely unsympathetic, even annoyed, and GVT was not willing to adjust the bill even though I was blatantly given incorrect information about the cost of the treatment before I agreed to it - the tech admitted that indeed I probably was quoted $20 since that is the price per dose of BNT. The only option they reluctantly offered me was that I could ease the expense by paying some of the bill then and the rest later.

I opted to pay it all on the spot because I am not planning to go back. They want us to return in two weeks for a re-check and a probable re-application of the BNT but if my dog's infection isn't cleared up within two weeks, we will be going to PAWS and asking them to re-prescribe the old medication.

It doesn't matter what your business is, it is NOT ethical to tell someone that  a service will cost one amount and then charge them four times that amount after the service has been rendered. If you went to a restaurant and ordered a dish listed at $20 on the menu, would you be okay if it was then listed at $80 when your bill came? 

This has been by far our most frustrating (not to mention our most expensive) experience with GVC and, as someone else hinted at in their recent review, I think the new vet may be partly responsible as we did really like Dr. Weiner. But my main reason for writing this review is because, after having been a client for two full years now, I really take issue with the idea that Girard Vet Clinic operates as clinic for pet owners who are low-income, or otherwise cash-strapped. Yes, their base rates are reasonable but don't expect to have any idea what your total bill will be until you check out. And if you try to ask or express a need to know? Expect serious attitude and exasperation from the staff.

My top recommendation for low-cost vet care in Philadelphia is definitely the PAWS Wellness Clinic.

This is my go to place for lattes. Coffee usually runs through me, but not here. Their menu is short, and simple, but the food is good. The cornbread waffle with sausage gravy is worth a try. Get the fried egg on top, don't be cheap. Good for small groups, nothing crazy.

I've been to Chhaya twice now and both times really enjoyed the simplicity of their breakfast.  Smaller menu but the food is very nicely done.  Not oily, no extra fillers, just classic breakfast.  Their coffee selection is amazing.  This time I had a VERY smokey Guatemalan pour over which was so tasty.  Service and ambiance is a nice, peaceful way to start the day.

Nice treat for those who walk the Forbidden Drive trail! 

It was the perfect Saturday to do a two-ish mile walk from the Bell's Mill parking lot. Many were either jogging, biking, sightseeing, and breathing in the nature all around. It's a popular brunch spot, and luckily, there were some tables available on their front porch. It was slightly chilly, but I would have taken an outside table over the inside to do some hardcore people watching. Kids, adults, and dogs were bountiful, and I enjoyed the background and the tranquility of our surroundings.

I ordered the French onion soup, and the grilled cheese sandwich with sweet potato fries. The fries are made in-house! The soup was a warm welcome, and found it pretty much perfect. Not too salty, not too hot, just enough onions, and a very thick layer of cheese. Each spoonful was delicious.

That sandwich! I will want to make this at home. The sandwich is a mix of brie, gruyere, cheddar, and provolone cheeses, caramelized onions, tomatoes, and bacon on grilled Challah bread. Ah-mazing! Since I was going to walk off my meal, it didn't matter how much butter or calories that meal had. I will gladly eat anything with cheese and bacon in the same bite. The chips also need an award because they were salted every so lightly, crispy, and took up more than half my plate. Again, not complaining.

I would recommend this to anyone that seeks outdoor dining. It was definitely worth the four miles.

Criticizing a college dive bar for their food is like criticizing athletes in the special olympics for their talent: it's unfair and mean-spirited. Still, I've got to stick to my guns. Cruel to be kind, you know how it is. Am currently digesting a bruschetta burger with bacon. Still wondering why they put what is clearly a fajita-esque topping on my bruschetta burger (sauteed tomatoes, red and green peppers, and onions). If I'd wanted a fajita burger, I would have ordered one. Burger itself was cooked well, tasty wedge fries. Sorry I can't be more specific. If you've had one mediocre bar meal, you've had them all.

You don't come here for the food, obviously. You come here because you want someplace within drunken-stumbling distance of your place, and because you don't mind taking a shower when you get home. And I'm not referring to having a sweaty dancin' good time, I'm talking about feeling like you're in danger of contracting a low-level illness if you spend any measurable amount of time in here.

We are visiting the Philadelphia area for a while, and visiting friends in the suburbs, so decided to stay for a few days in the Rittenhouse.
