One of the procedures recommended was so extract 4 baby teeth. I was given a price quote of 500 dollars with the opportunity to save 80 dollars if I scheduled it that day. I denied the offer, planning to get a second opinion. The following week, 2 of those teeth fell out and 1 is currently loose.
I have ordered from here 4 times since they opened and everytime was exceptional.  Ingredients are fresh, pizzas are hot and the service is outstanding. I love this place and you will too!
The food isn't too bad, the delivery on occasion something to be desired. They are a good standby and they do offer a nice variety of well prepared food

My dinner guest said the drink should be called "Kettle Two," because it was diluted with an equal amount of H2O.  I didn't dare drink, as I was worried I would drive into a ravine or the hindquarters of a deer with a single sip.  Getting directions out, I took the bridge instead of how I came in off Henry Ave.  I was told I'd run into Walnut Ln. if I went straight, but it turned out to be another Mazeadelphia misadventure.  However, the food was amazing and the fellow diners were few in number and pleasurable to be around.
Espresso is solid. Chia is deliciously spicy. But the almond milk was the richest/flavorful I've ever had.

I came to Meghan for a corrective color after reading good reviews online. The fact that she won 2008 Philly colorist of the year is really what encouraged me to go to AMS. I came in with horrible highlights (bleed marks, stripes) and left with very well blended highlights. Meghan did a wonderful job correcting my color done by my usual salon. She explained everything she was going to do, and seemed very knowledgable and confident. I'm very pleased with how my hair turned out. I'm also pleased with the service. Everyone was professional, friendly, and helpful. I'm fairly sure I will be returning to Meghan in the future for highlights.

Could've given a better review, if me and my friend who were completely sober at the time got denied into the bar cuz my 24 year old friend had a legit ohio license, but got completely denied by the bouncer. Bouncers asked us to pay $10 per head to skip the line, we said no thanks and for that reason we couldn't even get in...wtf

Chhaya is the best brunch place in South Philly. 

You know the saying, "Dont judge a book by its cover," right? Well, that advice applies to Chhaya. From the outside, it looks like a little coffee spot, not unlike dozens of others in South Philly alone.

But go inside, see the menu and wow, will you have a surprise on your hands. Yes, the French pressed coffee is fabulous (among the best in the city, and I've had them all) but what really pleases is the breakfast selection. 

A menu based mostly around waffles isnt exactly ground-breaking. Yes Chhaya's delicious fluffy waffles are the perfect base for a number of delicious, creative plates. 

Are you interested in sweet waffles? Well, you're in luck. Choose from a number of delicious options, including Pumpkin and fruit adorned waffles. And there is a yogurt parfait, which I have not had but looks delicious. 

If you are more inclined to choose a savory breakfast item, Chhaya's got ya covered as well. I had the sausage gravy on a cornbread waffle. My wife got the eggs benedict waffle, which looked amazing. I can tell you the Hollandaise sauce was magnificent. There is also a waffles which comes with vegetarian chili, cheese and a fried egg. Outrageous!

As for the service and environment, there is simply a good feeling in the place. Maybe it is the synergy of a place on the verge of busting out, maybe it is people who really care. I dont know, I just love this spot. 

This is exactly the sort of place my wonderful home of East Passyunk needs more of.

We had our wedding reception there! The place is adorable, it has a great atmosphere, and the scenery is amazing! Food is great as well, and the event planner there pays a lot of attention to detail. Would not recommend it for a summer wedding, as I don't think they provide air conditioning for the venue...

Always find great stuff at Ross for good deals. This Ross is no different. It's pretty big compared to their average stores. There are always great brand name clothing to find for cheap prices. They sell all kinds of things from bathroom, to bedroom to kitchen items in addition to the clothes, shoes, backpacks and luggage.

The location is fantastic--I had several lunches on the porch/patio this summer and really couldn't have asked for a better setting. Where else can you dine in a forest 20 yards from a stream in an Inn that's 150 years old? The food is at least good and sometimes great. The service has been great when it's not crowded and pretty slow when it is crowded. Overall, it's a place that I will go back to again and again.
To have informed care for a member of our family, while at the same time being both reasonable and delivered with thoughtfulness and kindness, is invaluable.  This place offers all this.

I went to this restaurant with my father and cousin about a month ago.  I ordered the crab cakes, and my cousin ordered the steak.  Both of us were quite sick for the days to follow.  We both missed two days of work and the sickness was quite violent.  We told my father of this and he called the restaurant to let them know what happened.  He was blown off completely at first by the manager.  The manager was quite rude to him, and did not offer to do anything about the situation.  My father called back on another occasion and asked for the owner, who matter of factly told my father it was not his problem that both my cousin and I got sick.  My father requested his money back for the dinner, since my cousin and I were not able to keep it down anyway, but was quite clear that he wanted the waitress to keep her tip as she was very attentive, especially considering she was the only waitress working that night.  The owner said he would absolutely not give us any money back, nor would he apologize for the inconvenience.  Frankly, I feel food poisoning is no joke, and the fact that both the owner and the manager do not seem concerned that their restaurant is POISONING people, makes me question how their restaurant is run and managed.  Where do they get their meat?  How long was that crab meat sitting in their kitchen? And furthermore, they should at least admit they made a mistake.  To not apologize at all, not only do I feel these people poisoned me, but that also feels like a slap in the face.  I am strongly encouraging anyone, and everyone, not to go to this restaurant.

Went there for post softball brews and wings. Had a large party but service started off slow. Place was ok but not where I would go to eat. Wings were ok and the blue cheese tasted a bit funky. They don't have a city wide special either!

This is a great spot! Found on yelp, love the vegan/vegetarian options! My boyfriend still got to eat "normal" food like "a man"...but I got my style too. Love that they have oat milk for coffee creamer! Great coffee! The chicken & waffles were good, chicken a little salty but still good. Love it!

Breakfast and brunch at Chhaya is award winning! The selection of tea and french press coffe is stellar. Chhaya offers a cozy cafe atmosphere tucked away on Passyunk Avenue. But the delicious food is a bonus! We have enjoyed Nutella muffins, classic waffles topped with fresh berries or huevos rancheros, and fresh sandwiches, goat cheese wraps, and paninis. My favorite dish may be the Kate sandwich! Every order is more satisfying and tasty than the next. The servers are pleasant, relaxed, and sincerely kind, friendly folks. A local gem! We look forward to our next brunch at Chhaya.

The other night, the weather was finally warm enough to enjoy some al fresco dining! So my husband, 6 month old, and my father-in-law visiting from FL decided to check this place out for the first time. What a surprising delight!

Before the baby, I used to frequent the Wissahickon trail, and I would run past this place over and over, never really thinking to actually dine here. In fact, as we were making our way down the road to the Inn, my father-in-law skeptically commented, "Frances, are you sure there is a restaurant down here??" 

After finding a parking spot (there are two parking lots), we had to walk just a bit... so if you have bad knees, I would recommend parking in the closer parking lot! We had our BOB stroller, so it was actually perfect for us.

We decided to sit down to eat in the patio area, with a nice view of the trail and the creek. I was a little skeptical because we were the only ones there, but it was early evening, and as the time went by, several people began to fill the seats in the patio. The atmosphere was very relaxing, being surrounded by nature while dining was just so delightful and refreshing. We took a peek inside, and the antiqued interior was authentically charming as well.

The food we sampled was satisfactory to good. Because we were not that hungry, we decided to just taste a few small plates. We tried the calamari, the spring rolls, the curried crab cake, and the mussels. Out of everything I would recommend the mussels and the crab, so I cannot speak for the entrees at this point. But the view actually makes the whole meal, and the ambiance alone earns the 4th shining star of this place.

I understand they do cater events, as I've seen weddings in the past as I run by. Not sure if I'd want joggers and cyclists constantly being in the background of all my wedding pictures, though (just my opinion!). 

I'd definitely recommend bringing a date here, and enjoying a romantic stroll on the trail, if the weather permits. At the same time, we were a party of four (including a baby), and the staff still made it comfortable and accommodating for children.

Pros:
Being in the middle of nature
Relaxing and peaceful ambiance
Can be romantic or more family friendly
Food is decent

Cons:
Not easily accessible
Food was just decent (but we only sampled a few plates)

We will definitely be back, and I hope to try some more food, especially BRUNCH!

Cornbread waffles. I never knew about cornbread waffles. This place changed my life with their
taco waffle - chorizo, cheese, salsa, avocado, sour cream on cornbread waffle
and good coffee

oh and staff was pleasant and on their game even on mega busy weekend

make it happen

My family and I recently dined here to celebrate my daughter's graduation from pharmacy school. We were seated in an entirely empty room, at a table for 4. There was not an empty spot at the table and was way too small. I asked for a larger table and was denied stating they were full of reservations. (no one else around). That was fine and we remained uncomfortable. One other table came to be seated by the time we left.
The food was great !
 Our server was the WORST I have ever come across. She was rude from the minute we sat. She did not smile ONE TIME the entire dinner. I believe she thought her job was to get us out of there as soon as possible. She saw we were celebrating this once in a lifetime occasion and never even asked us once what the special occasion was. She made us feel uncomfortable for the entire dinner.. The dinner was over 200.00. We tipped according to her service. Definitely not what it should have been, but more than she deserved. She called my cell phone an hour later and asked why not the proper tip. DUH?????
I have since reported her to the manager. My hope is enough people will call to report her and she will be replaced. She is losing business for this other than for her,  fine food restaurant.

Upon arriving at our much anticipated reservation at this establishment, it was unfortunate to have the most unpleasant server experience as our first time dining with Valley Green. 

Today was Mother's Day. We arrived promptly at 4:30. My family and I stood patiently for about ten minutes before having to, in essence, seat ourselves. Nobody greeted us. The the menus were soggy. With a reservation, we were seated in a silent room more fitting for a funeral home than a Spring holiday. Soon after, we were seated beside a four top with two hyperactive screaming children, no music to buffer the grating sound. I was embarassed, to say the least. 

The food was cold and tables unkempt. Our server was the biggest disappointment of all. It is sad when a restaurant of a specific caliber reaches far below advertised expectations. Rude and condescending are not two words that should come to mind when you are paying someone twenty dollars an hour to pour water. Table 17 for anyone who needs to know.

Thankfully, the dessert buffet and location/hike afterwards made up for the disservice we recieved. Not to mention the buzz from the overpriced cheap wine we bought.
This place is awesome,  the pizza is out of this world. And the raddicio Caesar salad is unbelievable. Service is great. Definitely s must  try,

Hands down the best Dominican Food in Tampa!

If you are in the mood for something different, maybe ethnic food, then try this place out, you will not regret it.

We ordered a Chimichurri (Dominican style Burger), Mofongo with longaniza (Mashed plantains with Pork belly and Dominican style sausage) and grilled chicken and fries for our little one.

Everything was excellent, fresh authentic Dominican food.

We will definitely be back!
The veggie chili waffle sounds strange, but it tastes like being wrapped up in a blanket on the couch watching three hours of The Wire (on a cold day)
This is a good bar to watch a game, have a drink and enjoy some above average bar food!  Lots of beers on tap and a good menu selection.  Overall a good time!

The ambiance of this place is very charming. It feels like it did when I went there 40 years ago and thought it was dreamy. I don't know of any other place that has this degree of cozy, historic charm - and it doesn't even feel contrived. My girlfriend thinks it feels like Bilbo Baggins' house from 'The Hobbit'. (She likes it.)

I've been here twice recently, and once the food seemed just about perfect and the other time it was respectable but unremarkable. The first time I enjoyed a superb vegetable risotto, hot with very fresh tasting vegetables, perfectly seasoned and with a pleasing texture.  The bouillabaisse I had there last night featured an impressive array of seafood, including a tough lobster tail, in a thin layer of dull broth. It would have made a nice photo.. My girlfriend's mushroom risotto was barely warm when it arrived.

The manager of the Valley Green Inn is not particularly friendly or helpful. For our 5:00  pm reservation last night, with more than 3/4 of the tables empty, they could not accommodate a request to sit at a different table - after telling me on the phone, no less, that they don't reserve specific tables for people.

If you were to have told me before Friday the most heavenly of Tuscan-style meatballs from the skies above would float down gracefully onto my plate of waffles in a shaft of light-filled glory... all this with Jeff Buckley's Hallelujah as a musical backdrop, I would never ever have believed it. But, oh it happened. And my gosh it was a beautiful experience that you missed out on. And free wine??? Where am I? I'm sounding like a broken-record, but where's the LA equivalent?? Seriously, details need to come flooding into my Yelp inbox now, please. 

My week-long jaunt on the east coast is proving magical, and this pit-stop has been the highlight so far that it demanded a second visit today for coffee/lunch. Going back to Friday dinner though, the figs w/ blue cheese and prosciutto, a mouth-watering bacon wrapped cheese thing, and an eggplant relish sang to us, ...and I'm not afraid to admit I cried with joy. 

Today, to confirm I wasn't dreaming, I went in again with a friend to show off this discovery--my first taste of expertly-prepared siphon coffee (Intelligentsia in LA needs to get with it!), veggie chili waffles and the moistest of vegan cupcakes I've ever had. They gave us a bag of Chhaya trail mix on the house, and [sigh] ...tears yet again. No shame.

Not to be fooled by name, this is not an Indian restaurant but a great breakfast place. We went on 4th of July weekend and their next door expansion was in works.

Healthy, organic breakfast items and their own baked bread. A great way to start the day!

Decided to give this place a try today in lieu of the other Philadelphia brunch spots and I must say I was glad I did. The wait for a table was typical for a weekend morning / afternoon. The staff was pleasant and prompt. The menu for food was very extensive but I was more impressed with large coffee menu with options of single origin beans as well. I ordered the special stuffed waffle French toast. No longer will I have to choose between French toast or waffles while out brunching. Love the flavor since the neither the French toast or waffle taste was overpowering but rather a nice balance. For my caffeine fix I had a dulce de leche latte which was just the perfect amount of sweet and airy. I got no complaints and will probably be a repeat customer.
My daughter and I get delivery from here almost every week.  Great sushi and Chinese dinners.  LOVE the avocado salad and vegetarian general tso's tofu!

I am so glad I found Chhaya Cafe during my work trip in Philadelphia.  It is a casual cafe with wifi and some amazing sandwiches!!  The staff at the counter are always kind and helpful.  I love my BLT sandwich with a fried egg.  I love it even more because it comes with a small salad with strawberries.  I've also had the smoked salmon sandwich with a fried egg, which was equally great.  But the BLT definitely blew me away!!  I wasn't a big fan of the chai latte..which is why I'm giving it a 4 instead of 5 stars.  But the sandwiches here deserve some praises!  Get some!

Stumbled on this place in 2011 while walking a trail across the way and thought, "Hmmm, you don't saaaay...".

Long story very short: this venue is very beautiful and romantic! I love love love LOVE the idea of a wedding or picnic at this location. 

Talked with Ken briefly about planning an engagement dinner or brunch for my sister and he was totally awesome! Showed me around, explained certain things about the space and was all around friendly. 

I will update this review when I can make sometime to eat here for lunch.
Worst pizza ever! The delivery took about an hour and a half, and the waiting wasn't even worthy, horrible pizza, it was cold, just some pieces of ham and  chewy mass

The coffee is excellent, the food is good, but the service is challenging.  I have yet to ever see the owner greet any of the customers. The servers follow his lead because they rarely acknowledge or greet customers when they enter the restaurant. It would be nice, if just once, the wait staff would ask how the meal was mid way through. Getting water or coffee refilled becomes a chore at times. This could be a great place but it lacks overall consistency with service.

I was staying at a local hotel and had this menu under my door. i decided to order dinner tonight tuesday at around 4pm. while the delivery was fine my food was not. i ordered a childs portion of spaghetti and  meat balls. the size was good but there was about 2 tablespoons of sauce on it. I basically got noodles and some meatballs. I also ordered the pasta famiglia which contained chicken and shrimp the shrimp weren't done and the food was luke warm bordering on cold. Very unappy with my order 2 pasta dishes cost me around 15.00 and it was not worth it

Bf and I decided to have some brunch around the area. So chhaya it was. 

Parking around passyunk stinks. Sometimes you get lucky but sometimes you just gotta take a nice walk to get to your destination. 

Chhaya is a cute but small restaurant. Usually the restaurant gets packed quickly since there isn't many tables, however there are outdoor seating as well. We kinda wanted to eat inside so luckily we were able to get some seats. 

Their menu is not so overwhelming to read from so choosing a meal was easy to pick. I got " the Kate sandwich which consisted of scrambled eggs with roasted tomato, smoked Gouda on wheat bread and a side of strawberry arugula salad. The bf ordered the grilled ham and cheddar with herbed dijonaise and a side of chicken florentine soup. Presentation of the food was on point as well as the food. No complaint with our food since It tasted very good. 

As the place started to get packed , the South Indian decoction I ordered first thing took a while to get to the table. I was told it would take some time but I didn't expect it to get to my table as I finished my food. So I took it to go. This coffee is simply filtered coffee which is a sweet milky coffee made from dark roasted coffee beans.

Upon leaving , the waiter gave me a discount on the coffee since it came to me in the end. I thought that was nice of them. 

Overall experience, I would come back again. Service was good and flavors of the food was great.

This place deserves better review.  I had my sick puppies in and out quick today.  Walk in hours in the am; brilliant!  The vet we saw was super caring with both my puggers and suggested we not get antibiotics, that the kennel cough will run its course, as they showed no signs of anything more.  Office visit $42 per pup, and we had heartworm check while there too. $40 per pup.

Super nice front office staff, and vets were professional.

I absolutely love this place. Definitely the place to go on a nice day to grab a drink and a meal and walk/hike the park. I had the grilled cheese which my heart absolutely MELTS for...(ha..ha)...but seriously - the best grilled cheese I have had probably ever. The prices are of course very up there, but the ambiance, in my opinion, is worth it.
The Prosciutto pizza is delicious! The salad on top is very light but satisfying with a little kick to the pizza sauce. It works and I love it!
This place was a find. Great thin and crispy crust and nice fresh toppings. We had the 2 mediums special, a pitcher and a 2 liter soda for $30. We loved it! Thanks guys!

Seriously.  Megan and Alex are super talented at reading your style/personality and matching it with what you tell them you want.  So many times I am disappointed with stylists and colorists.  I typically have gone to salons just closing my eyes and crossing my fingers that they don't screw up too bad.  I've tried many places since I moved from NYC and while this place is 45 minutes away and a pain to park depending what time of the day...they simply RULE, give you trendy cuts and color, and are worth the trip and $$$ every time.  Thank you for learning the best techniques to keep up with delivering the best product!!  We loyal clients appreciate it.

If I had more money I would want to build something like this in the valley.

What I love about this place:
Live band
Awesome people
Beautiful view of the water
Boat and swan ride
Arcade 
Food vendors
Beers
Hammock 
Colorful Lights
Jumbo games like chess, connect 4 and etc.
And the atmosphere 

Perfect place to hang out after a long day at work.

Chhaya cafe is a really cute, quaint, little cafe very close to my neighborhood. I really have to check out more restaurants by east passyunk since it's so close to my house! Really glad I got to try this place with a couple of friends today.

I thought it was more of a restaurant with full service, but you actually seat yourself and order at the counter (just like most cafés) so I don't know what I was thinking. That was fine though! We chose a couple of dishes from the menu and they were all pretty good.

The sausage gravy on cornbread waffle with fried egg on top was pretty good. I think it could have used more of a breakfast sausage flavor but it was still good (better when I added ketchup lol). My friends got the egg toast which was very interestingly different. It had arugula which tasted like it was tossed in a bit of lemon juice, an over easy egg, and maybe a bit of cheese in between over a ciabatta bread I think. The bread was a bit tough to cut through. I'm not sure how I feel about this dish. It was... different. The best dish was the simple waffle with Nutella and fresh strawberries. Can't ever go wrong with Nutella!! Sandwich was good too with fresh ingredients. The veggie chili was a bit too salty. So salty, we couldn't finish it (they may want to reevaluate the recipe).

Overall, this place was good. I like that it's small and independent. The dishes tasted fresh and prepared well (guess you can't really mess up brunch). I'll definitely come back to support this business!

Right off the bat this place feels like it has a long history of providing cheer and beer for it's happy patrons.  Although I only stayed for lunch while en-route to UFC 133 I had a decent sandwich (rueben special) and an awesome beer (Leinenkugel's Summer Shandy) which I highly recommend on hot days if you like blue moon beer and the bar tender was very pleasant and seamed to know everyone who walked in.  Classy bartenders who know their job in and out and do it with pride are hard to come by.  A few people did ask if they would be showing UFC fights, which they weren't, so hopefully next time they will, but I would definitely go back, hopefully to buy a six pack of summer shandy.

We went here for brunch recently and were seated right away near the cozy fireplace. The food was impeccable and you get a lot of bang for your buck with the prix fixe pricing. The only downside from me was the service, and in all honesty was not that bad. What was odd to me is this isn't a large place but there were two hosts and almost one server for each table (that were occupied). It seemed excessive and there was a lot of standing around by the employees who clearly had not much to do. Also, for essentially having our own waitress, she was very nice but a little bit less than attentive. The busboy cleared our plates, cutlery and essentials very quickly, even though we were going to have more coffee. We had to stir our sugar and cream with the empty packets because we had no spoons and our waitress disappeared. Other than that though, we had a great experience and will definitely come back.

Had to write a great review because I love this place and come here regularly with my boyfriend or roommates. First of all, the staff are all personable and friendly. They really make you feel at home and welcome. Their deals are AMAZING. Where else can you get 6 wings a slice of pizza and a soda for 6.99? (PickUp) Not only that, but everything tastes great too. My favorite are their mild wings, prob one of my favorite places to eat wings. Def. Recommend.
i was in this bar when jfk was killed 11/22/1963. i was under 21 and eating a cheese burgher with a beer. i was 18 and they didn't card me.

Tucked away on E Passyunk Ave in South Philly - this is first and foremost a coffee shop that does a solid brunch. I got a huevos rancheros waffle with chorizo. It was a cornmeal waffle that was thick and filling and was topped off with a runny egg, ground chorizo, beans, and sour cream. It was a filling meal, but the waffle (to me) seemed like it did not go with the savory components quite as well. I also got a chai latte, which was great, especially if you don't like sweeter chai's. They get bonus points for using their own custom concentrate instead of outsourcing it!

A little blip when ordering food to go but Trish came out and rectified the situation immediately.  She went above and beyond.  Shows she cares for their brand and customer experience. 

Rico ... I order carry out once a week at least for the last month...Will continue to support your restaurant.

Went to dinner there the other night, and to my surprise there was a brand new menu. Had all my favorites picked out before hand ... French Onion Soup, Baked Brie & Duck. My mouth was watering, None of the mentioned was on the new menu. So I checked things out & decided on a watermelon salad, paperdelle with exotic mushrooms for my entree. It was soo ....oooo YUMMY. My dinner started with a fresh basket of homemade bread.(had to order a second basket) My husband had cavettelli with spinach pesto.We bother licked our plates clean. Shared a cheesecake to finish off, It was light & fluffy. Also it was a delight to dine outside on the porch, service was friendly & professional. Cannot wait to return. My birthday is in Sept. & that is where I want to celebrate it! We both left the Inn with a full belly & smiles on our faces.
2 DIFFERENT bouncers inappropriately touched 2 of my friends asses while here. maybe they should background check their bouncers. ha ha
Ehhhhh this place is okay. The portions are really small. The place is also small. I rather spend my money elsewhere and get more for my money.

I have gotten taken out from here a few times. The soups are great! The Pad Thai was wonderful. My kids loved there food also, and one of them is very very picky. I'm going to try the sushi next time. Fast and fresh.

My boyfriend and I went in one recent afternoon and we were completely ignored by the guy behind the counter. He didn't even acknowledge that the door had opened. He went about his business making some beverage or something. After about two minutes, he looked at us finally and said, "just a minute." We'd already been standing there longer than that! About three more minutes passed and he deigned to look at us again. This time he asked how he could help us. I said we'd like a table. He said, "there's a twenty minute wait." I made sure he understood we weren't leaving because of the twenty minute wait; we were leaving because of the five minute wait to find out about the twenty minute wait. I usually go to Black & Brew but on this day I wanted to try something different on the Avenue. Instead we ended up at Black & Brew where, as usual, we were waited on right away by someone who greeted us as soon as we walked through the door!

Love this vet. Dr. Balzer can be really intense and abrupt at times, but has taken great care of my many pets over the last few years. She saved my senior pit bull's life - twice! Have recently worked with Dr. Weiner who is great. This place definitely isn't for everyone, but I'd recommend it to anyone who has some thick skin.

We went to busch gardens and received a flyer for Pizza Famiglia at our hotel. I went and picked it up. It was waiting on my arrival. We got a large pizza and salad. It was quite economical aound 17$. All the food was good. Nothing exceptional. Better than fast food pizza, but not great.

Favorite brunch spot in the area. Super friendly and awesome service. Great coffee and food, lots of vegetarian options. My favorite dishes are probably the bagel sandwich, truffled egg toast, and sausage gravy cornbread waffle.
The best breakfast place I have been to in a long time. I love the new space. After having been away for a few years the flavors and ambiance are just as remembered. Can't wait to come back

I felt the Irish revenge when I got home and sat on the toilet. I used to regularly come to this place for their wings (which are not even great but benefit from a local monopoly on the supply) and regularly get sick when I get home. I initially struggled to make the simple, yet evident link to the consumption of Cavanaugh's food. However, my strong perspicacity and my ability to read health reviews made by local agencies prompted me to consider the link of my bowel movements and my time at this "restaurant". Hopefully, mice shit won't appear again in the realm of ingredients.

One of the gems that makes Philly a special place to live or visit! A beautiful setting (5 stars) with good (3.5 stars), but not great food. 

The Valley Green Inn is a late 1700s inn - still open for business. It sits in the middle of Wissahickon Park, a picturesque ravine with a babbling creek, bike, hiking and horse trails and a covered bridge. On a fine day, sit on the porch and enjoy the scenery. If you are nearby, don't miss this gem!

I was torn between 4 and 5 stars. 

First, this is a wonderful place to eat. The location is terrific. We hike about 5 miles to Valley Green, indulge in a sumptuous feast, and hike out a little over 4 miles. And it's a lucky thing because we eat rich foods. Their soups are rich, creamy, and to die for.

The price is up there--way up there. But the atmosphere is unrivaled (especially in the winter) by many places in urban areas. You feel like you're somewhere in Europe or old'n USA. 

Again, the food is very, very good. I'm not a huge fan of their brunch frittata, so don't order it. But everything else I've eaten, mostly their soups and muffin/bread basket, are top notch.

This is why I visit several times a year.
great new location... carousel is free.. chicken wings are awesome. excellent location if you have children.

Dr. Wilkinson, Albert, and the staff here are top notch and go the extra mile to make sure my pets are comfortable and healthy. I recommend this clinic to everyone. We had a very serious emergency with our cat Princess Penelope this past month that only Girard Vetinary Clinic was able to resolve, and they did it at literally a fourth of the cost that we spent at the emergency room. They've been our regular vet for check ups, and they've also performed a successful dental surgery for our cat in the past year. This clinic continues to astound me with its professionalism and genuine care. They are budget friendly, too!

My wife and I recently ate here for a special occasion. My verbal evaluations to her have encouraged me to post a yelp review. My perception of Valley Green Inn is that of high-scale dining and therefore my expectations are higher than if I were to eat at a regular national chain like Outback, Chili's, or Red Lobster. 

Menu:  Both of our menus had wet and wrinkled paper inside the covers along with other slightly older stains and wrinkles, making me feel like I'm being served used tableware and dining leftovers.
The lunch menu at first glance looked appropriately sized, but after further inspection, looking for something desirable, I found that my options were strictly limited due to a combination of my kosher lifestyle and their numerous menu items with pig products and other treyf. I think I was limited to three options after deducting everything that had either bacon, pork, catfish, or more bacon. Sure I could have ordered an item w/o bacon, but I'd still be paying for it, and I don't like picking apart ensembles while up-scale dining. One of the three resulting menu items happened to be a tuna salad sandwich, and since I was already ordering the salmon salad, I felt my options for my lunch entrée way too limited and therefore sorely disappointing.


Food -- 

Appetizer: French onion soup. Very rustic and potent. The cheese was flavorful but overly chewy. I ordered it because I wanted to try it, not having had much of it in my lifetime; sort of a new experience. The soup was an experience, but I won't order it again out of palate preferences. 

Salad: Salmon salad. This is the second time I've ordered this item. It tastes great. At first glance one might find the three slices of smoked salmon a little skimpy but since they're packed with fishy flavor, it's plenty to go through along with the rest of the salad, consisting mostly of garden mix and a heap of capers.

Entrée: Steak. I asked it to be cooked medium, but it came out a little less than rare as it was still sorely bleeding in the majority. Though disappointed, I was hungry and didn't have it returned. The size of the meal was a tad small, but filling nonetheless, that is, after an appetizer and salad. Yet, I had still wished for more mashed potatoes and/or haricot verts, since the steak portions are probably strict. The flavor of the steak and its dark sauce is wonderfully mouthwatering. For that alone I'd order the entrée again if I were to happen here upon an occasion.

Dessert: Crème brûlée. Due to the occasion and by our request, we were granted dessert on the house. This was surprisingly delightful, with the bottom of three layers carrying what looked to be loaded with vanilla beans.

Drink: Hot cider with rum. Ghastly. Perhaps I shouldn't compare every cider I have with Normandy's cider, but even if I don't in this case, the cider I had here was extremely bitter with an aftertaste akin to bile. I'm sure there are people out there who love it, like our waitress who professed having it often, but for my wife and me, it wasn't palatable.


Service: I was asked multiple times if I had reservations, which I did, even after we sat down, as if we shouldn't be present or be allowed to eat there. The way it was asked made us feel a tad unwelcome and out of place.
Our waitress was cordial, professional, and timely. The busboy, however, left us with a poor impression. For instance, when filling my glass with more water I asked for no ice, so the bus boy was careful in putting only half the amount of ice cubes instead of the regular lot I would have received had I not said anything. 'No ice' for me really means water that hasn't had ice in it, but even more so, water that doesn't have ice in it. He didn't even acknowledge his oversight or carelessness.


Dining Environment: While cleaning used tables and setting up tableware, the busboy placed items on the table as if he were setting up game-night with the fellas. Utensils, napkins, and much of the rest was plopped on the table, and often across the table, without any regard to detail or order, that which I associate with fine dining. 
 There were festive Christmas decorations dressing fireplace mantles and other holiday accoutrements. Tasteful and charming, these added an appropriate sense of celebration and glad tidings.


Price: I think the most expensive lunch menu item was the steak entrée, running about $18. I was expecting higher prices, so was pleased to see more affordable ranges for most everything offered. For two appetizers, two salads and two entrées, after tax and tip, we spent about a hundred dollars.


Overall, we were satisfied with dinner at Valley Green Inn. After this experience I'm reconsidering how up-scale I regard this place and may have to lower my expectations a little, which may, as a result, move me/us to find a different location for special occasions, and come back here when we just want to eat somewhere nice... with a hundred bucks to spare.

Service was very slow. It seems to me that the bartenders don't care about the drinks in front of me. All staff were watching football instead of serving people. Additionally, I was asked twice to switch my channel.
excellent place for booze please come here its great

I have been taking my dogs here for several years. There have been a lot of changes over that time and it's gotten better & better. They treat my dogs and me like family. Having a place I trust will provide exceptional care and treatment (and LOVE) is such a godsend. Having tried other options on the Main Line and in the City, no other place has come close to what the Doctors and staff at Girard have consistently given us. Do yourself and your loved fur buddies a favor and get to know Girard.

Yoo college!  Everyone in this bar is in it.  Wednesday they have 75cent drinks til 12.  There's over 40 TV's in one room - plus a huge projector. It'd be a nice place to watch a game - esp. if you live in the area.  Def fun on Erin Express.

Consistently excellent tacos. The drinks are great, as is the service. The only negative is you might have to wait to get a seat on busy nights. Also, $1 taco night every week is a real steal. Cash only.

If you are looking for everything and anything you could possibly want in terms of Needlepoint, this is the store for you and if they don't have it, they will find a way to get it for you.  The owners are definitely "out of the box" thinkers who will do what is right to service their customers.  

The other unique aspect of this spot is the community that is felt there.  You will meet people from all walks of life that are brought together to craft and there is truly a sense of caring and community.  You can stop in at any hour and sit down and have a sip of tea or water and just relax in the creative energy and spirit of the environment!

They slipped a flier under my hotel door. Wanted someone who delivered and thought I would give them a shot as it was not a chain restaurant. 

Ordered 2 pizzas and some salads. 

Pizza was average. Salad was basic but fresh. 

Delivery was estimated at 45 min and took 1 hour and 5 minutes. Not cool. 

They forgot extras that I requested: marinara and parmesan cheese. 

I would not order from them again if I lived here.

I'm really impressed by this place. The food is inventive and satisfying, great coffee, and cute interior.  Last time I was there, I got the arugula and egg on brioche. Simple ingredients, but really tasty. My boyfriend got the cornbread waffle w/ sausage gravy which he really enjoyed as well. Our server was friendly and attentive...all things combined, what else do you need from a restaurant?

Literally every part of our breakfast was perfect.

COFFEE:

PROS:
They list their available coffees from lightest to darkest.
Nothing comes from an urn, only Hand pour, syphon, etc.
The people serving the coffee actually know what they are doing/talking about which is refreshing.

Mama-bear had a chai latte which she really enjoyed.

CONS:
none

BREAKFAST:

I had the cornbread waffle with sausage gravy it was incredible. There was a very slight grittiness but it was actually enjoyable. The sausage gravy was just wonderful. It never clotted up or separated, it held it's consistency and the sausage was really high quality.

Wifey had the Oat+wheat pancakes with berries and they were super good. There were not just berries atop them, but included between each cake. They had a great texture and the berries (black, blue, rasp) were all plump and sweet.

It's worth noting that she also got a scrambled egg on the side which she described as "the most perfect scrambled egg i've ever had in a restaurant." That may seem like a small thing to you, but I consider little stuff like that essential to a good restaurant.

Mama-bear had the parfait, which was a kind of lame choice, but it was really yummy with good granola + yogurt + the same berries as the pancakes.

Absolutely amazing place for brunch!! Had eggs cocotte which was delicious , also tried waffle french toast which was great as well. One thing to note that unlike other places for brunch the potion sizes here are very appropriate. You don't regret the whole day after having french toasts if you know what I mean.. Also I used Level Up to pay and saved 2 dollars which was great as well. I would def return to try some thing new.

The answer is YES. Yes, I want a waffle. And I'll have one at any given time of the day. Cause that's what I do now. I don't have to make threats, I can go to Chhaya.

Let me assure you, a waffle is the perfect snack. This statement is  especially true as Chhaya offers them in both savory and sweet incarnations. I do tend to stick with the sweetness, but I've had shared tastes of sausagey concoctions, or huevos rancheros, even. 

I do so love a waffle, and their coffee is good stuff too. This is a lovely Passyunk spot for quiet, little break and your daily waffle.

Simple food done well.

It's a small place which gets packed on weekends so make sure you call ahead.  I generally order the chai latte and either The Kate (egg sandwich with avocado and arugula) or the waffles with berries.  It's a great place to relax, enjoy the artwork which changes somewhat frequently, and enjoy a solid brunch.  Portions aren't too large so you don't walk out feeling terrible for the rest of the day but you can be satisfied.  Parking in this area isn't always easy and driving here isn't too fun but it's worth the aggravation.  I have no complaints about the service I've ever received there.  The bill comes rolled up in this miniature espresso cup so that's cutesy too.

Too bad I don't live a little closer so I could just hang out here for a few hours every day.  Cheers.

this place kind of run down but its a good place to go if you want to catch a game or sports event on tv.  TVs are everywhere. 

Food-wise, the wings (hot and honey) were really good.  Delicious.  
I ordered the grilled cheese for dinner and with 5 different cheeses, I should have known it would be greasy but it ended up being too greasy for me.  fries were just ok. 
If I were to go back, I will definitely stick to the wings.

Don't waste your time with this place.  I stopped in on a Monday night after checking their website for specials.  $1.50 well drinks and 1/2 price appetizers, which were listed as "every day specials,"  seemed like a pretty good deal.  After ordering drinks and food, however, the check showed well drinks were actually $3 and appetizers were discounted only 25%.  Apparently it had all been changed, but not updated on the website.  The service was lacking.  This is hard to tolerate when there's two bartenders and about ten customers.  I can't imagine how they handle a crowd.  The food does nothing to redeem this place, either.  The wings (3rd degree) didn't have a lot of flavor.  They were overly salty for the most part.  Same goes for the spinach and crab dip.  In addition the dip, which was supposed to have some kind of garlic toast, was served with a random assortment of crackers and two cookies.  Yes, cookies.  Some sort of honey-graham, I think.  For spinach and crab dip.  Note:  They did comp two well drinks to compensate for the price difference and removed the spinach and cookie dip from the check.

We went without a reservation on a Sunday afternoon during the dinner hours.  We were able to sit on the porch along with a number of other diners who did not have reservations.  Our waitress wasn't rude, but she was definitely unpleasant bordering on grumpy.  The Caesar salad had grit in it like the lettuce wasn't washed properly.  When we informed them of this, they did take one salad off of the bill (which was not the point of our informing them, but certainly nice).  

The menu looks great and I would try it again, but the atmosphere tries to be fine dining in an area that is more casual on a weekend afternoon.  A bit stuffy and all of the staff seemed harried and not friendly.

The wings were pretty darn delicious.  The rest of the food was ...meh.  I got a fishbowl that tasted just like every highschool party I ever went to, pucker and watermelon something.( That wasn't a compliment just so you know.) Its a great location, and its pretty nice inside, just probably wont make a vist next time in town.
Unbelievable coffee and what a great bagel - sounds crazy, but both were really, really amazing.  I'd love to go back to sit and eat.

i must say, tho i love waffles. they rarely satisfy me as a main plate; i always feel i have to get some sort of egg or meat concoction to say i had a proper brunch. as such, i rarely order them... as my meal. i DO, however, order it as a SECOND dish. and often. (yes, fatty fats fats).

none of this matters at chhaya because the waffles are topped with savory or sweet delicious things that make you forget you are, in fact, eating just this carb-y thing. 

the VEGGIE CHILI WAFFLE is everything you want it to be. the spicy kick is just kick-y enough and the fried egg is GLORIOUS. of course, no great dish would be complete without melting cheese on top. all these things topped 2 square cornmeal waffles that were quite filling and savory.

the waffle twist on the huevos rancheros waffles are made them a must-order dish. 

the eggs benedict waffles are also delicious, but the portion size was definitely much smaller than some of the other items. 

for those of you concerned about needing an enormous quantity of food to start your day, i'd go with the veggie chili waffle or one of the sweet topped ones. it seemed that some of the specials were smaller.  

the coffee is certainly awesome, but a bit pricey, as expected. on weekends you can get the bottomless coffee which is a great deal.

I have to admit, when I looked outside this morning, I debated whether or not the free beginner's class at Rittenhouse Needlepoint was enough to drag me out of my cozy bed on a snowy Saturday morning. I was meeting fellow Yelper and friend Leah, who I love hanging out with, so I decided to strap on my boots and down vest and take on the elements. I was beyond thrilled with my experience. The owners are amazing and funny and incredibly patient, especially with our Beginner's group. We sat around a table and chatted, kind of a modern day quilting bee. There are samples of current projects throughout the store and many Philadelphia-inspired options for patrons to select from. It was the perfect thing on a snowy Saturday, we were offered tea and coffee and Stephen taught us the Continental stitch. I cannot wait to go back next Saturday! I want to be good enough to start a project soon!

I may be dating myself - but I went here when I was in college at Penn in the mid nineties.  Cav's is still kicking (and they also have the "River Deck".

It's your basic bar.  Bar food.  Bar Music.  Frat-boy (and college-gals) crowd.  Meat-marketing and bozzing of the basest nature.  Decent wings as I recall. 

I preferred Smokey Joe's.

Got delivery from this place. Ordered a medium Hawaiian pizza, hot wings, 2 liter of Pepsi and a gyro. Delivery time was quoted at 30 to 50 minutes. Took just over an hour, and they forgot my 2 liter of soda. Pizza was pretty good - Crust, and sauce was good. Ham was mushy... Hot wings were fantastic! Gyro was not very good at all.. I know, should have known better than to order a gyro from a pizza place right? Came to $29. 
The price was right on the wings. I recommend the hot wings, and the pizza.
Pretty mediocre, everything was okay but nothing was great. The pad thai was eh but the spring rolls were good.

I generally find it hard to find a good, consistent sushi restaurant in this area. Even harder to find an exceptional Chinese place.

AF&S is noteworthy in that it does both well, and at a reasonable price too. This is the first time I've ever ordered General Tso's and genuinely loved it. Their sushi is also great, and at a price that beats any of the other local sushi houses.

In short, solid food and a good value. It's become an addiction in our apartment.

The Coffee Masters!!!

I love this place :-)

I come in religiously and get an iced coffee in the summer, pumpkin chai latte in the fall and winter, and a latte more than anything else.

The service is great and the coffee is amazing. Also the Bagel Sandwich with egg is awesome.

Upside: The ambiance is nice along with very friendly service and the tables are reasonably spaced out so you're not dining on top of people.

Downside: We waited 45 minutes for our food. By the time it came my egg sandwich was cold, the pancakes were cold, while my boyfriends meal was nice and hot. It seemed like they mistimed everything. Not sure if it was the fact that the sandwich was cold but it wasn't all that good. 

We also didn't get a ton of bang for our buck. Pricier than I expected since everything is added on a la carte basically.

i was unsatisfied with my experience. i ordered the baked ziti for delivery, which included breadsticks and a salad. when i received my food, the first thing i noticed was that i did not receive my breadsticks! when i went to eat my salad, the lettuce was beginning to brown and i also received the wrong dressing. the baked ziti was extremely flavorless as well. i feel that perhaps because my meal was ordered to-go they did not put much attention towards it and just threw it together with no care. unfortunately this turned me away from this restaurant and i will not be returning to give a second chance.

went there for Thanksgiving dinner so lemme break it down....turkey,ham,prime rib and roast beef all were excellent especially the turkey it was so moist it melted in your mouth!!! sides...apple stuffing,sage stuffing,mashed potatoes all were great especially the garlic mashed potatoes...sweet potatoes,mac n cheese,string bean casserole were not very good and flat the sweet potatoes tasted like they came from a can.The dessert table was awesome!!! they had everything from pies to cakes to cookies it was worth the 40 bucks alone.The location is awesome inside Fairmount Park it has great scenery.The staff was great!! my table wasn't ready at the time of my reservation so they let me eat at the bar which allowed me to be able to watch the football game and they didnt charge me for the 4  diet sodas I drank.I heard from some of the people at the bar that they have a great Sunday brunch for under 20 bucks so I will be back for that.I loved walking part of the Wissahickon trail to the restaurant.The whole day was awesome!!!

Back when I was on a ramen budget, Thursday nights were all about Cavanaugh's wing special, and although the wings are no longer 25 cents a piece, at 35 cents, they are still a great deal.

You can get them with a variety of buffalo-style sauces, but I like the plain fried wings even better than coated with butter and hot sauce...(yes, that's really what goes into buffalo sauce.)  The plain wings are nice and crispy and delicious with just a light sprinkling of salt and pepper.

PARTING THOUGHT: I like the wings better than the drummettes, so it was a total bonus when I went with my drummette loving roommate because we'd divvy up our pile 'o poultry Halloween booty style

Tasha, Tasha, Tasha! I got married this past weekend and Tasha came to my hotel and did the hair of my wedding party. From the moment we did the trial months before this, I knew Tasha was awesome. She's fun, talented and sincerely wants you to love the way you look. We had a dance party morning - singing along to our favorites and she made us look and feel amazing.

I will say that there was a few moments in emails when scheduling and planning where there was a bit of miscommunication but everything ended up great in the end. I think it's completely normal for that to occur in emails and perhaps there was unclear communication on both ends.

Overall, Tasha did my hair better than I could have imagined. I even adjusted it slightly the day of and have killed it. Thank you, Tasha and AMS!

I have always had great experiences at Peter Piper Pizzas until I came to this location. I work with a youth program where I get reimbursed for my expenses and the manager refused to write me a handwritten receipt for the money I spent on tokens. Simple. Not only did he say we "don't do that here", he was beyond rude to the point where my youth wanted to leave. I will NOT be coming back here and will be telling my entire group of 50+ people to never come to this location.

Street Side is one of my go-to places to eat. BYOB (and across the street from fine wine & spirits), great service, awesome food. I think I ended up eating here 3 times in one week. Very accommodating for vegans, the mushroom dumplings, veggie net rolls, and tofu noodle bowl are my faves. You can even call and reserve the upstairs room for large parties or birthdays.

We took a wrong turn and ended up in a parking lot in the middle of the woods.  This place is literally in the middle of no where (on Forbidden Drive), but since we were starving,  we tried it out for dinner.

Appetizers: Fried calamari. Crab cake.  The calamari was cut in thin rings,  and I much prefer thick cut calamari.  It was also really salty. I'd skip it. It's too common of a dish and this one wasn't very good. The crab cake, on the other hand,  was yummers.  Lol. Fresh jumbo crab meat. Good seasoning.

Dinner: the chicken dish. The salmon dish.  The chicken dish was bland.  The eggplant in the dish had way too much vinegar. The salmon dish had a savory piece of Salmon but the julienne cut veggies were sour.  For $22 dishes,  they missed the mark.  

The food was 2 star. This place got +1 star for the remote (& pretty cool) location.
Good coffee, good food. What else could you want?  This is a place that does all the simple things right with their food and has a nice atmosphere to go along with it.
I was not pleased with service, The home fries we ordered were old we had to send them back and have them remake a new order and there was a hair in my cornbread waffles. Very disappointed

I am not a sushi expert, and as a vegetarian I can't comment on the fish sushi, but if what I just ate was any indication, it's probably pretty good. Ditto the Chinese and Thai selections, none of which I have tried yet.

Fresh and delicious vegetables, perfectly cooked and seasoned rice, kickin' wasabi, yum. And they deliver. Oh, and I got a BUNCH of sushi for about $20!

I can guarantee you I will order from this place again within the next 5-7 days. And I don't take my guarantees lightly.

One night my wife decided she would like to have pizza at home. This idea came up because we had just brought home our first baby a week prior. We decided to try a new place as we had become bored with the same old delivery pizza. I opened my Yelp app and searched for highly rated pizza places near our home. Pizza Luna popped up as one of the highest rated pizza places in Tucson. I read a couple reviews, checked the menu, and we decided to give it a try. Boy oh boy, are we glad we did! We decided to get something close to our "usual" so we went with a traditional pizza, topped with pepperoni, garlic, and feta. This pizza did not disappoint. It was done a couple minutes early, so I did not have to wait when I picked it up, as it had just been pulled from the oven and cut. I was greeted immediately upon entering the door, and it was though they knew who I was before I even said so! The pizza itself was delightful. Crust was not too thin, and not too thick for a traditional pizza. The sauce is tasty, had enough quantity so you knew it was there, but wasn't overwhelming, and has a nice kick! The pepperoni was tantalizing, thin, and also appropriately used. The feta tasted as feta should, and the garlic was roasted to perfection. I'm not ashamed to say we finished the entire pie between just the two of us. It could probably feed 3-4, but we had a one-week old, and were a bit ravenous! Thanks pizza Luna for bringing artisan pizza to our neighborhood!

This is the best veterinary clinic or animal hospital I have ever been to. I had a cat that had an unidentified disease and only Girard Vet Clinic was able to help me out. Eventually my cat had other issues and needed to be put to sleep and they sent me a sympathy card. Something you would never expect from any other clinic.
Found this Jewel on yelp. The reviews don't do it justice. Food was delicious, amazing service felt like I was back home. Will be coming back.

Amelia is the best colorist I've ever come across. And she's incredibly kind, funny, and personable. I was unhappy with my hair because of how it had been getting dyed at another salon, and she knew exactly what I was talking about, why I didn't like it, and fixed it. The whole staff is welcoming and personable. 

I went for my second balayage today and my hair has never looked better, seriously. I have total trust in her, she's so intelligent and has a fantastic eye for what will work. I cannot say enough how much I love my hair and how much I enjoy Amelia doing my hair. 

I love chatting with her, and look forward to getting my hair done again. They use awesome products, but Amelia and her skill and talent are what keep me coming back. You absolutely won't regret Amelia doing your hair, the woman is a magician.

Received the flyer in the mail so decided to try it out. We ordered a supreme pizza with pineapple and wings. The pizza was alright. The toppings were applied very sparingly. I literally had only one pineal piece per slice. The wings were tough and dry. Overall it is a mediocre place and I wouldn't go back.

I went to valley green on Valentine's Day with my girlfriend. I had some trouble finding it but once I called the restaurant and got directions I was ok.  We sat in the fireplace room. I really liked that the place felt like being in a home dining room. The fireplace was also lit which was nice.  For my first course I had the oyster tempura. I had a similar dish at another restaurant so was a little hesitant however I really enjoyed this.  My second course I had the pork belly.  This was probably my favorite of the 3 courses, amazing.  I had filet mignon for my 3rd course. All of the food was great and the staff was very friendly. Definitely a place I will be back to.

I brought my cat Myla for a second opinion as to what is going on with her ear.  The appointment cost $44 for a consultation which I thought was a fair cost especially since Dr. Weiner really took his time speaking with me.  Further I felt that he was truly interested in providing Myla with the best care.  He explained to me what was going on in a very succinct and eloquent manner.  I felt that he was highly competent.  I also found the ladies at the front desk to be helpful and competent as well.

If I could give this store 6 stars, I would. I started going here with two friends for the beginner needlepoint class. Stephen was our instructor and was extremely patient since we all needed a lot of assistance with our beginning stitches. Our group was so pleased with the instruction and our new found hobby that we went back for the more complex basket weave stitch class with Wendy. Wendy was helpful was able to answer all of our questions and provide advice on our first projects. I came in the store the other day to pick up a new project and was amazed at the level of customer service. The staff at Rittenhouse Needlepoint makes what could easily be a very intimidating hobby into a very enjoyable experience. I guarantee you will be excited about needlepoint after leaving this store!

Chhaya is a cafe that specialises in various roast-styles of various coffees.
I went to Chhaya this afternoon with a group. The four of us got various things each. I ordered the masala chai (I fiend for good masala chai). I wasn't disappointed with it, too much... to be completely honest, the taste was great, but subtle. Too subtle. I don't much care for a masala chai that whispers sweet nothings in my ear, to be frank. I want one that'll punch me in the face and yell "CHHHHHHHHHHHHAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAIIIIIIIIIIIIIII," but even if it wanted to, this one in particular was too weak to do it.
Don't let that deter you from trying it: it's still very good, but nonetheless, more subtle in taste than to which I am accustomed.
Another order amongst our group was the so-called "South Indian Decoction." The name threw me off; I had no idea what this item might be, but when I saw the familiar metal container used in brewing it, I understood immediately what it was: coffee. 
For those familiar with Turkish/Arabic/Greek-style coffee, this is very similar. It's brewed in a similar fashion, too. Ultrafine coffee grounds are put into cool water, heated until it foams, then removed from the heat. The process similarities, however, end there and the grounds used in this brewing method often have chicory added and are made not just from flat-shaoed coffee beans with which most of us are familiar, but also with the rounder "peaberry" coffee, which is reputed to be of better quality somehow, but I don't really know how or why. 
Anyway, after foaming, the coffee is then allowed to cool and the grounds allowed to settle. Once they've settled to the bottom, the decoction is carefully poured through muslin, cheesecloth or similar filter. From that point, the coffee decoction is poured into a cup or tumbler with some sugar (I've also had it with honey) and some milk is heated (alone, not with the decoction.) Often, the milk is watered down a little bit, but I'm not sure if Chhaya does that or not. When the milk is near boiling, it is poured into another tumbler of equal volume, but half the height and much wider than the one for the coffee liquid. It is then poured from the squat tumbler into the taller one, then back into the squat one, back into the taller one and so on and so on and so on, usually from increasing heights each time. This aerates and froths the coffee/milk mixture somewhat and thoroughly dissolves what sugar was there. 
I had a sip. Again, as with what I'd ordered, it was less strong than other Madurai-style coffees I've had, but nonetheless good.
A third in the group ordered an iced masala chai. Good news: they don't charge you for ice cubes! A novel idea (I'm glaring at you, every other cafe place, ever)! It wasn't as good as the hot one I'd had, and we all agreed on that, but decent nonetheless. 
A brownie was also ordered. It was fairly standard and nothing to write home about, but the iced coffee and espresso were both above standard for the area. 
I asked one of the workers about the various methods of brewing and various types of coffees Chhaya carried. A problem was met: he didn't know the origins of the beans, and a place that's supposed to pride itself in it's coffees really should. He'd said that the roasts were generally indicative of the region, which may well be true, but he couldn't speak with certainty about where each may have been roasted.
Chhaya boasts an impressive array of methods for brewing coffee. In addition to the one detailed above, there is also siphoned coffee (previously, only Ray's in Chinatown had this method in Philly, to my knowledge), Chemex and I suspect automatic drip, though I didn't see the machine and didn't scan the menu enough to see if they did, indeed, carry it, but it would be an anomaly if they didn't.  Chhaya also offers the full gamut of espresso-based drinks from cappuccino to latte and beyond.
I've yet to try their food menu as they currently do not yet carry the food menu in its entirety, but from what I can see, this is a place to watch out for. Regardless of how harsh my review may seem, I'm going to be retrying and updating it as it comes.

Came here for breakfast for the first time - I thought the ambience of the place was really neat, sometimes too loud, but their lighting decorations and seating layout was aesthetically pleasing.  I had the make your own breakfast sandwich was great, my friend had the "Bagel Sandwich" which she loved, and my other friend had the Kate. The service was attentive and always ready to refill our coffee!

Can't say I'm all that impressed. The prosciutto pizza is ok, but it's nothing you can't get anywhere else in town. The little gems salad wasn't anything to write home about. Limited choice on drinks. No desserts. It's a nice looking restaurant, service was fantastic, good ambiance, but food needs some work. Which is difficult for me to say about a salad with bacon.

You don't know me, but I know pizza. I've travelled, okay? I've sought out the deepest pie and thinnest slice known to man. Believe me when I tell you this is THE BEST PIZZA IN TUCSON. 

Let's start with the dough: They take the time to ferment it right, and oh how perfectly it melds with the sauce. 

THIS IS A TRULY ITALIAN PIZZA JOINT. If you want "pizza pie" or some "New Yak" slice go elsewhere. If you are in fact a true pizza enthusiast, get the Mediterranean pepperoni if you know what's good for you. They also have a great option for simply cheese if you're vegetarian. 

An Italian man in Naples once told me "You can't bite just one eat", which I took to mean he disagreed with Mr. pres of barstool sports when he says "one bite, everyone knows the rules". 

Fact, you will eat more than a bite, and you will love it. 

Don't forget the beer (draft IPA known as Dragoon) which is a local craft favorite for all the right reasons! 

Also, I bet you expected a picture. Well, that's not happening because through the course of this review, I've eaten every bit. You'll understand when you go here.

We have been taking our two dogs and four cats to Dr Balzer for almost three years now. 

Dr Balzer is great with our animals and we are very happy with the care that they get. Her prices are also very reasonable compared to the Center City places that we have gone to. The office is not fancy and I feel like they care more about taking care of your pets than having a fancy waiting area. 

Afternoon appointments do need to be scheduled out ahead of time - at least a few weeks - but I like the option of coming in unscheduled in the morning. You will wait and will need to be there early to get seen, around 7:30am, but a little waiting is worth it if we feel the need to get one of the animals in right away. 

We also had to put down one of our dogs earlier this year - she was an older shepherd mix that we rescued a few years earlier. Not a great time but Dr Balzer and all the staff were extremely caring and considerate throughout the whole process. They made sure that Pinky was comfortable and gave us all the time we needed to say good byes.  

Yikes - getting a little teary thinking about it. 

It is hard to explain but we feel like Dr Balzer and her staff are more concerned about caring for animals than they are for coddling owners.

I would have given this place 5 stars it averages 4 when you factor in the 3 I'd give it for the extra costs they include to dry your hair. 

5 starts for color - Megan is a spectacular colorist. I'm blonde and prefer very natural highlights. She nailed it. You absolutely cannot tell that I have them and I'm not just kidding myself. 

One complaint, in order to really see the color, you need to have your hair blown dry. For this, they charge an additional $35, which, to me, was unheard of. It should be included in the coloring charge, but it's not. So, for $100 you get great highlights but will pay $135 just to have someone do what we are all already capable of doing ourselves. 

I found the owner/stylist to be very surly, especially when I balked at the additional blow-dry cost that they tacked on.

This is a great place for Sunday brunch! I took my parents who were visiting me in Philadelphia because I wanted to show them the area. 

 I have jogged past it many times while on Forbidden Drive and decided it was time to finally see what it's like inside.  The location is very unique because it's nestled in the woods of Fairmount Park making it a true neighborhood gem! If I didn't jog by it I'm not sure I would have known where it was. 

 The brunch was only $18.95 per person that includes a choice of salads; fruit, Caesar or house, an entrée of your choice and coffee, tea or juice.  Each table is also served a basket of breads and muffins baked on premise.  

The brunch is a great meal and I think that just under $20 is a good deal for it.  

I had the omelet of the day which was a large three egg omelet stuffed with lobster, tomatoes, onions and basil. The stuffing was similar to a bruschetta topping and it was delicious. The omelet was served with a side of roasted potatoes and sausage. 
I'll def. be back here again! 

Ps. Parking gets very limited on Sunday mornings and afternoons so wear comfy shoes and be prepared to walk a bit.

So I just arrived in Philadelphia and we just ordered a bunch of Chinese food from China King Restaurant.  We had the Sesame Chicken, General Tsao's Chicken, Chicken Chow Mein, Beef Chow Mein, Chicken and Broccoli, and Steamed Chicken with Mixed Vegetables.  The food was inexpensive and worked perfectly for delivery to our hotel close to the airport.

Great place for kids party! The place is giant since it used to be a retail store. Pizza was also much better then others. Our host took great care of us. Great place for summer parties to stay out of the heat.

I took my cat to see Dr. Weiner at Girard Veterinary Clinic for advice on behavioral issues. Dr. Weiner was very knowledgable and gave me good advice. I though the service at Girard was professional, friendly and valuable. I will continue to take my cat there for treatment and was impressed with the kindness and expertise of the  staff.
The prices were very reasonable compared to the vet I had been using in the Philadelphia suburbs. I will continue to use Girard Veterinary Clinic.

Visited on a Saturday around 1130/12p; we were sat immediately, however were slightly forgotten about because of how busy it was-I went to alert someone that we had waited a while with no coffee and another server came to help us immediately. Servers and Staff were very friendly and personable.

Vibe is definitely warm and cozy-we had a comfy seat in the window. Tables could be a little higher, felt like I was slouching to reach my food.

I ordered the tofu scramble with the soy chorizo sausage on the side. The scramble was great and the potatoes were cooked to perfection. Their soy chorizo was not appetizing-flat and dry- barely took two bites and not worth trying again. I'm new to soy meat-like products and I've had better from grocery stores and other restaurants.

Overall, I would definitely return and become a regular.

Shrimp lo mein was okay. Shrimp was great but lo-mein was really greasy. Chicken and broccoli was good. Spring roll was soggy. I got this delivered. Can imagine it being better if I had ate in or picked up. Will be back.

I frequent here only because it's convenient. Most employees are unfriendly and hardly welcoming. One time they even went out of their way to charge me .80 cents on my debit card because they rang something up wrong the first time they charged me. The food is overpriced and their coffee is just ok. I hate that this is the closest coffee shop. B2 and Black and Brew are definetly better AND the employees are a lot nicer.

We stopped in on a Saturday and luckily we were seated on the patio without a reservation. The front patio is a great spot for brunch on the weekend. Its $18.95 and comes with a basket of bread, mini cupcakes etc.. You get a choice of one app and an entree.  Coffee and juice are included.  If you like to people watch this is a great spot as the Forbidden Trail is only feet away.

Our server came over after a few minutes and he was very nice.  After informing us of the specials he took our orders.  We had the fresh fruit bowl and tomato bisque for our appetizers.  The soup was very good with a bit of spice to it and the portion of fresh fruit was perfect.  There are several menu additions on the other side of the menu that are $4.00 more.  Some of those additions were Filet Eggs Benedict and the Shore Omelette with crab meat.  The stuffed French Toast looked very tasty but don't plan on walking far after eating it.  The portion was huge!

For my entree I tried the Heuvos Rancheros and my Fiance had the Pecon Belgian Waffles.  They have a few good choices of draft beer and I chose the Sam Adams Summer.

The Heuvos plate was bright and visually appealing but I thought the flavors were nothing special. A side of home fries and (2) tiny sausage links came with my meal.  I would give the sides a below average rating.  The waffles were large, fresh and had big Pecons inside.

The interior of the Inn did look cramped but I didn't explore inside too much so I'm not 100% sure.  I will return again for bunch so I can try more of the brunch menu.
A fun sports Sunday. The drinks, food and crowd were excellent!

Meritus, is one of the worst companies to get service from in this industry. I have experience nothing but terrible things from this company. The customer service is horrible, they do not care about their clients. The front desk representative BEVERLY has a very nasty attitude, & doesn't even know how to transfer a call properly. She loves to get under your skin. What person deserves a job that always seems to always hang up purposely, talk unprofessional, dress unprofessional, & does not sincerely care about assisting. 

Brian & Eric, are the owners of this company. They are just as terrible, every time a question is brought they pass it along to their employees to handle when they have no knowledge of what's going on. It seems they just hire people with no educated background nor area of expertise. This place is a disaster!!! I have only dealt with two very nice representatives at this company, & they are no longer with the company. I'm very disgusted with this place, & I hope no one has to deal with this unprofessional place. STAY AWAY FROM THIS COMPANY!!!

Due to my proximity to Chhaya, I've been here daily since my review Tuesday past; it's quite literally straight down the street from me.
I stand by my previous assessments of the masala chai and the decoction: for me, they're not as strong-tasting as I'm accustomed, but other people seem to rave, so what do I know?
Nonetheless, now that I've tried just about every possible thing on the menu, I've got quite a lot to say, and ALL of it is positive.
Firstly, the coffee. My gosh, I rather enjoy the press. The El Salvador coffee from the press pot is my go-to drink when I'm at Chhaya. I was warned that it's strong, but I didn't find this to be the case; at least as far as the taste is concerned. "It's bitter" I was told, but I couldn't disagree more; I found it pretty smooth, in fact.
The strength came later. Chhaya should really market this as their signature "wake-up" beverage. The caffeine content is through the roof and likely enough to wake the dead themselves, the lazy bums. 
V, the proprietor, prepares every food item (save the bagels) that Chhaya serves to its guests. The muffins and waffles (ESPECIALLY the waffles) are superb. I've had the opportunity to sample a variety of the baked goods Chhaya offers and have not yet been let down. Of the muffins I've tried, fig, strawberry and cream cheese and blue-or-blackberry (I'm now not quite sure which of these two the muffin was), the strawberry and cream cheese was my muffin-of-choice. Sweet, somewhat tartish, moist and delicious, it was the most well-balanced of the three. The fig muffin was cinnamon-spiced somewhat and good as well as very sweet. The blue-or-blackberry was standard, moist and not skimpy on the berries so I wouldn't be surprised if it becomes their most popular.
Now... the waffles. 
Dear me, the waffles are superb. Not burned (Bonté could learn something), firm yet moist and not too sweet, they seem to go well with everything, which is all for the better since Chhaya intends to serve them with, well, everything.
I've had now maple and blueberry topped waffles, a South Asian rendition of chicken and waffles with the titular bird served in a curry sauce rather than deepfried and waffled eggs benedict. The waffle served as the perfect catch-all for each of these toppings. The curry-soaked waffle being my favourite of the three, the eggs benedict comes as a VERY close second. The hollandaise sauce is buttery and not too lemony and just perfect. I never thought the standard English muffin could be usurped, but waffle is now the lord-regent of the land of Benedict.
I now await a marriage of the curry and benedict where curry replaces hollandaise but leaving eggs and ham as they are. I'd be convulsing in foodgasm.
I've had, also, the espresso. At first turned off by the idea of an American roaster producing it, I was surprised with exceptional glee at how smooth it was. A cappuccino made from this coffee was sweet without the need for added sugar.
The staff (just how many people work here? Six? Seven?) is courteous, helpful, friendly and quick and V is knowledgeable and proud of Chhaya's ever-changing menu (daily, in fact).
