I was craving pizza and I'm in town for a couple weeks so I decided to finally try this place! I'm so glad I did! I ordered on their website since they're only doing takeout + delivery right now due to Covid. I picked it up in 15 mins and it was hot + fresh and so good!!! I got the meatball but they might have given me sausage based on the other pictures? I'm not mad, it was still good! The crust was light and fluffy and the sauce and cheese was delicious. I also got the radicchio Caesar salad and it was AMAZING! Also the staff was super friendly! Would definitely go again!
Really enjoyed the pizza, both white and regular.  Pleasant staff, great place, and really solid pizza.
The green goddess dressing is so good!  The pizza crust is chewy and crispy; the oerfect complement to the prosciutto pizza.  I don't think you can go wrong here.

Craving a slice of GOOD pizza while running errands.  I was on the Eastside of town when I thought I'd quickly check "Hot and New" restaurants.  This is totally a GREAT find!  I had their lunch special a slice and salad.  Nothing average about the choices.  I had the simple green salad (perfect!) And a slice of their pizza special- fresh figs with Humboldt goat cheese and pancetta.  The owner is from Portland and has restaurants there.  Portland is a total Foodie Haven. To boot I had had their homemade fresh daily "Blackberry, basil lemonade". A perfect flavor packed but not too heavy lunch.  Truly an awesome find!
Toured Juniper East today with Shelly Smith and the place is beautiful. Shelly was on time and friendly. Thank you for all the help!
Great service! Delicious pizza and salads! Made right in front of you. Staff was super polite and courteous!

We usually have good service when we have birthday parties at Peter piper we usually go to old Spanish trail location this time we did something different decided to make our party at the Broadway location. Service was awful we kept having to look for our waitress to
Place orders or pick up empty trays from the table. We waited 20 minutes from when the party started to find our host. Just bad service overall

These amateurs post in there menu that 30 wings cost $14.99. I place an order  for 30 wings for delivery (i live literally like 4 minutes away). Dude on the phone tells me it is going to cost $17.99!!! That is roughly a 30% tax. Seriously?! Not only do they charge an outrageous tax, they took over an hour to drive less than a mile. And to top it all off I pay in cash (like I said I would over the phone!) $20 and the clown delivering doesn't have any change. Pizza Famiglia = ROBBERY.......

We are certainly in weird times. Instead of dining out on Friday evening, we dined in with Pizza Luna. Yay Quarantine! Yay Uber Eats!

We ordered the Fig, Pig, and Goat Pizza and the Radicchio Cesar Salad. Everything was delicious. The pizza combines sweet and savory in a delightful way. The fig with the fat pancetta and the creamy goat cheese is a match made in heaven.

The salad was good. I am a fan of cesar dressing that has a hint of anchovie and boy does this one have it.   

Looking forward to visiting Pizza Luna as soon as I can.

This place used to be one of my staples, having gone there about once a month for the last 6 years, but this place has gone to hell. I came in with the intent on sitting at a table with my friend and was not greeted after standing at the door looking around for any sign of staff. We then decided to sit at the bar, still no greeting. I had to beckon the bar tender to get off her phone and serve us. She stared at me like she was clueless, did not know the specials...even though after I spoke with her I could see them on two signs hanging behind the bar, and she just didn't seem like she cared to be there. My food was luke warm, there was no head on my beer and the fruit flies that surrounded the taps leads me to believe that this place hasn't been cleaned in a few weeks.....wreaking of sour beer.We didn't stay for another round, and proceeded around the corner to City Tap House for the Happy Hour experience we wanted. I'll give this place another try in a few months to see if the service improves.
4+ solid stars for quality ingredients, nice dough with just enough chew. Held up well to delivery. Margarita ever so slightly lacking in flavor (for my taste) but the sausage Rosa was spot on.

This pizza was amazing. Chewy crust, gorgeously spicy Italian sausage (made in house) with plentiful mushrooms, and a kickass Caesar salad to boot. Too bad Grub Hub messed up the delivery - again - and I got cold food. I'm wondering what is so hard about texting or calling a person (since we give them our phone number) once they arrive? This is the third time I've received botched meals because of the grub hub delivery driver via Yelp and found my food by luck 30 minutes later. I complained to Grub Hub but I thought I'd post here so you know to just pick up the order or dine in if feasible. At any rate, LOVED the food, even tho the pizza was cold and the salad was slightly wilted. Radicchio in a Caesar salad tho?? Who knew how amazing that would be! And your homemade Caesar dressing had just the right nuance of anchovy and spice. I'll be back! In person next time. Ha!
Probably my favorite pizza in tucson area. Great salads also. Beer selection is limited but very good beers on tap!

We were sat promptly for Sunday brunch and brought our drinks, and ordered pretty quickly. Then. Nothing. For 45 minutes. No one came by to notice we hadn't gotten our food. I had to flag the waitress down to point out we hadn't received our food and the table next to us who sat down at least 20 min after us had just gotten their meals. 
She does some investigating and finds out the kitchen.l never received our order and they were just starting to make it. 

Ok waited to receive the food and see how the delay was handled before applying a rating to this. Because, after all, accidents happen - it's how you recover. 
1. The food: mind you, we were probably more critical than if we had gotten our food in the proper amount of time, but we were also hungrier so it would have balanced out. Anyway, as objectively as possible, we'd rate the food 2.5. It was just a little bit better than edible? How do you F up quiche?
2. Staff reaction: still not apologetic enough in my opinion  (former server here) and took way to long to even acknowledge the situation as a whole - clearly not paying attention at all to customers. Our waitress was apathetic, and the restaurant applied a 30% discount. 

Suggestion: go to Barcelona down the street and take notes on their service. I know these are two different types of restaurants, but good service and making sure your customer is getting was they asked for is universal.

I had an outstanding experience here at Pizza Luna. The place is very chic & clean. The food here is wonderful, I had many items off their menu, but Salami Pizza is especially great in my opinion. I became great friends with the staff, who are all great and super friendly. Pizza Luna....Nothing but win.

I have ordered not delivery and pick up from here several times and they never disappoint. Delivery is fast, even on nights/weekends. The supreme pizza was so flavorful, it has the perfect amount of garlic that really puts it up there for me. The gyro is always great, they put a good amount of sauce on it which I especially love. It came with fries that were still crispy upon delivery - awesome! I will continue to support this local business and you should too!

Completely amazing! The ambiance is cool and the employees are helpful and friendly. We ordered the Luna lemonade without knowing anything about it and it was amazing! It's not like lemonade at all! Lots of berry flavor and basil! I wish I had a gallon of it! We had the Luna board and the pig, fig and goat pizza. Both were awesome but the pizza was outstanding. I wish I had bought an extra pizza to bring home since we don't live close by. They had a busy flow of orders being picked up- I must have heard them say margherita 10 times, so I'll have to try that one next time. Looking forward to my next visit!

This place is pretty sweet.

On the recent day of a one Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Beakaboo and I were due for some breakfast and catch-up.  Our first few attempts failed because the #openinphl hadn't been updated.  She suggested Chhaya and we called, they were there.

The space of this restaurant is very cool and cozy.  There are seats near the window, there is a center table where people can congregate and there are seats and nooks around the edges if you're the type to lounge and study.  We opted for an edge table and ordered our breakfasts.

My chemex, which they offer in 12 or 16 oz quantities was a nicely made cup of coffee which tasted very pleasant.  My tofu scramble was on the smaller side but I feel was priced appropriately given the size of the dish.  Service was pleasant, prompt and I think this place is certainly an example of a well run establishment.

I'll be coming back here to try more menu items as I was very impresssed with what Chhaya had to offer.

Disappointing mail order experience. 

Was initially put off by the steep flat rate shipping cost, but according to the website, the threads I wanted were in stock so I placed a sizeable order that made the shipping cost palatable. Received my order and less than half of the threads I ordered shipped with a note saying (paraphrased)  "Sorry, some items were out of stock. please try again in 3-4 week."  

The threads themselves are perfectly lovely, but considering items on site are listed as in stock (when I ordered and even now as I write this review), but actually aren't, I'll pass on ordering from this shop again. As I'm local, I may give in store shopping a chance when the pandemic is over. If so, will update my review at that point.

Awesome pizza and salad. Sauce is homemade and you can tell. Salad is salad but the dressing is fabulous. You can tell it's homemade. I want to try the Sicilian next. My go to pizza place now. Great owners. Very personable. Everybody in South Tampa should try this to see.

I ordered a veggie pizza because I am a vegetarian. I was so hungry that I just opened the pizza and grabbed a slice and ate it. It had pepperoni. I called and told them and the owner said "well in our defense she's not blind is she, she could've seen the pepperoni before she ate it" 
I asked for ALL veggie

This place is great! Food is really good...prices are cheap and the family who runs are really nice. Wish I had this place in SF!!! Only in Tampa for another 2 days so definitely going to try to squeeze it in again.

Ordered dinner from her last night I'm not one to go off negative reviews till I try it for myself! Glad I tried this place I ordered a pizza, wings and cheesy garlic bread and Marinara sauce. The marinara was the best I ever had and everything was cooked to perfection! Pretty fast delivery and food was nice and hot. Well definitely be my pizza place for now on.
The pizza is so yummy. I had two different kinds of pizza and they both tasted so good. The garlic knots were also one of the best I've had. I can't wait to eat here again.

1st timer. Ordered brisket sandwich. It was good sized for the price. Brisket was all very grisly and cut into chunks, not medium-small, chopped or sliced. Extra 'spicy' dipping sauce I  requested  was not in bag or charged. Sauce on bread was OK, but nothing to write home about-supermarket BBQ sauce on sale level. Stuffy over bearing Sports Bar environment is not pleasant. Pleasantly nice service and average wait time, but looking into that kitchen, the floor and equipment made me queazy. One cook had a boil or something on his forehead so large I could see it from dining room. Where were the hairnets? No covid masks worn by employees. This place could not stay in business in Texas. Will not return.

Definitely not worth it! Unless, you enjoy being ignored by staff and receiving dirty bottles of hot sauce with hair stuck to it. When addressed with management they had no issues. Poor service and explanation. Manager was more incline to argue than to make it right.

Horrible plain slice. Over priced. $39 for a 1/2 pepperoni+cheese large pie that was 1/4 as good as Digiornos. The only positive is that they are open until 4am in an area that a lot of people walk home - so if nothing else they Atleast provide a tiny bit more of security to those pedestrians and potentially a place to use the bathroom if the dude running the window doesn't rob you first. Absolutely do not eat here if you like pizza. I know a lot of people like to know if they were wearing masks or not ... I don't remember. But what I do remember is that I'd rather eat my dead grandmothers mask right before she gets buried than eat this

The pizza is really good! Came from Spring Hill, Fl to try it because pizza in Spring Hill area is not that good. It was worth the drive. Definitely have to order the Greek salad with your pizza, the salad is good. The staff is friendly. We will be back soon!

This place just opened a couple months ago and if you haven't tried it, you gotta check it out. Anthony was awesome and hooked me up with a delicious sausage pizza. The crust is the perfect amount of thickness and they're open until 4 am, can't beat that! Very nice guys that work there, highly recommend!

Pizza Luna is a great place for some fast and easy Neapolitan pizza! I go here a lot and always get Takeout, love the quality of their food and how consistent their food remains all the time. I always get the Bianca, or Margherita, alongside their Garlic knots. But today I decided to get the Bianca with figs and balsamic added ontop! Service is always great, these employees work super hard with everything going on. If you want some delicious pizza and are on the run, head over to the east side and get some Pizza Luna!!

Delicious pizza and excellent lunch specials available including 1/2 off small or large pizzas, and 8.25 for your choice of slice and a small salad, which is actually quite large! Otherwise, can be a bit pricey.

Hey guys! Do you want to pay a premium for bland, flavorless food? Does being humiliated by discrimination excite you? I got you fam--come on down to Valley Green Inn!

I went to this restaurant as a lunch stop on a bridal tour for lunch. There were 3 parties of brides (and their crews) total in our group. Completely dead inside the tiny building, couple of families seated outside eating. We were the only black bridal party. 

We saw our waitress like 3x times the whole time (and I see a couple of people who mentioned that they got ignored when they visited.) Took forever to even take drink orders. The waitress never cleared our plates or refilled drinks after ordering. Never updated us in the food. The food didn't even come out for LITERALLY an hour. No joke, no exaggeration. Wonder why, since all the other parties got theirs well before us. (Even the large 7-person party.) We were the only people who had problems.

When the waitress finally showed up again, I told her it was time for us to leave for the next stop on the tour and that the food was super late. She said she "didn't know we were on a time constraint." First of all, that's beside the point. Which I find funny because the inn was a sponsored stop on the bridal tour. I think she even waited on another bridal party. Even if she somehow "didn't know" or notice all the brides with toy veils on...do you normally leave customers waiting for food for an hour without any type of attention? Probably not. 

I talked to the manager about the situation and he was very understanding (even though the first words out of his mouth were "the trolley won't leave without you.") The waitress kept repeating that she "didn't know", which is not a valid excuse. But here's the icing on the cake...she brought our food out in to-go boxes and said that the bride's food had the wrong dish name written on it. She opened the box to look at the food and said "Oh, the food is right." No worries right? 

We get to our trolley and the bride's food is completely wrong. Meaning this girl looked us RIGHT IN THE FACE and lied, even after all the mess-ups earlier. And the food we got boxed? It's like no one in the restaurant heard of seasoning...is it that hard to use salt?? C'mon man...

Tried to give the situation the benefit of the doubt, but too many coincidences for this incident to be anything other than discrimination. Wouldn't come back if I got paid to.

Finally, a fantastic pizza restaurant in the heart of Hyde Park! Their meatballs are by far the best I've had!! And I'm a meatball connoisseur! And their pizza is delicious!! Their staff is friendly and the atmosphere is cozy! I give it 5 stars and all thumbs UP! If you like pizza and meatballs you have to check it out!

I'm going through a pizza and salad craving currently and they hit the spot! I did the lunch Pepperoni and Caesar salad with a Neapolitan slice on the side. I preferred the pepperoni more but both were good especially for the price. The Caesar salad was pretty good as well but it was a bit spicy in some bites. 

Their Luna lemonade was exceptional! Do try it if you go. I also had a 1/2 dozen of the garlic knots and honestly I don't see what everyone else was talking about. They were very bland and didn't have a hint of garlic. The serving sauce with it made up for the blandness. 

Overall if you're looking for a good place to dine in Tucson with friendly staff and affordable prices, give them a try.

With not very many places around town to host a children's birthday party Peter piper pizza tops the list for most people, this location in particular is constantly busy, located centrally in town,  and one of the very few locations that offers a carnival ride indoors, it's a fun place for children of all ages has a little play area; for younger children but it could stand a better cleaning.  As far as pizza goes it's wonderful when it's piping hot, and being that this place is so busy they do get the pizzas up fairly quickly, only downside is the parking it is hectic trying to find a place to park, be prepared to either park in the Savers parking lot or in the dark in the back of the building near the dumpsters, other than that it's not the Dave and busters but it is fun for all children and adults. I'm sure I'll be visiting again soon.

Common to the area you find this restaurant in a strip mall. I'm fairly new to mofongo, so no expert. I feel like trying it multiple places is required to compare it and this was a very good example of it in my opinion. My husband has been less than enthusiastic but he too liked his chorizo-like mofongo. I chose the pork and it was delicious. Garlic in the mofongo was just perfect and u don't know what other magic he included but it was moist inside and very well seasoned  port rounded it out. The folks that met us at the counter when we came in were patient and helpful and spoke English much better than i can speak any broken up attempt at their language. We really enjoyed our meal and we're glad we tried it.

We discovered Pizza Luna on a whim. I am endlessly grateful we did, because Pizza Luna has hands down the BEST pizza. Their menu offers a variety of classic or bold options. Our children love it - we consider that a high honor, as one loathes pizza for the most part - and even our pickiest friend quite likes their food. Needless to say, Pizza Luna is one of our top places to eat in Tucson and the number one choice for pizza.

Great Pizza, I stopped in for a slice and was so impressed with the staff and delicious food they have. I have ordered Pizza now several times and each time I was delighted. I ask them when ordering for pickup that they pat bake the pizza so they don't cut the pizza and leave it mostly baked but ready to take home and pop it in the oven for a short time and it's perfect for eating.

I want to start by saying the food was excellent and the location was wonderfully serene.  However, the service that my friends and I received this afternoon was absolutely TERRIBLE!  Our server, Taylor, was completely inattentive, aloof and slow.  It started when she attempted to fill the glasses with water while my friends were washing their hands, in the restroom.  She spilled the water all over my menu and on the chair next to me.  She then asked if I thought my friend would sit on that chair.  I said, "likely not" because she had her purse in the other chair.  Well, a reasonable person would assume she would eventually come back to wipe off the chair or replace the menu - it never happened.  

We placed our orders and after the food came, I noticed that the sausages (which were included with my order ) were missing.  I tried to wait to see if she would come back to check on us, but that never happened, either.  I asked another server to get for me.  When she came, I explained that the sausage links were missing.  Her response to me was, "that's strange."  At the point, my friend asked for ketchup and more hot water for her tea.  It took her 10 minutes to bring the ketchup.  She never brought hot water.  My other friend started to wipe off the chair with her napkin, and Taylor says, "I guess I should have done that, but you weren't sitting there."  When we asked for the bill, I immediately gave her my card because I didn't know how long it would take her to come back.  She pauses, looks at my friend and asks, "Do you still want the water?"  Really? Really?

I don't believe that Taylor's no-care-attitude is a reflection on the business.  The server who waited on the 4-top behind us, was completely attentive to his customers. He even sang to them as he gave them their orders.  It was cute; you had to be there.  

Taylor, we didn't need a song.  We simply needed courteous service from someone who looked like they wanted to be there.

Just passing through on a move from Vegas to San Antonio. 

So glad we decided to eat here (takeout). 

Two pizzas, cheese for the kids and a prosciutto and rocket pizza for the adults. My wife had the caprice salad as well. 

A little pricey but very very good. A nice treat on our trip. Not sure if I would eat there all the time for the price but it was very good.

Just what I was looking for. Tasty, healthy food that left me not wanting dessert an hour later. Sweet potatoes and Brussels sprouts were a nice addition to the bowl. Will definitely be ordering again!

When I was first looking for a caterer for my wedding I was discouraged because all I wanted for my guests was good food and not expensive. I came across D'Lysh on google and never been more happy. The service I received since day one was outstanding! We kept in contact the whole time I was planning! My guests are still talking about how good the food was! They were on time, professional, the price was amazing, food was delicious! Any event I ever need catered or family or friends there is no question as to who I will use! There isn't enough stars for D'Lysh they receive 10 stars from me!

10/25 I brought my cat Herbert into Girard Vet Clinic because he was peeing outside the litterbox. After an x-ray determined that he had bladder stones, they flushed the stones back into his bladder, to hold him over to surgery the following Wednesday.

10/30 Herbert had a cystotomy to remove the stones. Total cost was about $2000. Included in that cost was analysis of the stones.

Herbert recovered poorly from the surgery, not eating very much, and not seeming to be able to urinate. A vet tech friend recommended that I take him back in.

11/1 I brought him back to the clinic. At the appointment, I was told that Herbert was a little dehydrated and his temperature was a low, but other than that was recovering ok. He was given transdermal fluids.

Over the next two days his condition deteriorated rapidly. He would only lie down and couldn't urinate. He suddenly became very bloated (see picture); he's usually a scrawny 10 pound cat. He seemed to be shaking and wouldn't eat or drink anything. My vet tech friend told me I should take him to Penn Vet Emergency which I did on 11/3.

Penn told me he was definitely blocked and that the sutures had broken, causing urine to leak from the bladder and into his body. The cystotomy would have to be done again, this time for a cost of $8000.

11/3 I called Girard Veterinary Clinic and left a message that Herbert had needed emergency surgery to revise the cystotomy. I received a call on 11/4 from Dr. Haugen asking if Herbert was any better. It seemed they had not received my voicemail, and I said Herbert had emergency surgery because he was blocked and had been leaking urine into his body. She told me "that doesn't seem possible."

11/6 Herbert was discharged. I spoke with the vet who did the surgery about reasons why this could have happened. She said it's possible the sutures were not done correctly or the urine just took the path of least resistance and broke through the. Because the sutures were broken, a part of his bladder had become bad tissue; the bad tissue was removed resulting in a smaller bladder for Herbert

11/7 I had a two week follow-up appointment scheduled for Herbert with Girard Vet Clinic. I realized that having a two week follow-up didn't make sense, so I called Girard on 11/6 at 8:15am and left a message cancelling the appointment. 11/7 at 10am, I received a call from Girard Vet Clinic telling me I was a no-show for the follow-up appointment; they had not received my voicemail again.

I completely understand that animals are not machines and that it's challenging to predict exactly how they'll respond to something or what they'll need. It's possible the sutures were not done right, but it's also possible they were done well and he got blocked because of his physiology and that undid the sutures. However, I feel something was missed in his care on 11/1 when I brought him in when he was not recovering well. I feel not great that my vet tech friend was able to give me better advice without seeing the patient.

11/12 At the suggestion of several veterinary industry friends, I followed up with Dr. Haugen and asked if Girard Vet Clinic would cover part of the cost of the emergency revision surgery. I was told she would have to talk to Dr. Wilkerson about it and get back to me later that week.

12/6, Still no response so I called again and left a message with the receptionist that I had not received a return call. They said that they would put a message in his chart for them to follow up with me. Still no callback as of 12/10. I also haven't received any information about the stone analysis (which I know can take at least 3 weeks).

The combination of the surgery needing to be revised, not finding anything wrong with Herbert when I took him for his follow-up, not checking for messages that I had left, and not receiving a call back for weeks goes beyond the variable nature of caring for an animal. It seems more like questionable business practice, and I think it's important for potential patients to know what they might be in for.

I wish there is 0 star for this restaurant. The food is not clean and filthy. I went there twice because I wanted to give them a second chance because the first order was not good. Anyway, the service is unbelievably rude. I didn't expect much from any casual restaurants but this one makes me so pissed off. The cashier did not understand or forgot that I ordered in. Half way through my meal he came and scolded at me because he thought I ordered togo. Are you serious? Is it really a big deal when there were only 2 customers in the restaurant at the time? and I got yelled for that? Anyway, I walked out and told him there will not be next time for me to come back. Don't come here unless you want to be treated dis respectfully and eat filthy food.

Here are some positives to living through a pandemic. Take-out done right. A business that protects their workers and the public (wearing masks and gloves before the Mayor mandated them). 

We've worked hard to support local businesses, and we've had mixed results. Pizza Luna rises to the top on a number of fronts, hence the five-star review with only two visits. Two! 

Both times I ordered over the phone, as we prefer to pay in cash. No problem there, I didn't feel rushed. Accurately took my order and repeated it back to me. The honey went to pick it up.

Both times their pizza bianco. Yum, yum, yum! Just a hint of fresh garlic, the fresh basil is a dream in every bite, a crust that's chewy, not crunchy (it peeves me to no end to get a crunchy crust), hearty but not heavy, and four types of cheese. (fior di latte. trust me, you won't regret it. we also got manchego). We add some mushrooms and voila! An easy and reasonably priced dinner. A small is a good size for the both of us, one time with leftovers (really great cold the next morning) the other time we gobbled it up. 

I'm glad we found a local business that does pizza right. I'm a Manhattan, born-and-bred New Yorker, and a bit of a pizza brat. Enough said.

I came here last night for the "classier" half of my birthday celebration and this place definitely delivered.

Set within the seemingly endless realm of Fairmount Park and along the Forbidden trail, the Valley Green Inn radiates an unparalleled rusticness complemented by unique, mouthwatering cuisine.

Never in the US has it been so easy to hop on a bike and ride through scenic greenery to a restaurant! I love that. And what a classic place.  You enter to the familiar floorboard creaks, narrow doorways, and stone walls of true historic homes where you are escorted into a home dining room-like setting.  It was so quiet and peaceful; it truly felt like you were sitting at your own kitchen table. 

Our very informative waiter explained with precision the history of the business (which has existed for over 300 years) as well as specific descriptions of each menu selection with his oh so eloquent cuisine-infused verbiage.  

Highlights: the crab cake soup in a sweet potato/coconut broth and the purple asparagus salad (asparagus grown in half light and half dark conditions).

Overall great venue for a special occasion and the perfect place if you're someone looking for a park adventure.
So good. Me and my daughter absolutely loved it was not greasy thin crust it wasn't salty it was perfect best pizza I've had in a while
I love this place. I always use them of I'm looking for good Chinese in South Philly.

This is a nice hidden gem outside the urban flavor of Philadelphia.  Its located in the Wissahickon Valley, apparently built in the late 1600s, and is decorated with quite the colonial flair.  The dining room has about 15 tables and is very cozy.  The ambiance makes for a very romantic meal.  

As for the food, when you crack open the menu, you'd expect the prices to be significantly higher for what they were serving.  I was there for lunch, so dinner is a little more pricey, but for lunch, nothing was priced over $13, and it all sounded tasty.  I ordered the crab cake, which unlike many crab cakes I've had before, was significantly more crab than cake, which is always a plus.   It was very straightforward, but incredibly good.  They also have an outstanding grilled cheese, made with brie, gruyere, bacon (and who doesn't love bacon), and a few other small fixings.  The menu covers a wide range; steak, chicken, fish, theres going to be something you'll like.  

When its warmer out, there's outdoor seating, and the soothing sound of the canal (river?) should make for a great meal.

I was very hesitant to try this restaurant given that the yelp ranking was 3.5 and the house while quaint and pretty also looked like somewhere Jordan Peele would tell you to "Get Out" of. Overall very pleasantly surprised with my experience there. The service was so nice. We were sweaty and gross from our hike so it was nice that they had outside seating so that we didn't feel like we were stinking up the place lol. The food was pretty good I have to say. The prices ehhh but it's also the only place to eat here haha. 

We had the country pate for appetizer. Pretty dang good. The port reduction with the caper berries provided a great sweet contrast to the more earthy flavors of the pistachio and pate. We had the cat fish and the pork chops for entrees. The pork chops were cooked well, slightly dry but the the juices from the dish really moistened it up that you didn't really notice. The Brussels sprouts were amazing and I have no idea what the juices were on the dish but they went well with everything. I didn't love the sweet potato puree because it was too sweet but overall a great dish. My boyfriend had the catfish etouffee and he really liked it. It's almost like a jambalaya. The crust on the catfish is cornmeal and I was scared it would overpower the fish but it was nice and light. The rice pilaf was flavorful and fluffy. Loved the shrimp - the creole seasoning was pretty spot on. 

It was a great and romantic way to end a whole day hike and stare at nature.
Amazing pizza. I had an 'authentic' style with mushrooms, spicy sausage and olives. pizza toppings are fresh and delicious. The crust is out-of-this-world good!

Dominican restaurant that provide a lot vibe and economic dinning for the local. Many people are here for a meal in saving price. We are here to try out the food for the first time.

The restaurant has the two choices for the food. You can pickup by cafeteria already cook or from the menu. We have order two dishes from the cafeteria and one from the menu. The first dish is a soup with tripe, pig feet, and veggie. Most people only cook tripe soup by it own. It is good twist with the pig feet. Good soup. 

The second dish is a tomato base whole fish. It look awesome but it not my liking taste. Fish meat is too loose. The third dish is a cook up dish of grill steak with onion. I can hear they pound the steak at the kitchen. I like my steak grilled with no sauce. But Dominican steak has sauce on top but a bit salty. 

The food is average. If I choose Latin food, I would go with Cuban style bistec. Service is cafeteria style.

I am the luckiest girl in the world. Great pizza just moved into the neighborhood. The crust is perfect. The meats and vegetables are perfect. The house made cheese perfect. The Caesar dressing was garlicky perfection. 

The staff was kind and attentive. Thank you Travis for your helpful advice and your PERFECT housemade lemonade. 

You get the drift. If you haven't been there go immediately! Come with friends so you can try everything.
Best pizza I've had so far, in Tucson, and their Caesar salad is wonderful! I highly recommend.

I've been hearing nothing but great things about this place but unfortunately we were not impressed. Food was ready quick but the flavor on the pizza was peculiar. Also when I got home I was sad to see that my garlic knots were burnt, hard, and hardly any garlic flavor.

Quaint atmosphere, good service, interesting menu! Went for lunch on Saturday! Lovely surroundings and the restaurant is in my favorite place...Valley green! Treat yourself and visit! Food was good and appetizer...tempura cauliflower was so good!
Absolutely LOVE this pizza! The staff is always helpful and fun, and the food rocks! Our favorite the wild mushrooms and arugula Neapolitan!

Excellent pizzas of amazing ingredients! I stumbled across them when I was in Tucson. I picked up pizza from here for my extended fam and it was a huge hit. The two guys working the place were friendly and shared their amazing story. Best of luck to them!
Waited 15+ minutes for my order to be completed and when I got it, it stunk so badly of cigarettes I could barely eat it.

Beware: Unauthorized charges placed on multiple credit cards across different people's accounts. This is clearly a SCAM that they are running here on unsuspecting patrons. Charged $35 for an $18 pizza and $43 TWICE for another $18 pizza.

The pizza itself was subpar and there are ZERO covid precautions being taken and the kitchen looked FILTHY.

pizza is fantastic! If you like brick oven pizza and really like a good crust with that  brick oven char and awesome homemade sauce this is the place for you I have had everyone of their specialty pizzas and they are all excellent very impressed. It's a little pricey but in my opinion it is well worth it. Staff is also very friendly and accommodating. Would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone

These reviews are not lying, there's truth behind all of them. They currently handle our HOA and are so incompetent. You rarely ever get a response and if you do, it's because you've had to followed up 10x! The employees there do not review any of the things that you send them and can't spell to save their lives! How is this business even considered a business or professional? The reviews on Yelp and Google do not lie. If you are going into a community that has this company as their HOA or CDD, I would highly recommend that you reconsider because it is more of a headache than anything. I honestly think all HOA and CDD companies are useless, they're just there to collect your money and not take care of any important issues. They have so many rules and instead of just drawing everything out for you since they know so much, they want you to do all the work just for them to deny it.

We love Pizza Luna! The pizza is fresh and tasty. They have great offerings and their Pepperoni Pizza can't be beaten. Just got take out from them again last night. They are doing a great job of taking precautions for COVID which has been most appreciated. They recently added a Caprese salad to their menu and it's to die for! We are regulars and are so appreciative of them and the quality of their food.

Where do I begin ,I am so so disappointed from the service and food .First of all I made the reservation at this place way in advance and was taking my boss who was visiting from out of town there .They were out of chicken ,pork ,and salmon for dinner entree so we end up ordering appetizer and drink .I was so embarrassed that waitress was unprofessional and I felt like I was bordering her to asked her about the dinner menu .we end up with no dinner and no service at this place .I wouldn't recommend this place for dinner on weekdays .maybe they do better on weekend .thats all for now

Delicious!! Heard so much great reviews, I had to give Luna a try. Garlic in their sauce is a powerful burst of flavor! Crust was perfectly baked and held the pie together perfectly! Awesome customer service was the cherry on top

I don't usually review things very often but I was soooooo disappointed in this meal that I had to make a review. I ordered the Jerk Salmon Alfredo with broccoli and candied yams with UberEats and I was so excited to get it. I took one bite of my pasta and salmon and stopped to take a picture because I was appalled. It was clearly jar Alfredo sauce. Actual jar sauce. Disgusting. From scratch Alfredo sauce only has a few ingredients-Parmesan/Romano cheese, butter, garlic, heavy cream. So simple and makes a HUGE difference. Jar sauce is disgusting. The broccoli was frozen and had almost no seasoning. It was also too hard. The candied yams were from a can. The salmon was dry and overcooked. Disappointment in a platter. I tossed it. 


I'm only giving 2 stars because they were nice when they called about my order, honestly.

Went with some co-workers to catch the first day of NCAA tournament action.  Prices are decent, service is attentive and plenty of screens to watch all the action.

The club sandwich and fries are decent, the hot wings are very solid and ordered a Blue Moon to wash it all down.

The downside, the place could use a little sprucing up.  The table was rickety and the seats and floors were sticky icky in spots.

Have visited Pizza Luna at least once a month since it opened. I was very excited to have an excellent pizza place on Tucson's east side! All pizzas are amazing (yes, I've tried all of them). The crust is perfection. Toppings premium quality. Salads are delicious, too!
Best pizza I have had in a long time! Worth the trip and delivery is just as good. While on a short trip to Tucson I ordered Luna for delivery and was not disappoint.

This is the most disgusting, filthy, unkept Wawa I have ever been into in my life and I'm from PA.  Where to begin: everything is covered with dirt, the gas pumps. The trash and. The concrete pads are disgusting.  Vomit and urine are a nice touch outside.  I guess Wawa overlooks this location because it makes money being across from the casino.  The bathrooms aren't just dirty they are run down with rust on the hand dryers and faucet.  The faucet sensor was so dirty the faucet won't run, can't wash your hands.  Who cares about the water when the hand soap dispenser is open and empty.  The floor in the mens room had so much urine, my shoes slipped out constantly when I tried to use the urinal.  How can Wawa have a location like this? I guess their brand standard being trashed isn't their concern because the location is busy?  The washer fluid in the windshield washer buckets was empty and the window washer was broken. 

Trash all over In the parking lot.  Cigarette Butts on the carpet with leaves in the vestibule. 

I wish I'd taken photos because it's so gross honesty.  We won't be back. 

And I'll bet they blame it all on lack of staff, LOL

Do yourself a favor and just go somewhere else.
Ordered seafood caesar salad from Cavanaugh's this past weekend. I added toppings and subtracted others. One of the best to-go salads I've ever had.
This is the worst bbq I've ever had. It tastes light lighter fluid used to start a grill. Served on a junk bun.

Searching for a quick bite and cane here because a place up the street closed. Ordered a Sausage Rossa and it's delicious!!! Wish I had found this place sooner! Will definitely be making this a regular stop! Delicious sauce, perfect crust and the lemonade is top notch too!

Was at perer piper pizza on Broadway in tucson. The soda machine 1/2 of the sodas were carbonated water told man behind counter  he said he knew and would get to it.
 Always goes there some time games arent working. But today was bad. There was 8 birthday parties going on not including the people walking in.and noone on floor playing game had to go 2 x's to get someone to fix game we were playing went to have grandson cash in his tickets  
could get someone to get another one fix and 
he said " when there down there down" he 
walked away. Then took grandson to pick out 
somthing at prize counter and of course no

and he said it will be just a minute he had to 
put tickets in a machine. So mad ask man behind counter who the manger was he said he was. I ASKED if i could talk to him he said I'll BE RIGHT WITH YOU  WELL THAT NEVER HAPPEN WAS SO MAD asked employee at countet what the mangers name was he said Paul .  Very unprofessional 
Will not go back
This place is adorable. There are so many really yummy things to try, sweet and salty. It's very reasonably priced and there's a lot of seating. A great place to hang out with pals!

Had the most amazing takeout here! Supporting local business during the COVID-19 regulations and this was our first time trying Pizza Luna. It was amazing! I had the prosciutto pizza with gluten free crust. It was light and delicious. I don't usually finish a whole pizza in a sitting but in this case I did!

Ordered the large Meaty Meat pizza and both the Tampa and Greek salads.  The website for online ordering was very simple and fast (I did carry out).  All items were very good.  The crust was fantastic and a bit crispy on the bottom which I love.  I felt like the ingredients in everything I ordered were of high quality.  I only wish the sandwiches were available before 10 pm as being an old man I am typically in bed before they'd be available.  I will definitely be a return customer.  The "small" salads were huge and I believe could easily serve two people.  The pizza was also very large and at $20 I thought a great value.

Nah...I love pizza and this pie did nothing for me.  Cheese was wayyy too sharp...they must use some sort of blend instead of mozzarella.  Additionally, the pizza could have used an extra 2-3 mins in the oven. 

Overall, I rate this as not good pizza but it's probably suitable for the drunkies after the club/bar.

On to the next!!!

Okay, hate to ruin the local vibe and easy walk in. But this pizza joint is da Bomb. Da Bomb. 

Hands down the best pizza in Tucson. Trust me hands down the best Pizza joint in Tucson.

Dough thin & bread thick towards the crust,  crispy, chewy, sauce- tangy garlicky goodness, cheese is on point, topping are, are slap your momma great deliciousness.

Pie are cooked to perfection or near perfection every time, and topping ratio is on point. 

And staff is PRO.

Wow, this was truly the worst dining experience I've had in memory! Absolutely comedic, like The Three Stooges​, except with like 10 chaotic stooges running around, and heaven knows how many more in the kitchen. So, okay, you come here for the locale in the heart of the beautiful Wissahickon, and you can't beat the scenery from your table looking over Forbidden Drive into the woods. But the pleasantness stops there. The service is none existent​ -- not from lack of staff, but rather lack of basic competency. We literally had to stop every server passing by and repeatedly beg for water, place settings, and someone to take our order. Our waiter never showed up (mind you, it was not even particularly busy), and we had to practically demanded (politely, of course) another waitress to take our order. 

Brunch was prix fixe with two courses, bread, and beverage, but the bread basket muffins were supermarket quality at best, and the juice was the overly sweet carton variety, not fresh squeezed as one would expect. Further, they struggled to accommodate gluten-free, which in this era should be something every respectable kitchen is prepared to handle. When the entrees finally arrived, the simple omelet was uninspired and overcooked, and the Mexican egg concoction was frankly disgusting -- like a plate of nachos with a greasy​ fried egg on top. Even drunk, you'd be wary​ to eat it. 

It's a real shame, as Valley Green Inn could be such a gem if only someone who knows how to run a restaurant and a reputable chef of a certain caliber would take it over. For a "foodie" town like Philly, we shouldn't settle for less.

AMAZING Chinese food. Seriously! It was fresh, hot (we did pick up) and super flavorful. They have a nice Covid conscious set up for pick ups (basically built a take out window). Looking forward to ordering again.

Decided to try this place after reading an article about them on Tucson Foodie, and boy was it a good call!  Smaller place but they do also have patio seating.  The place is so new they're still waiting for their liquor license to arrive. Thin style crust, three different types of sauce available. We had the Sausage Fresca pizza and it was delicious!  This is going to be our go to pizza joint from now on!

Great Pizza.  Pepporoni pizza is very simple but delicious.  Oven brick taste, good cheese and Pepporoni good quality ingredients. Only complaint they didn't have ranch; but pizza is so good it made up for it.  I wish they were closer to Marana.

New to the neighborhood and trying to figure out where the next brunch spot is going to be. What a mixed bag. We got the chicken and waffles, yogurt parfait, two cold brews and a side of home fries during a Sunday brunch rush. Coffee was excellent, second only to maybe Rival Brothers in the city. Food was satisfying and reasonably priced. Service was terrific. Despite the wave of new parents desperate to cling to the vestiges of youth, with their mewling babies slung over their shoulders, they did a really good job of keeping things moving and getting people in and out. 

Now let me tell you about the horn. For some reason, I did not ask why, they have decided to use a horn as their order up signal. Not a bell. Not a light. Not even just a normal human voice saying "order up." A horn. You know, the tool that a clown uses to perplex and disarm an audience. I cannot stress how strange it is to have your entire auditory experience during brunch consist of a Taylor Swift album being played straight through with intermittent horn pierces. This is the reason to either come to or avoid Chhaya. The beautiful calligraphy on the coffee bar menu. The Edison lightbulbs. The calming hip nature of the staff. All obliterated each and every time the horn honks. I still do not know whether or not I like the horn. Sometimes it would make me laugh. Sometimes it would make me uncomfortable. Each and every time, though, I hoped it was a very special choice that had been made with a lot of careful thought. "What am I being told when a restaurant honks a horn at me every 7 minutes?" Am I being told "this is a serious restaurant run by a serious person. Am I being told "hey, I know the world is ending but lighten up." No, I feel like I'm being told "honk honk little piggy, here comes the slop!" And you know what? I kinda like that. Maybe it's a temporary thing? The bell pulled a hamstring and honky the horn did his best to go out there and be a substitute. I hope not. Because although there is good food and patient service for you to enjoy the horn is the star of the show. It is a slap in the face of people who love the idea of brunch. It is a defiant celebration of those same people. The horn hates you. The horn loves you. You love how much you hate to love the horn honk. It is truly a shame Yelp will not let me leave a one star and a five star review because you will have both at the exact same time should you be so fortunate as to venture into Chhaya. Honk if you love great service.

I stopped here for lunch when they opened their door, so there was only a couple items ready to order since they were still cooking.  I got the roasted pork and rice, and I got the beef , corn, and yuca soup and it was great!

I was really intrigued to check this place out when I read about it so my boyfriend and I tried it out for brunch. As soon as we walked in, I was impressed with the cute and cozy set up. We must have gotten there at the perfect time because although it was almost a full house, we got to snag a little table right at the window. Little did we know, this table was anything but ideal to sit at when you're having a meal. Although the seats were comfy, they were so high up from the table. We practically had to hunch over to eat our food!

I got the Masala Chai Latte for my beverage which was ok. It was a little too frothy for my liking and lacking in the masala spice. For my meal I had the Truffled Egg Toast which was good, but nothing to rave about. 

All in all, I'm glad we checked this place out, but I'm not sure if I would go back. Maybe I'll drop by to give their coffee a try, but the food was mediocre.

I am so pleased that I have the opportunity to review this place. Pizza Luna has a killer pizza. Wow! It is exceptional.

At Pizza Luna, we ordered a 12" pie with half pepperoni and half mushroom and extra cheese. The crust was thin and crispy on the outside, yet soft and baked well on the inside; basically wood-fired to perfection. It had just the right amount of tangy tomato sauce. The meat, cheese, and vegetables were so fresh and cooked to perfection. 

The front-of-the-house staff was remarkably friendly, engaging, and genuinely cared about safety. Everybody was wearing a mask!  The place was clean as a whistle.  The cherry, though, they were playing excellent music in the lobby (P.O.D, Saliva, Slipknot)! 

Please, please everybody, go to Pizza Luna. They have a stellar crew and they make a beautiful pie.  Thank you all, Tucson is a better community because you are responsible, honest, and humble business owners with a caring staff. Cheers!

On 6/27/20 we went to NYPD up the road and left the place because line staff (cooks, prep, etc.) were not wearing masks. The NYPD business owner also mocked us when we brought it to their attention, and he allowed an employee to take it upon herself to remind us that AZ is a gun-carrying state (and that we should be 'careful' about confronting people) Uhm, what the actual ****.  

(update 6/29 - NYPD has made some changes and acknowledged some of their mistakes)

Anyway, we found Pizza Luna, and it is one of our new local go-to pizza joints.

10:40PM on a Friday and denied service due to "staff shortage"... poor management, period. Sad excuse for a company after speaking with corporate and them basically saying "there's nothing we can do." Uhhh hire people?? Maybe that location can't retain employees due to such poor management, get it together. I'm sure it's not their fault but if other convenience stores function fine with 2 employees I will just take my business there honestly just close that location down if you can't "staff it" properly. Avoid this location at all costs other reviews are not wrong!
Great pizza, reminds our family of a New York style or Brooklyn type pizza. Great, good and delicious!

Pizza is definitely fresh with unique ingredients paired well together!... I ordered the sausage bianca, added white onion and extra Basil... But they forgot my extra basil :( called and told them. Travis automatically apologized and made things right.... my next visit get same size pizza and toping amount for free!!... although pizza did not have the basil it was delicious.. only downfall is it needed more cheese... Love my cheese!!

I guess somethings should just be left to the imagination when it comes to places that are part of the fabric of America. Valley Green Inn in all probability looks exactly as it did 200 years ago. Which is fine but it has a heaviness they gives the appearance of shabby. And I do offer forgiveness to service in the age of Covid understanding that things may be a little slow. 

The restaurant is dated but historical. Two of us dinned on this day I ordered the hot chicken sandwich which was very good and my guests enjoyed a portion of it as well. The pork sandwich with broccoli rabe and sharp provolone cheese I really enjoyed because I like the flavors that meld together however my guest was less enthusiastic about the sandwich.

I found the price is reasonable the food and service  fair, the scenery different. Would I return again? No but I would not discourage anyone from trying Valley Green Inn.

The pizzas (particularly the Margherita &  Puttanesca) and the salads (looking at you, Radicchio Caesar) are delicious. Pizza Luna has a surprisingly decent wine list and the staff is wonderful. I find myself here regularly, and happily so. The only negative as I see it is that the prices are a tad high.

Early this morning, experienced some really uncomfortable and racist comments from the girl at the checkout. Was a bystander during altercation between the employee and another customer. The staff member continued to repeat the comment "Black people don't know how to act" "I'd rather serve white people." This employee, we didn't catch her name but she made Wawa look bad last night.

At times like this I wish we could give out half stars because Pizza Luna would definitely be 4 1/2 stars!  The pizza dough is crazy good and everything tasted fresh.  We ordered smalls of the Neopolitan, Traditional, Sausage Bianca, and the Fig, Pig and Goat so we could all sample as this was our first time ordering.  My favorites were the Fig, Pig and Goat (definitely a pizza you savor!) with its contrasting flavors and textures as well as the Traditional.

Ordering online was super easy and straight forward although when I ordered for pickup "ASAP" the confirmation email had the pick up time as 15 minutes later.  I highly doubted it would be ready in that amount of time and my husband went there about 20 min after ordering and the place was super busy and the wait was at least 40 min from ordering.  Wish there was a way for the restaurant to relay more accurate pick up times, but probably next to impossible for an automated system to do so.

The main reason for less than 5 stars is that the Radicchio Caesar Salad had huge pieces of lettuce that would be more convenient to eat if presented in more manageable pieces.  Yes, we can tear the leaves ourselves (and did), but just something that would lend to the ease of eating a salad.

I was visiting my friend who just moved to University City. We wanted a bar to watch some Saturday college football. At noon it was dead but slowly started filling up. When we ordered we were one of 2 tables in the bar. You would think our waitress would focus on our tables. After delivering our food she went MIA and never came back to check on us. We needed more napkins and water, I spotted her sitting at the bar talking on her phone.. I COULDN'T BELIEVE IT! We finally flagged her down to pay our check. Besides the poor service, the food was just ok. Wouldnt go back.

Went there today and as soon as we walked in it smelled weird. We then we proceed to order and we got wings and she asked us bone-in and boneless. We said bone-in and went about the day. Got the food and went home. Opened our wings and they were boneless. She heard boneless and charged us for that but we actually said bone-in. Pretty upset because we hate boneless wings. Not going back to this location. Every time we go there something happens. No thanks!

Highly recommended.  Best pizza in the city of Tucson.  On a whim tried their Puttanesca Pizza for take-out -- ready in record time (just about 10 minutes).  The secret, says the staff, is the 700 degree pizza oven.  Thin but chewy crust and a beautifully blended set of toppings (note the Puttanesca is a "white" pizza and does not have any red sauce).  As for dining in, there are a few outside tables.  The inside is modern decor that was clean, bright and functional, but not very cozy and limited in size.  Beer (in bottles and cans) is available, as in wine.  Happy hour is from 2-5 ($3 slices).  Looking forward to my next excuse for some pizza take-out!

Pizza was pretty darn good. But the wings... the wings must've been from new born chickens. The smallest wings I've ever seen. Tasted great but man for the price they are and the size you should get double the amount of wings. Just do better at picking product!

That cannoli changed me! The food (we ordered an extra large four cheese pizza, a chocolate cake and a cannoli) was so good we made a second order for more! Definitely a place to keep in mind for a reliable meal delivered in a timely manner!

We ordered their pizza for the first time yesterday and had it delivered through GrubHub. I have specific expectations for my pizza and Pizza Luna met all of them. I like a firm, yet foldable, thinnish crust and a complex sauce. We bought 3 small pizzas so we could try different flavors. I very much judge a pizza parlor by their plain cheese pizza. Their Traditional Cheese pizza is the best I have had in Tucson because their sauce is that amazing and the crust is great. Their Sausage Rossa pizza was tasty,  with just enough spice in the sausage. The Fig, Pig, and Goat pizza may be the most unique pizzas I have ever had and I would definitely get it again.

Very fun bakery. There is a lot of seating and it's surrounded by windows so it's bright and open. We got the guava pastry, the cream cheese tornillo, and bread. It was all very yummy. The cafe con leche was also great. The staff is very friendly

I just came here with my daughter , the place is not very busy but it is filthy , every table is dirty it was very hard to find where to sit with 90% of tables empty , we managed to find one that only has finger prints and a little grease  and not a bunch of stuff spilled and cheese cups or plates on it , all the floors are dirty specially around each table , there's a bunch of teen working behind the counter but looks more like they are just talking and goofing around ,stuff not wearing mask or if so with their noses out anyways , I think they forgot all about COVID , I don't dare enter the bathrooms , carousel is not working or the other fast ride half matachines are broken and the ones that work have issues are very worn don't take the coins or spit it out

Dr. Cindy Balzer is an excellent veterinarian.  She possesses true empathy and love for all animals.  She has set the bar that I compare all other veterinarians to.  

Several years ago I was found by two stray kittens and they decided to keep me.  At the time, I was a full-time grad student and on a tight budget.  The Morris Animal Refuge referred me to Dr. Balzer.  She accepts Morris' neuter/spay vouchers and also administered all the necessary shots and tests for a reasonable fee.

Girard Veterinary Clinic is situated in a low income neighborhood and provides a tremendous service to the local community while remaining affordable.  Only walk-in appointments are available.  Sometimes the wait is long, but Dr. Balzer is worth it.  

Dr. Cindy Balzer is also one of the few veterinarians in Philadelphia who handles and treats ferals.  

I was awakened one night  by frantic sounds outside my apartment.  I ran outside to sadly discovered that a possum had attacked and killed a tiny kitten.  Here a feral cat had recently given birth and was she was nesting nearby.  I immediately became very attached to "Mama Kitty".  I fed and made a shelter for her and her brood.  Once she weened the remaining litter --  I was able to find homes for all of them.  Unfortunately "Mama Kitty" was too feral to tame and bring indoors.

With Dr. Balzer's guidance I was able to trap "Mama Kitty" and brought her in to be spayed and vaccinated.  I felt relief to be able to release her back into urban wilds knowing she'd now have a better chance of survival.  

Dr. Balzer's compassion enabled me to help this poor creature and play a small part in controlling the local feral population.  

We need more vets like her.

Delicious Philly cheesesteak. Definitely recommend. They also have chicken options for those who want to reduce the red meat. Keep in mind they are cash only. There's an ATM on the premises but I always prefer to just bring cash when I know places are cash only. Moreover, it gets packed QUICKLY--so if you want to try this place I recommend getting there when they open to avoid a wait. We went at 11 and already there were people waiting. 

They currently have tables in front for outdoor seating during the pandemic. There's also a football field right across the street which I've seen people sit and eat at. Just make sure to always take your trash with you and put them in the trash so they don't fly away. :) 

Tip: you can order for pick up in advance and it'll help reduce/avoid any waiting in line :)

When it comes to pizza there are a lot of options around ... and the list keeps growing.

Pizza Luna has thrown their hat in the ring and I will say they are a contender for the champ.

You get quality ingredients like San Marzano tomatoes, Fior di Latte cheese and Sopressata. All this on top of a crust that's been babied with love and attention for days. This, and a screaming hot oven produces a pizza with a crisp, chewy crust that's heady.

I can't even imagine ordering from the big national chains when you get quality like this and these l businesses need all the business we can throw their way right now.

They are rumored to have one of the best cheese boards around. They also have some salads that pique my interest. I dunno... with pizza this good it'll be hard to stray from the pizza. I will have to make that sacrifice someday. These are truly first world problems!

BEST PIZZA IN TUCSON!!!!!!! We love this place..GO HERE! Order anything..it will be good...this is on par with NYC pizza or better..And we lived in NY for years.. oh man..I dream about this crust!! Also, they have a crazy special every day of the week!

What. The. Shit? 

Seriously the exchange that I had here was so awesomely horrible that I'm almost at a loss of words to describe it. And it was so bad that I still can't figure out the punch line. After we left Carnivolution my friends and I decided to take the evening to their backyard and chill with some beers. Since they did it the last time I volunteered to make go on ahead and pick up a six pack at a nearby spot. Unfortunately the closest spot to the Tiberino Museum had so much shady activity going on outside of it that I decided to go nowhere near the inside. and that's what bought me to Cavanaugh's in the first place. 

Upon first glance it didn't seem horrible, and just seemed like your typical 3 star college bar with a decent selection of take out six packs. But the exchange that I had at the bar when I tried to pick up my six pack was hands down the WORST that I ever experienced. After waiting by the bar for a good 4 minutes with a six pack and $ to pay for it clearly visible I had to put up with the same 3 female bartenders looking right at me and walking by totally ignoring me, and a guy who clearly looked to be in another world of busy. I was tempted to leave by then, but it was past 1:40 am by then, and the last thing that I wanted to do was risk arriving empty handed, so I put up with the bull crap. Finally I caught the guy who looked to be in another world of busy standing by another register. So I made my way over thinking that it was where I had to pay all along, and the bartenders were just bitches who didn't feel like telling me. But as I got there, found out that the register was closed for the evening, and watched the guy use the previous register to get my change, I realized that they were just bitches who chose to flat out ignore me. To add insult to injury, as I was watching this horrendous exchange unfold, a polite server was kind enough to come up and inform me that I could have just paid for my six pack by the bar. Thanks Cinderella, now maybe if you could just deliver that memo to your evil step twins (maybe that's the punchline.). 

I realize that getting a six pack isn't much of a basis to form an opinion of a place. But if it can make such a simple exchange so damn complicated then I have no desire to find out what else they're capable of screwing up. epic fail Cavanaugh's. EPIC FAIL!
I absolutely love this pizza place! You can taste the quality in this artisian pizza. The employees are professional and friendly! I always have a great experience here!

We live close to this pizza shop and we've ordered many times. The pizza is delicious, fresh and comes hot! I will warn that it is a little greasy and it's definitely a thinner kind of bread. But I prefer it that way, so I don't mind. We are always pleased with the quality and quantity of the pizza. Also, the customer service is great!

Pizza was delicious, we got so many garlic rolls that were warm and tasty, and we got garlic parm wings that were our favorite so far in Tampa. They also have great deals and bundles for game day. We will definitely be back!

I had a bad first experience at the Valley Green Inn, but their customer service after the fact made up for it completely. My first experience was a Friday night celebratory dinner, when I had the catfish. A few hours later I came down with the most violent food poisoning imaginable. I called to warn them and never received a call back; which led me to originally write a poor review.

I was then contacted by the owner, who was extremely nice and apologetic. I have worked in the restaurant business and feel I can tell when someone is just saying what they need to say to satisfy a customer. I did not get this feeling at all from him, he was genuinely upset by the situation and disappointed by his restaurant's performance. He had even went back and found my check and also the invoices for the fish I ate. He was nice enough to offer me a generous gift card, mailed with a hand written apology note. 

I went back with a few friends and had a great experience. We all enjoyed our food and nobody got sick (which was a relief)! After the genuine customer service and having a second chance, I would go back again. Thank you Valley Green Inn!

This place is a pretty far-across-town drive for me, so unfortunately I don't get to come here regularly; however, the two times I have visited now have been such a fun experience I wouldn't hesitate to make the drive again! On the first visit my husband and I really enjoyed chatting with the owner and tasting their wine selection, hearing about the different wines they offer, and all about their business. We ordered the antipasto/charcuterie to start and it was AMAZING. We don't order boards a lot but for some reason this one really called out to us and was a great way to start our meal. Everything was fresh and snackable. I highly recommend this, even if you aren't hungry for a meal and just want a quick snack to enjoy. We also got a pizza (I don't remember which one because our visit was awhile ago) but I do remember that it was delicious enough we both agreed we would love to go back again and eat more. I also loved the chile oil offering for dipping my crust in. SO TASTY.
My second visit here was in the afternoon for some slices with friends, and I ordered a slice of sausage rossa and a slice of sausage bianca. Both were very good. While this isn't exactly my favorite pizza in town, it ranks high up on my list. The neo-Neapolitan style is good, but does lack that wood-fired depth of flavor. All you Tucson Eastsiders: I highly recommend this place! If you are on the east side of town (say, heading west from a trip up Mt. Lemmon) this is a great place to stop!

So good. So, so, SO good. Honestly the best pizza I have had since I visited New York earlier this year. 

In August I spent a few weeks in Tucson and I ordered from Pizza Luna three times. Their white pie is amazing and the pepperoni is perfect for kids. Be prepared--these pies are huge so they will last you a couple days. 

I miss Tucson for a lot of reasons, but PL is in the top three.

First time here! 

After getting my nails done I was starving! This place was less than a mile away and bookmarked so I went for it. 

The place was quite empty for a Saturday around lunch time. They had the foods displayed so that you can choose what you want just seeing how delicious everything looks. I decided on baked chicken, rice, beans and a piece of Dominican cake called Biscocho. Everything was delicious and I ate every single ounce of it. They filled the tray up to the top so I definitely felt I got my money's worth since they are slightly more expensive than most of Spanish restaurants. 

They man behind the counter was extremely nice and tried to get me to try the 'flancocho' which is mixture of flan and biscocho. Next time, my friend. Next time. I will most definitely be back and I feel like this may be my go to for my arroz con gandules fix since it's so close by.

There's lots to like here. The salads are outstanding and the pizza is very very good. They do several things which I approve of the first being that you can get a salad and either large or small size. The second is that they not only have pizza by the slice but that they have four specialty pizzas by the slice. In Practical terms this means you can have a salad and one or two pieces of pizza which is a big Advantage if you're a single Diner or you have different tastes than your dining companion. The restaurant is very attractive the service was good the wine was reasonably priced. I didn't get a chance to try the antipasto platter but it looked wonderful.
There's also a high inventiveness rating here. One of the things I like best about the place is that many of their ingredients are made on site like the lamb sausage I had on one of my pizzas or the lardoons or the salad dressing on the salad I had.
In any event they occupy a space which is never been successful for any restaurant but I think they're well on their way to reversing the hex.

I'm a new/first time cat owner of a cat a friend of mine rescued. She got him neutered and some shots but I knew he probably needed a closer look so I brought him to GVC. I have to say I was not disappointed. I called to make an appointment and got an appointment time for the very next day. The girl was very friendly and accommodating over the phone. And when I showed up for the appointment she was just as sweet.

There was little to no wait time and I was in and out in about an hour, maybe less. The tech (sorry wish I remembered names better )was also super friendly and approachable and gave me some great advice on caring for cats which I really appreciated. 

The Dr. couldn't have been nicer and more approachable. I felt really comfortable asking questions and not feeling like an idiot. He seemed very knowledgeable and I didn't feel pressured into getting a bunch of things done for my cat just to rack up the bill. He gave me some options and his opinions and told me to consider them, which I ultimately agreed to and I have to say the prices were reasonable. 

I can imagine this place might be a nightmare if you don't have an appointment so definitely try to make one! And also the waiting room is very small but my cat and I were the only ones in there at the time so it was no problem for us. Just a fore warning to future patrons. 

Definitely will be going back. Staff is wonderful!

Brand new to Tucson, I was so excited to try Pizza Luna, which got rave reviews. I am a born and bred New Yorker and went there with high expectations. When you walk in, you are treated in a warm and friendly manner, the guy at the register was sincere and helpful. I ordered a Ceasar Salad and a regular Neapolitan pizza.  The salad came first while the pizza was cooking. It looked gorgeous. The lettuce was extremely fresh, sprinkled with grated cheese. Unfortunately, this was a case looking great, taste - eh! It was not bad, it just did not taste like much of anything. The dressing was totally bland and tasteless. I was not looking for the traditional heavy Ceasar dressing, but this just missed the mark. Then the pizza came. Again, looked great. I will say the crust was sublime. It is different than NY crust but excellent. That being said, three things make a pizza, crust, cheese quality, and THE SAUCE. The sauce on Pizza Luna's Neapolitan is made with "San Marzano Tomatoes, Fior di Latte (homemade mozzarella), Chopped Garlic & EVOO." Sounds heavenly, perfect ingredients. The results - the sauce is really disappointing. San Marzano Tomatoes form a light sauce with delicate flavor to be sure, but the results here were really disappointing -  bland, no depth, flavorless, but doused with lots of garlic. I am the type of person that if a recipe says to put in 2 cloves, I put in 4. A true garlic lover! The garlic here was overpowering and you will be tasting it for hours. The sauce needs some herbs, salt, pepper, and a touch of sweetness, something to take it up a few notches. This review is exclusively about the Ceasar salad and Neapolitan pizza. The crust was good enough to entice me to return to try with regular and specialty pizzas, like the fig, pig, and goat pizza that sounds awesome.

I hate giving one star reviews, but this place, IMHO is overhyped.  From the outside the restaurant looks contemporary and modern, but that's where it ends.  Marketing is slick with their logo.

The pizza tasted bland, no different from any other franchise pizza chain in Tucson.  It lacked quality Italian oil, if there was any, mostly a lot of sauce and cheese on dough. After the first bite it was uninspiring!

When I read some of these 5 star reviews, it makes sick.  Have they been paid the reviewer?  That s what comes to mind when I read those reviews. This is unauthentic pizza, but if this what you are used to,enjoy.

Between the impressive selection of Coffees, and the amazing things that it manages to do with waffles, Chhaya is a perfect brunch spot that will have you coming back for more!

its welcoming atmosphere and interesting art on the walls (They usually have an opening every 2nd Saturday) offer enough ways of putting you into a zen like state. Especially when you factor in the many smells of fresh ground coffee. Chhaya not only utilizes a pour over method for their brews; they also have a siphon and French Press system. whether you enjoy coffee, espresso, or tea; or even Belgian hot chocolate, masala chai, or South Indian decoction; you'll be a fan of the many varietals that you'll find under their roof. 

between pumpkin waffles, French toast waffles, and cornbread waffles with sausage gravy; I was having a hell of a time deciding which one would send me into waffle heaven. but the fully loaded huevos rancheros waffle that came with chorizo sounded ay to pass up. and in the end it proved to be equal parts caliente and fresco! But if you're not a fan of waffles you'll at least get a kick out of their many sandwiches, pancakes, yogurt parfait, eggs, oatmeal, or other. Because at Chhaya flavor comes first!

Stumbled upon this place during their happy hour and ordered the Fig, pig, and goat pizza. It's The most delicious pizza I've ever had! It's the perfect combination of savory and sweet. I can't wait to have another one. Service is quick and friendly also.

I got my mocha in a soup bowl with a coffee cup handle. It was hilglorious, a word I just made up now when something is both hilarious and glorious. If you don't like my new word then that is unfortunate for you.

Apart from the generous portion, it was also a really good mocha.

The eggs benedict waffle has a baller piece of thin ham in it. Also, it is a cornbread waffle. I love cornbread and I love compartments in my food so it makes sense that I would love the cornbread waffle that the eggs are served upon.

The cinnamon sugar waffles with chocolate chips are fine.

I'm probably going to return because I am intrigued by the vegetarian chili waffle idea. Protip: get there early and sit on the vintage chairs in the storefront window on a nice morning. It is the kind of scene that you'd expect in a Ben Stiller montage about 3/4 of the way through the movie right before the make-it-or-break-it dilemma(which he obviously overcomes and gets the girl).

Cute place in Wissahickon, its casual but has great food. We made a day date starting here for brunch - we got the burger and fries and the cheese plate with a couple of drinks. We walked it off after with a short hike. If you have reservations, you can park at the bottom of the hill near the restaurant which is an added bonus.

Would definitely come again if I wanted to tack on a meal with my trip to the lovely Wissahickon.

Great place for brunch, especially with out of towners...with the parking situation a bitch on the north side of the park, its worth the price of admin just to park, eat and hike.

Good service, great scenery..good solid food.

I wished I could have tried more at Chhaya, and will hopefully return -- but I was sad to find that they stop serving food at 3 (because no one eats after 3?) so I was left to get a limeade ... and they were out of it ... but the raspberry lemonade was really quite good. The place has a bit of a "cooler than you" vibe that I'm not really into, but I could see how it may be nice if you have time to chill and stay there for a while. I'll likely try it again.

Girard had a nerve to post on FB yesterday( after weeks) regarding.y PrettyGirl Prada. If it were left up to them my furbaby would be dead!
