I couldn't believe how great the reviews were for this trailer-based operation, but they're entirely deserved. I assumed the offerings would be breakfast burritos or something simple to mostly make in advance. But no, I got a perfectly prepared, made to order frittata full of quality ingredients. Delicious!

Even the grits were good, and I don't like grits. The coffee was perfectly prepared and fresh. All for a very reasonable total of $7.50. The fellow running it is friendly and attentive. When I headed there, I wasn't sure where I'd eat, but he had put out a couple small tables to enjoy your food in the park.

For a few reasons, I really wanted to like it here. The service was great from start to finish and overall, I really enjoyed myself. However, there's just something missing...the pasta special I got was good, the escargots were just ok(I like parc and beau monde's better). Entree was pork osso bucco which I was excited about, but it was only ok...almost lacking in flavor, though I needed a gallon of water after the meal. I was very happy about the la Colombe cappuccino with dessert, but not overly impressed with the cheesecake.  I wold go back if a group wanted to go, but unfortunately for the price, it just didn't make an huge impression. For 3 glasses of wine between myself and my fiancée, two apps and two entrees with cappuccino and dessert(one to share) our bill was about $160 including tip. I kind felt like I could have great pasta at porcini and bring my own wine and have a better meal. Just sayin...

Service is lacking. Complained about it and I got the vibe that I was overreacting. Our server ignored us. It was busy, but there is a way to acknowledge everyone and work the floor. They tried to make up for it but it was pointless because they were dismissive of my concerns. Don't come back and try and fix it, listen the first time. Ordered a flight and two of the beers were kicked. Chicken teriyaki lacked flavor and sauce, probably should order some on the side. I was so irked I lost my appetite, so I can't tell you how the pot pie is, I had them bag it up. I'm giving it to someone on my way out.

The food is excellent, prepared on site and all local and the beer... OMG the beer. Philly Special IPA is one of the 5 best I've ever had. Dank, juicy, and super hazy. Great place, great service and excellent prices.

Came here with my boyfriend a few weeks after they opened and he was excited because we always go to Iron Hill by where he lives. 

The service was quick and the food was good. I usually get the lobster flatbread and eat almost the whole thing. My guy loves their beer selection and free beer samples.

Center City's Iron Hill Brewery doesn't disappoint.  Super convenient location (for us downtown dwellers!), upscale atmosphere, loads of big-screen TVs, great cocktails and a varied menu (we did the filet mignon and the pickled steer sandwich, plus cheesesteak eggrolls and a coffee cake dessert) await.  We were seated promptly at a super-cool people-watching window table (we had a reservation), our server, Matt, was attentive, and our food came out piping hot.  The restaurant manager even checked on us.  We will back for another date night or a meal out with friends.  And don't hesitate to bring the kids -- we saw several families (tourists, it appeared) and everyone looked happy.
Didn't get a chance to try any of the food here, but they have awesome beer flights! Fun, semi-loud atmosphere and great location in the middle of the city.

I come to this location whenever I need a good and relaxing massage. When you first walk in the door, Kelly the front desk receptionist always has a smile on her face and remembers your name when though I haven't been there in 6 months. Colleen my massue was AMAZING! Just the right amount of pressure. Very friendly and very professional. Love this place and staff!!!!
Amazing food. Extremely fresh! He's awesome extremely genuine and he remembers his customers.

Very chill microbrewery with a clean feel. I watched a distressing Eagles game here against the Vikings, and despite the outcome, the drinks and food were pretty good and the environment was very tidy. It wasn't the most expressive venue, but for a simple place to grab some good drinks and food while catching a game at the bar, it was a really nice change of pace from the typical sports bar, where the beers and food always seem subpar.

Beer was was Ice cold and delicious. The food was just Ok. Skip the Lobster Bisque. It was not chunky like the waiter said it would be. The Brewskie burger was thick and juicy but the lettuce and tomato looked like yesterday's. And my fries were tired.

Great service, great drinks and great food! If you visit Philly come here! 
Try their pomegranate margaritas they are fire!!! Everyone has been great here and this is our second time here.

We came in the afternoon as we were just exploring the city. I make it a goal to step into many breweries as I can while traveling. 

It was really easy to get a table but we went to the bar as it was more interesting. The bartenders were really friendly and helpful. We spent hours just hanging out and was never pressured by the staff.

The only good thing about our night out at Iron Hill Brewery was the time my friends and I had together. We sat at the bar and ordered food. I ordered food when I arrived and after 30 minutes i was still waiting for my order. I called the bartender and he said he forgot to pit it in. As we sat and talked the ceiling started to leak. More like rain onto us and our food. The manager did come to apologized but that was it. We moved to a table away from the bar and the server came over to take our order. We explained what happened. Moat of us had finished but my friend wings she enjoyed but had not finished about three of them. We explained this to the server and  she said she would bring some more wings out. She was not very friendly. When she returned she literally brought out a plate with exactly three wings. Not a new and full order! Three wings! They also replaced the drinks of three of my friends and the replacements were not make correctly. The server dis not engage us and seemed as if she didn't want to be there. She gave us our check and on our way we went, damp clothes into the cold. Will not be back!!!
y'all, if you're looking at reviews tryna find a place to mack on, bruuuuuuh this the one.

What a great breakfast spot in downtown Tampa. I stopped over before I headed in to work. I had the english muffin with goat cheese, bacon, egg and spinach. It was delightful. Fair prices and great breakfast.

I rarely write bad reviews, but our experience here was miserable and therefore short-lived.  We had a reservation outside, but none of any of the tables were bussed (we tried 3 different empty tables).  There was a large group of teenagers running around a playground right by all the tables, maskless.  We were seated by three tables of 20-somethings who began taking pictures, maskless, next to our table for about 10 minutes.  All the meanwhile, we were not greeted by a server for a solid 15 minutes.  We were so uncomfortable being so close by so many maskless people and the restaurant clearly was not taking safety precautions, so we ultimately left.  Really a disappointment, considering we were really looking forward for our first experience here.  Also, indoors is no safer--we saw patrons walking around indoors with drinks, unmasked.  We felt very unsafe and will not be returning.
Ate here 3 times during a 3 2 day stay, atmosphere and food was excellent. Took a larger group back and was pleased with service and a wide variety of their menu.
I had John and he was amazing! I have a lot of stress and tension in my neck and shoulders and he took care of me.  Everyone was friendly and helpful.

Came here with family sat mid afternoon.food quality was pretty good. Portion for nachos was ok but on small side. The issue was service. Food arrived in timely manner, but then was abandoned and had to flag down passing wait staff just to get a refill on a water. Nobody came by to see if food was acceptable. Had to go chase them for the check. Was not overly busy, so frankly. It really an excuse for this poor a level of service.
Sat at the bar and our bartender was awesome! He found the perfect drinks for us and made our day. Very friendly atmosphere and we sat right down. First time here and would recommend.

Located in a great location right across from the Pennsylvania Convention Center and near public transportation. I was in the city for the Auto Show and wanted to grab some food and drinks before hand, so of course I expected the place to be packed! Knowing there was going to be a wait didn't phase me at all and I was half hoping for a seat at the bar, but no luck that day. But you can still at least order some drinks while you wait to be seated!

Getting here.... I prefer taking public transportation.. I took the Patco and got off at the 8th and Market St stop. But if you prefer to drive, there are several close parking garages and lots available within walking distance!

FOOD/DRINKS
The drinks were good... I'm more of a Porter and Stout gal so I went with their Signature Porter to of course try out their own brews and I was not disappointed. Husband liked his beers as well, he went with one of their seasonal beers (Full Throttle Blonde Ale) and then one of their signature brews (Vienna Red Lager) which he liked more. They do have options for flights so that you can taste a variety and then eventually order a bigger size. They have an option to join their King of the Hill club where it's a one time fee of $15 to get their perks of their beer club and get more beer for your money. Great deal if you love their brews and plan on coming back often.

The food was mediocre, but I also didn't go with anything fancy. I went with their Brewski burger. Their menu said it paired well with my Porter that I chose and I had actually wanted a burger so it worked out well. Didn't wait too long for the food to come out, but I was slightly disappointed. The bottom of my bun came out soggy and my burger was a little underdone. I had asked for it medium well but it was little bit more medium almost medium rare. I didn't complain tho cuz I was starving. But the flavor was good, bacon on it was really crispy. Fries came out good and crispy and well seasoned. My husband got the Drunk Monk Burger and his was better than mine! The mushrooms with the Brie and Rosemary Truffle Aioli that came with the burger went so well together. I would order that next time if I wanted a burger again.

Service
I was pleasantly surprised at how fast we were seated when the line was out the door. I believe they said wait was around 30 minutes but was seated in about 15 minutes. In the beginning after we were seated, it was a little bit slow, which I half expected due to the Auto show being that weekend, but it still took maybe about 15 minutes to even be acknowledged. But once our server came, her name was Aaliyah, it was fine! Took a while to get a smile out of her, but she finally smiled, was friendly and took care of us. So thank you Aaliyah!

Overall, experience was good. Restaurant had plenty of seating and even has lots of options for big groups. Will definitely come back to this location to try more of their items  and more of their brews!

Probably the most upscale restaurant in South Philadelphia. Definately suited for a special occasion or celebratory dinner.
Located on the revived Passyunk Ave, you can also people watch the gentrification from the front of the restaurant.  

Stellar menu, which surprisingly included rabbit, with an uber professional waitstaff. 

South Philly finest!!!
I saw that they had green tea on the pictures of the menu, when I asked for that, he didn't have any. Major bust!

My wife and I have both had accounts at Massage Envy (River Rd. West and Oracle Rd.) for many years.  Around 2018 services began to deteriorate.  While the therapists were still great, the corporate culture began overtaking customer service and customer concerns.  We began to have repeated problems.  Finally, with the Covid-19 pandemic hit, we both tried to cancel our membership, but we found it nearly impossible to do so.  We got nothing but the run-around, and were told repeatedly that one cannot cancel without going into the spa and speaking with the manager--the last thing we wanted to do during the pandemic!  The months rolled by without resolution, and we kept being charged on our credit cards.  I finally got very angry and rude and they canceled mine (although I'd wasted around 4 months of monthly payments, which they would not return).  My wife finally gave up and we filed a dispute with our Visa bankcard company (she racked up over 6 months charges since she began trying to cancel her membership).  An awful (and costly) experience for both of us.

Let me begin with why 2*. The goods-Service was above average and the place is clean, large well decorated, and the bacon burger was real good with fries. Also can recommend the red wine vinaigrette which was very good. 
The not so good-The online ahead seating was worthless. We did this thru Yelp and still waited for all the groups ahead of us to seat our party of two.  I saw online that they had a filet, get there no filet. Server says they don't update their online menu.... Take it down then. I pivoted to the ribeye. The only thing with more fat on it in that restaurant was me. Worst steak I have had in years and $27. Half the potatoes were over cooked and the other half were under. They over did the lime on the asparagus which wasn't horrible but a little less would have been more enjoyable. Did a flight and all 4 were average to below average for craft. It was like big commercial style craft beer. Now I accept that I probably shouldn't order a steak at a brewery - but they shouldn't be serving one either. 
Stick to the burger and fries - nuff said.

Wooooorst! The wooooorst! 45 mins later! They need a manager, they have a manager but someone who acts like a manager. The cashier did great and was very apologetic. The whole time the manager stood in the back watching the whole thing and wasn't very helpful. The line was piling up and she just stood there. Do something lady! When we got the food. It was the saddest burgers I've seen. Never again!

Firstly, Paradiso accepted a reservation for 14 on a Saturday. Had to call 6 restaurants before Paradiso that would take a reservation at 7:30 w/o a set menu. Secondly, food was delicious.  Finally, service was very very good.  We will return

First time ever visiting an Iron Hill Brewery establishment and I've been wanting to try their happy hour for awhile. Nice spacious bar area and the staff is very attentive.

I believe they have about 10 beers on tap. I was able to sample a few beers before selecting one. I forget the name of the beer I tried, but I enjoyed it. My friend and I ordered several happy hour snacks. Sweet potato fries, although not crispy enough for me, was delicious with the two sauces (sriracha aioli and a sweet bourbon cream). The naked burger sliders were tiny, but flavorful! Would order those two items again. The pretzels were what turned me off. They were hard as rocks! Totally disappointed, but our server was so nice enough to order another batch. The second batch was significantly better. I wouldn't order it again just because I don't want to risk getting another terrible batch. Our server even mentioned that they're not consistent! But seriously, major props to our server for providing such excellent service!!

Would I return to Iron Hill and/or recommend to friends? Sure, I would, but I'd tell them to stay away from the pretzels. lol. I picture it would be really nice when the weather gets warmer. There's a nice little area beside the restaurant that would be nice to hang out and relax.

Food was okay it was not the best. I believe this is a tourist trap who goes in the city.  

We went here with my fiancé, and let me tell you the waiter that we got was super rude!!!! He was more talkative with his friends next to us and serve them with the best customer service he did than us. Oh god!!! Can you believe my fiance wanted to get a drink, and he told us you need to be 25 yrs old to be able to buy a drink!!!! Dude we're 23 we can get drinks anywhere else except that time we were here. 

After that experience, we never wanted to come back anymore!!! Just horrible...

Right in the heart of center city on Market, the Iron Hill just invites you in for a drink! I love the high tops and comfortable bar booths. This brewery is fairly priced with numerous options. I liked the blue dog after tasting it in my $8 beer flight selection. The food was a little mediocre but does the trick! Happy hour is available here as well. Service was kind and attentive. We stayed more than 2 hours but felt very taken care of and not rushed.

The look of the restaurant is very inviting as well as the customer service from the staff, but the food... not so much. I've been to this restaurant before, but at a different location so I was expecting the food to be up to par. In short, the food wasn't. Starting with the cheesesteak egg rolls, one of the only good things from this order, they were made well and came out hot and crisp. I enjoyed them so much I ordered another set of them. Another appetizer we ordered was the calamari, it was unappetizing after a few bites. It was overly salty and left you not really wanting to eat it and other foods the rest of the meal. Our entrees came next, I ordered the chicken n baby back ribs whilst my aunt ordered a salad. She said the salad was good ,but it shouldn't be hard to not mess up a standard salad. My chicken and baby back ribs on the other hand were less than lukewarm as if they were sitting in the back for a while (not under a heat lamp). I'll admit the meat was falling off the bone easily, but the overall taste with the bbq sauce and the temp of the food made it drop dramatically. I believe I took 5 bites of it and didn't want anymore. We were hoping to finish off this meal on a good note so we ordered the chocolate lava cake (forgot to take a pic). The cake was not as expected it was more on the overcooked side for a lava cake and was not hot as it should be. It was as if it was sitting in the back for far to long and it took a while to get to us. The service of our waiter is what granted a single star for this review. Please do better

Let me start by saying that I was actually excited to try this place out. However, I think host Juliet is absolutely terrible at customer service. I greeted her with a friendly hello to which she did not reply, must be clueless on manners and what her position requirements are. While we put in our name, she appeared to be completely in a pissy mood. Young guy behind the bar was clueless too as I had to ask him to wipe the bar section I sat at due to spilled beer and also had to ask for a drink menu. You would think it was second nature to him. Overall with the improvement of customer service, I'd say this place would improve.

Last night my wife had her heart set on going to Los Cabalitos for some Margaritas and Guacamole on the hottest day of the year, but it was packed and I didn't feel like waiting.  So instead we strolled up Passyunk Ave and landed at Paradiso.  

I knew I would like this place when I walked in.  It has this feel of your Grandmother's living room in S. Philly but it is much larger; and they had the Phillies game on at the bar.  Our waiter was great.  He almost seemed excited to tell us about the menu and the specials.  I started with the Asparagus wrapped in pancetta with a truffled egg.  It was excellent.  What a good combination of truffle and saltiness.  My wife had a beet, ricotta cheese, and watermelon salad.  It was also delicious but rather sweet and probably could have been a dessert instead.   For dinner I had Olive Oil poached Halibut with mussels, clams, and calamari in a tomato broth.  The Halibut was great cooked this way.  It was juicy, not dry like when you bake it.  The tomato broth was bread dipping good also.  My wife had Black Bucatini with crab and calamari.  A very simple yet flavorful dish.  Bucatini holds the sauce so well and the squid ink gives it a nice flavor.  I skipped desert but my wife could not.  Although I cannot remember the name of the desert it was remniscent of the Dip Sum Donuts at Buddakhan.

Prices for both food and drinks were reasonable.  Overall, I highly recommend this restaurant and I will personally be going back.

I would endure getting another parking ticket to come here. The guy is so nice and friendly and makes AMAZING breakfast. 100% worth getting up early and enjoying a breakfast sandwich on the river walk for.

Awesome experience with our server Kristen! 
She was super helpful and attentive with allergy questioning about the beer and food list. The vibe of the outdoor dining was very enjoyable and my husband loved the few beers he tried. I had the Raspberry Lemonade cocktail and it was DELICIOUS. I only had one (don't know if I'm a lightweight or the bartender was generous- hehe) and I was feeling fantastic.  
Definitely will be back soon!!

Now known as motel 6, this place is run as a place to screw people out of money. They don't do the proper upkeep or cleaning of the rooms during the pandemic and then claim that the pictures you have and the discussion you had actually never occurred. So now you can all make the decision to not stay here

We were in town for a conference and came here twice. The food and beer are delicious, specifically the Nashville Hot Chicken Sliders and Truffle Fries! Also the service is on point. The table never got cluttered, the beverages were always topped off, and the consistency with checking in was timed perfectly. If you go, ask for Summer!! She's awesome and will make sure you're very well taken care of. Thanks for everything Iron Hill....we'll be back soon!
The chicken roti was so good. I'll definitely go back for that. Plantains and cabbage we're also great
Great food- great drinks!  It is a very popular establishment so make sure you make reservations.  We used Open Table and just walked right in to our table.  Highly recommend!!

This was a delightful find across from the Hilton in Tampa.  Our crew ate here every morning before our conference meetings started, even though the conference was offering free breakfast.  The cajun frittata was delicious and the grits went nicely with it.  The coffee was well above average. All for 8 bucks. Go here and watch the guy cook your breakfast in a trailer a bit larger than a phone booth.  You wont be disappointed.

Barbara is absolutely fantastic and I signed up just because of her. I got, hands down, the best massage I've ever received. 

I will admit I was not a happy camper when I first walked in.  I was in severe pain, carrying all of my stress in my neck and shoulders. I was thrilled that I got in on short notice, same day. When I got there and filled out my paperwork is super perky front desk girl ask about 9 million questions and I was getting supremely annoyed because I don't like the telephone game and I would rather just have the conversation with the massage therapist. She could tell I was annoyed so she backed off so good for her.

I didn't have to wait long to be seen and like I said, Barbara was absolutely fantastic. I feel like I am walking out of there a new person. The fluidity in her motion was just amazing. She is really really good and if she quits then I will be screwed because I'm stuck with a one-year membership but if I get to see her once a month for the next year I'm pretty sure that my back will never be in pain.

I used to frequent their Ardmore location back when I attended Villanova U., so I was excited to discover that they also had a spot in Center City! Comprehensive beer menu, friendly service, and perfect mood lighting -- I couldn't really have asked for more. 

I highly recommend getting out of your comfort zone and ordering a flight because they have so many fun and interesting beers on tap. 

I'm also a sucker for sweet potatoes fries and theirs came with two dipping sauces -- a bourbon vanilla cream and a paprika aoli. Can you say bone smack the teeth?? (Aka bon appetit for all you non-memers)
The food was fine. The service was good. But they played like 2 Pat Benatar songs, 2 Billy Idle songs and not ONE by Stevie Nick's while we were there. I almost asked to speak to the manager.

I am shocked to see this place has 4 stars. Went for dinner on a weeknight. The food was bland, cold, burned, or not fresh. Ordered the hummus and onion straws to start. The onion straws were charred and burned.  The hummus was tasteless and the "salad" with it had mushy tomatoes, odd colored cucumbers. The entree was no better.  The Thai flank steak salad was barely edible. Tough steak even though I got it medium rare. Wilted lettuce. A confusing "peanut dressing" that was just an Italian dressing with a sprinkle of peanuts on top. Beer was decent. Hence the one star.

The customer service here was absolutely amazing, COVID restrictions in Philly dictated that our group of 5 wasn't allowed to sit at the same table, but they worked it out with us and got us next to each other. The food was fantastic and the pair of brother waiters were super awesome. They took care of us and were very personable.

I just had the pleasure of sampling the beauty and wonder that comes out of this tiny food truck, and let me tell ya, I was floored! 

I had a breakfast sandwich that stands up to any breakfast sandwich I've ever had... And it was a TKO, my friends. It was The Opener on Faedo's Cuban bread. Beautifully done eggs with spinach, tomato, delicate cheese all toasted just right for a flaky, messy, delicious piece of perfection. There is a little coffee area with a selection of 3 brews, making it convenient to walk up and grab a cup while you wait a surprisingly short time for your meal. They say perfection takes time... But not here. It was quick and absolutely wonderful.

Equally as wonderful was the service. I learned after my sandwich was ready that this is a cash-only truck. And to my dismay, I really thought I didn't have cash. As I anxiously looked on at the gorgeous dripping of egg yolk over the wilted spinach and juicy tomato, I panicked.  But the gentleman chef kindly explained how he was going to trust me to go to an ATM and return with my payment, which was enough to restore my faith in humanity. I repeatedly promised I would, and I sat down and took my first bite of this delicious, delicious sandwich. When did, I heard angels singing and I had a romantic slow dance in my mind, down by the river, with this sandwich perfection. When I came to, I frantically dug around in my purse in hopes that the universe would miraculously make cash materialize in there and boom- I remembered I was holding my mom's wallet because I stopped by there for a bite as I waited for her to have a quick surgery nearby. Well, to my- and his- luck, my mom ended up having cash in her wallet and crisis was averted. (Thanks, Mom!!) But the fact that he was so kind was really heart warming and I won't forget that. 

If you are ever downtown around breakfast time, do yourself a favor and stop by this little wonder of a food truck. I guarantee that you will also have a romantic moment with the deliciously crafted fare there.

I went here pre-opening and wasn't that impressed.  The food was okay other than the fried cauliflower.  I ordered the linguine with cajun shrimp. When they brought it out they said it was a stew which makes no sense for linguine. The sauce was more consistent with broth and didn't stick to the linguine so it was bland.  The shrimp were overcooked and didn't have much flavor because the broth sucked it up. The thai chicken lettuce wraps were salted and didnt really have any elements of typical thai flavors.

For dessert I had the brownie and it was extremely dry and I could tell it was slightly burnt. They also forgot to put caramel sauce on mine.

The service was okay which is not surprising considering it was a test run and everyone is getting used to things. I can't say that I would go back with so many other food options in the area.
Very very good service. Attentive staff, Brandon was really great and personable.  Joined the King club and it's worth it! Get the bourbon stout

I was in town for a few days and happen to walk past this place. My group of four went for dinner on a Wednesday night around 6ish and there were a good amount of people at the bar and at tables. 

The food was absolutely delicious. Everyone in my group loved their meals and we all raved about the brussel sprouts, I highly recommend. I split the goat cheese grilled cheese and falafel burger with my friend. Both were great. 

I dock one star because the service is iffy. We had to ask multiple times for a soda I ordered and for water refills. There were also times when it waiter didn't come over to our table for extended periods.
Watched LSU beat Alabama while having some good food with great service.  More than just bar food menu. Call ahead or you'll wait awhile because it's a busy place.

This is a chain, which isn't inherently bad, but it does preset my expectations. However, we had a good time. Drinks were good, beers were cold and the food was fair. Chicken sandwich wasn't very impressive, but the philly egg rolls were good. The best part of our experience is because of their service and putting up with our big group.

WARNING: DO NOT PAY USING A DEBIT CARD! If they make a mistake you will not get the money back In your  checking account for 3-5 business days. We came here for restaurant week. We have been before and enjoyed it very much. The food was excellent- deserving of 5 stars. However the server gave us the wrong check charged to our credit/debit card. We pointed out the error and he said he would take care of it. He did not and the next day our checking account was over drawn as we were charged 156 dollars in addition to what we charged for our real bill. The place is closed Mondays so I was left with leaving messages and sending an email to an address on their web site. Heard nothing back. They are open Tue so I called them AGAIN and the person acts like its no big deal that I'm still out of 156 dollars and overdraft charges. "It should be credited by the end of the business day". Thx for NOTHING. It has now been 4 days and the 156 dollars has STILL not been credited to our account. Really left a BAD TASTE in our mouths, be careful if you dine here.

Went to this establishment for the first time today and I had a wonderful experience. I had nachos and a burger for an entree and the food was prepared very well. The quality of the food was great and all of the produce tasted very fresh. I also enjoyed the set up of the restaurant and being able to see the kitchen from my table. The restaurant was really clean and our waiter was so kind and helpful. I also appreciated how patient the staff was because my party sat and socialized well after we were done eating. I will definitely be eating here again and I recommend this place to anyone who enjoys good quality and great service.
Horrible.  The staff was rude, they lied about their prices, and won't let you pay via credit card even though they said they did.

Yolk, White & Assoc. made a tasty egg sandwich but there were two problems with it. First, the Cuban bread was pretty tough. I'm not sure if this was a matter of it not being freshly made or due to the heat/humidity outside. Secondly, without going into much detail, it gave me stomach problems at least three times that afternoon. It was the only thing I had eaten all day. So my first impression wasn't the best but I'd be willing to give them another shot since the ratings are generally high. It may be an isolated incident so I'll give them the benefit of the doubt and give 3 stars for now. Service was good. Prices slightly higher than average.

I've walked past Paradiso about a billion times in the years that I've lived in East Passyunk and I FINALLY made it to Paradiso!

First impression:  The inside is just as inviting as the outside.  Tables are spaced far enough apart so you aren't sitting in your neighbor's lap, but close enough so it doesn't feel like an Applebees.  Hostess and wait staff were all very welcoming.  Great vibe- I could have sat there all night.  AND just an FYI, Sunday is BYOB!!  We found this out ahead of time and came armed with a bottle of vino.  

The Food:  The meal started with some bread and dipping sauces.  There were three dips- a white bean, a pesto, and a roasted red pepper.  All three were amazing.  I was a bit disappointed in the bread- it was a bit cold, but otherwise tasty.

For our appetizer, we chose the burrata with tomato sauce.  Holy smokes.  This dish PROBABLY changed my life.  For those of you who don't know (I didn't until just recently), burrata is a cheese that has a hard outer shell of mozzarella and filled with a creamy cheese.  It's like a cheesy Cadbury egg.  And it's amazing.  I also really liked the bread that came with the burrata.  GET THIS DISH!

At this point in the meal, I was ready to give Paradiso five stars.  Until our entrees came out.

I'll admit that I probably made a poor entree selection.  I tried to step out of my comfort zone and went with the stuffed veal breast.  I thought it was a little too fatty and a little too rare, but I'm a pansy when it comes to meat.  My husband got the chestnut fazzoletti with wild boar ragu.  I tried a bite- it was decent, but I thought the brown pasta with a brown sauce looked a little unappetizing :/    For the record, hubs loved both dishes.

Bottom line- I WILL be back to try one of their more veg-friendly pastas (there was one with ricotta and swiss chard that was calling my name).  I'll give Paradiso another chance to earn that 5th star ;-)  And next time I'm out, I'll try not to step too far out of my comfort zone!

The Iron Hill Concept is well replicated in the Center City Space on market street. 16 different beers on tap, including the well known standards like Pig Iron Porter. I had the Oktoberfest Marzen which was a good representation of the style without being overly sweet. Service at the bar was efficient considering it was a crowded Thursday evening. Look forward to returning.
Very good food. I only wish it wasn't so noisy bt that's expected with a place like this. We really enjoyed it none the less
I just stopped in for a beer flight at the bar but the service is excellent, the beers are delicious, and there is a wide variety of things to choose from. I would definitely come back!

I had a great meal here, salmon with a Mediterranean style orzo and asparagus. All was cooked perfectly. Also had a pretty good beer of theirs that was on tap. The service was good and the prices were pretty good for Philly. Don't be put off because it's a chain because it's a good one!

I've been here a couple of times now and the experience was great both times. The menu is big enough that you will definitely find something for everyone. They have a great flavor, the chef definitely knows what he's doing back there. Some of the items are traditional and others are a little more creative, but all are very good that I tried so far. They also make a great old-fashioned!

Tucked away on the Riverwalk sits a tiny food cart that shows up as the number one breakfast spot in downtown Tampa. Being the adventurer that I am, I of course had to check it out for myself. 

With a clever name that fits in well with the area workers, Yolk White and Associates is a one man show under their roof. With a building that is roughly 4' x 6', everything is within an arms reach for the cook. The menu consists of several varieties of breakfast sandwiches, all are made to order, because there isn't room for much else.

I ordered, "The Opener". A spinach, tomato and cheddar cheese delight wedged between a piece of sliced Cuban bread. I added bacon because my wife wasn't with me. It took a few extra minutes from the time my order was placed until my sandwich was ready, but there was plenty of beautiful scenery around me to enjoy while I waited. Trust me when I say the sandwich was HUGE, so much that I will probably skip lunch. Note that there is no place to sit and eat at a table, but there are plenty of park benches around for you to sit and enjoy your coffee while you wait.

Was it worth the high ranking? Maybe. I did enjoy the experience. If I find myself back downtown on another early morning , I will be sure to seek it back out.

I will never go there again the general manager told one of my coworkers that he was too load told him to tone it down i asked him if we were at a church or a bar never responded they lost a lot of money when we get togeth cfdfdvvddvtdcer we spend a lot of money i guess we were not the right color and the waitress was very nice it was n't her fault
danny choe in the service department took good care of me and my camry

If I could give 0 stars I absolutely would. I went for a massage during the night and the staff was so rude to me. I was the only person in the lobby and they ignored me until my masseuse came out. They did not even want to check me in. I also had to ask to get checked out because they kept ignoring me even though no one else was in the lobby but me. I believe one of the people in the front was the manager, which was even worse. I also had a horrible massage to make it worse. The masseuse was nice but that did not make up for the massage or the terrible service in the front. I have been to many Massage Envy's in Arizona and in different states and I have never been treated like this. I will not be going back and neither should anyone else if they expect to be treated with respect and to have a good massage.

This was such a fun spot. You have to ask for Scott as your bartender, he was on point according to my vague description of what type of beer I liked. The food was fresh and the salmon with the power salad was just perfect for the hot day. The ambiance is nice and people are very nice. Definitely will come back

Opentable roulette wins again. Came here for dinner on Saturday night. We opened up our trusty open table app and they had a open spot for the 4 of us. Seated right away and on our food adventure in south philly. Started with a bottle of wine and some calamari. The wine was great, and the calamari had great flavor. The smelts could of been left off and that was probably our only negative of the night. I had the black ink pasta which was amazing. The seafood with the pasta was cooked well. My wife had the mushroom pasta which she said was tasty as well. My sister had the ravioli and loved it. We will be back

Fantastic brewery! Our waitress was amazing and we talked beer with her for quite a while. She even gave us a tour of the brew house. The food is great as well. Highly recommend this place. May favorite in Philly so far.

If I could leave a zero I would. The food was horrible. Do get caught up in the thing between pats and Geno's. They should feed this stuff to dogs, but wait that would be cruel to the dog. This is pure vomit!

With just a short walk away front our hotel we decided to give these guys a try , once seated we started with some beer, I had a Pale ale not bad hubby had an IPA good as well. 
Appetizers we tried the Philly cheese steak egg rolls , yumm these were very tasty also tried the Jerk Shrimp , good as well has quite the spicy kick to it. 
Main dishes I had the Steak salad this was very good , decent steak nice taste good salad & dressing hubby had a Burger w Fries .. burger was good as well. 
Not a lot seems to be open late in the area these guys were good over all , big place , service was good & prices were reasonable we enjoyed our meal.

Let me start by saying I attended college at University of Delaware and have been a long time fan. Their beers are great especially the seasonal selection. They keep the place super clean and they truly hold their wait staff to a high level constantly testing them on the menu. They care about the quality of their food and offer a good selection. Their wings are great and classic. The chipolte flavor are great when looking to switch it up. I don't know why but they have my favorite blue cheese whether I'm dipping wings or having a salad. It's soo good. I love that there is now a location in Philadelphia.

It has been a very long time since I have been to Philadelphia and unfortunately it was for a convention so most of the nicer places were all filled up so we settled on Iron Hill. 

The service was very solid and much better than I expected. They were leaving tables open due to the labor shortage so they are being smart!

We had  cheese steak egg-rolls and Shrimp for appetizers and I had scallops for my entree. The egg-rolls were a bit greasy, the shrimp were well prepared and the scallops were cooked perfectly and delicious. 

All in all this was a good meal with even better service!
Delicious food, reminds me of a nice comforting meal from back home. Thank you very much, I will definitely be back!

I was recently in Philly for a work trip. Our Team was staying at the Marriott in Downtown Philadelphia across from the convention center. We went here on our first night and liked it so much we went again the last night. They have some great high top tables in the bar that accommodated our party of 8 and 10 nicely. 

The servers here are on the ball. We were never neglected for too long. Food came out quickly as well. 

We ordered apps only both times we dined. The wings, chips and guacamole, and pretzels were all amazing, however the star on the app menu are the Philadelphia Cheese Steak Egg Rolls. Heaven. We had to get two orders because they were that good. The beers are also really good too. Pumpkin Ale for me!

Easy to pop in, grab a beverage, and hang with the Team!

Wonderful food and beer! Our server, Justin, was amazing and super sweet. Working in a restaurant myself I could tell that management was not helpful in any way. I watched him yell at the servers, while he was on his phone all night. Management is supposed to be helpful not scary. The longer my visit went on the more I was enraged with the way the manger talked to the servers. Come here for the food, beer and servers. Not management.

Pros:
1. This is a great place for everyone! When we went here there were families with small kids, couples, folks grabbing a bite after work, and seniors. I had a problem with another patron & the Hostess quickly addressed it and made me feel comfortable enough to stay.
2. The service is fast.
3. The beer selection is good. I tried the flights; I'm not very familiar with beers and the descriptions on the menu really helped me make my decision.

I recommend the wings and beer flight. The seating is socially distanced. Idk how they're handling masks but I'm assuming they're not required bc no one was wearing them. The staff are friendly and helpful, and the restaurant is clean.

Cons:
The other menu items aren't that good. I DO NOT RECOMMEND the Meat Trio Pizza & Salmon Burger. We also ordered the  Philly Cheesesteak egg rolls and they were just okay; I've had better elsewhere.

We were shopping in center city and needed somewhere for a bite to eat. We tried Hard Rock but it looked a little understaffed so we went across the street and had an amazing time. Service was prompt and thoughtful. The server brought us some beer to try and they were all really really good! The cheesesteak egg rolls were really yummy! My husband got the ribeye, which was a little thin but still cooked perfectly, and it was delicious. Dessert was a little underwhelming as far as choices went. It felt a little too chain restaurant for us. The highlight was the patience the server had with my mother and father who didn't speak english. Natalie? Was very patient and helped us through the menu. With all the mediocre spots in the area, this place stands out.

Well, that was a nice escape after feeling a bit claustrophobic across the street in Reading Terminal Market! Pleasantly surprised with a juicy beer and nice lunch after flying into town for a conference. 

As to be expected, they were plenty busy on a summer Monday at noon, especially with plenty of people enjoying the World Cup playing on TV. After a 30 minute wait I was able to sit, relax, and tune into a conference call with my iPhone and earbuds in a booth. It was a bit of chaos at the host stand, but their text system when your table is ready worked great. 

Enjoyed the newly popular glass style with the strawberry hazy IPA, which was a juicy representation of the popular New England craze. Really like the salmon banh mi burger, cooked perfectly and light, with a nice accompaniment of a small salad. 

Solid brewpub with actual food, not just burgers and fries. Good service and nice variety of beers that was not dominated by IPAs. I wasn't planning to stop into Iron Hill, but glad I did upon arrival into town.

Large selection.  Food fresh.    Foodies can find something to like. 

You can fill up on varied small plates/appetizers. 

Staff nice and accommodating.

Need cash! Go to nearby Well's Fargo ATM, which is outside on opposite corner relative to where the stand is. 

Yup. All the things everyone else said. Worth the walk. 

We received two high quality breakfast items and a coffee for what our hotel would have given us for one basic dish. ***Take the walk and bring this back for a way better breakfast-in-bed than your hotel would have provided!

Grits were good; seasoned well. Not the best, but we lived in NC for a while. 
Cajun frittata was excellent. 
English sandwich great. Bacon Goat Cheese spread was not shorted, and the sandwich is very well balanced. 

Guy running the place was friendly knowledgeable and efficient.

Visiting from out of town and the service here was horrible! Took at least 20 mins for someone to come take our drink order, and then not return for another long while with just water. As we were about to leave because our server forgot about us , she see us in the booth but then she decided to tend to the tables before returning with our drink order. I wouldn't recommend coming here at all. Find a different brewery
Dylan was very nice and the food was absolutely delicious! When back in Tampa we will definitely be there again!

I moved to the E. Passyunk area on Saturday and did not plan ahead.  Thus, finding a restaurant to eat dinner at without a reservation was a serious adventure that night.  My adventure was not helped by the unseasonably warm temperatures.  After trying several restaurants with an impatient family member who was unwilling to wait, we finally came across Paradiso.  It was a miracle--8:00 pm on a Saturday night and they were able to seat us (though the host didn't look thrilled that we had no reservation and we felt bad, but were too desperate after our search for a restaurant to dwell on it for too long).  

The wine prices were decent for a restaurant like this (seemed to be trying for a fine dining vibe).  All of the house wines were $8 to $9 a glass, with several bottles coming in under $40.  I had the New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc, which was typical, crisp and cool.  Our waiter informed us that all pastas were available by in appetizer sized (half) servings.  Hearing that, I decided to start with the beet salad--my version of which came with toasted pistachios and housemade ricotta.  The beets were nicely cooked, not overdone.  The plate was less of a salad and more of a giant plate of earthy beets.  I couldn't finish, as the dish was too sweet for me by the end.  There were a few greens tossed on top of the beets, but they seemed more like a garnish than a serious element of the dish.

For our entrees, my companion and I both got the spinach and ricotta gnocchi in a brown butter sage sauce.  The gnocchi were light, and you could really taste the spinach and cheese.  The gnocchi was topped with a ton of the brown butter (there was a pool of it in the bottom of my bowl when I was done my meal).  I only found one sage leaf in the entire dish and wouldn't have minded more to give the butter a stronger sage flavor.  I ordered the appetizer serving and my companion ordered the full dish.  Both were decently sized, the appetizer portion was, in fact, about half of the full-sized portion (though the price was not half the full sized), and I was perfectly full at the end of my meal.  

Altogether the meal was okay and we left full and not disappointed.

Wendy's is my absolute favorite fast food joint. Let me tell you about my shit experience today. The drive through speaker is trash and the volume is awful, change it out and update your restaurant a little come on it's 2018! The person at the drive through repeatedly asked me "anything else" after every word I said!!! She didn't ask me what drinks I wanted nor did she ask what I wanted in the kids meals, she was obviously preoccupied and didn't give a shit about any customers considering I was the only one in the drive thru at the time. My fries tasted like cardboard and they were super old. The meat on my baconator looked like the chick in the drive thru shit it out onto a bun. Avoid this trashy "restaurant" at all costs don't waste your time or money.

There was a time where I would have scoffed at you if you told me that something like Iron Hill Brewery was going to open in the epicenter of Market East! There was also a time where I never thought I'd see somewhere like Iron Hill move any closer to Center City Philadelphia than its East Falls location. 

But many things change over time, and the huge construction that's been happening on Market Street has contributed to bringing in what might just be the largest Iron Hill Brewery I've seen yet.  As a card carrying mug club member I was destined to come in and imbibe on a few glorious brews. But it also provided some incredible food and a stellar happy hour!

I'm one of those people who rarely jump on card deals for restaurant spots. But I love the life long King of the Hill membership that Iron Hill does since you get a point for every $1 spent on food purchases, and a $20 gift for every 200 points. You also get to drink out of a 22 oz mug for the cost of a pint, get invites to exclusive events, and get updates from their local brewers!

Whether you enjoy sitting outside, by the bar, or in a comfortable booth, you'll find that perfect seating option at this Iron Hill. For me I like slipping into the bar during their Happy Hour and grabbing a good burger deal for $10, or hitting up their Taco Tuesdays. But I also enjoy offerings like their Kennett Square mushroom soup, ahi tuna poke, voodoo chicken flatbread, and fried brussel sprouts for appetizers. And I love sandwiches like the lager braised pulled pork, the Santa Fe turkey burger with guacamole; and the grilled Brewben that puts corned beef, bacon sauerkraut, and gruyere cheese on marble rye.

For beers they occasionally release a solid special beer named for things like Philly's favorite orange mascot and Superbowl play. But they also have plenty of damned good IPAs, lagers, Belgian ales, and other winning beers!
Fantastic breakfast!! Omelettes and frittatas were wonderful, along with grits which we don't really have in Michigan. Thank you, Dylan! We will be returning tomorrow.

Amazing location, beautiful scenery, the worker was very nice and kept good conservation while waiting on food, which was not long. The cutest little food truck with amazing food. This was my first time and I will be eating here more than a breakfast/brunch restaurant.
Absolutely fantastic - $5/6 for a breakfast you would pay $15 for at any decent breakfast joint. Cajun Frittata and Dujour Omelette are delicious.... homemade grits are a bonus

Iron Hill is a microbrewery with delicious bites and exceptional brews. There are multiple locations in the Philadelphia area, however, I took my parents to the location on 12th and Market Street. Both the atmosphere and menu are similar to that of your typical brewery and restaurant. They do offer a variety of beers and are very generous in their taste testings. If you like IPAs, I suggest trying the Philly Special with flavors of tropical fruit and pine.

I was out of town on business in Philly and literally stumbled across this brewery just by walking around. The place is always packed for the early evening specials but do not be discourage it moves pretty fast and is worth it. I tried a few of their beers and was not disappointed they had a few delicious full bodied IPAS yet my favorite was the Philadelphia style, the bar service was very attentive, fast, courteous, and fun. I sat at the bar by myself and a few guys sat next to me making friendly conversation, turns out it was one of their vendor distributors and a brewery investor, so I was treated to a few more tastings by them. I had delicious wings cooked the way I like them super done and crispy along with their home made blue cheese dressing.overall a pleasant experience. 
And keep this in mind  "you never know who's sitting next to ya at the bar"

Stopped by Iron Hill for a late dinner after spending time in the Fashion District. We were seated immediately but it took a little while for our waiter to get to our table. When the waiter came we ordered beers to start. I ordered the Tangerine Scream and he ordered Bedotter. The Tangerine Scream was pretty good and had a nice tart taste. My boyfriend's beer, however, was delicious and I highly recommend it to anyone that likes Belgian Tripels. As for food they only had the late night menu which was mainly just appetizers. We ordered the Margherita pizza, cheesesteak egg rolls, and Nashville hot chicken sliders. The pizza was okay, we agreed it wasn't the best or worst pizza we ever had. The cheese steak egg rolls were fantastic, probably some of the best I've had. I highly recommend trying them. The chicken sliders were also delicious but I have to say the chicken on them was very skimpy and didn't have much substance; other than that the flavor was excellent. 

Overall, I think I would return to Iron Hill in the future, but probably during their regular menu hours!!

Worst experience ever, and I've been a client for over a decade. This location is the pits. The girls in the front are rude, crass and immature. My session was rudely ended by the therapist with a personal problem and the hustled me out the door like a cow. If you want unprofessional, go here. Otherwise go to the other locations. At least their front staff actually greets you..

After being well received in every restaurant Ive been too with my baby I thought it was about time to write this review. 

I was very disappointed by Iron Hill Brewery & Restaurant. I was looking for a lunch spot to meet another mom(pre-pandemic), both of us were new moms and had 9 week old babies. I purposely looked for a "child friendly" restaurant that would accommodate us. Its a lot to venture out with a new baby but from the reviews I had read I thought this place would be perfect. I was wrong... I was greeted by a very hostile hostess who was not happy about the fact I had a stroller. I was made wait for 20 minutes and when she found a seat that would apparently work for us she ushered me in and pushed my stroller in after me, it was between my table and another table with 4 people. I was trapped couldn't leave my seat without pushing out the stroller first and the baby was facing outward!!! When the other mom arrived and saw the situation she complained and we were then reseated to a booth which fitted with baby's bassinets. All in all for one of my first trips out as a new mom this left me feeling deflated. The food was average the waitresses were nice. The hostile hostess was appalling she made us feel like a nuisance and not welcome.

After having a membership for a few years, This summer I decided to cancel- mainly because I don't use it that much and we are trying to cut monthly expenses. On Tuesday, July 23, I spoke with Liz (River Rd location in Tucson AZ) and she cancelled my membership for me without issues and said I had 2 credits left to use, so she scheduled an appointment for me to use these remaining credits. 
Today (Sunday July 28) Candace called me back and said in order to cancel my membership,  I would have to use the remaining credits for my last membership fee-that I was never going to use. She said I had two choices-I could use my remaining credit to pay the future monthly fee,  or pay the last fee to keep my credits. Since I am well out of my contract, and as a customer for at least 3 years, I think it is in very bad taste to not allow me to use my remaining credits just because I was going to cancel.  It is extremely unprofessional to call me back five days later with a completely different contradicting story. She was unprofessional and not very polite. I will never return or recommend to anyone. I've also noticed they have an extremely high turnover. Since I've been a member there I have never been able to have a consistent massage therapist because they are always leaving.

We stopped in late night last night for about the last hour and a half before they closed after having dinner and we just wanted ass place to sit and chat and have some fun wine and cheese and possibly dessert. Everything was very nicely done the bartender and waiter or very friendly and very helpful when the owner came over and we talked quite a while at the end of the night truly an enjoyable experience we will definitely be back for a full dinner as soon as we can get down there again

Every year I look forward to my walks around the river walk and morning chow at yolk, white and associates .  Always good food a nice chat  in the mornings I'm in town for a conference!   Highly recommended instead of the hotel food!
The food was good, the beer was great our server  Madelyn was busy but attentive. I had fish tacos which are really good. My friend tried a burger she was happy with

Iron Hill joins the Market East revamp with a new and highly visible brewpub right across Jefferson Station/Convention Center!

Atmosphere: great airy feel with large windows, affording architectural views of surrounding buildings. The brewpub decor and layout is similar to other Iron Hill locations - with bar, high top, and table seating.

Food: Menu is still evolving, but had a good mix of bar fare/snacks, as well as healthier options. The crab cake was plenty crabby!

Beer: solid selection of signature and seasonal beers on tap, ranging from IPAs/Lagers to Porters/Stouts ... Iron Hill scores GABF bling pretty much every year, so definitely try these!

Perks - Happy Hour: M-F, 4P-6P. $2 off drafts: 12oz, pints, King of the Hill mugs only (tentative schedule, activation pending).

Perks - King of the Hill: $15 one time fee for a lifetime membership. The perks are sweet and plentiful, but highlights include: 
- 150 bonus points at sign up, 
- $20 reward for every 200 points, 
- 1 point/$1 food purchases,
- 22oz mugs for the cost of a pint (16oz ), and
- Exclusive appreciation nights and event invites.

With a highly accessible location close to mass transit, hotels/businesses, and especially the convention center, I anticipate a constant thrum of activity at this spot ...and recommend making reservations. I look forward to many very happy hours here with friends and family!

I am a breakfast person! Yes, it is important meal for me. Not often do I need a big breakfast, but I always love something tasty. So I decided to check out this place and on my first visit I was truly blown away. I had the Cajun and it was so good. 
But you know what also makes everything taste even better? It's the ambience. It's the interaction with the people who make or serve the food. And this is were my personal experience gets even better. Today was my second visit and again, just a very nice, friendly interaction, with some good conversation. It goes super well with the food. Give this place a try. 

Tell the Chef The Swiss told you to come. He may tell you a funny story about my bad bad slaughtering of the Menü name...

Really amazing beer selection. Outstanding service. Very nice place. It was an oasis to my boyfriend and I after walking and sightseeing all day to have somewhere we could kick our feet up and drink. Very lovely. Highly recommend !

I have to be honest that I am not a huge fan of chain restaurants, but when I came here for a work lunch I was pleasantly surprised. First, the staff was really friendly and attentive- we had a reservation for fewer people than we ended up being, and they accommodated us without issue. They have a pretty extensive menu, with salads, sandwiches, entrees, etc. Someone in my party had a gluten allergy and they not only were able to accommodate her, but also had a manager come over to speak with her to ensure everything would go smoothly with her order. The food came quickly and was correct- I asked for no olives and dressing on the side for my salmon salad, and I'm glad they paid attention to that! I enjoyed my salad and ate the whole thing. The salmon was cooked well and it was flavorful. The salad was nicely sized, but I will say for nearly $18 it did feel steeply priced.

Tbh, I don't know that I would come here and pay these prices myself; but for a company sponsored lunch it was perfectly good.

I visited Paradiso for the first time this past Saturday with a friend of mine.  Clearly, a popular spot, as it was very busy.  It seemed as if the staff was a little overwhelmed, as it took awhile for anyone to actually notice we (and a few others) were waiting at the hostess stand.  We were passed by a number of the staff, and no one even acknowledged anyone was waiting, or said they'd be with us in a moment.  It was a little strange that at least three parties that were waiting to be seated were essentially ignored completely for about five minutes.  Would have been nice for someone to at least let us know they'd get to us as soon as they could.  

The room is very nice, with some artistic track lighting hanging from the ceiling, and art on the walls.  It's pretty tight, and they clearly have packed as many tables as possible in what is a decent-sized space.  Many of the restaurants in S. Philly are converted row houses, and are very narrow...this space is much larger, though again, it's pretty packed with tables.  They have a nice bar off to the side, which was also very busy.  The kitchen is at the rear of the room, and is semi-open.  

They have a decent wine and cocktail list, and I got an apple martini that was very good.  They had a few specials added to the menu...one was a salumi plate, and the other was a layered veal dish with veal and sausage.  We opted for the burrata and beet salad, the salumi plate (which I {after my drink} mistakenly called charcuterie, which the server was quick to correct), the duck breast, and the veal special.  My friend asked for her duck to be cooked medium, and the server explained that the chef only cooks it medium-rare, and that if she wanted it cooked medium she'd best order a different dish.  Not that I haven't heard of this kind of thing in the past, but it always surprises me.  Some chefs still think they're cooking for themselves, and not their customers.  

Everything was ver nice, with the exception of the veal...which was somewhat dry.  I can't help but draw some irony between the dry veal dish, and the curt response of our server about the chef's unwillingness to cook the duck to medium, ostensibly because it'd dry out.  

The service was a bit on the slow side...it took about 20 minutes to get the check. They were pretty busy, but the courses seemed to drag more than they should have.  I was also a bit surprised that they don't seem to have a pasta course and meat or fish course, but have appetizers, entree pastas, and entrees.  Not a huge problem, but it's always nice to be able to sample a pasta course and a main entree in a good Italian restaurant.  While I didn't ask specifically, I doubt they'd have made any accommodations in the portion size.  

Overall, the quality of the food was good, save the veal, and it's certainly a popular and long-standing establishment.  I could do without the attitude, frankly, though that's just my opinion, and someone else may not care as much.

Went here today for lunch while visiting the Christmas Village. We were immediately seated by a very sweet hostess. Our waitress brought our drinks out quickly and was very attentive and pleasant. I ordered the Nashville hot chicken sliders. Three mini sandwiches containing a burger bun roll, spicy fried chicken, mayonnaise, & bread & butter pickles. Super tasty. Only downside was I felt like the menu didn't have a big enough selection. Would definitely go back though.

The food is good when they don't forget anything. But the staff needs training when it come to their attitudes. No matter how polite & patient you are they are rude & disrespectful. If you ask for something THEY forgot they act like it's your fault. Never once has a cashier greeted me kindly at the window. And forget about asking for a drink carrier it's apparently too much trouble. If you're in a good mood don't go here they'll ruin in. Also this review isn't based on one visit but many. The male manager is exempt from this he was very kind.

I enjoyed the Nashville fried chicken sliders. Very crispy and spicy. We had a large group and service was excellent. Many people had burgers and said they were very good. Two people got their burgers wrong (over cooked and undercooked) so they  exchanged. The kitchen should have a way of marking them. I will return there and recommend it to friends.
I had a very nice beer and crab cake here! The waitress , Ariana, was both friendly and efficient, and the location , near the conference center, is convenient. All in all, a very nice experience!
This place is amazing! Great service, prices and quality! If I was working in the area I'd def be here daily! By far the best breakfast in downtown Tampa! Healthy quick and doesn't break the bank!

It's not often I visit a brewery before noon. I mean most places won't even open until that time...unless said brewery doubles as a full-fledged restaurant which is in the name here at Iron Hill Brewery. My buddies and I visited this Philly brew spot back in late July to culminate a final day of bachelor weekend festivities for our soon-to-be-married chum.

So like I said, despite the restaurant aspect at Iron Hill, we were only here for beer. No food was consumed which means my review should be taken with a grain of salt (or sip of beer if we want to stay on the suds topic). Though while you mention sips, these were some relatively tasty ones. 

Let's take one step back as we legitimately strolled into the spacious Iron Hill Brewery (& Restaurant) just as the doors first opened. We were given a nice high top table in the bar area with a waiter who was super friendly and explained each and every beer we drank. He also threw in an extra taster for us all of his favorite for anyone who didn't order it. Nice.

Back to the beer, a flight was the way to go in really getting to try a large portion of what Iron Hill had to offer. With more than a dozen brews available, the styles and choices were aplenty. An $8 flight for four was also fist-bump-worthy. A rockin' way to start.

So why not five stars? Honestly some beers were good, and some were just okay. I mean the Brambleberry farmhouse ale was legit and the Rocket Popz sour was quality (and blue in color!), but the others were mostly forgettable in flavor (sorry Dunkel, Porter, and Kolsch). Don't get me wrong, these beers weren't bad and with the brews available of types I didn't try, I could definitely see a return trip here.

Overall, Iron Hill Brewery & Restaurant is a great location in the heart of Downtown Philadelphia. They have a nice space and friendly service with respectable beer options, some stronger in quality than others. I'd love to come back to drink up more of their menu and perhaps actually eat something here. A little tasty food and we could be looking at a five star review in the future.
Friendly and helpful staff as soon as entered.  Helpful in explaining menu.  Ordered fish subs and fried butterfly shrimp.

We stopped here on a whim after arriving in town late on a Friday night.  Great music, beer, service and surprisingly excellent food.  We had the fried Brussels sprouts, fish tacos, caesar salad & my daughter had a simple cheese quesadilla.  The beer was good, which I expected, but the dessert was AWESOME.  Ever had a cheesecake in a ramekin?  Uh, yeah.  It totally works.  And the locally-sourced ice cream was perfect - not too sweet and very creamy.  Well done, Iron Hill.  I'm already looking forward to our next visit...

$18.95 for nachos with chicken and a tiny little 2 oz. ramekin of guacamole. 3 stars? My table was incredibly salty about paying the extra $2.00 for a 2 oz. ramekin of guacamole when the table beside us got like a heaping 8 oz. scoop of guacamole piled on top of their chicken nachos. That price is hefty for some darn nachos, LOL.

Service was great though, and she was super friendly. She took our orders and ran our cards in a timely manner. We honestly came here for some drinks before the Drake concert. The wait time was quick since we grabbed a seat at the bar.

The place was clean, and the bathrooms were maintained. It was pretty busy inside, and the menu looked like it can accommodate any diet. The beer was served cold and tasted great. Our green tea shots arrived as our last order, and they were sufficiently strong. 

It wasn't my vibe, but I'm sure this place is a great spot for food and drinks for anyone else.
This little truck is soo good. Everything is fresh and made on the spot. Sucks they are not open on weekends, but on the week days I'll be there.

Ok, what do you do about 2 star service with 4.5 star food?.  You get three stars.  Given that appetizers are $10-14 and entrees are $20-28, service should be better, but there were only two people as waiters, bartenders and maitre d.  I asked for an extra spoon to sample the soup but it never arrived.  Ok, a simple oversight.  But the check took 15-20 minutes to process and return, finally arriving after two other tables came and left.  Not good.  Unfortunately, the poor staffing and mental lapses by the wait staff turned a great wine into a sour experience.

That said, I highly recommend the zucchini blossom in puff pastry.  Delicate and very tasty.  The gazpacho was very good made with heirloom tomatoes, although the spicy version at Avenida is better.  The tilefish, cooked with artichokes and butter was perfectly cooked with a crisp top sear. 

Come eat here, but be prepared to wait and wait, if there are only two staff in the dining room or get up to get the waiter's attention.

I have always been a fan of Iron Hill Brewery and this location is a great addition. I came here on a Monday late afternoon for their happy hour and I think I have found my new happy hour spot in the city. The happy hour prices can't be beat and since Iron Hill is a brewery first, their craft beers are a must. Became a King (Queen) of the Hill rewards member since I know I'll be frequenting the restaurant now that this location is up. 

I was greeted immediately upon arrival and seated promptly. I ordered a drink and sweet potato fries to start while I waited for the rest of my party to arrive and wow! Highly recommend. The philly cheesesteak rolls were a bit oily but still fantastic. 

Even over the drinks and the food (both excellent) I loved their customer service most of all. Our server Haley was a phenomenal waitress. She brought all of our orders quickly, gave great recommendations and encouraged us to sign up for the King of the Hill rewards program. My cousin mentioned it was my birthday the next day in passing and Haley brought over a complimentary dessert! Matt, one of the managers of this location, came by and personally wished me a happy birthday as well, taking the time to talk to us about the area and about other Iron Hill Breweries in the area.
Best dumplings in town. Try the soup dumplings, but be prepared. They are hot and loaded with soup!

Just wow. Get the Cajun frittata and grits! Everything was so delicious and the frittata had the perfect amount of spice. I arrived 30 mins before closing and Dylan still offered to make a fresh pot of coffee which I thought was really nice. Parking can be tricky downtown but honestly it's worth the hassle. I will definitely be back!

I'm a frequent regular here because its really good food at most reasonable prices .
Servers always good with special commendation to Cosi ..always friendly fast courteous and professional.
The hostess Mel always finds me a good table and busses it when needed prior to my seating 
Everybody rocks here 
Thanks so much !

My friend and I ate here around New Year's 2019. I am originally from Media, PA, home to one of the first Iron Hill's. I have very fond memories of the artisan pizzas they used to rotate on the menu. The entire chain used to have a crafty 'we're not a chain' kind of vibe. 

Sadly, they seemed to have lost that vibe. The craft pizzas are gone. The specials they were running included prime rib and a rotating burger. I ordered the prime rib and my friend ordered the burger. Along with my prime rib, I also ordered an old vine Zinfandel & a side of mushrooms, to accompany the beef. The huge floor had servers scurrying across its vastness. First, my server brought me a glass of white Zinfandel. A far cry from old vine Zinfandel. Upon sending it back, I didn't get the correct wine until after my prime rib had started getting cold. When the meal was delivered, it was quickly dropped off. Too soon for me to note that they'd forgotten the mushrooms. Our server was nowhere to be found. I actually asked someone near their open kitchen to grab me a side of mushrooms, as my meal had already been delivered. I never saw that person again. In complete frustration, I searched the floor for any server. Eventually, I found one and got my mushrooms and my wine.

It would be one thing if the errors in service were made up for by the quality or innovation of the food. They weren't. My friend's burger was decidedly tiny (which is weird for this sort of brew pub, which usually features too-large portions...) And my prime rib was unexceptional. Accompaniments were a ho-hum baked potato and broccoli.

I understand that Iron Hill has changed their business model and is trying to expand to become a regional or national chain. All I can say is that, based on my dining experience, they've succeeded. My meal was completely unsatisfying and unexceptional, in a way often associated with chain restaurants.

Since moving to Tucson from Scottsdale, I have had a hard time finding a good location for my massages. After a long work week I was definitely feeling the pain in my neck and back. I was super pleased to see I could not only book an appointment online, but also customize the experience if I wished. I made the appointment this morning for an 8:30pm appointment tonight. I absolutely love that I can get a massage so late and feel relaxed right before bedtime. The lady who checked me in was super kind and friendly (a rarity here in Tucson). Alfonso, my massage therapist, greeted me right on time and intently listened when I explained my areas of concern. His massage was absolutely PERFECT! I'm pleased to say I have finally found the Massage Envy in Tucson that is right for me. I highly recommend this location and Alfonso for massages and some relaxation time.
I'm not sure why I always have issues with the food at this location of iron hill. I don't have any issues at the other locations with food or service.
Ugh. Got the trout. Tasteless. Even got lemon to try to add flavor. I don't know what kind of oil they use but it must be wd40. Even the broccoli and side garnish is tasteless.  The porter is ok

I went for the first time in a Monday evening and it was busy! I found a seat at the bar and ordered a white sangria.  The sangria was a little dry but good.  I then ordered the cheeseburger, medium fine with pepper jack cheese and sweet potato fries.  The burger arrived, the fries warm.  When I cut into the burger it was very pink.  As much as I hate to, I had to send it back.  The bartender was very understanding.  A new plate arrived and the bartender stated she'd return in a few to ensure it was to my liking.  True to her word she did and the burger was perfect.  A few minutes later, a woman whom I assume was a manager followed up to ensure the burger was good.  I'm giving 5 stars because they were quick to fix my order and the customer service! I'm definitely going back. Do to the burger issue I didn't get a picture.

Food and beer was great. Our server Justin was great. Management however was terrible. We noticed quite a few times that while the servers were running around and working hard, the manager was on his phone. I work at a restaurant and have management that is always helpful on the floor. When the restaurant is busy, it should be management's responsibility to support the staff, especially during such tough times in the service industry. And that was not the case here.

The food was just OK.  The beer was great!! (And I'm not a beer drinker.)  We had a variety if things: philly cheese egg roast, fish & chips, chopped salad, curry muscles and pretzels. The service was top notch, which made the dining experience enjoyable, but the food was nothing I would run back to get.
Had dinner here today with the family and pleasantly surprised with an outstanding meal! Service was phenomenal and we all were very pleased! Will visit again! Thanks for great experience.
Best breakfast in town!!! If you haven't stopped by for breakfast you're missing out. Fresh ingredients and the best Cuban bread .

4 stars overall.
The food = 5 stars.

Amazing service.  Great portions.  Great prices.  Food was perfect.  You will never leave hungry, and you'll  never leave wanting more flavor.

Octo, burratta, tuna, and zucchini were all just perfect.  Great seasoning, flavors and freshness.

Ahi Tuna can be so "yesterday" at most places, not here.  It's sushi grade.  I've heard so many people claim that, but this is the first time that I've tasted it in a LONG time.  I've eaten tuna all over the world and this was very well-prepared.

Only reason that I wouldn't give it 5 stars overall were two minor issues:

1) They have a liquor license and I am so anti-PA LCB anymore it's sick.  Sun is BYO night.  Sunday night was perfect.

2) They wouldn't swap out a veggie for the peppers on a standard app.  When it's not busy, just make the customer happy when it's a simple substitution. I know how to cook, so I can understand no substitutions on complicated dishes or when it's crazy. 

Service was also great.  We had a gentleman in his 30's or maybe 40's who was full of life and on top of it.  Later, a female serve came out and introduced the cheese plate.  Wow!

I haven't seen a great cheese tray in Philly in ages.  Great selection.

The freshness of their seafood and the willingness to manage a cheese selection (it's very difficult to store), shows what pro's the folks at Paradiso are!

We'll be back!

This was the worst experience I've had in a very long time.
